preamble

decisions.summary: one make detector shared by the log and the guards, the gate's crate-scoped form read as rust-<cmd>
decisions.why: FR-001's classing by target; fixes a found defect (R1) in the task touching it.

decisions.summary: one bucket_of table shared by writer and readers, readers book by the make field, every line carries task
decisions.why: FR-001's one table the readers share; re-booking a past log serves the GM's retrospective.

decisions.summary: bg on launch, BgEnd from the task-notification prompt, inflight on Stop; subagent ends from the subagent transcript
decisions.why: FR-002 and the approved 'logs that end from its completion notice'; the transcript read is where the plan states no hook carries a subagent run's end (R2).

decisions.summary: build, test, cover-run, lint and format phase lines per crate, wall-clock spans
decisions.why: FR-003 as written.

decisions.summary: cover-build phase line per family (naming its crates), not per crate
decisions.why: Physically impossible per crate: one coverage build compiles the family's crates at once, so no per-crate seconds exist to log. The line names every crate it served. The GM's own words ('append their phase seconds') carry no per-crate requirement, and the compile-vs-test split ('how much time ... recompiling') is kept whole.

decisions.summary: land writes cheap, gate, cohort, claims, push phases and an end line with exit code
decisions.why: FR-003 (make land's phases) and FR-005's refused-landing rework count.

decisions.summary: Agent PreToolUse records task; SubagentStop records deduplicated tok, ctx, task; reader keeps last per aid
decisions.why: FR-004 and the approved 'records it at each agent's stop'.

decisions.summary: where-time and feature-report read the same columns module; critical path apart from agent-minutes; rework counted; UNTIL=
decisions.why: FR-005 clause by clause.

decisions.summary: a builder is any agent whose agent_type names no .claude/agents file - every defined agent exempt, where the spec exempts a defined REVIEW agent
decisions.why: The spec's own exclusion, made mechanical. As the plan states (R3, not in the bundle), the rule caught every builder that passed the cap in the window. It would only reach too little if some defined agent that is not a reviewer were dispatched with a task's brief. If such an agent exists in .claude/agents, it must be capped too.

decisions.summary: a general-purpose agent dispatched with no task is capped too
decisions.why: It narrows nothing. The test is structural, so a builder cannot escape the cap through how its brief is worded, which is the real-enforcement reading. As the plan states, every general-purpose dispatch is a brief.

decisions.summary: context_cap_hooks refuses a builder's every call past CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS (GUESS 300k) but the handoff Write; CONTEXT_OK or a recorded make context-ok permit escapes
decisions.why: FR-006 and FR-012. The knob is the spec's GUESS. The handoff Write is tested through the whole guard chain.

decisions.summary: SendMessage to a builder past the cap refused
decisions.why: FR-006 as written.

decisions.summary: SendMessage to a builder whose task has landed: the task is taken ONLY from the meta description's T<n>
decisions.why: FR-006 says a SendMessage resuming a builder whose task has landed is refused. D8 itself says a builder with an unnamed brief exists and must not slip through. Yet D10 finds the task only from a T<n> in the description, so for that builder the landed-task refusal never fires, and its resume leaves no record. Working out the task is not impossible: D2 already has a fallback chain (the task the agent's lines carry, else the clone's task-starts entry at its dispatch). Fix: D10 uses D2's chain, and a builder with any landing of its task after its dispatch is refused, with a red case for a builder whose description names no T<n>.

decisions.summary: every session's and agent's make static runs count toward the task, the main session's too
decisions.why: FR-007 counts runs in one task and names no agent.

decisions.summary: the count window starts at the later of the task's last task-starts entry and its last landing
decisions.why: FR-007 has one reset: 'since its last landing'. Lines are already filtered by task, so a start bound adds nothing except a second reset, and the plan gives no reason for it. Whether an open task can gain a second task-starts entry is unmeasured. If it can, running task-start again zeroes the count with no recorded escape, which turns the refusal into an instruction. Fix: count the task's static lines since its last landing only (or since its FIRST start where it has never landed), with a red case where a second task-start does not reset the count.

decisions.summary: a make or cargo run backgrounded with & and then waited on in the same call passes
decisions.why: The approved fix targets a run whose end no notice reports ('no completion notice came, and it sat idle'). A call that waits on its job does not return before the run ends, so the harness tracks it. Refusing it would refuse a tracked run and serve none of the rule's purpose.

decisions.summary: the pass test is 'no wait later in the command': no command position for wait, and nothing ties the wait to the make job
decisions.why: D12a's reason holds only for a wait that covers the make job, but the plan's test is any later 'wait'. Under it, `make static & echo wait` and `make static & sleep 5 & wait $!` (which waits only for the sleep) both pass, return with the run detached, and leave no record: exactly T225's untracked run. The plan already asks command position for nohup, setsid and disown, and asks none for wait. Fix: pass only a wait at a command position that covers the make or cargo job (a bare wait, or wait $!/%N naming that job with no & between), with red cases for the two forms above.

decisions.summary: main session only (no agent_id), on both permitted no-poll paths including the POLL_OK-escaped loop, longest sleep over POLL_CHECK_S (GUESS 60 s) refused; SLOW_POLL_OK escapes
decisions.why: FR-008 as written. POLL_OK does not bypass it.

decisions.summary: knobs recorded as GUESS constants and a docs/guards.md knob table; make tunables not extended to the tooling crates
decisions.why: The GM's request names no knob register and no make tunables, and no cited FR does either, so leaving tunables as it is narrows nothing asked. The spec's Assumptions text was not in the bundle, so this rests on the plan's statement that the spec names tunables only as where retuning happens.

decisions.summary: a deferral must carry a reason, 'a task id T<n>' and 'lands before T<n>' - checked as a form, not as a FILED task
decisions.why: FR-009 asks for 'its filed task id'. The plan checks for a string T<n>, so a made-up id that is in no tasks.md passes make decide with no record: a form check where the request asked for real enforcement. Checking it is cheap (the feature's tasks.md and tasks-done.md). Fix: the deferral's T<n>, and its lands-before T<n>, must name tasks filed in the feature, with a red case for an unfiled id.

decisions.summary: a class-of-defect fix must carry an observed-date-and-method line
decisions.why: FR-009's second clause as written.

decisions.summary: make land splits T= on commas and whitespace
decisions.why: FR-011, the approved 'Accept commas in T='.

decisions.summary: task-add: if quick is still red after withdrawing the line, the line is restored and the run only reports - no comparison of failures
decisions.why: FR-011 refuses 'on any failure the new line introduces'. When make quick is already red for another reason, a line that adds a failure of its own is restored and passes with no record (T19's third case pins this). It is not impossible to catch: compare the failures with the line to those without it. Fix: refuse and withdraw whenever the with-line run has a failure the without-line run lacks, and keep the line only when the failures are the same; add a red case with a pre-existing failure plus the line's own.

decisions.summary: suites split into numbered shards, the runner stamps the suite when every shard is green, SHARD_BAR_S GUESS about 20 s measured, never a gate
decisions.why: FR-010 and SC-004.

preamble

decisions.summary: One make detector shared by the event log and every guard; command positions also take (, flock, nice, time, timeout N; l7r-gate.sh rust <cmd> read as rust-<cmd>.
decisions.why: FR-001 classes each make run by target; one detector is how that holds. Unchanged since the last reading.

decisions.summary: One bucket_of table shared by writer and readers, past logs re-booked by their make field; every line carries task (T= of the command, else the subagent meta description's T<n>, else the clone's last task-starts entry).
decisions.why: FR-001's 'by one table the readers share'; the task field serves the GM's per-task breakdown. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Background run end from the task-notification prompt (BgEnd), inflight on Stop/SubagentStop, subagent ends from their transcript's queued_command row, an unended run open to the window's end.
decisions.why: FR-002 as written, which is the approved 'logs that end from its completion notice'. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Phase lines carry wall-clock spans; coverage builds are timed per family (naming the family's crates), not per crate.
decisions.why: FR-003 says per crate, but one coverage build serves a whole family at once and the runs go side by side (R6), so a per-crate cover-build time cannot be measured. That is physical impossibility. The line still names every crate in the family. Unchanged since the last reading, so the ruling stands.

decisions.summary: land writes cheap/gate/cohort/claims/push Phase lines and an end line with its exit code and tasks (T= split as D16), read by D10 and D11 for foreground and background landings alike.
decisions.why: FR-003's landing phases and FR-005's rework count. The new tasks field is how D10 and D11 recognize a landing, so it only enforces FR-006 and FR-007.

decisions.summary: Agent dispatch task from its description; SubagentStop records tok (deduped by message.id), ctx and task; the reader keeps the last per aid.
decisions.why: FR-004 as written. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: where-time gains the tests/compile/gate/land/review/background/model columns and UNTIL=; critical path apart from agent-minutes; rework = refused landings plus plan re-rounds; feature-report reads the same columns module.
decisions.why: FR-005 clause by clause; it is the GM's request for the overall breakdown. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: A builder is a payload with agent_id whose agent_type names no .claude/agents/<type>.md; a general-purpose agent with no task is capped too.
decisions.why: This is a mechanical test of the spec's definition ('dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent'). Requiring a T<n> would let a builder with an unnamed brief through the cap, which would not be real enforcement. Anything it over-catches has the recorded make context-ok escape. Unchanged since the last reading, so it carries forward. Note: 'among defined agents, one call' is a count with no date or method; it is unchanged text and does not block.

decisions.summary: context_cap_hooks: past CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS (GUESS 300k), a builder's every tool call is refused except the Write of its handoff file, naming the path and next step; escapes CONTEXT_OK and a recorded make context-ok permit; the handoff case runs through the whole guard chain.
decisions.why: FR-006's cap and handoff exit, with the escape and message FR-012 requires. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Resume refused for a builder past the cap or whose task SUCCESSFULLY landed (end code 0 naming it, or ticked or archived) after dispatch. The task is found by meta T<n>, else its FIRST line's task, else the task-starts entry in force at dispatch.
decisions.why: FR-006 as written. The revision closes what the last round raised: no description-only lookup, the first line rather than the latest, the entry in force at dispatch, a background landing found through its end line's tasks, a refused landing not counted. T13 carries a red case for each of these.

decisions.summary: When no task can be found anywhere (no T<n>, no line carrying one, no task-starts entry before dispatch), the resume passes and 'context-cap: resume, no task' is written to the guard log.
decisions.why: Physically impossible: with no task there is nothing to test for having landed. It is only reachable when the feature had no task-start before the dispatch, because D2 stamps every later line with the active task. The pass leaves a record. LEGITIMATE only for the landed half. A builder past the cap with no task is still refused, because the bullet does not reach the cap. The plan should say so, and T13 should carry a case for it (see the D15 entry's list).

decisions.summary: static_runs_hooks counts a task's make static PreToolUse lines (every session and agent) since its last SUCCESSFUL landing, else since its FIRST task-start; a later task-start resets nothing; the third is refused naming the delta's crate-scoped checks; STATIC_OK escapes; knob GUESS 2.
decisions.why: FR-007 literally: 'a third make static in one task since its last landing'. It counts by task, so the main session's runs count too. The revision removes the last round's unrecorded resets (a second task-start, a refused landing), and T14 carries a red case for each.

decisions.summary: A make or cargo job followed by & is refused unless a wait that COVERS it follows: at a command position, in the same list and shell, unconditional, not backgrounded, and bare, wait $! with no & between, or wait %N. nohup/setsid/disown at a command position are refused. A saved-pid wait is refused. DETACH_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-008 lists & with no exception. But the approved fix was 'a guard refusing that pattern', meaning T225's detached run whose end the session never learned of. A covering wait keeps the Bash call open until the run ends, so the harness tracks it. The exception is implied by the request's own words, and refusing it would serve no part of the request's purpose. The revision makes 'covers' real: words, other shells, conditional waits, a backgrounded wait and a stale $! are all refused, each with a T15 red case. Refusing the saved-pid form is stricter than FR-008 and is within it. Notes, not blocking: wait %N has no case either way in T15; setsid and disown have no firing case (only nohup does); and whether D1 sees '{ ...; } &', 'VAR=x make ... &' or 'env ... make &' cannot be judged from this bundle, so T02 or T15 should pin those forms.

decisions.summary: On both permitted no-poll paths, a main-session (no agent_id) loop whose longest sleep exceeds POLL_CHECK_S (GUESS 60 s) is refused naming the 60 s form; SLOW_POLL_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-008's second clause. It turns the approved 'shorter poll loop on my side' into a refusal, as 'real enforcement' asks. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Knobs carry GUESS at their point of change and a knob table in docs/guards.md; make tunables is not extended to the tooling crates.
decisions.why: The GM's request never mentions make tunables. Its mention is a spec Assumption about where retuning happens, and the knob table (knob, value, label, the data that retunes it) serves the same purpose. Unchanged since the last reading, so the ruling stands.

decisions.summary: deferral_unformed: a non-none Found-and-left item must carry a reason, a task id and 'lands before T<n>', both ids FILED in the feature (a box of tasks.md OR an entry of tasks-done.md); a class fix needs an 'observed <date>, method:' line; DEFER_FORM_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-009 asks for 'its filed task id and its order ("lands before ...")', so that a deferred defect actually gets fixed, and in a known order (the approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task'). Accepting an entry of tasks-done.md, which T17's second variant passes on purpose, guts both. (a) An order 'lands before T124' where T124 has already landed cannot be kept, so it orders nothing. (b) A deferral to a task that is already done will never be fixed by that task. Any feature has dozens of done ids, so a done id passes the check as easily as the made-up id the last round flagged: the hole has moved, not closed. That is a word-level reading of 'filed' that is fatal to the rule's purpose. Required, all in one revision: (1) at make decide, when the item is judged, both ids must name an OPEN task (an unticked box in the feature's tasks.md), and a section already decided is not refused later because an id it named has since landed; (2) the order's id differs from the deferral's own task id ('T123 lands before T123' is refused); (3) T17 drops the passing tasks-done variant and adds refused cases for a done deferral id, a done order id and a self-order, plus the case T17's own heading names and its list lacks: a reason and a filed task id with no 'lands before' at all, refused. Also, from D10-no-task: say that a builder past the cap with no task is still refused, and add that case to T13.

decisions.summary: land splits T= on commas and whitespace. task-add runs quick's check lines (from make -n quick) each to its own end, with and without the line, compares the findings as a multiset with line and column numbers masked, refuses and withdraws on any new finding, and restores the line only when the findings are identical; QUICK_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-011 as written. 'On any failure the new line introduces, withdraws the line and refuses' now holds even when an earlier check is already red or a finding in the same file is shifted, and T19 carries a red case for each. Restoring the line when the findings are the same is FR-011's own boundary (the line introduced no failure), not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Hook suites may be sharded as test-<name>.<k>.sh, stamped green when every shard is; entry-gate split by its two cases, the other two by case groups to about 20 s or less (SHARD_BAR_S GUESS, measured, never a gate).
decisions.why: FR-010 and SC-004. The approved improvement 5 is a split, not a refusal, so FR-012 does not reach it. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Constitution check: event_log_hooks fields move to fields.rs past the file cap; XIII baseline in a detached worktree; the two defects found while measuring (the disagreeing make detectors, booking by the frozen cat) are fixed in T02 and T08.
decisions.why: Process the constitution requires; the XIV fixes are defects (wrong answers) inside FR-001 and FR-005's own scope.

decisions.summary: T12 first captures a real subagent PreToolUse payload under L7R_GUARD_DUMP, removed before landing, and pins it as the fixture.
decisions.why: It measures the schema the cap depends on (R2's 'not yet observed') and adds no behavior that survives the landing.

decisions.summary: The close measures SC-001, SC-002 and SC-005 on the first full day after landing, checks the knob table, and writes the feature report.
decisions.why: The spec's success criteria, measured as the request asks ('I'd like to see some actual numbers').

### T04 (FR-002: no line marks a background run's end, so a wait cannot be booked to the run behind it - research R2)
### T24 (<why: the finding or measurement that files it>)
### T24 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A BgEnd is written only for a prompt that OPENS with a <task-notification> whose <tool-use-id> stands before any <result>.
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for a background run's end logged from its completion notice; this is how the notice is recognized, and it drops no notice: of 3,390 user rows carrying a <task-notification> in the -diagram and diagram-backlog transcripts of the last 4 days, none held two notices and none failed to open with one (observed 2026-11-20, method: python -I tally of user-type rows by count of <task-notification> and by whether the text opens with it).

decisions.summary: An agent's notice (summary opening 'Agent "' or an Agent launch line) writes no BgEnd; its SubagentStop is its end.
decisions.why: An agent's end is still logged, by SubagentStop, so FR-002's purpose of booking a wait to the run in flight still holds. The earlier CLEAR T04 approach already said an agent notification writes none; this only fixes the test after the measurement that agent notices carry a tool-use id too.

decisions.summary: A Workflow's and a Monitor's notice each write a BgEnd, wider than data-model's 'a background shell ended'.
decisions.why: FR-002 says 'a background run', not 'a background shell'. These are runs the session waits on, and booking a wait to them is the request's 'which run a wait was waiting on'. It widens data-model.md's wording, not the spec, and it is not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: The BgEnd goes in the log holding the launching call's line and copies that line's make, cat, task and fallback mark, with the launch's t as t0. A launch no log holds ends beside the prompt's line.
decisions.why: This serves FR-002's 'with its span' and its pairing of a wait to its run. Filing by T26's chain would put the end away from its launch. No requested behavior is cut.

decisions.summary: A BgEnd's t is when the notice reached the session, which can be later than the run's end while the session is mid-turn. T08 may take the end from the queue's enqueue row where it needs the span.
decisions.why: FR-002 logs the end FROM the completion notice, and the notice's arrival is what the hook sees. The lateness only covers time when the session was mid-turn, so it was not waiting, and booking a wait between turns, FR-002's second clause, is unaffected. A run's own duration is read by T08, which has the enqueue row as its route; this block hands the reader no wrong wait booking.

decisions.summary: append_row stamps t where absent, takes sid from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, files the row by its task through T26's chain, and writes nothing for a row with no ev.
decisions.why: This is D4's writer for FR-003's Phase lines, already accepted. These are mechanics, not a change of what is logged.

decisions.summary: events::load_all returns the stream and the ASIDE kinds (BgEnd, Phase) separately, keeping a line repeated whole only once.
decisions.why: This is the already-CLEAR guard keeping the new kinds out of the time-gap stream (the T207 failure). Dropping exact duplicate lines removes no information.

decisions.summary: The live BgEnd was replayed through the clone's built l7r-guard, since hooks run the mirror's binary until landing. The first real one is read off the log after landing.
decisions.why: This is a verification route, not a scope decision, and it narrows no FR-002 behavior. No refusal is involved, so the GM's real-enforcement instruction is not engaged.

decisions.summary: task-add's unfilled template for T24 (heading, approach, checklist part A).
decisions.why: Placeholders decide nothing. When filled, the block's digest changes and it is owed review again.

### T05 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A fresh run's one-crate-at-a-time cargo test in answer's loop is preceded by a `cargo test --no-run` with the run's own words, booked `build`, then the `cargo test`, booked `test`.
decisions.why: This is the split D4 and the GM's 'how much time are we spending on recompiling things' ask for, and it answers the earlier ruling. The extra call's cost carries a one-shot label (0.044-0.047 s, 2026-11-20, method stated). It is a phase line on the requested path, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: test-no-counters' cargo test gets the same split: a `--no-run` booked `build`, then the run booked `test`, both with its features.
decisions.why: Same split as the fresh run, adjudicated on its own. Its compile is now booked `build` and its tests `test`, as D4 asks. The earlier NOT LEGITIMATE no longer applies.

decisions.summary: A build that named no binary: binary_key's `--no-run` already wrote its `build` line, and the following cargo test is booked `test` alone. A failed binary-key build is asked again plain and booked `build`, and nothing runs after it.

The block answers it with a one-shot measurement (2026-11-20: no Compiling line, Finished in 0.03 s, method stated), and a red-first test pins it to one `build` line. So no compile is booked as tests. Re-asking a failed build plain is compile time booked `build`, which is the requested split.

decisions.why: A kept result ran nothing, and `dead` reads source text with no cargo, so there are no build, test or cover seconds to book.

decisions.why: It is a stage run of the work budget, not a check's build, test or cover, which are the kinds FR-003 names. Its Bash call is still booked whole under its make target by FR-001/FR-005.

decisions.summary: `test-times` writes no phase line.

decisions.summary: cover-build writes one line per family's group (crates named), and a failed group's crates asked again one at a time each write their own.
decisions.why: This carries D4's own per-family reading, which D4 names for the plan review, and it is not a decision of this section. A coverage build serves the whole family at once, so it cannot be timed per crate.

decisions.summary: Lines are written at kept.rs binary_key (build), side.rs run_built (test), cover.rs build (cover-build) and run_one (cover-run, none for a failed build), and lint and format per crate in answer's loop, never inside check.

blocks: ### T06 (FR-003: a landing's cheap pass, gate, claims round and push are one span - the spec's User Story 1)
### T06 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: T06 (data half, FR-003, 'Performance work? no') runs ahead of the refusals after the GM's 2026-11-20 reorder; it comes before T10, T13 and T14, which read its end line
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-20 words put the six improvements first. D10 and D11 (two of those improvements) read a landing from this end line, so T06 is a prerequisite of the improvement fixes. Doing it first serves the order.

decisions.summary: A new land/phase.rs writes each step's line through append_row_for in T05's row form (ev Phase, src land, step, t0, t1, t, code, make, clone). land.rs wraps each step and long_runs.rs the cohort
decisions.why: This is FR-003's 'make land its phases' seconds ... as event lines' and D5's Phase lines, written through the one writer.

decisions.summary: The steps tile the landing: cheap, gate (the whole second pass, wider than D5's '(make done)'), claims, push (the ticks, their commit, the push, a failed push's revert), and the push's tail booked to after-push
decisions.why: FR-003 names the cheap refusals, the gate, the claims round and the push. Booking every part of the landing to one of them serves the request's 'where our time went'. A wider gate books more of the landing's real time and drops nothing.

decisions.summary: cohort has its own line, nested inside the gate line's span; its code is minus the signal when a red gate stops it
decisions.why: D5 lists cohort as a step. Nesting it keeps the time from being counted twice, and its own seconds are still on its own line.

decisions.summary: cheap and claims write code 2 when they refuse; a raising step writes code 1; a step that did not run writes no line
decisions.why: These are D5's exit codes made concrete for each step.

decisions.summary: For a landing whose push went out, end is written the moment the push goes out (exit 0 or 3): landed true, and its code is the push's. It is no longer the last line, and a tail that raises leaves end at the push's code while the process exits 1. A landing that never pushed writes its end at its exit with landed false
decisions.why: D5's wording is 'a last end line with its exit code'. D5 says what that line is FOR: refusals counted from the landing's own line, and D10 and D11 reading whether a task landed. D7 reads landed 'whatever its code', so a pushed landing whose tail raised is a landing, and the tail's exit 1 still stands on the after-push line. No reader loses a fact. A refused landing still ends with its own code and landed false. This is the mechanism the previous round asked for, and it makes a stop in the tail read as landed. It departs from D5's wording, not from its outcome.

decisions.summary: A new step, after-push, books the push's tail (the fresh block's start, the work-budget view after an engine landing). It comes after end, and a raise there is its own line's code
decisions.why: FR-003 names 'the push' as a phase, and this is the push's tail, split out so that end can be written at the push. Every second is still booked to a named line. A new step name for part of a requested phase only makes the requested breakdown finer.

decisions.why: D5 requires tasks split as D16 splits them. D7 and D11 define landed on the end line.

decisions.summary: Each phase line carries the first task landed as task; end carries every id asked
decisions.why: A run of several tasks cannot be divided between them. D5 puts the full list on end, which is where D7, D10 and D11 read a landing, and every second is still booked.

decisions.summary: main's own refusals (no NOTE=, no feature directory) write an end for the tasks they name; a usage refusal that names no task writes none
decisions.why: D5 defines end by 'the task ids it was asked to land'. A usage refusal was asked to land nothing, so D5 owes no line for it.

decisions.summary: landed is true when the push went out (exit 0, or 3 MERGED). D7's rework, D10's and D11's landing, T13, T14 and the data model's Landing read landed, restated with this task
decisions.why: D7 and D11 in the accepted spec say exactly this. The restatement brings the other tasks into line with the spec and does not widen it.

decisions.summary: append_row_for(root, feature, row) beside append_row in the held writer (make guard-edit) files a line in the feature its word names, before T26's chain. A blank word or one naming no feature leaves the chain as it was, and T05's callers are unchanged
decisions.why: FR-005's readers read per feature. Without this, a landing of a task never started in the clone would be filed under fallback, where T13 and T14 would not find its end. It reaches only the new callers and adds no behavior beyond what the requested lines need.

decisions.summary: make is the outermost make's first goal, read from /proc as T05's lines read theirs; land when no make is above
decisions.why: This is T05's row form applied to this source.

decisions.summary: A landing stopped (make land-stop, TERM) before its push went out writes no line past its last finished step and reads as open, never as refused
decisions.why: A stop is not a refusal, and a landing stopped before its push did not land. Reading it as open answers D7, D10 and D11 correctly. The running step's split is lost, but FR-002 still books the run's span.

decisions.summary: A landing stopped in the push's tail (after-push) already has its end written, landed true
decisions.why: This closes the previous round's NOT LEGITIMATE finding. The end at the push now carries landed true before the tail starts, so D10 and D11 read the task as landed, and red-first cases cover a tail that raises after the push.

decisions.summary: One window stays open. A stop while sync-with-main.sh done runs, after the remote took the push but before the script reports it, writes no end. The section points to the push's tick commit on main as the record
decisions.why: Last round's exception rested on implementation awkwardness ('no signal handler's work'). This one rests on knowledge: until the push command reports, the landing process does not hold the fact that the remote took the push, so no writer in the landing can record landed true in that interval. A pre-push guess would write a false landed whenever the push then fails. The rule is impossible here, not merely awkward, and the section has already shrunk the gap to that interval. The tick commit on main is not what makes this legitimate: D10 and D11 as cited read the end line, not main. The real outcome in the window is that the landing reads as open, never as refused. D7's rework count therefore stays right, D10 misses a resume of that task's builder, and D11 keeps that task's static count unreset. That is one rare interleaving (a manual stop during the push itself), with the outcome confined to that one task. This is the one case the previous round's requirement ('once a landing's push has gone out, a later stop must not leave it reading as unlanded') cannot reach. The ruling covers only the interval before the script reports the push went out. The block also says 'before the script exits'. If sync-with-main.sh reports success and then goes on working before it exits, that stretch is not unknowable: end must be written when the report comes, and an end held until the exit would be outside this ruling.

decisions.why: Each fix makes the guard read FR-008 and D12 correctly: a heredoc body or a grep -c argument is a mention, not an invocation (constitution XVIII, cited by the block), and D12 already says 'wait $!' covers only the last job. The corpus refusal it adds is a real 'setsid nohup make done ... &', which FR-008 names. Nothing that was asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A BARE 'wait' in an enclosing list of the same shell covers a make/cargo job inside a loop or if body ('for t in a b; do make $t & done; wait' passes), where D12 and T15's line say the wait must be in the job's own list; 'wait $!' and 'wait %N' still cover only in the job's own list.
decisions.why: This narrows the guard's literal reach under D12. It is legitimate because refusing the case would defeat the request's own purpose, not because it is more convenient. The approved fix was 'a guard refusing that pattern': T225's plain '&', whose end sent no completion notice so the session sat idle. D12 gives the reason a covering wait passes: 'Such a call does not return before the run ends, so the harness tracks it.' A bare wait waits for every child of its shell. This review measured it on 2026-11-20 by timing bash -c runs with $EPOCHREALTIME: 'for t in 1 2; do sleep 1.5 & done; wait' took 1.51 s and 'if true; then sleep 1.5 & fi; wait' took 1.51 s, so the call cannot return early and the run is tracked. Refusing it would block a tracked run that is not the pattern the GM approved refusing. The reading keeps every other condition D12 sets: command position, same shell (not a subshell), run unconditionally, not backgrounded. It does not widen to 'wait $!' or 'wait %N', which would be wrong after a loop. The earlier CLEAR text had accepted a broader wording ('same list read as same shell' for any wait); this one is tighter.

decisions.why: FR-008, D12 and FR-012 settle this. It is the GM-approved improvement 3, 'a guard refusing that pattern'.

decisions.summary: A bare wait after a loop, if or case body run in the same shell covers the jobs started inside that body. D12 literally asks for 'a command of the same list as the job's &'.
decisions.why: This is unchanged from the ruling of 2026-11-20. D12's own test is that a covering wait means the call 'does not return before the run ends, so the harness tracks it', and a bare wait 'waits for every job'. Bash runs (timed by EPOCHREALTIME, 2026-11-20) showed that a bare wait in the enclosing same-shell list waits for jobs started in for, if, while, case and { } bodies. Refusing those calls would refuse tracked, correct work, which is a defect under XIV. The purpose of the request, refusing the UNTRACKED pattern, stays whole. The block keeps the ruling's limit: compounds in another shell stay refused, and wait $! and wait %N cover only in the job's own list.

decisions.summary: A compound that runs in another shell stays refused even when a later wait follows. 6 compound-in-a-pipeline cases are pinned (for ...; done | cat; wait, { make x & } | cat; wait, ..., the sixth ( make x & ) | cat; wait), and 2 waits inside the part pass. For a bare ( ), a backgrounded loop and $( ), the block states they are refused.
decisions.why: This is D12's literal rule ('in the same shell (not in a ( ) or $( ) of its own)'), and it is the limit the previous ruling set. The block says the 6 pipeline cases were already refused before they were added. With the pipeline's subshell cut deleted, 5 of the 6 went red, and the sixth is a ( ), which is a separate shell whatever the pipeline does.

decisions.summary: wait $! and wait %N cover only in the job's own list.
decisions.why: This is D12's literal rule, the stricter reading.

decisions.summary: The shared readers' defects are fixed in T15, with T30 folded in. strip_heredocs takes a heredoc whose opener line continues past its delimiter. strip_quotes keeps a quoted string only after an interpreter's -c (flags joined: bash -lc, sh -ec, python3 -c), never after grep -c or git -c, and blanks the strings quoted inside a kept one. make::invoked reads setsid [opts] as a wrapper, reads 'make;' as a call, and reads a goal-less make as .DEFAULT_GOAL; a goal it cannot read (make $T) still names none. Each fix has a red-first test, and no_poll_hooks reads through these readers, with its own readers retired.
decisions.why: This answers the previous BLOCKED finding in the first way it offered: fix the shared readers in T15 and point the guard at them. These are defects (a check passing bad work or refusing good work). Fixing them in the task that found them is the GM-approved improvement 4 ('Briefs that default to fixing in the task') and fix-as-we-go, and it serves D1's single shared detector. It adds no behavior the request did not ask for. The gate's land and rustc callers skip a goal-less make's .DEFAULT_GOAL as they skipped its empty goal before, so they keep their behavior. make $T naming no goal is not a defect left. A goal held in a shell variable cannot be read from the command text, and the job is still refused when it is backgrounded: 'for t in a b; do make $t & done | cat; wait' is among the refused cases. 'Found and left? none' is now true.

decisions.summary: Every guard is replayed on the four frozen corpora (1,134 commands) before and after the shared fix. 3 verdicts moved, each named as a correction: no-poll refuses a setsid nohup make done & launch; no-poll brackets a pkill -f "pytest" it had missed; main-tree honors a # MAIN_TREE_OK: reason that the old misreading swallowed. main-tree-refusals-2026-09.json row 130 is relabeled from rewrote to allowed, and its split moves from 109/64 to 110/63.

It does not change what the guard does.

decisions.summary: slow_poll in no_poll_hooks, called first in the POLL_OK-escaped branch and before file_wait; a payload with agent_id passes untouched; -c strings and backgrounded calls judged too

decisions.summary: the pace is the longest sleep at a command position inside a loop, head counted, s/m/h/d units read and several numbers summed as GNU sleep reads them; a quoted string, a sleep with no loop and a sleep after done are not a pace
decisions.why: FR-008 refuses a 'wait loop' that checks less often than 60 s; reading the loop's actual interval as the shell would is the rule. A non-loop sleep and a quoted string are not a checking loop, so passing them follows FR-008's wording.

decisions.summary: a sleep whose number the text does not give (sleep $N) is no pace and passes
decisions.why: FR-008 refuses a loop that checks less often than 60 s, and this lets one through unjudged, so it narrows. It is legitimate because the hook reads the command text before the shell expands it, so a pace absent from the text cannot be judged. Refusing every unreadable sleep instead would refuse compliant loops (sleep $N with N=5), which would be new behavior the GM did not ask for. The 45-of-45 replay does not support this: it selected literal sleeps of 300 or more. The bundle does not say whether a literal assigned in the same command (N=480; ... sleep $N) is resolved. blocks: ### T14 (FR-007: `make static` was the edit loop - the spec's User Story 3)
### T14 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A make static call another guard refused (a PreToolUse line and no result line) is not counted as a run.
decisions.why: FR-007 refuses a third `make static`; a call refused before it ran is not a run of make static on the plain reading, and counting it would spend a run on nothing (measured 1 of 33 and 8 of 340 such lines, one-shot labeled). D11 is restated to it; the restatement matches the request rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: A make static still in flight (no PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure line yet), e.g. a foreground run in another session of the same task, is not yet counted.
decisions.why: Ruled on purpose. The request's improvement 2 targets make static as the edit loop: each iteration of a loop waits for the previous run's result, so every run that feeds a loop has its result line and is counted; the in-flight window only admits a run concurrent with another in the same task, and that run is counted the moment it finishes, so the next call is refused. The edit-loop pattern cannot live in the gap; the purpose survives. Not ruled on an impossibility claim (the bundle does not measure whether the guard log could tell a refused call from an in-flight one).

decisions.summary: The event log writer adds `makes` (every target of a multi-target call) and the count reads `make` or `makes`, so `make rust-test CRATE=x && make static` is counted.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-007: without it a compound call escapes the count while the trigger fires on it. Delete FR-007 and the field has nothing to do.

decisions.summary: Count keyed on (feature, task) via filed_at's chain, reading only that feature's log; main session and builders share one count.
decisions.why: FR-007 counts per task; D11: every session and agent's run counts.

decisions.summary: Since the task's last landing with landed true naming it in `tasks` (any exit code), else its FIRST task-starts entry (second stamp compared as .000Z), else every line.
decisions.why: FR-007 'since its last landing'; D11/D10's definition (landed true resets, a refused landing does not; a later task-start resets nothing). Reading `tasks` rather than `task` makes a batch landing reset each of its tasks, as D11 requires.

decisions.summary: A call whose line carries no task passes, logged passed/no-task.
decisions.why: FR-007 is scoped 'in one task'; D2 files a task on every line where one is known, falling back to the clone's last task-start for the feature, so a call with no task is outside any task and has nothing to count against. Note: the block cites 'D10's precedent' for this, but D10 as quoted in spec-cited.md carries no no-task clause; the citation is unsupported and the decision stands on FR-007 and D2 instead.

decisions.summary: Refusal names, per crate of the delta (merge-base diff plus untracked files, mapped to nearest [package] Cargo.toml), `make rust-test CRATE=<c>` and the gate script's lint/format/cover --crate; `make quick` when no crate changed; then make static once before land; STATIC_OK escape; each named command pinned as passing the Bash-reading guards.

Note: FR-012 asks for an escape reason of two words or more; the block says 'a bare token refused' and 'with a reason' and does not state the two-word floor - silence, not a decision, so no ruling, but the built check should be the FR-012 one.

decisions.summary: slow_poll (split into no_poll_hooks/pace.rs under constitution X's 1,000-line bar) is called first in the POLL_OK-escaped branch and before file_wait; a payload with agent_id passes untouched by the pace check; -c strings and backgrounded calls are judged too
decisions.why: This is D13 as written: both permitted paths, before either returns, and the main session only (no agent_id). A -c string that a shell runs is the same loop spelled another way, so reading it enforces FR-008 and adds no reach. Splitting the file is housekeeping, not a decision about scope.

decisions.summary: the pace is the longest sleep at a command position inside a loop, with the head counted, s/m/h/d units read and several numbers summed as GNU sleep reads them; a quoted string, a sleep with no loop, a sleep after done and a redirection after a sleep are not a pace
decisions.why: FR-008 refuses a 'wait loop' that checks less often than 60 s. Reading the loop's real interval the way the shell would is that rule. A sleep outside a loop and a quoted string are not a checking loop, so passing them follows FR-008's wording.

decisions.summary: replaces the earlier pass of sleep $N: a variable the command sets (N=480, export, quoted, an env prefix, several assignments) is read at the largest value it is given, and a length still unreadable ($N set nowhere, arithmetic, a substitution, infinity) is refused as endless, naming the literal sleep 60 form, with SLOW_POLL_OK as the escape
decisions.why: This no longer narrows. Every main-session wait loop now gets judged, which is FR-008's rule with no carve-out. Refusing a length the guard cannot read is enforcement of the requested rule, not new behavior. The guard cannot show that such a loop checks within 60 s. The refusal names the compliant form and offers FR-012's recorded escape. The spec already does the same for D12's unreadable 'wait $P'. Taking the largest value assigned is a conservative reading of the same rule. The GM asked for 'real enforcement and not just instructions', and this closes the gap my earlier ruling left open. The plan-blocks review overruled that ruling (LEGITIMATE), and this block follows the review.

decisions.summary: a pre-existing defect is fixed: SLEEP_RE and sleep_in_loop required a digit, so a loop whose sleep takes a variable (until curl -s x; do sleep $N; done) never reached the loop branch and passed even the busy-wait refusal, a subagent's included. The branch is now entered wherever the pace reader finds a sleep in a loop
decisions.why: Under constitution XIV this is a defect: a check that passes bad work. HEAD's guard was observed letting the loop through (rc 0, with a method recorded). It sits in the file and the reader T16 changes, and fixing defects as they are found is the standing rule. The fix does not create new behavior. It makes the existing busy-wait refusal reach a spelling that had slipped past it, and the frozen corpora show 0 of 1,134 verdicts moved. That is consistent with 'the existing no-poll cases unchanged'.

decisions.summary: the refusal names the same command with every sleep over the knob at sleep 60. SLOW_POLL_OK escapes and is recorded, and it is masked before POLL_OK is read, so it grants nothing POLL_OK grants. Thin reasons (empty, one word quoted or bare, one word after the colon) are refused and pinned
decisions.why: D13 names the compliant form and the SLOW_POLL_OK escape. FR-012 requires an escape with a reason of two words or more, recorded, and a message naming the compliant command. Pinning the refusal of one-word reasons enforces FR-012's exact wording. The masking makes the escape do only what it says.

decisions.summary: the guard's own rewrites and offers, fed back from the main session, are never refused for their pace
decisions.why: Those forms are at or under the knob, so FR-008 does not reach them. Testing that they pass enforces the compliant side of the rule.

decisions.summary: a defect that predates T16 is fixed: shared::wait's condition grammar did not read proof_of_life's clause, so the guard refused its own invited file-wait rerun as a busy-wait. One existing test's expectation is changed to ask that the fed-back wait get no answer
decisions.why: The guard was refusing correct work on one of D13's two permitted paths, the path T16 adds its check to. That is a defect under XIV and is fixed as the work goes. The changed test is where the defect was hidden ('rewritten()' read a refusal as no rewrite), so changing it does not depart from 'the existing no-poll cases unchanged'.

decisions.why: FR-008 and D13 name the knob as 60 s and GUESS, and D14 asks for the label at the point of change.

blocks: ### T17 (FR-009: two of the window's first-round plan-review blocks were deferrals with no order - the spec's User Story 5)
### T17 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A found-and-left item that says it is fixed in the task (fixed here, fixed in this task, before its tick, before T<own> lands) passes without a reason, filed id and order, unless it names an id it is filed as or lands before.
decisions.why: D15's visible sentence requires every non-none item to carry reason, id and order, so this narrows D15's text. But FR-009 refuses only an item that DEFERS a defect, and an item fixed in the task defers nothing; the GM approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task', so requiring a filed task id of an item that is fixed would contradict the request. The guard that an item naming a filed/order id is judged as a deferral keeps the pass from being used to hide one.

decisions.summary: An item that says it is not a defect (not a defect, no wrong outcome, constitution XIV) passes.
decisions.why: Narrows D15's 'any non-none item' wording, but FR-009's own words reach only an item that 'defers a defect', and constitution XIV (the GM 2026-11-19) holds that a difference with no wrong outcome is not a defect and is not to be fixed. Demanding a filed fix task for a non-defect would apply a standard the GM struck. Same id-naming guard applies.

decisions.summary: A deferral owes 'Not fixed here' plus two words of reason, filed as T<n> (or added to / folded into), lands before T<m> (lists read whole), order id not equal to filed id, each id a box of tasks.md or tasks-done.md; make decide adds that each id is an unticked box now.
decisions.why: This is FR-009's three parts (why, filed id, order) made checkable; added to / folded into still name a filed task id; the open test at make decide makes the order real enforcement as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A class fix is detected by every/all the before writer, reader, form, file, caller, instance, copy, site or guard, or 'each of the', and then owes an observed/measured line with its method.
decisions.why: FR-009's named forms (every writer, every form, every file of a kind) are all reached and the list is a superset of them; a mechanical trigger has to be a word test, and nothing FR-009 names falls outside it.

decisions.summary: The class test reads the found-and-left items and checklist item 12 (Before any fix).
decisions.why: FR-009 asks about the section's FIX; in the plan template the fix is declared in item 12 and the found-and-left answer, so reading those is reading the fix.

decisions.summary: make plan-delta runs the timeless half (form and ids filed in tasks.md or tasks-done.md) on a changed block; a section whose deferral's task has since landed is not refused.
decisions.why: FR-009 names make decide; running the same rule on a later edit only enforces it against a decided section being changed into an unformed one (the GM: 'real enforcement and not just instructions'). Not requiring the ids to be open after landing narrows nothing FR-009 asks, which is a check at decision time.

decisions.summary: A section decided under DEFER_FORM_OK passes make plan-delta after its block changes, the escape found in the guard log; the escape excuses only deferral findings.
decisions.why: It relaxes only the plan-delta check, which is enforcement beyond FR-009's make decide; at make decide, where FR-009 places the refusal, nothing is relaxed, and the escape was recorded with its reason as FR-012 requires.

decisions.summary: The tool records DEFER_FORM_OK itself (guard log rule defer-form-ok and dev/bypass-log/) instead of D15's $(LOGESCAPE) line, and only on a run that passes (decide once decided, plan-delta only where it excused a finding); a thin reason is refused.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for an escape of two words or more that is recorded; it is recorded, once, whenever it is used. A run that is refused or excuses nothing did not use the escape. Mechanism choice; D15's text is restated to match (found-and-left).

decisions.summary: make plan-delta reads the guard log only for a changed block with a deferral finding, once a run, parsing only files naming the rule.
decisions.why: A cost choice that changes no outcome.

decisions.summary: plan-done.md is never read by make decide or plan-delta and the tick and landing call neither, so the 28 refused archived sections are not re-judged.
decisions.why: FR-009 is a refusal at make decide of a section being decided; archived sections were decided and ticked before the rule existed and no make decide runs on them. Nothing FR-009 asks is left out.

decisions.summary: Makefile FREE_TEXT and help lines for DEFER_FORM_OK, D15 restated, docs/guards.md row and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md plan row are fixed by the session before T17 lands, outside the builder's brief.
decisions.why: Fixed before the task lands, not deferred; matches the GM-approved default of fixing in the task.

decisions.summary: T17 is tagged [perf] under FR-013.
decisions.why: It is improvement 4 of the six the GM ordered first on 2026-11-20 ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'), and it shortens the builders' loop, which FR-013 names.

blocks: ### T12 (FR-006: builders past a large context slowed the window's critical path - the spec's User Story 2, research R3)
### T12 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: a new guard context_cap_hooks, PreToolUse *, after event_log_hooks in guards(); its files held by make guard-edit
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for a guard refusing a builder's tool call past a threshold; this is where and how it is placed. Nothing the request or FR-006 says is narrowed.

decisions.summary: payloads captured from Claude Code itself (claude -p, a scratch hook) rather than a dump in the clone, pinned as payloads.json
decisions.why: A method for finding the payload's real keys (agent_id, agent_type, transcript_path), labeled with date and method; it decides nothing about what is refused.

decisions.summary: no agent_id passes before any read (main session); an agent_type naming the clone's .claude/agents/<type>.md passes on a stat
decisions.why: FR-006 defines a builder as an agent with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; the main session is not an agent. Carries D8 as accepted.

decisions.summary: an agent_id that is not letters, digits, - and _ passes
decisions.why: Both the cap's measure (the transcript at subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl) and its one exit (the handoff file named by the agent id) are paths built from the id; an id that cannot be joined into a path leaves neither a context to measure nor a handoff to name, so refusing would refuse with no exit. The same capture shows builders' ids are plain names, so ordinary work does not reach this path and FR-006's enforcement is not gutted.

decisions.summary: context = input + cache_read + cache_creation tokens of the last assistant row with usage above zero; user rows carrying a child's usage and zero rows skipped
decisions.why: FR-006 caps the builder's context; this measures the builder's own model call and excludes rows that are not its model calls (measured: user rows hold the child's usage). It makes the cap measure what FR-006 names.

decisions.summary: no transcript file, or no such row in the tail, passes
decisions.why: Where no context is recorded there is no figure to compare with FR-006's threshold; refusing on no evidence would refuse builders that are under it. The capture (2026-11-20) shows the transcript exists beside transcript_path for a builder, so ordinary work does not reach this path and the request's 'real enforcement' holds.

decisions.summary: the tail is read backwards in 64 KiB steps to at most 16 MiB (both GUESS); a builder whose last usage row lies further back passes
decisions.why: What lies after the last assistant row is that turn's tool results; 16 MiB of them with no assistant row between is not a shape ordinary work produces, so a builder past the cap is not let through by it in practice. The bound is a labeled GUESS knob. Not measured that no real tail exceeds it - a premise worth a count from the event log when the knob is retuned, not a block.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS GUESS 300,000; at the cap passes
decisions.why: FR-006's own knob and value, labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: past the cap every call is refused but the handoff file's Write, the refusal naming the file and the next step (write what is done and left, stop, reply with the path; the session dispatches a fresh builder)
decisions.why: FR-006 verbatim ('but for writing its handoff file, naming the file and the next step'), and the approved improvement 1 ('a fresh builder per stage, with a handoff file').

decisions.summary: an Edit of the handoff file is let through beside its Write
decisions.why: Implied by FR-006's own words: the exception is 'writing its handoff file', and an Edit of that file is writing it. Confined to the agent's own handoff, it cannot carry task work, so the cap's purpose (no builder works on past a large context) survives.

decisions.summary: a Read of the handoff file is let through beside its Write
decisions.why: Ground that holds regardless of the stated tool behavior: a Read confined to the agent's own handoff file yields only what the builder itself wrote there, so it cannot carry task work and does not gut the cap's purpose, while the stated reason (the Write tool will not overwrite an unread file) would otherwise leave a builder with an existing handoff no exit. That premise about the Write tool carries no date and method in the block; it is not what this ruling rests on.

decisions.summary: any file in <git common dir>/l7r-handoffs/ whose name ends <agent id>.md counts as the agent's handoff
decisions.why: Applying the literal one-name rule, recomputed at each call from the event log's task, could refuse the very file the refusal named if the chain's task moved between them, leaving the builder no exit - defeating FR-006's handoff. Agent ids are unique, so no builder can write another's handoff (a case the suite refuses), and every such file sits in the handoff directory, where writing cannot carry task work. Ruled as stated, 'any file there' = in that directory.

decisions.summary: the handoff is named <task>-<agent id>.md from the event log's chain (filed_at), or <agent id>.md where the line carries no task
decisions.why: Naming the file FR-006 requires; no case is excused.

decisions.summary: a call outside any clone passes
decisions.why: On what the block establishes: D8's test of who is a builder is a stat of the clone's .claude/agents/, and the handoff path is under the clone's git common dir; outside a clone there is neither a who nor an exit to name, so a refusal there could refuse defined review agents and leave a builder no handoff to write. The premise that builders' calls are made inside clones in ordinary work is not measured in the block and no suite case is listed for this path - worth a count, not a block.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_OK="<reason>" in a Bash command, recorded as context-ok; a bare one refused
decisions.why: FR-012: an escape of a reason of two words or more, recorded.

decisions.summary: D9's make context-ok AID= WHY= per-agent permit not built in T12; filed as T13, to land before T22; CONTEXT_OK in Bash the recorded escape meanwhile
decisions.why: Judged against FR-012, not D9 (which this task restated): every refusal the cap issues today has a recorded route past it - the refusal's compliant step (the handoff, always let through) and CONTEXT_OK in a Bash call, recorded - so FR-012's escape exists and no builder is trapped. The permit was the session's design for a resumed builder (D10's resume); it is filed and ordered, not dropped. Nothing the GM asked for is left out.

decisions.summary: in the performance lane after T15 and T16, before T13
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM 2026-11-20 ('let's prioritize those remaining improvement fixes'); T12 is improvement 1.

decisions.summary: red-first unit and suite runs, the check-deleted run red, and the handoff Write's case through the whole guard chain
decisions.why: FR-012's red-first test and D9's whole-chain case; enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: docs/guards.md row and knob-table row, rust/guard/CLAUDE.md mention, D9 restated to what was built, written by the session before the tick
decisions.why: D14's knob table and keeping the spec true to the built guard; no behavior added or excused.

blocks: ## Decisions

decisions.summary: An item or fix names a class of defect when it says 'every' or 'all the' before writer, reader, form, file, caller, instance, copy, site or guard, or 'each of the ...'. A bare 'all' is not a trigger. Such an item must carry an 'observed <date>, method: ...' line. This replaces the plan's earlier list, which made any 'all ...' a trigger.
decisions.why: FR-009's class is defined by its examples: every writer, every form, every file of a kind. The trigger catches all three and adds more nouns. Dropping the plan's own earlier bare 'all ...' narrows nothing in request.md or the spec, which never name 'all'. This is the vocabulary already ruled within as T17-class-vocabulary. The changed sentence only makes D15's text say what T17 built.

decisions.summary: A deferral states why it is not fixed here, 'filed as T<n>' (or 'added to' / 'folded into') and 'lands before T<m>'. The two ids must differ. Both must be filed, which is checked in lint::refusal on decide and plan-delta, and both must be open, which is checked in decide alone. An item passes as none, fixed here or not a defect.
decisions.why: This is FR-009's why, filed task id and order. Text unchanged since the CLEAR.

decisions.summary: DEFER_FORM_OK on decide and plan-delta, read from the environment and recorded by the tool (the guard log and dev/bypass-log/). plan-delta honors an escape recorded at decide time.
decisions.why: This is FR-012's recorded escape. Text unchanged since the CLEAR.

decisions.summary: context_cap_hooks refuses a builder's call past CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS, except for writing its own handoff file. The per-agent context-ok permit is built with T13.
decisions.why: This is FR-006's cap and its handoff exit. Text unchanged since the CLEAR, which ruled it within.

blocks: ### T13 (FR-006: a SendMessage resuming a builder past the cap, or one whose task has landed)
### T13 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: judge runs the sender's own cap first: a builder past its cap is refused its SendMessage like any other call
decisions.why: D9 refuses every tool call of a builder past the cap but the handoff write; a SendMessage is a tool call. Applies the accepted rule, narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: a target whose meta agentType is a defined agent passes
decisions.why: FR-006 defines a builder as an agent dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; D9 says a defined agent is never read.

decisions.summary: a SendMessage whose target has no agent-<to>.meta.json beside the session transcript passes
decisions.why: Without the meta file the guard cannot tell a builder from a defined review agent (agentType lives only there) and has no dispatch id; refusing there would refuse defined agents, which FR-006 excludes from the rule by definition. Telling the two apart is impossible in this case, which is more than awkward. The block measured (2026-11-20) that the session's dispatched agents carry the file, so the pass does not reach the ordinary builder. The past-cap and landed refusals both fire wherever the meta exists.

decisions.summary: the target's task is found by the brief's T<n>, then its FIRST event line's task, then the task-start entry in force at its dispatch - not D2's last rung, the latest task-start
decisions.why: D10 refuses a builder whose task has landed since it was dispatched; the task in force at dispatch is that builder's task, while the latest start may be another task's. It is a more faithful reading of 'its task' and is tested with a later open task-start in the log. It refuses more often, not less.

decisions.summary: dispatch time = the Agent PreToolUse line whose id is the meta's toolUseId, else the builder's first line, else its transcript's first timestamp
decisions.why: This is how D10's 'since it was dispatched' gets measured. Each fallback is an earlier-or-equal instant, so no landing that FR-006 counts is missed. The facts it rests on are dated and measured.

decisions.summary: landed = an end line with landed true naming the task after the dispatch (a background make land included), or the task ticked in tasks.md/tasks-done.md; a refused landing (landed false) does not count
decisions.why: FR-006 says 'whose task has landed'. A refused landing has not landed. Counting a tick with no time bound is broader than the rule, never narrower.

decisions.summary: a target under the cap with no task found anywhere passes and writes a resume-no-task record; past the cap it is still refused
decisions.why: The landed rule has no subject when no task can be found: the brief names no T<n>, the agent's first line carries none, and no task-start was in force at its dispatch. FR-006's builder is 'an agent dispatched with a task's brief', and an agent with no recoverable task cannot be told apart from a helper that has none. Refusing there would refuse non-builders, so fail-closed is not possible without contradicting FR-006's definition. The cap still applies in that case (tested: past the cap with no task, refused), and every pass is logged as resume-no-task, so the gap is measured rather than silent. It does not gut the purpose, which is one task per builder, enforced wherever a task exists.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_OK in the SendMessage's summary passes and is recorded
decisions.why: It is D10's escape verbatim, and FR-012 requires an escape that is recorded.

decisions.summary: make context-ok AID= WHY= grants a permit keyed $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/context-cap:<AID>, read by the hook past the cap after the handoff check, valid an hour
decisions.why: D9 specifies this permit built with T13 through the guard-edit permit mechanism. The toplevel prefix is how the existing store is found, which is a mechanism difference that works. The hour bounds an escape and loosens no refusal.

decisions.summary: T13 is a [perf] task, ordered after T12, T03 and T06
decisions.why: It is improvement 1 of the six the GM approved (builder contexts small), and FR-013 says performance work goes first. The ordering follows its data dependencies.

decisions.why: D17 says the companion check 'accepts shards' and that a shard stands 'beside nothing else of that name'. SUITE AND SHARDS BOTH enforces that clause. ### T08 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Compile (the union of build and cover-build phases) is split out of ANY run a phase ties to, not only a tests run (data-model's wording); the critical path splits a main-session call's gap the same way.
decisions.why: D4's own text books compile 'inside the Bash call or background span that holds them', not inside a tests run; the GM asked 'how much time are we spending on recompiling things', and a landing's or gate's compile is recompiling. Widening the split books more of what was asked; it removes nothing.

decisions.summary: A phase ties to the run of its session whose span holds it and whose target is its make OR whose task is its task, ranked target, then task, then latest start; unmatched phases counted in the footnote, never dropped; a phase starting after the window is none of it.
decisions.why: D4 ties by session, clone and target; adding task as a second key moved 567 untied compile phases (60.9 min) to 170 (12.1 min), measured, so it brings more of the GM's compile time under its task (the per-task breakdown he asked for). It narrows nothing. Note for the caller: the block's restatement omits D4's clone key; since builders share the main session's id (D4), dropping clone could tie a phase to a same-task or same-target run in another clone. Not ruled on - the block is silent, not explicit - but confirm the code still keys on clone.

decisions.summary: A background run ends at the main transcript's queue-operation enqueue row naming its tool-use-id, before its BgEnd line's t.
decisions.why: D3 itself says a BgEnd's t is when the notice reached the session, not when the run ended (the notice waits while the session is mid-turn); the enqueue row is the nearer reading of the run's own end. More accurate booking of what was asked; nothing dropped - BgEnd remains the fallback.

decisions.summary: A background run with no enqueue row or BgEnd ends at the TaskStop call that stopped it (read from the session's and its subagents' transcripts), else open to the window's end.
decisions.why: A stopped run has ended; booking it open to the window's end was a wrong outcome (ten runs, 6,070 of 6,792 machine minutes booked 'other', measured). D3's 'open to the window's end' is the fallback for a launch with no end anywhere, and a TaskStop is an end. Adds an end source; narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A subagent's call inside the main session's turn is booked on the critical path as what the session was doing (the call it waits on, or the model); between turns it keeps the wait open. The session's own line moves state before a zero gap is skipped, and SubagentStart/SubagentStop keep it.
decisions.why: D7 defines the critical path as the wall clock partitioned by what the MAIN SESSION was doing or waiting on; a builder's line cutting the session's make static in two misbooked the session's own state. This implements D7 literally; builder runs are still booked in the runs table (machine minutes).

decisions.summary: A call running several targets is booked by the first of them in PRECEDENCE (land, gate, tests, review, docs, spec-kit step, other) in both tables; a phase ties to a run that runs its make at all; a landing's gate and cohort phases are split out as gate, less the compile inside them.
decisions.why: FR-001/D2 book a call by its target and are silent on a line with several; the day's 19 landings were launched 'make claims-owed ...; make ledger-owed; make land' and booked review by their first target, which misses the land and gate columns FR-005 asks for (land 4.2, gate 0.0 against 27.4 min of their own gate phases, measured). Cohort booked as gate follows D5 (cohort-landing is the landing's gate stage).

decisions.summary: where-time shows a critical-path (wall clock) table and a runs table of every session's and agent's Bash calls in overlapping machine minutes, never summed into the wall clock.
decisions.why: D7 asks for the critical path 'and beside it the summed agent-minutes'; FR-005 'the wall clock on the critical path apart from the summed agent-minutes'. The runs table is that.

decisions.why: FR-005 and D7 ask for UNTIL=; clipping rather than dropping keeps the run's in-window time booked.

It comes from the task line, which the bundle only restates (item 2), and the block does not flag it as a departure, it just says 'so the split was built'. Taken literally the condition is NOT met. It was a test of whether the split pays, and a literal reading defeats that purpose and the GM's 'prioritize performance improvements' (FR-013: 'makes ... the builders' loop faster'). Without the split, every one of the 520 edits rebuilds 32 crates. With it, the 246 hook edits (the largest category) rebuild 1 crate (1.1-1.2 s against 11.6-50.8 s) and make rust-test owes only the guard and checks. The cost is measured and small: 33 crates instead of 32 on a shared edit, plus a second compile of l7r_shared under test-env on shared edits, which was not timed. ### T11 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: feature-report shows where-time's columns through one reader (where_time::columns_text), in process, its UNTIL= kept, in a section after the session's time; each agent's own row left to make where-time
decisions.why: FR-005 and D7 ask that feature-report read the same columns through the same functions in one place and keep its UNTIL=. One shared reader is exactly that. The report carries every column FR-005 names: the critical path apart from the summed agent-minutes, the tokens, and the rework. Each agent's span and tokens under its task are still read by the same function and shown by make where-time, so no reading is lost or forked.

decisions.summary: the window feature-report passes is its own, first event to last when no SINCE/UNTIL is given
decisions.why: This fixes a wrong outcome found in building. With both empty, the report counted every feature's turn lines: 6,900 min of critical path against the window's 1,417 (labeled 2026-11-21). A report of this feature's time that counts other features' time is a defect, and the fix serves FR-005. The small token and agent-minute gap against where-time is the same reader over a window that opens seconds later. That is a difference, not a defect, and no exactness standard applies.

decisions.summary: plan re-rounds are a later round of one review on one subject, keyed by agent and MANIFEST subject (feature_report::tables::round_key), booked to the task its line names else the mark, the all row counting every one; spec-fidelity-verify not keyed separately because the hook logs a routed later round under spec-fidelity
decisions.why: The approved improvement 4 ('Fewer plan re-rounds') and FR-005 ('count the rework (... plan re-rounds)') mean a review sent back for another round. The first wording counted first-round reviews of different block bundles: 68 against 23 (the Measured table, labeled). That overstated the column it named and was a defect. The restated key measures what was asked and drops no re-round. An untasked one goes to the mark row and the all row counts all of them. A routed verify round is logged under spec-fidelity (none of the 451 log's 108 under the twin's name, measured 2026-11-21). A hand-dispatched verify is a spec round with no MANIFEST, so it is not a plan re-round.

decisions.summary: a spec-fidelity dispatch inside the window is a re-round when any earlier dispatch in the feature's log holds its key, inside the window or before SINCE; the log before SINCE is read a second time where SINCE is given
decisions.why: This is the correction the last verdict asked for, in its own words. A second round run inside the window is counted as that window's rework, whether its first round fell before SINCE or not. It is red first: a_re_round_inside_the_window_counts_a_first_round_before_since read 0 against 2 before the fix. It is measured on a SINCE that cuts a subject: 6 -> 7 between T44's second and third rounds, labeled 2026-11-21, with command. T10's bounds are unchanged at 23 because that SINCE cuts nothing. It narrows nothing. The second read's cost (about 0.25 to 0.35 s, labeled with load) is a cost, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: feature-report's existing rounds table stays counted inside the window and says so under its heading, rather than being re-read across SINCE like the re-rounds column
decisions.why: The rounds table is feature-report's existing table, and the request and spec ask nothing of it. FR-005's rework count is the plan re-rounds column, which now counts correctly across SINCE. The last verdict named labeling the table as one of the two acceptable remedies, and the label does what that remedy was for. The table and the column count two stated things, so they no longer disagree silently, and a reader is never told a wrong number. Where SINCE cuts no subject they agree (23 = 23 and 25 = 25, the Measured table). The report passes its own first event as SINCE where none is given, so for the default report the two read the same. Leaving an unrequested existing table as it is, with an honest heading, is a difference, not a defect (XIV v2.36.0). So it is within and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: an agent is booked to its first stop's task (the agent's meta file, D6), else its first start's, because before 451 T53's landing a start line carried the clone's active task (57 of 164 agents with both; 0 of 22 since), red first
decisions.why: D7 puts each agent's span and tokens 'under its task', and D6 takes the stop line's task from the agent's meta file. Booking 57 agents to the clone's active mark was a wrong outcome: T15's plan reviews read under T18 (measured 2026-11-21 with method). The fix-as-we-go ruling (2026-11-18) says a step fixes the defects it finds. The fix only changes which recorded field the requested column reads, choosing the one D6 already names. It is red first and changes nothing for agents started after T53.

### T59 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: fields::agent_cost re-reads the growing transcript every 5 ms (REPLY_POLL) while the payload's last_assistant_message is not yet the last assistant row's text since the last user row, so tok counts the reply
decisions.why: Makes the stop line carry the agent's token cost as D6 defines it (the transcript's sum, each message.id once) - FR-004 and the 2026-11-19 approval's idea 4. The cause is measured (60 of 83 stops short by exactly the reply; the probe shows the reply lands 5.8-89.2 ms into the hook), and fixing the writer instead of restating the claim follows from the measurement that the reply is readable during the hook.

decisions.summary: The wait is bounded at 1 s (REPLY_WAIT, ten times the probe's latest landing); past it the writer records what is on disk, as before
decisions.why: A Stop-hook writer that never refuses has to terminate; the bound covers every reply observed by a factor of ten, so FR-004's cost is recorded in every observed case, and the residue (a reply later than 1 s) is a design tolerance, not a case the plan excludes from what was asked. It also keeps the per-stop cost small, consistent with FR-013's priority on the builders' loop speed.

decisions.summary: ctx is read after the wait, so it is the reply's context rather than one call stale
decisions.why: D6 says ctx is the agent's last call's context; the stale ctx on the same 60 stops is the same defect, fixed together.

decisions.summary: A payload with no reply text or no readable transcript waits for nothing; a stop with no readable transcript still writes neither tok nor ctx, and the hook never refuses
decisions.why: Unchanged behavior, and the 4 such stops measured have no transcript anywhere, so there is nothing to sum; FR-004 is not narrowed by declining to invent a figure that cannot be read.

The final outcome is still guarded by plan-verdict's digest refusal, at the cost of a re-review, not a wrong verdict. Alternative (c), refusing the narrowing when the command detaches, is a cheaper partial cover that was turned down on a design ground (a second detach reader). That ground alone would not justify an exception, but no exception is needed here: the case that remains open is not a wrong outcome. It is a bounded rework cost, caught by a real mechanical refusal.
