blocks: ### T86 (a builder's closing checks went red on another builder's half-done files in the same clone: about 12 of the night's closing runs red only on another task's in-flight files, measured 2026-11-21 (the main session's reading of the night's runs, T86's line); 13 such red runs of 5 shapes, measured 2026-11-21 (item 4))
### T86 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The caller's files are the clone's uncommitted files less those that another task's non-fallback Edit/Write/NotebookEdit event-log lines alone name (newer than the file's last commit, inside a 7-day window); an unnamed file and a shared file are the caller's; the feature comes from F= or the latest task-start naming the task.
decisions.why: This is how the task's own fix is built (a closing run judges the caller's work, the [perf] builders' loop under FR-013). It errs to the safe side: a miss counts a file as the caller's and gives a false red, never a false green. Choosing it over the active-task mark and over a FILES=/CRATES= list is a design choice, and the plan measured all three.

decisions.summary: A new GUESS knob: an edit line claims a file only if it is newer than the file's last commit, within 7 days.
decisions.why: A parameter of the mechanism. When it misjudges, it counts more files as the caller's, so it can only make the verdict stricter.

decisions.summary: In static's per-crate steps, a red crate whose kept-key inputs read none of the caller's files is reported APART and not counted. The key inputs are factored out of verdict_key_with so the two cannot drift. A crate that builds on a caller's crate, or whose tests read the caller's file, is the caller's. A listing or key that cannot be judged counts every crate.
decisions.why: This is the fix the task's line asks for (shape (a), 5 runs measured). Every case that cannot be judged falls back to counting, as before.

decisions.summary: Tree-wide steps and hooks-test stay counted whole, and a crate holding both tasks' files is judged whole (shapes (d) and (e), 4 of the 13 measured runs, stay red).
decisions.why: This narrows the task's aim of a verdict on the caller's own work, but separating these cases is impossible with the instrument the plan has. Every hooks-test suite's key reads 994-998 paths of the guard's and the gate's crates (measured with l7r-guard deps), so a suite run on another task's edit also ran the caller's code, and no key can clear it. A crate's lint and cover verdict is one verdict over the whole crate. The tree-wide steps, measured through quick's full runs, fired on no other task's file. A red that is kept is not a wrong green, and none of these cases is a check refusing work that could be shown good.

decisions.summary: A counted red whose every error line names another task's file (the caller's crate or the gate binary unbuildable on another task's half-done dependency) is tagged BLOCKED, names the files and tasks, and stays red.
decisions.why: Nothing of the caller's was judged there, so keeping it red is correct. The tag only reports which task is responsible.

decisions.summary: With no T= the whole clone is judged as before. Only the script sets the listing, so make static, make done and a landing judge every crate by construction.
decisions.why: Keeps the landing's whole-tree check and the default unchanged. Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: T55's decide notice and foreground refusal (order.rs) and the third-static refusal (static_runs_hooks.rs) now name 'make closing-checks T=<task> F=<feature>' from the call's filed task, or T=<your task> when the call is filed under no task. closing-checks.sh's rerun line names T= and F= as given.
decisions.why: Without this the fix cannot be reached: a builder told to run a bare make closing-checks gets the whole-clone verdict that T86 exists to replace. Fixing the third-static message beside the other two is the same defect (constitution XIV), and its red-first tests are recorded.

decisions.summary: Files another builder writes through Bash (sed -i, heredoc, generator) leave no Edit/Write line, so they count as the caller's. This is left to T93 (a write-path field on the event log's Bash lines in rust/guard/shared's event_log_hooks), which lands before T22.
decisions.why: A defect, a false red on good work, is left out of T86, but it is not dropped. FR-009's deferral form is met in full: why it is not fixed here (a new field on the event log's Bash lines that every reader of the log meets, in another crate's files), the filed id T93, its order 'lands before T22', and an every-instance line labeled observed 2026-11-21 with its method. The GM approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task' (improvement 4), which allows a deferral that states why. The miss is on the safe side (never a wrong green, and make done judges the whole tree). It does not gut T86's purpose: the 5 measured shape-(a) runs all came apart under the replayed rule.

blocks: ### T84 (the finding as filed, measured 2026-11-21 over the night's 29 tasks: 43 builders, about 16 builder reports asking the session to file a task, and every MODE 4 plan review left to it; four causes, each measured in item 4: two concurrent `make task-add` runs could lose both filings, nothing held a builder's stop, only the briefs kept a builder from its own review, and the tick's and the push's plan gate judged the whole feature, so every landing took `PLAN_REVIEW_OK`)
### T84 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.why: A new constant, labeled a GUESS. The section does not say which way a timeout goes (block or let the builder stop). Either way the tick and push gate (T84-4) still refuse an undecided section, so a timed-out ask cannot land unreviewed work. Noted, not blocking.

decisions.id: T84-4a plan gate per task: an open task's section not judged
decisions.summary: The tick's and the push's plan gate (plan::tick_gate, task::push_owed) judges the blocks outside every task's section plus the sections of the task ticked and the tasks ticked before it, and never an open task's section; the land crate keeps no plan check of its own.
decisions.why: This narrows feature 243 / 375 D60's reach (every block owed) at the tick and push. Applying the whole-feature rule literally defeats its own purpose and the GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions': measured, all 16 of 451's landings took PLAN_REVIEW_OK, 10 of them on correct work, so the gate had become a routine escape. 243's purpose is that a task is not ticked while its decisions lack a verdict. That holds: the ticked task's own section, earlier ticked sections and every shared block are still judged, and an open task's section is judged at its own tick. No task can be ticked or pushed while its own section lacks CLEAR at its digest. The red test a_tick_answers_for_its_own_section_the_ticked_ones_and_the_shared_blocks pins it.

decisions.id: T84-4b a filled template's old heading not owed
decisions.summary: A '(removed) ### T<n> (<why: ...>)' block, the old heading of a filled task template, is not owed once T<n>'s section carries a CLEAR task verdict.
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from 4a. D60 owes a deleted block because a decision deleted by hand is a change. A template's placeholder heading carries no decision: the text replacing it is the task's own section, already reviewed CLEAR at its digest. Measured: 4 of 16 landings owed only this. This holds only as far as the forgiveness is limited to the template's placeholder heading of the same task with a current CLEAR section, as the section states. A hand-deleted decision under any other heading stays owed.

decisions.summary: A round-arbiter accept is not written to the verdict store as the task's verdict; T33, T46, T67 and T79 show BLOCKED there. Left to T92's line, lands before T22.
decisions.why: A defect that refuses correct work, left in the FR-009 form: its visible effect, measured 2026-11-21, why it is not fixed here (the accept is written by make arbiter-ruled, outside this task's files), filed id T92, and 'lands before T22'. That is the form the four accepts in rulings.md treat as enough. One gap for T92 to cover: the new stop guard reads the same store, so a builder of a task the arbiter accepted would also be held at its stop, not only its tick and push. Same defect, same cure, and an escape exists.

blocks: ### T81 (the million-step spelling test's 20 s wall bound failed good work under load, measured 2026-11-21: of the 69 `test` Phase lines on `rust/guard/shared` since T58 made it a crate, 7 red runs lasted 20 s or more (13:33Z to 14:08Z), 6 of them this test by name in the builders' transcripts (`--- FAILED`, panicked at its `recv_timeout` line), at a load average of 82.78 (T79's builder's `uptime`, 13:45Z); reproduced, measured 2026-11-21 (`/tmp/t81/slow.sh` and `load.sh 88`), on one CPU shared 16 ways (red at 20.08 s, the scan cut off after 1.25 s of CPU) and with 88 copies at once (33 of 88 red))
### T81 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The million-step spelling test's 20 s wall-clock recv_timeout is replaced by a bound on the search thread's own CPU time (schedstat's first field, polled every 100 ms), failing past CPU_BOUND_NS; a panicked search thread fails at once.
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md or 451's FR-001 to FR-013 settles this test's bound, so the choice of measure is the task's own. The block reports T81's line as asking that the bound count steps not wall time, or a ceiling sized for a loaded host; fancy_regex 0.14 exposes no step count but the limit firing (the block's reading of its vm.rs), so the thread's CPU time is the work measure. It keeps the bound's filed purpose (T185's section: a spin fails rather than hangs) - M2 still fails, at 30022000592 ns of CPU - and ends the refusal of good work the block measured (6 reds by name, 33 of 88 under load.sh 88). A check that refuses good work is a defect under XIV, and fixing it is the task.

decisions.summary: CPU_BOUND_NS is 30 s, a CONVENTION and a knob, with its why beside it (10x the scan's 3.2 s on the slowest core, 4x its 7.4 s worst at 88 copies).
decisions.why: Choosing the ceiling's value is the task's own design choice, labeled as a convention with its measured basis; no research claim moves and the spec settles no value.

decisions.summary: The test also builds the house style's pattern shape with fancy_regex's old 1,000,000-step limit and asserts it errs on the text, so the text stays past the limit the test exists for.
decisions.why: Enforcement only: it makes the test keep testing what it was filed to test (the step limit), the 'pin the step budget by counting steps' half of T81's line; deleting the test's purpose would leave it nothing to check.

decisions.summary: No engine code and no guard code change: the house_style_hooks test file alone; T88's set_down_hooks, T88's land crate and T93's event_log_hooks/fields.rs untouched.
decisions.why: The defect is in the test's bound, not the scan: the block's slowed run cut HEAD's scan off at 1.25 s of CPU, and the 55 green loaded runs used 3.5-6.1 s each, both far under any spin. The brief bounds the files. Nothing the request or FR-013 asks is cut by it.

decisions.summary: Eight other test files carrying the same 20 s wall bound (four in rust/guard/shared, three in the guard, one in reviews) are neither changed nor filed.
decisions.why: Under constitution XIV as the GM ruled 2026-11-19, a defect is a wrong outcome. The block censused the class (others.py, plus a --- FAILED census of every transcript) and found no transcripted failure of any of the eight but T185's own red-first run of 2026-11-19T02:05Z. Its unattributed reds (two guard-crate Phase reds at 20 s or more, named by no transcript, and the 13:56Z row) name no test, as the block itself says a long run alone does not. So no wrong outcome of these eight is measured. This crate's four take 0.2-0.66 s alone against this test's 1.6 s, and the other four were not timed. A latent difference with no measured wrong outcome is not a known defect, so fix-as-we-go does not reach it and leaving it is not a narrowing. The block names the CPU bound as the form to copy if one goes red.

decisions.why: FR-013 counts a task that makes the gate or the builders' loop faster as performance work. A check that goes red on good work under load costs builders re-runs: the block counts 6 such reds by name, at a load reading of 82.78 taken between them. The GM asked that performance work come first (2026-11-20).

blocks: ### T88 (builders ran three at once only 26% of the night's 580 minutes, a mean of 1.65, measured 2026-11-21 (each agent's span, T88's line): a landing refused any uncommitted file, so tasks landed in batches, and the Stop hook was silent whenever anything ran, so a freed builder slot sat empty)
### T88 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: With other work uncommitted in the clone, make land runs whole in a persistent landing worktree <clone>-land at the clone's HEAD, under a lock, seeded with the clone's kept results; the clone then takes the landed tip (update-ref, merge-tree/commit-tree, three-way merge-file, conflict moves nothing, exit 4).
decisions.why: A design for a [perf] task under FR-013 (the landings). It narrows nothing the GM asked: the gate still judges the tree pushed, the push's dirty-tree refusal and the stamp's disk key are unchanged, and the two other ways are measured and rejected on their costs.

decisions.summary: The landing refuses the landing tasks' own edits still uncommitted (PostToolUse edit lines under the task naming a dirty file newer than its last commit), naming the git commit command; dirty files no task's edit names stay in the clone, not landed.
decisions.why: Keeps the landed tree the task's own work; no requested behavior is narrowed. Red-first pair recorded (78/3 then 81).

decisions.summary: While something runs, the Stop hook refuses a stop when fewer than L7R_BUILDERS (GUESS 3) builders run and next_independent names an open task never started, after no open task, touching no running task's named files; escape is make set-down F= WHY=.
decisions.why: Adds a refusal in service of the builders' loop; it carries a reasoned, recorded escape and a named compliant command, and red-first is recorded (350/2 then 352). Narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: next_independent takes performance work first across every active feature, then the rest, feature-first then each active feature by its last task-start.
decisions.why: This is FR-013's own clause: the Stop hook's start-the-next names an open performance task before any other, across active features. The plan corrected an earlier feature-first ordering that broke it (r1 red, r2 green).

decisions.summary: Where the task the Stop hook names is not performance work, its named make task-start carries PERF_LATER_OK - which happens only when every open performance task is started, waits on an open task, or overlaps a running task's files.
decisions.why: This narrows how far FR-013's task-start refusal reaches in practice, so it is ruled. It uses FR-013's own escape, of a reason, recorded, for the case that escape names: a performance task that cannot start now because it waits on another task's landing (or is already running). The hook names a non-perf task only after no performance task can be started. Leaving slots empty in that case would not get performance work done any sooner, and would undo the GM's purpose ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'), which is ordering, not idling. Each start still needs the escape typed in and logged.

decisions.summary: Overlap is read from a task line's named files or *_hooks modules against running tasks' edit lines, with specs/, .git/ and the ledger excluded and common basenames matched only with a path; a line naming nothing fails toward a start.
decisions.why: A design detail of the dispatch rule; its stated cost (two builders in one crate) is judged by T86's closing checks. Narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: L7R_BUILDERS is a new knob, GUESS 3, labeled at its point of change (set_down_hooks.rs BUILDERS); D14's knob table row is T22's.
decisions.why: D14 asks for a GUESS label at the point of change, and T88 gives one. The knob table is a task the spec assigns elsewhere, so this sets no new rule. T22 has to list this knob when it builds the table.

decisions.summary: 449 T244's stop before the parked homestead stages is not built here; 444 is set down, so free_slot names no 444 stage task now, and a stop there passes by make set-down naming the GM's ruling.
decisions.why: The rolling-dispatch refusal does not force work the GM ruled to stop before: 444 is set down (measured from set-downs.jsonl and task-starts.jsonl), and the escape the refusal names takes his ruling as its WHY. T244 belongs to 449.

decisions.summary: The landing worktree's own target (13 GB measured) is not pruned whole; only the sweep's per-crate variant rule trims it, and a hand-deleted clone leaves its -land until the directory goes.
decisions.why: A stated cost, not a wrong outcome; nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The after-occupancy measurement is filed as T98, lands before T22, because it needs a night of rolling dispatch first.
decisions.why: It cannot be measured before a night runs on the change. It is filed with an order, as FR-009 requires, and the before-figure uses the replay's method, so before and after are measured one way.

decisions.summary: test-idle-tests-hooks.sh's wall-clock case refused good work under load (red at load 16.5, green on rerun); filed as T99, lands before T22, as another guard's suite outside T88's files.
decisions.why: A defect, but T88 is not the one carrying it forward. It is filed with its reason, its id and its order, which is what FR-009 asks of a deferral. FIX AS WE GO's rule about steps applies to 449's port, and this defect is still put ahead of T22. The GM did not ask T88 to fix this suite.

blocks: ### T95 (the closing checks' BLOCKED tag missed a coverage red: `blocked()` read only `-->` and `Diff in` lines, not cover's lines no test reaches, found by T86's builder, 2026-11-21; T81's second closing run red on cover alone, 3 files of T88's, measured 2026-11-21 (its kept run directory, item 4))
### T95 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: blocked() reads cover's '<path> - lines no test reaches: <lines>' lines (path stripped to the clone's, first line a real one) beside the '-->' and 'Diff in' paths; a coverage red whose every named file is another task's is tagged BLOCKED naming each file and task.
decisions.why: This is the defect T95's line names (a coverage red on another's files went untagged) fixed as found, in the closing checks the GM had filed as a performance task (2026-11-21). It adds no behavior beyond making T86's tag read the coverage output it missed.

decisions.summary: A BLOCKED red stays counted red; 'red' and the exit are untouched.
decisions.why: Keeps T86's rule as it was. The tag only informs the builder and blocks or passes nothing new.

decisions.summary: The tag's wording says which lines it read: errors only keep T86's words, uncovered lines only say 'yours are covered ... re-run once their tests reach them', both say 'nothing of yours failed there'.
decisions.why: Message wording that comes with D1. It neither narrows nor adds scope.

decisions.summary: A failed coverage run's marker '<crate> - lines no test reaches: 0' is not read as a path.
decisions.why: The marker names a crate, not a file. Reading it as a path would wrongly untag a run whose cover build broke on another task's file (the 12:47Z run, measured). Leaving it out keeps D1 correct, and the run is still tagged from its '-->' errors (red-first case: BLOCKED).

decisions.summary: An APART crate's block (its 'rust-checks: APART' header up to the next 'rust-checks:' line) is not read, so another task's APART lines no longer tag a caller's own red BLOCKED. The caller's own uncovered line beside another's error is also no longer tagged.
decisions.why: Two wrong-tag defects in the same function, found while building it and fixed here. The project's fix-as-we-go rule covers this, and it is not unrequested scope. Each is pinned by a red-first suite case.

decisions.summary: T81's run (the run cited in T95's line) stays untagged after the fix. Two of its three uncovered files were named by no task's event line before the run, so T86's rule counts them as the caller's. Naming them is left to the split's tasks T93 (Bash writes) and T96 (a Python program's writes).
decisions.why: The defect T95's line names (blocked() not reading cover's lines) is fully fixed, and the replay shows the fixed function tags T84's 17:10Z coverage-only red, which HEAD did not. T81's run stays untagged because of a different, already-filed defect: which files the split attributes to which task. Under T86's rule an unattributed file is the caller's, so the result is a missing tag, never a wrong one. Neither the GM's request nor the spec asks T95 to change attribution, so nothing is narrowed. The plan states T81's run is not tagged and does not overclaim it.

decisions.summary: Red-first suite cases (46 passed, 3 failed against the unfixed function; 49 of 49 fixed) and the task's own closing run as the exits. Other tasks' files (T93, T88, T97, T82) are not touched.
decisions.why: Verification of what the task fixes, plus scope discipline. Both are within.

decisions.summary: T95 is not classed as performance work (no [perf]).
decisions.why: The task changes what a tag reads, not how long a run takes. Under FR-013 the class only sets scheduling order. It does not narrow what the GM asked for or what the spec requires.

blocks: ### T82 (the plan bundle's requirement reader read only `- **FR-NNN**`, so a block citing a requirement a spec writes as a bold paragraph with no list dash got a NOT FOUND line though its text exists - filed by T48, 2026-11-21; measured 2026-11-21: 2 real citations of one by another feature's number across every plan, 449's plan-done.md line 967 ("FR-007 of feature 239", 449 open) and 383's plan.md line 503 ("256's FR-004", 383 closed), each bundled NOT FOUND on the plan crate unedited)
### T82 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: requirements gains a third pass (ANY_ITEM) reading a dashless bold FR/SC id, carried from its start to the next requirement of any form or the next heading
decisions.why: This is T82's own line: the reader answered NOT FOUND for requirement text that exists, a tool answering wrongly (a defect under XIV). Measured on the real 449 and 383 bundles; red-first tests named.

decisions.summary: the same pass also reads an indented sub-item with its own id (184's and 295's FR-005a..d), carried as a list item; labeled deliberate addition
decisions.why: It widens the fix and does not narrow it. The task's own bundle showed the same wrong outcome (NOT FOUND for existing text) in the same reader, and fixing known defects in the task is the GM's standing rule (fix as we go). The differential shows 0 of 4,751 existing reads changing, so nothing asked for is given up.

decisions.summary: an id a list item or heading already gives keeps that text; a dashless restatement of it is commentary and is not read over it
decisions.why: This keeps every existing correct read unchanged (the brief's constraint) and does not cut anything T82 asked for. The dashless ids T82 targets (287 in 21 specs) have no other form.

decisions.summary: spec_amendments keeps ITEM rather than sharing the new pattern
decisions.why: Measured: no spec writes a dashless id under an Amendment heading, so no wrong outcome exists there today. T82's line and brief name the requirement reader alone. A difference with no defect is not one that needs fixing.

decisions.summary: indented bold ids with no dash (192's, 198's) and a bare id opening a line are not read as requirement definitions
decisions.why: Measured as commentary on ids defined elsewhere, so not reading them leaves no requirement NOT FOUND. Nothing T82 asks for is excluded.

decisions.summary: exits and done: plan crate tests, lint, format, 100% cover, before/after bundles differing in the NOT FOUND line alone, closing-checks green; order before T22
decisions.why: This is enforcement and verification of the requested fix and of T48's ordering. It adds no behavior beyond the fix.

blocks: ### T97 (T93's Found and left: the walk's first use in a hook process cost 3.2-8.6 ms against 9-57 us a walk after, 3.89 ms of each Bash end's 7.30 ms in the event log, measured 2026-11-21 (T93's item 4: `/tmp/t93/cost.py`, and its scratch binary's `-first` mode, 5 commands twice each in fresh processes); main-tree's walk paid the same on every Bash start)
### T97 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Every walk static (40 in tree.rs, tree/bind.rs, tree/python.rs, tree/py_c.rs) becomes shared::regex::Lazy: built on first use as before, searched only where a necessary literal of the pattern stands in the text, else no match and nothing built.
decisions.why: This is the [perf] task T97's line files under FR-013 (the builders' loop, every Bash call's hooks), and the GM asked that performance work go first (request.md 2026-11-20). The plan states each gate is a literal every match holds; its replay of 9,646 commands shows the guards' verdicts unchanged, so the hooks still do their job. It removes work and narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: is_match/captures read a search error as no match, as every call site already did; captures_iter/find_iter keep yielding Result items so each of their 12 call sites keeps .map_while(Result::ok).
decisions.why: This keeps the existing handling and the checks crate's regex_scans rule. It is an implementation detail inside the task and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Five patterns that need no literal (CHMOD_MODE, py_c's WRITES, READ_MODE, ANY_MODE, EXPANDS) get a gate that passes every text.
decisions.why: These are unchanged behavior where no gate is sound. Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: PLAIN_QUOTE_BODY is replaced by plain code (plain_quote_body), with char::is_whitespace standing for \s, pinned by a differential test over every character to U+3100 plus U+180E, U+200B, U+FEFF.
decisions.why: It does the same job faster, and the differential test enforces that the answers agree. That serves the performance request.

decisions.summary: py_c's REPLACE (the literal replace\() becomes contains("replace(").
decisions.why: A literal pattern is turned into a literal search with the same meaning, faster. Within the perf task.

decisions.summary: A hand-written scan for ASSIGN's shape is not taken. About 12.4% of commands (an estimate, measured 2026-11-21) still build ASSIGN when they hold an = that is not an assignment.
decisions.why: Judged against request.md, FR-013 and this section's own statement of T97's line, since the line itself is not in the bundle. None of them sets a target for this task. Leaving a further speedup untaken is a design choice, not a defect (constitution XIV: only slower, every answer right). The task's purpose is still met: from a median of 12 builds a command to 2.

decisions.summary: A child-process pin test prints the patterns its process built (regex::BUILT, a list kept in test builds alone): simple commands build none, and a redirect builds exactly REDIRECT.
decisions.why: This is a test that fails only when the requested speedup is absent. Under FR-012 it is enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Fix a race in tests/hooks/test-no-poll-hooks.sh, outside T97's files, that turned its closing run 2 red. The case now ages the quiet file again first.
decisions.why: A flaky test that refuses good work is a defect under XIV. Fix-as-we-go asks known defects to be fixed as found, and this widens no requested behavior.

decisions.summary: The closing checks are not run a fourth time. Run 3's static was red at its format step on T100's in-flight file before reaching any T97 crate; T97's crates are shown green by crate-scoped test, lint and cover after the last edit.
decisions.why: No requirement in spec-index or request.md asks a task for a green closing run. FR-007 and improvement 2 point the other way: they cap make static at two, with crate-scoped checks while iterating and make static once at the end, which the landing's gate supplies. Run 3 was already a recorded STATIC_OK escape. This does depart from the plan's own exit in item 6 (a green make closing-checks), and the caller should square that line with item 9. It is not a narrowing of what the GM asked.

decisions.summary: shape's strip_heredocs and strip_quotes stay ungated: they are outside T97's files and are proposed as a separate [perf] task, not fixed here.
decisions.why: FR-009 bites only on a deferred DEFECT. This is not one: every answer is right and only slower (XIV, the GM 2026-11-19 definition), so leaving it unchanged stays within scope. Aside: no task id is filed for it yet, and under FR-013's ordering the caller may wish to file it.

decisions.summary: The saving over the dispatcher's whole event (about 2.7 ms at a Bash start) is left an estimate. A replay through every guard would write real guard state in a shared clone.
decisions.why: It is labeled an estimate and its arithmetic reconciles (3.23 - 0.21 - 0.30). It decides no scope: the per-guard saving is measured, and the estimate only reports what the task gains.

decisions.summary: T97 is classed as performance work ([perf], FR-013: the builders' loop).
decisions.why: It speeds every Bash call's hooks, which is within FR-013's 'the builders' loop'.

blocks: ### T101 (a ready task was refused "held by" the task started after it: T81, T88 and T93, each CLEAR and closing-checked, refused "held by T97" at 18:32:27Z, T97 started 61 s before, and landed only after the mark was moved by hand, measured 2026-11-21 (the 451 event log's land `end` lines, the clone's `task-starts.jsonl`); and T95, CLEAR, could not land alone because plan.md also held T82's and T97's unreviewed sections)
### T101 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The active-task mark stays one object (the last task started); only the hold changes; task-start's append and the event log's filing are untouched.
decisions.why: Leaves every other reader of the mark (measured search) as it is; the change is confined to the refusal the task was filed against.

decisions.summary: Where the mark's open task holds, a landing lands beside it when each of its tasks is started in the clone, its section passes `plan decided`, and no file of its delta (sectioned files and review ledger aside) carries an edit or shell write filed under another OPEN task since the file last landed; each failing reason is named with the hold.
decisions.why: This is the fix the filed task asks for (a ready, CLEAR, closing-checked task refused 'held by' a task started after it). 405 D4's purpose - no push of the worked task's half-done work - is kept as the files-its-own test, so the rule's purpose is not gutted; the mark's task is now protected the way every other started task beside it already was (D4: no other open box holds).

decisions.summary: A ready ruling exports L7R_LAND_READY; holding_with holds nothing for the ticks it names, so the push and the CI merge read the landing's own ruling; where the first pass did not rule, the push's step asks again (export_ready); the ruling never reads which task the mark names.

decisions.summary: The hold's one condition is edited in shared::speckit (holding_with) under make guard-edit, a labeled deviation from the launcher's file list; T97's shared/src/tree* and T82's files untouched.
decisions.why: The launcher's file list is not the GM's words; the edit sits where the rule actually lives (one rule, three callers) and touches no other open task's files. Implementation placement is not a fidelity question.

decisions.summary: Padding L7R_LAND_TICKS with the mark's task, and a new `l7r-gate land --held` verb, priced and not taken.
decisions.why: Design alternatives declined for stated correctness reasons (a padded TICKS would name a task the landing does not tick); nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: land-alone step 2, under its lock taken first, commits plan.md, tasks.md and plan-review.json built from HEAD with only the landing tasks' pieces replaced (temporary index, commit-tree, compare-and-swap update-ref), working files untouched; step 3's own-files refusal passes over the sectioned files.
decisions.why: Implements the task's second half (T95, CLEAR, could not land alone because plan.md also held T82's and T97's unreviewed sections); dry run on the real T95 case measured the commit carrying only T95's pieces.

decisions.summary: The staging lives in scripts/land-alone.sh's Python (PYLIB), not the land crate, so one program holds the pieces' rule for staging and take-back.
decisions.why: Placement choice; no part of the request reaches it.

decisions.summary: Where git merge-file conflicts on a sectioned file at take-back (measured shape: a tick's archive meeting another task's edit of the next heading), the file is merged piece by piece; a piece both sides changed differently still conflicts and nothing moves, as before.

decisions.summary: The files-own test does not see a file written by a Python program (the event log names no file for it; T96, open) and takes an edit older than 7 days as landed (land-alone's existing LANDED_SINCE bound).

Python writes: the file name is absent from the log until T96 lands, so the test cannot see it; the gap already governs every started task other than the mark's under 405 D4 and land-alone's existing own-files refusal, so T101 adds no new class of exposure, and the fix is an already-filed open task (T96). 7-day bound: it is land-alone's own existing bound, reused rather than introduced. Neither removes anything the GM asked for in 451, and neither guts D4's purpose for the work the log does attribute.

blocks: ### T99 (the idle-tests suite's case 5 check "the run started a FULL wait after the jump" failed good work: red in T88's closing run `20261121T180015Z-555985` (33 of 34, at a load of 16.5 beside a make done; `/tmp/t88/closing-1.log` is the same run), green on the rerun unchanged; measured 2026-11-21 over this clone's 24 closing-check runs (12:46Z on), the suite ran in at least 15 (its name on the log's timing line or a failure; the rest skipped on an unchanged key) and that was case 5's one red; reproduced the same day, 8 of 8 copies red with the suite's own `date` started 0.5 s late and 1 of 8 at 0.2 s, measured 2026-11-21 (`slowrun.sh` over HEAD))
### T99 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Case 5 is re-pinned by the guard's own events instead of slack: the clock seam holds the timer's first read on a gate until the first jump is written, jumps are paced by four timer reads each, each jump is stamped with $EPOCHREALTIME before it is written, jump k moves the clock B x 2^(k-1) s (B = 300) so each 'suspend detected' line decodes to the latest jump seen, and two checks pin the full wait after that jump (at least IDLE_WAIT_S of real seconds, and at least 24 timer reads), with a decode check on the reading.
decisions.why: T99's line asks for case 5 to hold under load by waiting on a condition rather than a clock, red first. A check that refuses good work is a defect under constitution XIV, and fixing it is fix-as-we-go. The fix keeps the regression the case exists for: a jump that is counted but does not restart the wait is red in every broken-guard batch (8/8, 16/16, 8/8, measured 2026-11-21). It also removes a timing used as a gate, which follows the 427 T03 ruling the plan cites.

decisions.summary: The plan states the guard is left untouched and case 5's changes stay in tests/hooks/test-idle-tests-hooks.sh, which goes from 34 checks to 37.
decisions.why: This keeps to the brief as the plan quotes it (the test file alone, the guard only if a timestamp had to be exposed, and the plan says none had to be). The three added checks (the held reading, the decode, the ticks) only check case 5's own property, so they enforce what was asked.

decisions.summary: Constants moved: the old check's 0.35 s slack is retired in favor of the IDLE_WAIT_S floor, and the jump size goes from 500 s to B x 2^(k-1) with B = 300, kept above IDLE_SUSPEND_S per jump and inside IDLE_GIVE_UP_S in total, by arithmetic.
decisions.why: These are internal test parameters that serve the fix in A1. The request has no requirement on them and no research claim moves.

decisions.summary: Case 7's upper bound on a condition wait is raised from 8 s to 90 s (a GUESS), fixed here rather than left. It was red in 3 of 64 loaded HEAD copies.
decisions.why: This fixes a check that refused good work, a defect found by this task, in the same file. A bound that a green run never pays is not a timing gate. Fixing a known defect in the step is what fix-as-we-go asks for, so it is not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Coverage: the new case 5 pins a full wait after the LAST jump the timer logged, not after ALL eight jumps as the old check implied. A timer that restarts on its first jump and never detects the later ones would pass, and the plan says so.
decisions.why: Against the GM's request and the spec this narrows nothing, because neither names case 5. It does narrow the old check's implied reach, and literal 'after all eight' would defeat T99's own purpose of not refusing good work. The plan reports that with the suite's sleep 1.0 s late a sound guard's wait legitimately ended after jump 1 alone (the stall path, 8 of 8 green copies under final.sh). A check demanding a run after all eight jumps would refuse that good work, which is the timing-as-gate the 427 T03 ruling forbids. The regression the case exists for, a jump counted without a restart, stays red in every broken-guard batch the plan reports. The plan states the remaining gap (a timer that detects only its first jump) openly, without claiming coverage it lacks.

decisions.summary: Case 6's 'the losers deferred (0)' red (1 of 64 copies at load 133.7) is not fixed here, because it is outside case 5 and a design choice. It is filed as T104, to land before T22.
decisions.why: T99's scope is case 5. The defect is deferred with its reason, a filed task id and its order ('lands before T22'), which is the form FR-009 requires, and it is fixed before the step T99's own line is ordered against. It is not left unfixed.

decisions.summary: The brief's T76 closing-run red was case 4b, not case 5. It was not reproduced in 472 copies, is not fixed here, and is filed as T104, to land before T22.
decisions.why: This corrects the brief's misattribution: the red is outside case 5 and has no diagnosis yet. It is deferred with its reason, a filed id and its order, so nothing the request or T99's line asks for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Order: after T88, before T22, independent of T97 and T101 (no shared file); budget one landing.
decisions.why: This follows T99's own line ('lands before T22') as the plan quotes it, and the plan reports no shared file with T97 or T101. Ordering is not a narrowing of what is built.

decisions.summary: T99 is marked 'Performance work? No'.
decisions.why: The mark changes nothing about what T99 builds. The bundle does not show which task the GM's 2026-11-21 'file that as a performance task' names, and FR-013's meaning is cut at [...] in the index. So this ruling does not settle whether the mark is right, only that it narrows nothing this section implements. Whether the mark is right is FR-013 and SC-006's scheduling question.

decisions.summary: Red first: T99's line asks for 'red first by a loaded run'. The plan reports that CPU load alone gave 0 of 96 case-5 reds on HEAD, so it takes its reproduction from a PATH shim delaying the suite shell's own date (8 of 8 red at 0.5 s, 1 of 8 at 0.2 s), alongside the original red in T88's loaded closing run (load 16.5).
decisions.why: The literal form, a red produced on demand by load alone, was not obtainable: the plan reports 0 of 96 copies red at loads of 15.7 to 79.7, because load slowed the timer more than the shell. The failure it does reproduce has the mechanism the plan diagnoses (the test shell's own lag eating the margin), and the one loaded red that exists is the T88 run it starts from. Red-first exists to show that the check fails on the failure before the fix and passes after, and the shim does that (HEAD red 8 of 8, the final case green under the same shim at 1.0 s). This is not a narrowing of the GM's request, which does not mention case 5.

blocks: ### T99 (the idle-tests suite's case 5 check "the run started a FULL wait after the jump" failed good work: red in T88's closing run `20261121T180015Z-555985` (33 of 34, at a load of 16.5 beside a make done; `/tmp/t88/closing-1.log` is the same run), green on the rerun unchanged; measured 2026-11-21 over this clone's 24 closing-check runs (12:46Z on), the suite ran in at least 15 (its name on the log's timing line or a failure; the rest skipped on an unchanged key) and that was case 5's one red; reproduced the same day, 8 of 8 copies red with the suite's own `date` started 0.5 s late and 1 of 8 at 0.2 s, measured 2026-11-21 (`slowrun.sh` over HEAD))
### T99 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Case 5's clock seam holds the timer's first reading behind a gate file. The first jump is written only once that reading is taken, so it lands inside the wait by a condition and not by the shell's timing.
decisions.why: This is the rule T99's line asks for ('wait on a condition, not a clock'), applied to the window that feature 169's eight jumps were betting on. It stays inside the suite.

decisions.summary: Each next jump waits for four of the timer's logged reads after the last one, so at least one tick falls between two jumps. Pacing ends once the run has started.
decisions.why: A condition replaces a 'sleep 0.15'. It makes the case hold under load, which is what T99 asks.

decisions.summary: Each jump is stamped before it is written, with bash's $EPOCHREALTIME and no fork of date.
decisions.why: This removes the shell lag that caused the red. It is a mechanism inside the asked fix.

decisions.summary: The full wait is pinned by the guard's own 'suspend detected' lines, with jump sizes B x 2^(k-1) decoded to name the latest jump seen. Two checks follow: the run starts at least IDLE_WAIT_S after that jump's stamp, and the timer reads its clock at least 24 times between seeing that jump and the run's start.
decisions.why: This restates case 5's property (a jump restarts the FULL wait) in the timer's own events rather than in slack. It is red first on HEAD under a shell lag and red on a broken guard, as T99's line requires.

decisions.summary: A decode check holds the reading itself: every line on the B grid, the jumps contiguous, and as many lines as the record's suspends. The suite goes from 34 to 37 checks.

blocks: ### T91 (T79's bind rule refuses two kinds of scratch write HEAD allowed, found by T79's second plan review, 2026-11-21: a name assigned twice in straight-line code is judged at each value, and past the 64-binding cap a lone loop falls back to T79's unknown reading, the mirror)
### T91 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A name assigned more than once in straight-line code is one binding: each bare assignment renamed, each read bound to the last assignment before it, a read before any assignment the environment's value or empty.
decisions.why: This is what T91's line asks for (a straight-line reassignment reads its last value). It is a fix of a check refusing good work, which constitution XIV and the fix-as-we-go rule ask to be fixed.

decisions.summary: A read whose last assignment follows && or ||, or that stands after a branch, a loop, a function or a source, keeps HEAD's reading at each value. Widening the rule to && was priced and not taken.
decisions.why: None of these is straight-line code, which is what T91's line names. An assignment after && or || may not run, so the read may see the earlier value, and judging each value is the correct answer there, not an over-refusal. No mirror refusal is lost. The moved pin's && form agrees: its last assignment follows a ;.

decisions.id: D-a (opaque forms in the stretch, filed as T145)
decisions.summary: A backtick, $(, brace group, comment or ${X:-$(...)} between the last assignment and the read keeps HEAD's reading at each value, so a scratch write that bash makes is still refused there. Filed as T145, which lands before T140.
decisions.why: This narrows T91's line, because these commands are straight-line code and the leftover over-refusal is a defect (a check refusing good work). The plan's stated reason, that bind.rs's flat scanner would need to parse substitution bodies, comments and brace groups, is a cost and does not make it legitimate by itself. What does is this: the defect is not dropped but sequenced, filed as T145 to land before T140, the task that waits on T91. So no known defect is carried into the next step, which is what fix-as-we-go asks. The GM's own words of 2026-11-22 are that tasks keep being filed at the current rate and are bundled when fixed, so filing a sibling task departs from no instruction. The deferral also carries FR-009's why, id and order. T91's purpose is met: ordinary straight reassignments are read as bash reads them. The exception errs only toward HEAD's refusal, and the either-end pin holds it there.

decisions.summary: A name read through ${D:=W}, ${D:-W} or ${D-W} is not taken as Straight and falls back to HEAD's reading at each value (added on T91's first plan review).
decisions.why: This prevents a regression the first cut introduced: a mirror write read as elsewhere. Keeping a mirror value at either end refused is in T91's line, and the exclusion only returns a name to HEAD's reading.

decisions.summary: The single many-valued name of a command is judged value by value up to 128 values. Past 128 it falls back to T79's unknown reading.
decisions.why: T91's line asks that a lone loop past the 64 cap be judged value by value, and the plan bounds that at 128. Some bound is physically required, because a guard that runs on every Bash call has to finish in bounded time: measured, 128 values cost 44.7 ms and 256 cost 171 ms (2026-11-22, T83's timer). The fallback is the conservative one (refuse, never under-refuse). The measured corpora hold no lone loop past 64 at all, so the bound defeats no case the purpose covers. The constant is labeled a CONVENTION.

decisions.summary: A command with several many-valued names keeps MAX_BINDINGS = 64 and T79's unknown reading, unchanged.
decisions.why: T91's line names a lone loop. Products of names are outside it, and the plan leaves them exactly as HEAD has them.

decisions.id: D-b gate-write's 7 product refusals not judged
decisions.summary: Whether gate-write's 7 refusals of over-cap product rows are right is left unjudged.
decisions.why: These rows are outside T91's line and unchanged from HEAD. No defect is established, so nothing is being deferred.

decisions.summary: Loop values are deduplicated by text, and bindings skips a name already bound.
decisions.why: These are mechanics of (b), and they change no verdict in the replay.

decisions.summary: The && form of a_name_assigned_from_pwd_is_where_the_shell_stands_then now reads elsewhere, as bash writes it. Its ; variant keeps clone and elsewhere.
decisions.why: This is a correction that follows directly from (a): bash writes there.

decisions.id: Found and left: T144 (${D:-W} and ${D:+W} default dropped)
decisions.summary: A defect that predates T91 (T79): replaced() drops the :- and :+ operand, so a mirror write can be read as elsewhere. Filed as T144, which lands before T140.
decisions.why: This is a defect left, and the more serious kind: a check passing bad work, because a mirror write can be read as elsewhere. It is ruled LEGITIMATE on the same ground as T145. It is not dropped: it is filed as T144 to land before T140, the next task that depends on this one, so it is not carried into the next step, and FR-009's why, id and order are all present. It predates T91 (it is T79's). T91's fix reads it exactly as HEAD does, because the default and assign ops are excluded from Straight, so T91 neither causes it nor makes it worse. Fixing it needs tree.rs's expand, which lies outside T91's bind rule. That last point is the plan's stated reason, not the ground for this ruling.

decisions.summary: active-task names the first member as task and every member as tasks. Each member's start is logged, the first member's last, so it is the task in force. All of a bundle's refusals are checked before anything is written.

decisions.summary: A member is refused when its box is not open, when it is a phase task (a parked stage's task included) or when its feature is held. The plan has no size test, so which tasks to bundle is the caller's choice.
decisions.why: The GM's words leave it to the session to look at the open tasks and pick the tiny ones, so leaving out a size test narrows nothing. A phase task is a stage of a staged plan, not one of the small defects the GM asked to bundle. A held feature or a closed box cannot be started alone either.

decisions.summary: Performance-first is checked for each member. A member that is not performance work is refused while an open performance task waits, unless that waiting task is a member of the same bundle. A performance task waiting outside the bundle still causes the refusal, with the same escape a single start has.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-013's literal start refusal. The GM's own words imply it: look at 'what set of tasks is currently open' and work them 'at the same time'. If the exception were refused, the performance member would have to go alone first, and every member would pay the fixed cost again, which is exactly what bundling exists to stop. It leaves FR-013's purpose intact, which is that performance work comes first and makes everything after it faster. The block says members are 'started, closed and landed together' and 'the landing ticks every member'. So a member that is not performance work can never land ahead of the performance member it shares a bundle with, and the end-to-end pin (land/tests/bundle.rs) lands the bundle as one unit. Counting each member as started for land-alone (T101) only lets the bundle land apart from other tasks. It does not let one member land apart from its own bundle. Any performance task outside the bundle still blocks as before.

The GM's words call for it: working the tiny tasks 'at the same time' with one builder is how the builder's reading-in cost is paid once, and that cost is one of the fixed costs bundling exists to cut. FR-006's purpose is to keep builder contexts small, and that is still enforced without change. The context threshold guard is untouched, and resuming a builder after its bundle lands is still refused, since every member is ticked. This ruling does not rest on the members being small: a large bundle reaches the same context cap as a large task.

decisions.summary: The record search runs in the tool at make claims-checked (silent.rs, called before the reply is vetted), not in the bundle builder, so IN-STEP claims cost nothing and OUTSIDE THE CHANGE lines are covered.
decisions.why: Where the task line's search runs is a mechanism choice; it reaches every line the task names, including row 210's own form (an outside line).

decisions.summary: A silent-finding line is HELD (not recorded, key still owed, exit 3) while any of the record's three nearest pages is missing from the bundle; once they are bundled it is judged again and recorded as written, and impl-drift.md tells the check a page that says it means fix: claim or nothing.
decisions.why: The task line asks that a hit turn the finding into a citation fix or nothing; word ranking cannot tell 'says it' from 'mentions the words', so the plan has the check read the hit and decide between exactly those two outcomes. The truly silent finding still files, which the GM's 'if there are real defects, then I do want to find them and fix them' requires.

decisions.summary: Lines held: a non-IN-STEP VERDICT that is NEEDS-RESEARCH, ends [section-mark] or uses a silence phrase, and an outside line with a silence phrase that names its effect (no-effect outside lines are dropped by T219 and not searched).
decisions.why: This is the task line's 'such a line' made concrete; the outside lines with no effect are never filed, so nothing is filed unsearched.

decisions.summary: The search covers the question and drawing pages (565) ranked by word weight; notes and originals are not searched, since they are not pages a claim cites.
decisions.why: The finding being tested is 'no page says it' and its fix is a citation of a page; the motivating case is a question page. Searching the citable pages is the search the finding's own words call for, not a narrowing of it.

decisions.summary: The task line names make canon / the registry as the search; the plan uses a word ranking over research/questions in the tool instead, because make canon searches the GM's setting notes and semantic-find did not return 0107 in its first five (measured 2026-11-24).
decisions.why: The parenthetical is the task author's guess at a means, not the GM's words; the substitute is the one that finds the motivating sentence, so it serves the task's purpose better rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: Read the nearest three pages then file; NEAREST=3 is a knob labeled GUESS; no score threshold.
decisions.why: A design parameter inside the requested behavior; labeled as a guess per the project's rule.

decisions.summary: The pages a hold named are kept in .git/claims-searched.json under the claim's key; the next reply on that key passes once those pages are bundled, however reworded, then the entry is forgotten.
decisions.why: Ends the round after one widened reading, which is what the convergence talk asks (no cascade of reviews that change nothing); the finding is still read against the pages the search named.

decisions.summary: A pass (IN-STEP) is not searched, so a GUESS judged IN-STEP whose cited pages are silent, where another page answers it, is still not caught; not built here.
decisions.why: The task is the filing of 'the pages do not say it' lines; a pass files nothing and nothing cascades from it. A conservatively labeled GUESS whose cited pages are silent is not a wrong outcome under XIV's defect definition (no map reads wrong, no finding is contradicted), so leaving it carries no deferred defect and needs no ruling.

blocks: ### T222 (the restatement audit, 2026-11-24: a dated log entry judged as a statement about the sheet today)
### T222 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: building-review.md: a dated entry of a sheet's notes (Review log line, line under a dated heading, entry naming its feature/task) is history, not held to the sheet as it stands; an overtaken older entry is no finding and owes no 'since superseded' pointer; only present-tense text (choices, program, Result/summary paragraph) is held to the drawing
decisions.why: Implements the convergence talk's 'a cascading set of changes that is mostly not finding actual problems' and constitution XIV's defect definition (a wrong outcome, not a difference): a log entry true of its date makes no map read wrong. The present-tense text, including the Result paragraph, stays held, so real defects are still filed; no requested review is removed.

decisions.summary: record-format.md: HISTORY rule kept whole, gains one sentence - a dated entry is history by its form, ruled on as HISTORY (useful kept, rest proposed for removal), never reported as a stale present-tense statement; permits no change log on a research page
decisions.why: Leaves the GM's 2026-09-07 HISTORY rule intact (dated entries are still found and proposed for removal); it only fixes which finding class they are filed under, so nothing the GM asked for is narrowed. One of the two agent files the task names.

decisions.summary: Verification by one ad-hoc agent following the clone's edited building-review.md over the two notes files as they stood before 452's fixes, since a dispatched defined agent reads the mirror's file (T219); record-format's sentence stated on the rule alone, no recorded case found
decisions.why: A method of checking the change, with a red case (Hayakawa T312/T299/T276 not filed) and a green case (the round-trip Result paragraph's figures still filed) that together show real defects are still found; narrows no requirement.

decisions.summary: Order: last of the restatement audit's five, after T219; classified not performance work; found-and-left none; no map changes
decisions.why: Scheduling and classification inside the task set; it is not measurement work (the GM 2026-11-20 rule) nor a speed-up of a tool, and leaves no defect unfixed.

### T220 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: impl-drift.md's FILED DEPARTURE paragraph re-judges a filed departure each time it is bundled: no longer departs -> DRIFTED fix: claim; departs but not a wrong outcome -> DRIFTED fix: claim; effect: none; only a standing wrong outcome keeps known (NNN Tnn) fix: code, with ask:417-T49-claims kept whole for it
decisions.why: Serves the convergence talk's purpose (reviews that change nothing are the problem) and constitution XIV v2.36.0 (a difference with no wrong outcome is not a defect, fixed by restating the claim). The arbiter's ruling stopped relabeling of a departure that stands; a departure that no longer exists or is not a defect is outside what it protected, and the one that stands keeps it whole.

decisions.summary: A procedure section's finding judged DRIFTED fix: code keeps a 'drawn' digest of every .rs file under rust/mode_a/src and is owed again (full check) when it differs; the over-owing cost accepted; per-claim unit pointers and re-owing every known drift each report priced and not taken

decisions.summary: Rows judged before the digest lands keep none; every standing row was re-judged and recorded in this task, and the one still a code fix (452 T24's compound shrine) now carries its drawn digest via make claims-checked; no fix: code section row is left without one, measured 2026-11-24 by reading the index's rows by key

decisions.why: Both motivating stale cases (genkan porch, kitchen garden) are drawn by rust/mode_a and are covered by the engine digest; the only sheet-only case (arch posts) was re-judged this task to fix: claim, so no standing fix: code row depends on a sheet, and the agent rule (a) re-judges any filed departure whenever it is bundled. decisions.summary: The six standing keys and 452 T24 bundled by make claims-bundle, judged by an agent told to follow the clone's impl-drift.md (the dispatched agent reads the mirror's), recorded by make claims-checked
decisions.why: Procedure for running the round on the edited rule; decides nothing about scope.

blocks: ### T223 (the round arbiter's process-fault, `ask:mixed-build-241-claims`, 2026-11-24: a green landing of 449 T423 T424 T418 T422 was refused at the push because T197's rule owed its unchanged doc claims a full impl-drift, the only route offered)
### T223 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The clean 'before' of a mixed row is read from dev/claims-index.json's own git history: walk from HEAD as far as checked_at, take the newest row whose build is not mixed.
decisions.why: The arbiter's tooling_fix (ask:mixed-build-241-claims) orders a mixed answer re-triaged by the clean build; a triage judges a change from a before, and the mixed row overwrote it, so reading it from the index's history is the mechanism the ruling needs, not a change of what it asks.

decisions.summary: At a landing only the fields a triage writes (research, pages, section, code, core, reads, triaged, cleared, triage, build) are withdrawn; verdict, note, date, claim and rests stay.
decisions.why: Withdraws exactly the mixed build's answer the ruling says must not be trusted, and keeps the verdicts the ruling keeps; no claim text or full verdict is touched.

decisions.summary: A mixed clear or agent triage owes what claims-owed's ordinary rules find between the clean answer before and the tree: nothing where the tree is back where that answer judged it (73), a tool clear then the agent where a section, page or code moved (147 cleared, 21 to the agent), a full check only where no triage judges the change (1, the rewritten barracks claim).
decisions.why: This is the tooling_fix verbatim in effect: re-judge with the clean build, mechanical clear first, then claims-triage, impl-drift only for what neither reproduces. Owing nothing where nothing changed since a clean verdict is the clean build's own ordinary answer and is the GM's convergence rule (2026-11-23: only a claim-changing edit triggers review). The ruling's 229/57 split is a count, not a rule; formerly agent-triaged rows the tool now clears are cleared 'mechanical clear first' as the tooling_fix orders.

decisions.summary: A mixed answer with no clean answer in the walk, or whose claim has no row in a commit of the walk, owes impl-drift with its files named (fails closed).
decisions.why: Presumed wrong and ruled legitimate on three grounds: it fails toward more checking, never less, so it can pass no bad work; the ruling itself sends to impl-drift a claim 'neither reproduces', and with no clean before in the walk there is no change for a tool clear or the agent to judge, so neither can reproduce it; and T197's rule that a landing never trusts a mixed answer forbids the only other outcome (trusting it). The replay found a before for all 242 mixed rows, so the case guts nothing the ruling asked for.

decisions.summary: A full impl-drift verdict is never re-owed: verdict_row builds a fresh row with no build, and the 14 edited claims keep their verdicts.
decisions.why: The ruling's what says verbatim 'The 14 edited claims keep their full impl-drift verdicts'; a row with no build is not mixed and so lies outside the rule being fixed.

decisions.summary: The route is L7R_LAND_ALONE=1 make claims-triage, which writes the withdrawal, clears what the tool can and bundles the rest for the agent; agent TOUCHES go to impl-drift; no command added; claims-owed and the push's gate say the count, files and command.
decisions.why: The tooling_fix names landing-mode claims-owed/claims-triage as the place of the fix. No verb is added, so ask:t197-rejudge-verb (which cut a withdrawal verb for T184's 81 modal marks) stands; the withdrawal here is the re-judging the later ruling ordered, inside the existing command. Naming the count, files and command is the project's guard-message rule.

decisions.summary: Outside a landing the index is read as it stands.
decisions.why: T197's mixed-build rule and the ruling's fix are both landing-mode only; nothing outside a landing changes.

decisions.summary: section_words also reads the kept words' own history (dev/claims-section-words.jsonl), so the 8 pruned base blocks are found rather than forced.
decisions.why: Required for the re-triage to work on the measured rows, and T210/T215's rule that a section's words are never forced where they can be found.

decisions.summary: Fix found here: clear_page_moves never stamped its build, so a mixed clear went unmarked and a clean clear of a marked row stayed marked; stamp_build fixes it.
decisions.why: A wrong outcome in the very check this task corrects (the landing answers wrongly either way); fixing a known defect in the task is the standing fix-as-we-go rule, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Committed before the landing of 449 T423 T424 T418 T422 is run again; the coordinating session then re-judges; red exits through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The ruling's what (1)-(2): make and commit the tooling fix before any re-judging, then re-run the landing.

decisions.summary: The task is not tagged performance work.
decisions.why: The GM's words class this kind of fix as a defect, not a performance improvement: on 2026-11-24 the cascade rules' over-sends (T210's 147 forced claims, T211's 22) were 'defects' to 'fix all 6 of those before we resume', and T223 is the same class - a check owing a full check to claims nothing changed for, refusing a green landing. Its time saved is the effect of correcting a wrong outcome, as the plan says. The label also moves nothing: the ruling already orders T223 before the landing re-run.

blocks: ### T224 (the round arbiter's `ask:mixed-build-53-record-answers`, 2026-11-24, continue with a tooling fix: a landing was refused at the push and 53 record answers owed again by T197's rule, when for 49 of them the uncommitted files were the claims crate's and a Markdown doc)
### T224 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A record answer is counted as mixed only by an uncommitted file in RECORD: owed, bundle, their path dependencies (core, pool, registry, research, rust/guard/shared), rust/gate/src and the record crate; the record crate's other dependencies (archive, downloads, pages, semantic, trials, uncited) are left out on a grep of every caller of write_answer/write_judged.
decisions.why: This is the tooling_fix of ask:mixed-build-53-record-answers: an answer is mixed only when a dirty path lies in the closure of the crates that built and recorded it (owed, bundle and their transitive deps). RECORD is a superset of that closure. It adds rust/gate/src and the record crate, which keeps more of T197 than the ruling requires. The crates left out are not in the ruling's closure in the first place.

decisions.summary: A Markdown file outside the table's crates never counts; a Markdown file inside a table crate counts (include_str! fixtures).
decisions.why: The ruling names rust/gate/CLAUDE.md as a dirty path whose code could not have run. Markdown inside a table crate still counts, and the closure walk flags any included file the table does not count, so no file that can run is dropped.

decisions.summary: tests.rs and tests/ files inside a table crate still count; no test-only exclusion.
decisions.why: This counts more than the ruling's closure would strictly require, so T197 is kept. It is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Any Cargo.toml, rust/Cargo.lock and .cargo/config.toml always count, and so does a path the rule does not know.
decisions.why: This is conservative. It keeps T197's rule for every file whose effect on the build the closure cannot rule out.

decisions.summary: The claims side's mixed-build test is narrowed the same way through its own table CLAIMS (the claims crate's path-dependency closure, rust/gate/src, and the record crate's one included file), through the single Landing::paths call.
decisions.why: The tooling_fix names only the owed crate's record gate, so narrowing the claims side's T197 rule goes past its letter. The ruling's own why gives the reason. The one case where it differs from the read-time rule is a write-time HEAD the landing later loses through an amend or reset. decisions.id: T237-7 keyed on the brief's STOP POINT marker; silent where the brief is omitted
decisions.summary: Only a builder whose brief holds a line opening STOP POINT counts as a code builder. A code builder dispatched without the template's marker is not read, and its claims dispatches pass 'by design'.
decisions.why: Purpose: the GM approved splitting the claims round off a code builder ('sounds good please do that ASAP'), under feature 451's standing 'let's make sure all of the enforcement is real enforcement and not just instructions'. The block's own finding is that 'the split was remembered (in the brief), not enforced'. Keying the guard on a marker that only the brief sets leaves enforcement resting on the session remembering to use the brief, one step removed. The block's own census sharpens this: the only builders that ever dispatched claims agents themselves (449 T426, T427, T429/T430, and T430's finisher: 5, 1, 4 and 3 calls) were unmarked, the very population this guard never reads, and the 12 marked builders made 0. Impossibility is asserted, not measured: 'the unmarked builder is no code builder it can tell' carries no count. The 579-transcript census does not report any unmarked builder, outside a claims-round dispatch, whose claims dispatch was correct work under the split (a page session, for instance). That count is the only thing that would make the obvious key, a D8 builder minus a brief opening 'Run the claims round', refuse correct work. D8 itself turned down a marker key for the same reason ('requiring a T<n> in it would let a builder with an unnamed brief pass'). 'By default' does not rescue it: a default's exceptions go through the recorded SPLIT_OK escape, not through an unrecorded omitted marker. Nothing in the bundle requires a code builder's dispatch to carry the marker. Either cure clears this: (a) key on D8's builder minus the claims-round prefix, or refuse a code builder's dispatch whose brief lacks the STOP POINT marker, so the unmarked gap closes; or (b) measure from the same 579 transcripts how many unmarked, non-claims-round builders made a claims dispatch that is correct work under the split, and if any are, name the key that tells them apart and state why the remaining gap cannot be closed.

It is legitimate on two grounds from the GM's own purpose. (1) The feature's request asks for the data 'in ideally a relatively cheap way' (2026-11-19), and a bound on how far back is read serves that. (2) With the cut named on every run, in the task's own heading and on a report line, plus a knob to read further, the tool no longer gives a wrong answer: it gives a labeled partial one, so it is not a defect left, and amendment (c)'s 'never silent' holds. Note that rulings.md is empty, because the block cites the arbiter in prose and not as an ask: ruling. So 'the arbiter's ruling of round 4 letting the knob stand so named' is not shown in the bundle, and this ruling rests on the substance, not on that citation.

decisions.why: This now agrees with the Which tasks item and with amendment (i). The round-3 item is settled.

decisions.summary: The name 'task time breakdown' goes at each gatherer, found by five commands: phase_row(, 'event-log phase' across the tree, event_log_hooks::append, write_dated(, ledger::cost::. Each command's hits are listed, with the name or the reason a hit is not a gatherer.
decisions.why: Round 3's item is met: every gatherer listed now has a command. Three gaps are left, none of them a narrowing that blocks, all to fix in the section. (a) The second command passes --exclude-dir=pool, saying 'the pool holds no code'. grep excludes by directory basename, so this also skips the pool CRATE that bullet 1 lists (pool/src/cache/phases.rs). Say so, or exclude by path. (b) The block now reads task-starts.jsonl, and D2 books by it, but no command searches that file's writer and no line says why it is not a gatherer. (c) The heading says 'written or computed through', but no command searches the reader's callers. make feature-report computes timing columns from the same lines (FR-005), and its Makefile help is one of 'the makefile comments that describe the timing' the GM named, yet only task-time's and where-time's help get the name.

decisions.summary: 'the GM' and 'the GM away' keep their minutes and show a share of the whole. Every other percentage (the category tables, the per-target table, the biggest-blocking list) is of the working time (the whole less the GM's). A 'working' row and a header line state the GM's minutes, their share, and which denominator each column uses.
decisions.why: This matches the GM's words: mention the minutes and their share of the total, and keep them out of 'the denominator when calculating the other percentages'. Folding 'the GM away' in is within: it is the same wait for him past a cap. Minutes denominators do not move because GM time is never machine time, which is correct.

decisions.summary: 'waiting: nothing in flight' becomes a family of classes read on every run from the event log (page session unmonitored; after the Stop's work had ended; until a notification woke it; until the session started again), plus a residual 'unexplained, then a <event> line'.
decisions.why: The GM asked that the row 'automatically gets broken down in the future'. This does it on every run. The residual names the event that ended each piece, so it is not a silent 'other'.

decisions.summary: A page session takes a wait's piece only where nothing else is live; among builders, runs and agents the one that ends last keeps the piece (critical path); no 'several in flight' row.
decisions.why: The GM's sentence is about the research number only ('if they were running in parallel with other things ... that number would be misleading'). Making page sessions yield to anything else applies it to research as he said it. The rule that blocking happens only with nothing else in flight, applied to everything, is the coordinating session's reading, and request.md marks it 'not his words'. Keeping the existing critical-path rule for builders, runs and agents keeps behavior he did not ask to change, so it is no narrowing of what he asked, and it needs no ruling. The asymmetry also fits his purpose: research is a queue implementation need not wait for ('before we could proceed with implementation'), while a builder's, a run's or a review's end is what the waiter proceeds on.

decisions.summary: 'Nothing else in flight' is read as nothing else THAT PAGE SESSION'S WAITER waits on. A main session waiting on page sessions alone books the wait as research blocking even while another main session (another clone) was implementing.
decisions.why: The GM: 'if they were running in parallel with other things, including running in parallel with other tasks which were not research-based, then that number would be misleading because it would essentially imply that we spent half of our wall clock time waiting for research to be done before we could proceed with implementation'. His words are 'other things' and 'other tasks', and 'we' is the project, with no limit to one waiter. The block says it applies 'nothing else in flight' 'literally to page sessions', but in its mechanism the words become 'nothing else its waiter waits on'. That is an unlabeled narrowing. Sessions do overlap: the block reads every clone's logs and sums every main session's clock, and the GM's '458 minutes ... 20% of the total time' puts the total near 2,290 min in a day of 1,440. So when one session waits only on page sessions while another implements, research still takes the blocking, and the number still implies implementation waited on research. That is the case his sentence names, and the fix's purpose fails there. The 'Working at once' header shows concurrency for the whole window, but it leaves the research number unchanged and does not say how much of it overlapped other work. Nothing makes the wider reading impossible: the walk already knows every actor at every instant (at_once()). Also, 'measured cause' carries no measurement, and no after-figure on real logs shows how much of the 949 the fix removes, so whether the narrowing matters rests on a premise nobody measured. What it should say: research blocking only where no other actor in ANY session read was working, the rest named in its own row or stated beside research's blocking as the share that overlapped other work, pinned by a test with two sessions. Or, if the session holds the waiter-only reading, it is the GM's to decide (through escalation), not this section's to assume.

decisions.summary: The header adds 'Working at once': the window's minutes with none, one, two, three or more actors working together (at_once()).
decisions.why: A report line that serves (k) (showing what ran in parallel) and amendment (d)'s parallelism question. It changes no booking.
