### T243 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Each piece of a main session's walked clock is booked to the task whose next step waited on it; round 4's project-wide reading and the round-3 page-session-yields rule withdrawn.
decisions.why: Amendment (l) verbatim: 'a minute should count as blocking. When something else is waiting on it to be done before it can be started', replacing (k)'s reading.

decisions.id: L2 the clue recorded with the data
decisions.summary: 'Blocks: <feature> T<n> | T<n> | none' in a dispatch prompt, page brief or builder brief's STOP POINT block, written as 'blocks' on the Agent call's event lines and on the page session's Phase line; 'L7R_BLOCKS=' read from a command's text; the line added to builder-brief.md and the research-record brief rules.
decisions.why: (l): 'to the extent that we can pass that kind of context clues to our tooling when the data is collected, whether through environment variables or I don't even know what else'. Reading the variable from the command text because a hook cannot see the shell environment is the mechanism, not a narrowing; the templates carrying the line are what make future data carry it.

decisions.id: L3 GUESS defaults where no clue is given
decisions.summary: Main session's own turns and waits block the task its lines carry; a builder's time blocks its own task, else its waiter's; a run or review agent blocks its waiter's task (a background run only from when it is waited on); a page session or research pass blocks nothing. Each labeled GUESS in book.rs's doc.
decisions.why: (l): 'not something our tooling can inherently know ... it doesn't have to be 100% exact ... only 90% of the time are we correct ... basically fine'. Labeled defaults for the unclued case are the approximation (l) accepts; research defaulting to nothing is overridden by a Blocks: line, which (l)'s decide-between-implementations case is to carry.

decisions.id: L4a prefer task-blocking work over work blocking none
decisions.summary: Among several in flight, what blocks a task is preferred to what blocks none.
decisions.why: (l): work done in parallel that blocks nothing 'is really not blocking anything'; a piece is never taken from a blocked task by non-blocking work.

decisions.id: L4b one owner per second across DIFFERENT tasks
decisions.summary: The walk gives each second of a main session's clock ONE owner even when that second blocks different tasks. Two cases in the blocks: (1) 'Among several in flight': among everything that blocks a task - any task - the second goes to the one that ends last; (2) 'Blocking minutes' / the defaults: the session's own turns and calls are its own and block the task its lines carry. So a research pass carrying 'Blocks: T4' gets no blocking for T4 while a builder for unrelated T5 runs longer, nor while the main session is in its own turn on T5; and the booking tests pin tasks + apart = each session's clock.
decisions.why: This contradicts (l)'s one concrete example word for word: 'that research would be blocking even if there was a different unrelated task happening in a different subagent at the same time', and its standard, 'a different standard than whether or not a different unrelated piece of work is able to be done at the same time'. It contradicts the section itself: (l)'s lead item books a piece 'never ... by what else ran', and both cases book T4's second by what else ran for T5. It is not the imprecision (l)'s 90% tolerance accepts (missing context clues): the clue is present and the rule discards it. And it leaves 'the window's blocking is the sum over tasks, which passes the clock where tasks ran side by side' true only across clones, never for tasks one session ran side by side (builder slots, bundles). Not a reopening of a settled block: the ends-last (critical) pick is untouched WITHIN one task's work, where it is right; what is new and judged here is the (l) build using it, and the own-turn rule, to choose BETWEEN tasks. The test row 'blocking by dependency' points the same way: with 'Blocks: T7' the page session takes all 10 s and the review's 4 s of blocking is gone - one owner per second over two task-blocking items (whether those are the same task cannot be told from the bundle). Required outcome: a piece's blocking for the task it blocks does not depend on what runs, or what the session does, for another task - in a second where several tasks each have blocking work in flight (or one is in the session's own turn), each of those tasks is booked its own (critical) piece; 'Waited on, blocking no task' takes a second only when no task-blocking work is in flight; the identity the tests pin is restated to match (the per-task sum may pass a session's clock), with a test of two tasks' blocking work in flight in one session. The mechanism is the builder's.

decisions.id: L5 work blocking no task named apart
decisions.summary: Where only work blocking no task is in flight, the piece is booked to that work on the header's 'Waited on, blocking no task' line by category, never in the blocking columns.
decisions.why: (l) says such work is not blocking; amendment (c) requires nothing silent, and a named line satisfies both.

decisions.summary: 'waiting: nothing in flight - a page session running, no monitor on it' blocks what the page session blocks: its brief's task, else nothing (apart).
decisions.why: The same dependency rule as L3 applied to an untracked wait; keeps the (j) class and books it by (l).

decisions.id: L7 window blocking as the sum over tasks; denominators
decisions.summary: The window's blocking is the sum over tasks, the landed tasks' sum beside it, the header saying it passes the clock; every blocking percentage is of that sum less the GM's rows (amendment (i)), never of the clock; the GM's rows show their share of the whole.
decisions.why: Checked against (i) by name: the GM's minutes stay out of every other percentage's denominator and his share is stated of the whole, as (i) asks ('those minutes should not be part of the denominator when calculating the other percentages'). Excluding work that blocks no task from a blocking denominator follows (l)'s definition of blocking; a denominator that is the sum over tasks keeps each table summing to 100 when that sum passes the clock, and the header names each column's denominator and that the sum passes the clock, so no percentage math is left to the GM. Consistent, and stays consistent once L4b is fixed.

decisions.summary: A start no stop follows ends at the agent's last own call before its next start (flight.rs span_end), at the window's end only with no call at all; where-time's agent minutes move with the shared reader; a live long call understated by at most that call, labeled GUESS.
decisions.why: A wrong outcome in the shared reader (three actors 'working' all day, 1,439.9 of 1,440 min at three or more) fixed in the one reader FR-005 requires both reports use; fixing a found defect is owed, and the residual approximation is labeled.

decisions.why: Widens the census toward 'everywhere that we're gathering these timings'.

decisions.why: A writer that records no timing is not a timing gatherer under the GM's 'everywhere that we're gathering these timings'; the reason is stated.

### T235 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: `which` kept in ASK only as the interrogative (`which (one |of these|...)?(do you|would you|should I|shall I)`)
decisions.why: The task is to stop statements firing as asks (the task line, and the GM's 2026-11-25 question about efficiencies in the check). On the corpus this alternative fired on 18 F (relative clauses) and on no T that another alternative missed, so no ask is lost; the interrogative form is kept.

decisions.summary: A STATED decision (`your call`, `needs your ...`, `ask you`, `waiting on you`, ...) is exempt when `nothing`/`none`/`nobody`/`neither`/`no one` stands earlier in its clause, or `not`/`never`/`-n't` within two words before it
decisions.why: Exempting a negated statement (`Nothing is waiting on you`, `didn't ask you anything`) serves the purpose: the GM asked for efficiencies and each false firing costs an escalation-check run. But the bound as written also exempts ordinary asks, which feature 429 FR-002 says are refused and which this section's own goal (item 1) and its Recall paragraph say still fire. The `-n't` within-two-words window exempts `This can't land without your call.` (can't [land without] your call). The clause-wide `nothing` exempts `Nothing else needs your decision except the budget.` and `Nothing is left but your call on the split.` The old rule refused all three. A tighter bound is possible: the negation governs the stated phrase itself, with no `without`/`until`/`unless`/`but`/`except` between them. So the case is not impossible, it is not implied by the GM's words, and the literal rule does not defeat the purpose. ### T232 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Route (1) is not built: an answered unit on an unchanged fingerprint is already not re-owed (make record-owed).
decisions.why: Nothing changes, and the block says why: the incident's re-run was forced by an arbiter ruling, not owed by the tool.

decisions.summary: Route (3), another contract line on its own, is rejected because the variance came from a line an agent did not follow.
decisions.why: This is a design choice between routes the brief offered. It drops nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The git-history proxy (30 pairs, 25 differences) is not used because it measures fix rounds, not same-fingerprint variance.
decisions.why: Measurement method. The block states the reason, which is measured (2 to 10 minutes apart, counts falling).

decisions.summary: The claims-triage 5-then-2 is declared not measurable as variance on one bundle, because the claims crate held T223's uncommitted fix between the two dispatches and no triage reply is kept. Nothing is built for it.
decisions.why: The finding is measured and leaves no defect: the two bundles differed. The block states this rather than assuming variance.

decisions.summary: make record-checked marks an answer at a fingerprint the unit was already answered at (rerun: the fingerprint and the earlier result). The answer is still recorded and re-stamps the build. The mark clears with the next answer or settle at another fingerprint.
decisions.why: Bookkeeping that makes a re-run visible. The forced re-run still does its job of re-stamping the build. A test enforces it.

decisions.summary: Route (2), for text an earlier round judged and passed: a re-run's new EDIT on a pop-up whose text that answer stood on is held and kept in noted.jsonl, not applied mid-landing. RERUN_OK applies it. A dry run holds nothing.
decisions.why: This is implied by the GM's own words: 'settled choices stay settled' and 're-reviews scoped to the change' (the seven rules he approved on 2026-11-23), and on the cascade, 'cascading set of changes that is mostly not finding actual problems ... we have to fix that before we move forward.' The sheet/barracks case is this class: a scoped round 6, then a re-run that raised a different NOTE on a paragraph earlier rounds had passed, with two EDITs. Holding that re-litigation serves the request's purpose.

decisions.summary: The hold makes no distinction between a factual correction and a style note. It keys on the unit's fingerprint, not on what the earlier round covered. So a factual EDIT on text the earlier round never opened is held as a noted.jsonl row too: the incident's own alcove gap, which the morning round said it 'did not re-open' and which the GM's commit 1b064aa0de landed. The block says this costs 'one session's delay'. But its own constraint line says such notes are 'listed and kept, never filed or applied' (451 T219, T229), and the only route it names for applying one is the RERUN_OK bypass.
decisions.why: Judged on its purpose, not its wording. The GM separated factual findings from style: 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies ... when we are cascading, we are only interested in factual inaccuracies'. He approved 'only factual findings cascade' and asked on 2026-11-24 that 'we really are cascading in situations that do call for it.' 'Settled choices stay settled' protects judgment calls that were made, not a factual gap in text no round opened. Run through this tool, the incident's valid finding ends as a never-applied note. The block's 'one session's delay' names no mechanism that delivers it, so the decision does not do what it says. That also cuts against 'fix defects where you find them' (constitution XIV), which the block cites as a constraint. One argument is stretched over two unlike things: a style re-litigation and a factual correction. To pass, the block must do one of two things. (i) Name the route by which a held factual EDIT is applied: a target the next session runs, or each one filed as a task ordered before the next step, with a test that a held EDIT reaches it. Or (ii) not hold an EDIT that corrects a factual error (or a GUESS/attested label), so the hold covers only re-litigated notes and wording. The cause of the morning miss (no line saying what a round covers) is deferred to T249 while this hold lands first. That deferral is why the hold must not, meanwhile, swallow the factual findings that miss produces.

decisions.summary: apply-edits holds every EDIT on a pop-up file whose unit carries rerun at its current fingerprint 'for any of the reply's checks'. A reply that mixes a re-run check with a first-round check therefore has the first-round check's EDITs held as well.
decisions.why: Taken on its own, this reach is outside even the rule that justifies the hold. A check answering a fingerprint for the first time has had no earlier round pass that text, so 'what an earlier round passed stays passed' cannot apply to its findings. Nothing in the GM's words settles text that no round of that check judged. The block must hold only the EDITs of a check that is itself a re-run at that fingerprint. Alternatively it must state, measured, that a reply never mixes a re-run check with a first-round one, or that its EDITs cannot be attributed and why holding all of them is still confined to re-judged text.

decisions.summary: Found and fixed here: the measurement's replay overwrote sheet/guest-quarters' kept round-5 snapshot, which produced a false change section. The snapshot is restored to the text that round judged, and a rebuilt bundle shows no change section.
decisions.why: A defect found and fixed in the task (constitution XIV, fix as we go).

decisions.summary: A re-run of a record check on a research page is not held. This is filed as T249 and lands before T246.
decisions.why: This is not a wrong outcome. The EDITs are findings, and applying them costs re-owed checks but changes no map or verdict wrongly. No record-check re-runs on pages have been measured. The deferral carries FR-009's three parts: why, filed id, order.

decisions.summary: When a subject's last round predates the kept snapshots, a later round gets no change section and no line saying what it covers. This is filed as T249 and lands before T246, because bundle::earlier lies outside this task's hold.
decisions.why: This is a real defect by the project's definition: a round passed text it never opened and missed the alcove gap. The deferral alone stays within because it carries FR-009's why, filed id and order inside the feature, and the bundle does not show that T246 is a later port step. T249 must land before the next port step (fix as we go). Its interaction with the hold is ruled under hold-factual-finding-with-no-route. Note too that the block rejects route (3) as 'another line would repeat it', while T249's fix is itself a bundle line.

decisions.summary: 'Performance work? no.'
decisions.why: A declaration. Nothing is decided against the request.

decisions.why: The task's goal ('a check run again on text nothing changed leaves that text's wording as it was') is generic and the build reaches pop-ups only, so it narrows. Legitimate because it is scheduled, not dropped: FR-009's form is met (why: a page's units are its notes and questions, a different mapping; filed id; order 'lands before T246'), no record-check re-run has been measured to occur, and the observed incident's class (pop-up re-runs) is fully covered. The GM's 'settled choices stay settled' is still owed in T249.

decisions.id: D12 no line saying what a round covers (found and left, T249)
decisions.summary: Where a subject's last round predates the kept snapshots (451 T189), a later round gets no change section and no line saying what it covers - the cause of the 2026-11-24 morning round missing the alcove gap. Not fixed here (bundle::earlier, outside this task's hold); filed as T249, lands before T246.
decisions.why: This is a defect (a check round passing work with a factual gap), so leaving it narrows. Legitimate as a scheduled deferral meeting FR-009 (reason, filed id, order before T246), not an abandonment; the factual finding itself still lands under D3, and the arbiter-forced whole-text re-run caught the gap. blocks: ### T233 (`docs/gm-rulings.md`, section 'NOT a ruling', 2026-11-24: 0006's comment calling dry plots against the canal a ruling of his was never his; the audit of that day found 74 of 180 such comments with no recorded words behind them)
### T233 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A static text check, gm-attributions, run in make quick and the push's checks, registered; not an Edit guard
decisions.why: The task line (request.md, T233 section) asks for 'a check'. The Edit guard was the other way to build it, and turning it down narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: HTML comments of research/questions/*.html; CANON claim lines in rust/ as claims::units::walked walks them (tooling trees out, rust/parked in) and the two procedure docs
decisions.why: The task line names 'a research page's comment or a claim's CANON label'. A claim is what the claims system walks, and the plan keeps parked claims in rather than dropping them.

decisions.summary: The task's three forms, the comma date form, and the near-twins rule/doctrine/correction
decisions.why: These are the task line's three forms. The near-twins are named in the task line's baseline ('the about 60 unaudited near-twins'), so they have to be detected. The comma form is 'GM <date>' with punctuation. All of it widens the check toward the purpose.

decisions.summary: An existing path: specs/<slug>/request.md or gm-request.md, docs/gm-rulings.md, or specs/<slug>/gm-review.jsonl; a bare 'request.md' or 'feature 280' is no pointer
decisions.why: These are the task line's three record kinds. gm-request.md holds his request verbatim, so it is the same kind of record. Refusing 'feature 280' as a pointer is stricter than the task line. Pointing at the gm-review.jsonl file rather than one row is the same coarseness ruled on under existence-only.

decisions.summary: The check confirms the pointed-at record exists, not that it holds the attributed words
decisions.why: Measured against the GM's own words (2026-11-24: rulings he never made must not be built on as his) and the session's task line. Two grounds hold. First, no static text check can judge whether a paraphrase is supported by a record: that takes reading and judgment. docs/gm-rulings.md puts that judgment 'before anything is built on it', and the pointer makes it possible. Second, the purpose survives. 0006's comment had nothing to point at, and under this check it would need a path a reader can follow, so a silent attribution becomes one that can be checked. A deliberately wrong pointer passes, and the plan states that cost. The ruling does NOT rest on the GM's 2026-10-25 words: they concern a map choice the research does not settle, and the strictness of a tool is not that kind of choice. Nothing measures the premise that a verbatim rule 'would refuse most correct pointers', and the ruling does not need it.

decisions.summary: dev/gm-attribution-baseline.jsonl keyed by a text hash; three refusals (unlisted, stale with --prune, entry the merge base lacks); --seed only where none exists
decisions.why: The task line asks for the baseline to shrink as pages are edited, and these three refusals enforce that. Seeding the old attributions into the baseline is the requested mechanism.

decisions.summary: The baseline holds 341 comments (176 four-word, 165 near-twins), more than the task line's '74 and about 60'
decisions.why: The task line's counts were estimates from the audit. The census also finds the audit's BACKED rows that name no path, and the comma-form near-twins. Each listed entry still owes a pointer when its text is edited, so the larger baseline excuses nothing for good.

decisions.summary: The 3 rust/parked CANON claims get their request.md pointers here
decisions.why: This fixes found defects in this task.

decisions.summary: The 341 page comments are not fixed here; a follow-up, filed by the coordinating session, runs once the research switch reopens

The ruling's purpose survives: such a cause still gets its look. The arbiter rules on it under FR-011 and can rule continue, which is exactly how the 374 ruling itself was reached (the cap tripped at round 3 and the arbiter ruled continue). FR-010 says the tripwire 'does not stop the feature'. The GM's 2026-11-24 words, 'that we really are cascading in situations that do call for it', still hold: the cascade owed by a read page's change still runs, through modal-triage and one ruling, and is neither dropped nor settled silently. blocks: ### T257 (the parallel trials, 2026-11-25: spec-fidelity ran make plan-verdict from the session clone, where a worktree task's section is still the template, and was refused on a section-hash mismatch in five tasks)
### T257 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The bundle's MANIFEST names the tree the bundle was built from (<tree>/specs/<feature>/, made absolute) and gives the recording command as `make -C <tree> plan-verdict F= TASK=|BLOCKS=1 FILE= AS=spec-fidelity`, in both bundle forms; spec-fidelity.md's 'run from the clone's root' becomes 'from the tree the MANIFEST names'.
decisions.why: This is the task line's first constraint word for word ('the review bundle's MANIFEST names the tree and the exact recording command with its root'). `make -C` is a means of giving the root, not a change of what is asked, and the agent-file wording only points the reviewer at what the MANIFEST now states. Nothing is excepted.

decisions.summary: On a section-digest mismatch, make plan-verdict searches the trees `git -C <tree> worktree list --porcelain` names (the session clone and every worktree of it) for one whose plan gives the reviewed digest for the task's section or the refused block, and names it with the command to run there; with none, the refusal keeps today's message; the search runs only on a refusal.
decisions.why: Carries the task line's second constraint ('refuses a tree whose section differs naming the right one'). The worktree set is where a worktree task's section can live relative to the clone it was made from, and it contains the observed failure (a reviewer recording from the session clone while the worktree held the text). The 'none found' fallback is the case where no tree holds the reviewed text, so there is no right one to name; it removes no case the task asks to cover. Running the search only on a refusal changes cost, not behavior.

decisions.summary: Both section checks are fixed - the task route (make decide's bundle, record_task) and the blocks route (make plan-delta's bundle, record_blocks/check_named); the whole-plan route, which is not a bundle's, keeps its message.
decisions.why: The task line is about the review BUNDLE's MANIFEST and a SECTION that differs. Both bundle routes are covered, which is the full reach of that wording. The whole-plan route records against plan_sha256 with no bundle and no section, so the constraint as written does not reach it; leaving it alone keeps the task to what was asked rather than carving a case out of it.

blocks: ### T256 (the parallel trials, 2026-11-25: every carry-over of a worktree's task into the session clone conflicted on specs/451-time-retro-and-efficiency/plan-review.json and was merged by hand as JSON, both sides' entries kept)
### T256 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The route is a git merge driver for specs/*/plan-review.json (l7r-gate plan merge-record), not per-task verdict files; no reader changes.
decisions.why: The task line offers exactly these two routes ('each task's verdicts in their own file, or the record merged by a git merge driver') and requires make plan-verdict and every reader unchanged in what they read; choosing the driver is a choice between the offered routes, and it is the one that leaves the readers untouched. The cost comparison is labeled measured 2026-11-25 with its method.

decisions.summary: Three-way, key-by-key merge of the top level and the blocks and tasks maps; an entry is taken whole, never field by field; a both-changed key goes to the later 'reviewed' day, a tie to the incoming side.
decisions.why: This is how the requested driver keeps both sides' entries. Taking an entry whole means no verdict ends up paired with a digest nobody cleared. The tie-break covers only the case where both sides changed the same key, which the goal (two builders each adding their own task's verdict) does not produce. Even a wrong pick only leaves a block owed a review again, because the gate re-compares the digest. Nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: block_reviews is merged as an append-only log: ours, then the incoming rows not in base and not already in ours, order kept.
decisions.why: Keeps both sides' rows (measured 303 to 305) and keeps each side's order, which the review-round guard's trailing count reads. That serves 'both verdicts with no hand merge' and 'every reader unchanged'.

decisions.summary: Registration via sync-with-main.sh ensure_git_config at every sync-in, idempotent; the driver runs with L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1; if it is unregistered or the binary is older than the verb, git falls back to its text merge.
decisions.why: A merge driver's command lives only in local git config, so registering it is how the task line's route works at all. It is registered on the session clone that the goal names, and its worktrees share that config. The fallback is the state from before the task, not an exception to it. Item 5 orders sync-in before the first carry-over it serves.

decisions.summary: A side that does not parse as JSON fails the merge with our side untouched, and the message says to merge it by hand as JSON, both sides' entries kept.
decisions.why: This is a case the driver leaves to a hand merge. It is legitimate on the physically-impossible ground: a structured JSON merge cannot run on a side that is not JSON. It also does not gut the purpose. A record written by make plan-verdict through the recorder's own pretty writer parses, so the two-builder carry-over the task exists for is always handled by the driver. Only a corrupt or hand-broken file falls out, and it gets today's hand merge with a message naming it.

### T254 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: make task-start writes <common git dir>/task-marks/<feature>/<task>.json (feature, task, bundle tasks, tree, time); no start overwrites another task's mark
decisions.why: This is the fix the GM approved by name: 'a started-task mark per task' (request.md, 2026-11-25, 'sounds good, please start with that'), answering trial 1's overwritten mark.

decisions.why: A migration that keeps a start made before the change counting. It narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: a mark goes when its task lands (the landed sweep, by task ids as given) or when its feature is set down in its own tree (marks::clear); other trees' marks stay; a ticked task's stale mark holds nothing
decisions.why: This narrows 451 T29: a set-down used to clear its feature's mark, and now clears only the marks this tree wrote. The ground is the request's purpose. With per-task marks, a set-down that cleared other trees' marks would wipe a parallel builder's started task, and that brings back the very failure the request fixes (trial 1, one start removing another tree's mark). When there was one mark, it was always the clone's own, so T29's scope in effect is unchanged. A ticked task's leftover mark holding nothing follows from every reader asking for an open box.

decisions.summary: each task-starts.jsonl row names its tree
decisions.why: The data the per-tree readers need. It adds no behavior beyond the fix.

decisions.summary: another tree's started task (its box open, not ticked by this landing) holds this push, make land or CI merge only when the push's delta carries one of its edits (T101's rule in speckit/touch.rs, read against every tree's prefix); L7R_LAND_READY still not held; a mark that is not an object fails closed
decisions.why: This narrows feature 405 D4 ('the active task holds, nothing else'). The plan turns D4 into every started task of any tree holding the push, so taken literally a push from any of the three worktrees would be refused while another builder's task was started. That is the exact refusal the trials recorded (port-talk-agenda item 1: 'a push of one task was refused while the other was started'). It would defeat the purpose of the GM's 2026-11-25 approval, which is three parallel builders, so the rule applied literally defeats the request. A push that carries another tree's edits is still refused, which is broader than D4 ever was, so the hold's purpose of keeping an unfinished task's work out of main is kept across trees.

decisions.summary: the pushing tree's OWN started task (a mark this tree wrote, box open, not ticked by this landing) no longer holds a push whose delta carries none of its edits; before T254 it held the push whatever the push carried (the section's own constraints item 2; feature 405 D4)
decisions.why: The section justifies the narrowing as 'the fix the trials asked for - a push of one builder's task refused while another builder's was started'. That covers another tree's task only: the trials' refusal came from a different worktree's start. The GM's words in request.md ('a started-task mark per task' ... 'sounds good, please start with that') approve per-task marks so three builders can work side by side. Nothing in those words, and nothing in that purpose, needs a tree's OWN open started task to stop holding its own push. Keeping D4's hold for the tree's own task is possible, the GM's words do not contradict it, and it does not defeat three parallel builders: each builder's tree lands its own task(s), and that landing ticks them, so they do not hold it. The rest of the plan's case comes from text outside the request. One is consistency with 451 T101's landing rule, which is cited by paraphrase only and is not in spec-cited.md. The other is that a push without the task's edits carries none of its work. Neither is a ground under this review: they show the exception does no harm, not that the request needs it. One justification is stretched over two unlike cases, and only one of them is needed. Cure: keep D4's hold for the started tasks this tree wrote, so one of them holds this tree's push while its box is open and the landing does not tick it, whatever the delta carries. Apply the carried-edits rule only to other trees' marks. Restate goal item 1 and constraints item 2 to match, and add a test that a tree's own open started task still refuses a push that does not carry its edits. Or bring the GM's words approving the own-tree case.

blocks: ### T259 (the GM 2026-11-25, `specs/449-rust-codebase/port-talk-agenda.md` item 13 and its "Order" paragraph: "should we move that item up to or near the front, so it can apply to all of the other optimizations we're building at the moment?")
### T259 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Prose mechanisms are not detected: a rule line in a CLAUDE.md or docs/ file, a new mandatory round of an existing agent, a standing order in the builder brief. They are backfilled as found, and audit-register.md names the gap.
decisions.why: The GM's own words carry this exception: 'something like this limit on builder token window context size might not even show up as an optimization ... after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. He separated the easy-to-identify mechanisms from the hidden ones and sent the hidden ones to backfill-as-found. A new imperative sentence in prose has no form that tells it from correct documentation, so a detector would fire on correct work. The plan's own replay shows the cost: of 7 register-worthy landings in its sample of 20, the detectors caught 3. T254-T257 detect nothing, yet each gets an entry. That is the hidden class the GM described, and the entries written for them are his route, not a gutting of his purpose.

decisions.summary: Not detected: a new row of the push's checks table, or a new step of make land's Rust code. The stated reason is 'none has a form a check can tell from correct work'.
decisions.why: Two unlike classes share one sentence with the prose kinds. A push row is a mandatory check, and a land phase is a landing step. These are the very kinds the plan's constraints list, and they sit in the GM's 'easy to identify as a measurable and auditable part of our tooling' class, not his hidden class. The premise that they have no diffable form was never measured. The plan's own test 'push::tests::the_table_lists_its_rows_...' (26 rows) treats the push table as a list of named rows, which points the other way. The register is moved to the front 'so it can apply to all of the other optimizations we're building at the moment', and those are landing and push machinery. As written, a check that passes such a landing passes bad work. Fix: measure whether push rows and land phases carry a name that a base-vs-HEAD comparison can read. If they do, detect them as D3 does for constants. If they do not, record that measurement (date, method) as the reason and keep the gap in audit-register.md.

decisions.summary: Threshold constants are read only in rust/guard/ and the gate's checks crate. Other gate crates are excluded, the land crate's CLAIMS_WAIT_S among them.
decisions.why: 'The brief's words' is a session's scope, not the GM's, so it cannot make a narrowing legitimate. The measurement given is over the whole rest of rust/gate/: 74 names, 'many of them knobs of the research tooling'. That argument does not reach the landing crates. The plan's own named miss, CLAIMS_WAIT_S, is a landing wait that costs every builder time: an optimization of exactly the kind the register exists for, and one being built now. The detector applies to those crates unchanged (a module-level const line), so this is neither impossible nor implied by the GM's words. Fix: extend the constant scope to the landing and push crates (at least rust/gate/crates/land and the cohort crate the push lives in), with D4's filter measured over them, or measure those crates separately and show their passing names cost nothing.

decisions.summary: A constant is new only if its name is absent from the whole scope at the base. Known miss: a second constant that reuses a name already held elsewhere.
decisions.why: A per-file comparison would refuse correct work on every split the 1,000-line bar forces and on every move, which is a check refusing good work. The stated miss is narrow, and it falls under the GM's 'backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. It does not defeat the request's purpose.

decisions.summary: A name filter keeps names with a threshold word (55 of 84) and drops display sizes, fixed facts and unit-only names (29).
decisions.why: The GM's subject is 'this kind of optimization' and 'auditable optimizations and processes and procedures', not every constant. A display size such as LARGEST or a unit such as GB is neither. The filter was measured (2026-11-25, 84 = 55 + 27 + 2) and keeps every knob the agenda names. The pre-filter replay fired on T245's GB and LARGEST, so the unfiltered rule refuses correct work. A threshold whose name holds no listed word is a miss for backfill-as-found.

decisions.summary: Detector edges: only column-0 const lines are read; only integer and float types; a guard's submodule is not a module; a rename (R) adds nothing.
decisions.why: A rename or a submodule is not a new mechanism, so excluding them is correct rather than a loss. The column-0 and numeric-type limits miss some thresholds (a function-local const, a Duration-typed one), but these are stated edges of a path-and-name detector, not known mechanisms left out. The GM's backfill-as-found covers them.

decisions.summary: The initial backfill is ten named entries. Their sources are given (agenda items 1, 12 and 13, plan-done.md T244-T246 and T254-T257, process-decisions.md), but no search space is stated and no list of known mechanisms left out.
decisions.why: The GM asked for 'a list of all of the auditable optimizations and processes and procedures', with backfill-as-we-go only 'after the initial backfill', for 'things that we missed'. The plan's own census in D4 names known, enumerated knobs that no listed entry visibly covers: STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK (feature 451's own FR-007 improvement), the round caps PLAN_ROUND_CAP and SPEC_ROUND_CAP, and POLL_CHECK_S. Feature 451's other approved improvements (the background-run guard, the 60 s poll, the hook-suite split) are among 'the other optimizations we're building at the moment'. The check fires only on mechanisms absent at the base, so no landing will ever ask for these. Without the initial backfill they are never registered. Things already found are not 'missed', so the GM's backfill-as-found route does not reach them. Fix: state the initial backfill's search space, for example the four detectors run over the whole tree against an empty register, plus the feature 451 improvements. Either give every mechanism found an entry or a covers: line (unmeasured with first-audit where no measurement exists), or name each one left out under Found-and-left with its filed task and its order.

decisions.summary: Every entry's ten fields are checked on every run, and a malformed entry refuses whatever the delta adds.
decisions.why: This enforces the GM's 'documenting the logic behind it, the measurements that we took, and ... what we would look at that would falsify' against stub entries.

decisions.summary: An entry may say 'unmeasured' only if it names its first audit in first-audit: (for example, delegating to builders at all).
decisions.why: A measurement that was never taken cannot be recorded, so requiring one is impossible. Saying so and naming the measurement that will be the first audit serves the GM's falsifier and re-audit purpose. It is also where his item-12 ask lands: 'we should make sure to measure whether the complexity of the handoffs actually saves time'.

decisions.summary: Agenda item 12's three-way handoff measurement is not performed in T259. It is carried as the delegation and context-cap entries' first audit, and the never-audited entries are listed first.
decisions.why: The GM asked that it be measured, not that T259 measure it. Registering it as a first audit at the shortest cadence makes sure it is done. Item 12 is its own agenda item.

decisions.summary: Gate-chain targets are found transitively from eight fixed roots, through prerequisites and $(MAKE) calls.
decisions.why: This is how 'a gate or landing step' is read off the Makefile. The replay found make closing-checks and make _quick, both real additions.

decisions.summary: Each entry is a Markdown file with key: value front matter, one file per entry.
decisions.why: This is the form the task line asks for (one file per entry). Markdown over JSON is a design choice the GM's words do not decide.

decisions.summary: The check runs in make static and in the push, and the push row needs dev/audits.
decisions.why: This is enforcement of the register at the points a builder and a landing pass through.

decisions.summary: The escape is AUDIT_ENTRY_OK with a reason, recorded escaped or blocked in the guard log.
decisions.why: This is the project's standing guard form, and it lets the check be audited against its own falsifier.

decisions.summary: Cadences and every threshold no record states are GUESS knobs, and never-audited entries get the shortest cadence.
decisions.why: The GM gave no cadence. 'Each one would know the last time that it was audited' is served by this.

decisions.summary: There are ten front-matter fields where the task line says six, and make audits orders entries never audited, then overdue, then by due date.
decisions.why: The added fields (command, threshold, cost, cadence) serve the GM's measurement, falsifier and re-audit asks, and the ordering serves 're-audit to see if they still make sense'.

### T258 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A bare git mirror at <common .git>/tooling-state.git, committed from where the files lie, not tar snapshots
decisions.why: The mechanism that carries 'the tooling state' to the GM's repository; chosen by measurement (item 9, dated, methods named). Nothing the GM asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: Logs committed as whole-line segments (split -C, SEGMENT a GUESS knob), the mirror repacked each run
decisions.why: A storage layout that keeps every log line in the repository and keeps pushes clear of GitHub's per-file limit, which would otherwise end every push. Nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: The landing's push runs detached (push --detach); make land / land-tooling exit with their own code
decisions.why: Implements the task line's 'never refusing it'. The GM's words set no timing for the push.

decisions.summary: A detached push's failure is logged and said in one line at the NEXT landing; make state-push is the foreground form
decisions.why: The cost of D3a, named and priced against a foreground push. A failure is still reported, so the state does not silently stop reaching the repository.

decisions.summary: A push that meets a running push (flock held) is skipped; the next landing's push carries its state
decisions.why: 'At each landing' is in the section's quotation of the task line, not in request.md or the spec. On the block's own text, state written after the running push's commit is unsaved until the next landing, and so is all state written between any two landings. The skip widens that gap by one landing and does not lose state. The cost is named here rather than ruled as a narrowing.

decisions.summary: One branch per clone, named for the clone the common .git belongs to; a replacement container's clone of that name takes it
decisions.why: A layout inside the GM's repository. Every clone's state still reaches the repository.

decisions.summary: Never a force push; a fresh mirror fetches and merges the branch before its first commit; a refused push is fetched, merged and pushed on top
decisions.why: Keeps state already in the repository from being overwritten. Serves the purpose and drops nothing.

decisions.summary: Restore merges and never overwrites: answers by l7r-gate record merge-answers (newer utc kept), logs by appending missing lines; .tmp files not pushed
decisions.why: Restoring the state into a fresh clone is the point of the repository. A .tmp file is a half-written answer or log line, not finished tooling state.

decisions.summary: Session-clone setup is sync-with-main.sh sync-in, running restore --if-fresh (mirror made and restored in the background); a clone that already has a mirror does nothing; make state-restore by hand
decisions.why: A clone that has a mirror is not the fresh or replacement clone the restore exists for, and the by-hand door stays open. The background restore delays nothing.

decisions.summary: A clone whose origin is not GitHub main's does nothing unless STATE_REMOTE names a remote
decisions.why: Ruled class by class. (1) Other suites' fixture clones, which run sync-with-main.sh with local origins and made-up answers and logs: pushing them would put fake data into the GM's private repository and have tests reach the real remote. Excluding them is implied by the purpose ('for the tooling state', the real record-check answers and event logs), so this class is legitimate. (2) A real working clone whose origin is something other than GitHub main: the stated justification does not cover it, because its state is real tooling state. The bundle shows one real push, from diagram-backlog. It does not say whether make state-push goes through this origin check, or what any other clone's origin is. D7 says clones are made by a bare git clone, presumably of GitHub, and the block names no real clone the check leaves out. So no defect is shown here. If such a clone exists, STATE_REMOTE is its door, and leaving it silently unbacked would be a defect for its owner to fix.

decisions.summary: Token via l7r-gate github-token into GITHUB_TOKEN with the askpass script; credential.helper emptied; remote passed by URL per call, never stored in the mirror's config
decisions.why: Implements the task line's 'never printed, never on a command line, never in a config' for the GM's private repository.

decisions.summary: A shell script beside sync-with-main.sh and land-tooling.sh, not a gate crate; the answers' merge reused from the gate
decisions.why: A choice of implementation form. Not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: Only record-checks and l7r-events are added to the mirror's index; handoffs and caches stay out
decisions.why: Matches the GM's 'for the record-check answers and event logs' and the task line's exclusion.

decisions.summary: Found and left, not a defect: a grown log's last segment is sent whole (no thin-pack delta base), about 125 KB for a 7 KB diff
decisions.why: A size cost, measured with its method. There is no wrong outcome: the push is detached and every line still arrives.

decisions.summary: keep-both only for tasks.md hunks with empty base whose added lines are list lines, and plan-review.json via plan::merge_files; rewrites of one line or added prose stop
decisions.why: Nothing in the GM's request or spec asks for automatic conflict resolution at all; the narrower rule stops where keeping both sides would produce two versions of one task line (a wrong outcome), and a stop prints the next command, so nothing is lost. The 2026-11-26 conflict's shape is covered and pinned.

decisions.summary: make carry carries one commit; several are carried one COMMIT= at a time, oldest first
decisions.why: No loss of function: every commit can still be carried, and a hand-picked range left paused is refused by D1 (sequencer/todo).

decisions.summary: the history guard lets `git rebase --abort` through (exact form only); every other rebase form still refused
decisions.why: Loosens an existing guard by one exact command that rewrites no history (it restores the branch to where the rebase began), so constitution VI is untouched; without it D1 would print a command no session can run, and a refusal must name a compliant command. Its reach is no wider than that command.

decisions.summary: the audit register's check counts refusals in land/unfinished.rs beside land/cheap.rs; the entry's covers: lines name them
decisions.why: Enforces the GM's audit register words (2026-11-25: document each process with its measurements and falsifier) on this refusal, which the check otherwise missed; enforcement of what was asked, not new scope.

blocks: ### T285 (2026-11-26: the coordinating session made each builder a fresh worktree by hand and deleted it and its build cache after the landing, against the reused-worktrees rule of `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once" - a cold tree's first closing checks took 14-30 minutes against about a minute warm, measured 2026-11-26 (the day's closing-checks runs, that entry's figures))
### T285 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The pool is a registry in the clone's common git directory (.git/builder-pool.json) with an event log beside it; membership is the registry, never a name's shape; new trees are <clone>-b<N>.
decisions.why: Bookkeeping a pool needs so the tooling, not the session, owns builder trees: serves the GM's reuse of the build cache (request.md 2026-11-22) and real enforcement (2026-11-19).

decisions.summary: make builder-tree hands out the task's held tree, else the first free tree brought to HEAD, else one cold tree made under the cap with its guard binary prebuilt (1800 s GUESS knob, L7R_BUILDER_GUARD_SECS), said to be COLD.
decisions.why: The handout is the mechanism of reuse; making a new tree only when none is free, and saying so, is the request's reuse, not a narrowing of it.

decisions.summary: A free tree holding uncommitted paths whose content is not HEAD's is refused (paths named), with DISCARD=<reason> to take it over; the tool never passes such a tree over for a new cold one; paths identical to HEAD (landed work) are no hold.
decisions.why: Refusing rather than making a cold tree keeps the outcome the task exists for; the escape is the project's reasoned-escape form. Nothing in it narrows reuse.

decisions.summary: make builder-tree-release and make land's post-step free the tree, leave it and its cache in place, bring it to HEAD where nothing holds it; the release never fails a landing.
decisions.why: Freeing without deleting is the reuse asked for; a release that cannot fail a landing protects the landing and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: make land-batch has none of make land's post-steps and releases no tree; its trees are freed only by a hand make builder-tree-release.
decisions.why: The block never says take treats a tree held by an already-landed task as free, so after a land-batch every builder tree stays held and the next handout makes a COLD tree (under the cap) or is refused (at it) - the wrong outcome the task exists to end, the block's own D3 reasoning ('the cold tree is the failure the task exists to end, so the tool refuses rather than hide it') here inverted. The only reason given is that land-batch has no post-steps today, which is consistency with existing code and does not carry an exception; a hand release step is an instruction, not the real enforcement the GM asked for on 2026-11-19. What must hold: a tree whose holding tasks have landed by any landing path is free at the next handout without a hand step (land-batch releases as land does, or take frees a tree whose holders are landed), pinned by a test on the land-batch path.

decisions.summary: make builder-trees lists trees, holders, ages, cache sizes; builder-tree-drop is the one removal (reason required, held tree refused); builder-tree-adopt joins a pre-pool worktree under its own name.
decisions.why: Visibility and a single logged removal path are the enforcement of reuse; adoption brings the existing warm trees in.

decisions.id: D6 adopt by name, not rename
decisions.summary: The three trees of 2026-11-26 are adopted under their own names because a measured rename rebuilt every workspace crate (66.5 s / 41.7 s against 0.11 s / 0.08 s warm).
decisions.why: Decided by measurement in favor of keeping caches warm, which is the request's purpose; naming is not something the request settles.

decisions.summary: builder_pool::CAP = 4 (L7R_BUILDER_POOL), a GUESS knob; at the cap a handout is refused naming each holder.
decisions.why: A bound on standing caches answers the GM's disk words (2026-11-22 'clean up after ourselves', 2026-11-25 T245) beside reuse; it is a labeled knob set at the largest count ever run, and the count worth running is left to T284's measurement.

decisions.summary: A guard refuses git worktree add under <mirror>/.clones/, git worktree remove or move of a pool tree, and rm of a pool tree, its cache or a directory holding either; BUILDER_TREE_OK with a reason escapes; the tooling's own trees are exempt by call site (inside scripts), not by name.
decisions.why: This is the real enforcement the GM asked for (2026-11-19) of reusing worktrees: it refuses exactly the hand forms of the incident in the task header. Refusing move is justified by the measured rename chill.

decisions.summary: The shared walk reads git only by bare name, so a path-qualified git passes this guard as it passes every tree guard.
decisions.why: The failure in the task header is hand git worktree commands in their ordinary bare form, which the guard refuses; nothing in the bundle shows a path-qualified git in use, so this leaves no observed wrong outcome. It is the shared walk's limit across every tree guard, not a narrowing of this task's reach.

decisions.id: D9b cp -a / git clone not read
decisions.summary: A tree under the clones directory made by cp -a or git clone is not a worktree and is not read by the guard.
decisions.why: Not the hand form of the incident (fresh worktrees by git worktree add); nothing in the bundle shows those forms used for builder trees.

decisions.id: D9c cache budget may evict pool trees
decisions.summary: The cache budget's eviction (scratch_sweep_hooks/sweep/evict.rs, 100 GB knob L7R_CACHE_BUDGET_GB) may still evict an idle pool tree's profiles past the budget; the cache was observed over 150 GB on 2026-11-26; the budget is left unchanged as 'the GM's T245 rule'.
decisions.why: The block's own goal (Approach item 1) is a builder starting warm 'every time'; with the cache measured at over 150 GB against a 100 GB budget, the sweep is past its budget now, and idle pool trees - every free tree between builders - are what it evicts, so a free tree can be handed out with an emptied cache: the cold builder the task exists to end, left in place and not listed under 'Found and left?' (which reads 'none'; FR-009). The justification fails at its seam: the GM's T245 words (request.md 2026-11-25) ask for an audit of disk use and an automatic trigger below a free-space percentage; 'idle trees' targets evicted past the budget' is in the parenthesis marked as the coordinating session's build, not his words, and the 100 GB is a knob. His 2026-11-22 words ask for both cleanup and reuse of the build cache. What must hold: a free pool tree is not handed out cold because of the budget sweep - the plan decides how the budget and the pool coexist (for instance the sweep evicts other caches or profiles before a pool tree's, or the budget is re-set with a measurement), or, if the two asks truly cannot both hold, the conflict goes to the round arbiter rather than being accepted as a limit.

decisions.summary: A new cold tree's cache is not seeded from a warm one.
decisions.why: Seeding is an optimization nobody asked for, and the block's rename measurement indicates a moved cache rebuilds anyway; a cold tree is made only when no tree is free and under the cap.

### T285 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Pool membership is a registry at <clone>/.git/builder-pool.json with an event log beside it; new trees are <clones>/<clone>-b<N>.
decisions.why: This is how the tool knows which trees to reuse. It is the mechanism the GM asked for ('tooling ... automatically enforces and performs the correct behavior'), and nothing in it narrows that.

decisions.summary: make builder-tree hands out the tree the task already holds, else the first free tree brought to HEAD, else one new cold tree while under the cap; at the cap it refuses and names each holder.
decisions.why: Reuse comes first and a cold tree is made only when every tree is held. That is the reused-worktrees rule performed by the tool. A refusal at the cap creates no cold tree.

decisions.summary: A new cold tree has its guard binary built before handout, limit 1800 s (GUESS knob L7R_BUILDER_GUARD_SECS), not the wrapper's 45 s.
decisions.why: This is an implementation detail of making the one cold tree the pool allows. It narrows nothing that was asked, and the knob is labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: A free tree with uncommitted paths whose content is not HEAD's is refused for handout and names those paths. DISCARD=<reason> takes it over. Such a tree is never passed over for a new cold one.
decisions.why: It forbids exactly the outcome T285 exists to end, a cold tree made past a reusable one. The cost is a refusal plus one hand step, not a route to a fresh tree. The block says plainly that this was the builder's decision.

decisions.summary: Release frees the tree and leaves the tree and its cache in place. make land and make land-batch call 'landed' after a landing, and a failed release never fails the landing.
decisions.why: This is the second half of the GM's correct behavior: no tree or cache is deleted after a landing. If a release does not run, D6 frees the tree at the next handout, so the safety net does not make a cold tree.

decisions.summary: At every handout, a tree whose every holding task is ticked in tasks.md or archived in tasks-done.md is freed first, so a hand tick or a skipped release owes no hand step.
decisions.why: It closes the route by which a landing that skipped make land would leave a tree held and force a cold one. That is 'automatically ... performs the correct behavior'.

decisions.summary: 'A hold that names no feature is read by nothing there and waits for its release.' F= is optional on make builder-tree and on make builder-tree-adopt, so such holds arise from the pool's own advertised forms.
decisions.why: This is a carve-out from D6's own promise that 'no hand step is owed', and the block gives no reason for it. It leaves a route to the exact failure the GM named. A builder takes a tree with T= and no F=. Its task is then ticked by hand, or its landing's release does not run. The tree stays held for good, and the next take makes a new COLD tree while a reusable one sits idle. That is a wrong outcome (a cold builder, the tool answering wrongly), not a mere difference. Following the rule here is not physically impossible, the GM's words do not imply the exception, and following it does not defeat the request. Fix: make F= required on take and adopt (or derive it from the task's line in the clone's tasks.md, refusing when it cannot be found), so every hold is one D6's sweep reads. Pin the hand-tick case for that form in the any-route test.

decisions.summary: The three trees of 2026-11-26 (-t269, -t270, -t271) are adopted under their own names, because a measured rename rebuilt every workspace crate (66.5 s and 41.7 s against 0.11 s and 0.08 s warm).
decisions.why: Renaming would chill the caches, which is the failure being fixed. Membership is by registry, not by name shape, so the old names are full pool members. The figures carry a date and a method.

decisions.summary: CAP = 4 (L7R_BUILDER_POOL), a GUESS read from the sizing rule. The count worth running is left to T284 to measure.
decisions.why: A cap refuses past it and creates no cold tree. The number is labeled GUESS and its measurement is assigned to the task that owns it.

decisions.summary: The guard refuses git worktree add under <mirror>/.clones/, git worktree remove or move of a pool tree, and rm of a pool tree, its cache, or a directory holding either. Each refusal names the pool's command, and BUILDER_TREE_OK with a reason escapes.
decisions.why: This is the 'enforces ... without the opportunity for this kind of mistake' half. It refuses exactly the hand forms of 2026-11-26: a fresh tree made by hand, and a tree and cache deleted after a landing. move is refused because the measurement shows it chills the cache just as a removal does. The escape follows the project's guard rules.

decisions.id: D9a tooling exempt by call site
decisions.summary: land-alone.sh, land-tooling.sh, review-tree.sh and the pool tool call git inside a program, so the hook never sees those calls. A hand 'git worktree add .../<clone>-land' is refused like any other, and the suite pins both cases.
decisions.why: The exemption is by call site, not by name, so no hand form escapes through a tooling tree's name. The call-site census states its search space (a grep of 'worktree add' over scripts/ and rust/).

decisions.summary: Refusal (a) reads only worktree-add targets under <mirror>/.clones/. Scratch worktrees elsewhere pass.
decisions.why: The trees the process rule and the pool define as builder trees live under the clones directory, and that is where the 2026-11-26 mistake was made. A worktree elsewhere is a scratch tree, not a builder tree made by mistake. Reaching one would mean a session relocating its tree after a refusal had named the pool, which is the same class as the recorded escape, not the inadvertent mistake the GM named. Recorded so a later round can check it: the dispatch and the brief are what put builders in pool trees, and nothing in this block checks a builder's tree outside .clones/.

decisions.summary: The shared walk reads git only by its bare name, so '/usr/bin/git worktree add ...' passes.
decisions.why: Not ruled as a legitimate exception: the block's stated reason, that every tree guard behaves this way, is consistency with existing code and could not legitimate a narrowing. It is within because it is not a route the GM's 'this kind of mistake' takes. The mistake was a session using the ordinary form, which is refused and pointed at the pool. Spelling out a path-qualified git is a deliberate bypass of the same class as the escape. A PreToolUse hook cannot see git called from inside a program anyway.

decisions.summary: A tree under the clones directory made by cp -a or git clone is not read.
decisions.why: The GM's words are 'whatever tooling we use to create worktrees'. A copy or a clone is not a worktree and is not how builder trees were or are made, so the request does not reach it.

decisions.summary: A new cold tree's cache is not seeded from a warm one.
decisions.why: Seeding is an optimization the request does not ask for. The request is that existing trees be reused and not deleted, and the pool makes a new tree only when every tree is held.

decisions.summary: The cache budget's eviction (evict.rs choose) skips a registered pool tree's build directory. The pool's share is bounded by cap x tree cache (about 40 GB, a GUESS from three measured sizes), shown by make builder-trees and returned by make builder-tree-drop.
decisions.why: It narrows T245's budget, which holds every build directory. Two grounds legitimate it. First, applying the budget literally would defeat this request's purpose, as the block shows concretely: the cache was over its 100 GB budget at over 150 GB, a free pool tree ranks idle, so the sweep would empty it between builders and the next handout would be cold while called warm. Second, the GM's own words of 2026-11-22 imply it ('your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken'). His concern then, space eaten 'without us realizing it', is answered by a bounded share that is priced, listed and reclaimable. Not confirmed from the block: whether T245's low-free-space automatic eviction also goes through choose and so skips pool trees, and whether make disk-audit names the pool's share. Neither blocks this ruling.

### T285 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A clone's builder trees are a pool recorded in <clone>/.git/builder-pool.json with a log beside it; membership is the registry, never a name's shape; new trees are <clone>-b<N>.
decisions.why: The GM asked that the tooling that creates worktrees perform the correct behavior, which is reused worktrees. A registry the tool hands trees out of is that mechanism.

decisions.summary: make builder-tree hands out the task's own tree, else the first free tree brought to HEAD, else makes one cold tree under the cap with its guard binary prebuilt (1800 s GUESS knob).
decisions.why: This is reuse performed automatically. A cold tree is made only when no tree exists to reuse, and the tool says it is cold.

decisions.summary: A free tree holding uncommitted content that is not HEAD's is refused with each path named. DISCARD=<reason> takes it over, logged. The tool never makes a cold tree past such a tree.
decisions.why: The request settles nothing about leftover edits, and this narrows nothing in it. Refusing rather than making a cold tree past the held one keeps reuse, which is the request's purpose. The other choices, silently destroying work or silently making a cold tree, would each be worse against the request. The extra step is an implementation cost, which is not a fidelity matter.

decisions.id: D4 release, land and freeing by any route
decisions.summary: release and make land/land-batch free the tree and keep it and its cache. The release never fails a landing. At every handout a tree whose tasks are all ticked or archived is freed. A hold with no feature is refused.
decisions.why: This is the 'performs the correct behavior' half: the tree and cache survive the landing with no hand step. The feature-required refusal exists only so that the freeing step can read every hold.

decisions.summary: make builder-trees lists the pool. builder-tree-drop is the one removal: it needs a two-word reason, refuses a held tree and is logged. builder-tree-adopt joins pre-pool trees (the landing, tooling and review trees refused).
decisions.why: The drop is the form nearest the original mistake. It is not on the landing path, refuses a held tree and needs a recorded reason, which is the project's escape convention. The GM's disk words of 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-25 need some way to give space back. Deleting after every landing now takes a deliberate, logged act, not a habit.

decisions.summary: The three 2026-11-26 trees are adopted under their own names, not renamed, because a rename was measured as cold (66.5 s and 41.7 s against 0.11 s and 0.08 s warm).
decisions.why: Renaming would chill the caches the request exists to keep warm. Membership is by registry, so the names do not matter.

decisions.summary: CAP = 4 (L7R_BUILDER_POOL), GUESS. At the cap a new tree is refused and each holder is named.
decisions.why: The cap bounds how many trees are made. It narrows no reuse, and it is labeled GUESS with its source.

decisions.id: D8 guard scope and tooling exemption by call site
decisions.summary: The guard refuses a hand git worktree add under .clones/, a worktree remove or move of a pool tree, and an rm of a pool tree, its cache or a parent of either. BUILDER_TREE_OK takes a reason. The tooling's own git calls are inside programs and so are never seen. A hand add of a -land tree is refused.
decisions.why: This is the 'enforces' half, aimed at the exact forms of the mistake (hand creation, hand deletion of tree and cache). Refusing move is justified by the rename measurement. The exemption is structural, not a named carve-out, and a hand form of the tooling's paths is still refused.

decisions.id: D9a absolute-path git passes the guard
decisions.summary: 'Limits accepted': the shared walk reads git only by its bare name, so /usr/bin/git worktree add under .clones/ passes. This was observed in the guard's test and the case was removed from the test. 'Found and left?' says none.
decisions.why: A builder tree made by hand under .clones/ is the GM's 'this kind of mistake' however git is spelled: it is just as cold, and the request is 'without the opportunity'. The reason given, that every tree guard shares the limit, is consistency with existing code, which is not a ground. It is not impossible (matching git by its basename in the walk is plainly doable). The GM's words do not imply it. Covering it would not defeat the request's purpose. The section also observed the guard passing this form (a check that passes bad work, a defect), deleted the test case that showed it, and records 'Found and left? none', so the defect is left without FR-009's why, filed task id and order. To clear it, preferably fix the walk (or the guard) so a path-qualified git is read and pin the case back in the suite. Otherwise carry it under 'Found and left?' as FR-009 requires: why it is not fixed here, a filed task id and 'lands before ...'.

decisions.id: D9b cp -a and git clone not read
decisions.summary: A tree under .clones/ made by cp -a or git clone is not a worktree and is not read by the guard.
decisions.why: The request is about the tooling that creates worktrees, and the mistake was a worktree. git clone under .clones/ is how clones themselves are made, so refusing it would block legitimate work. This is outside the request, not carved out of it.

decisions.id: D9c new cold tree's cache not seeded
decisions.summary: A newly made tree's build cache is not copied from a warm one.
decisions.why: Seeding was not asked for. The block's own rename measurement (fingerprints hold the absolute path) shows a copied cache would not be warm, so leaving it out loses nothing the request asked for.

decisions.id: D10 the cache budget never evicts a pool tree's build directory
decisions.summary: The sweep's choose skips a build directory named for a registered pool tree. The pool's share is bounded by cap times tree cache (about 40 GB GUESS, 174 GB free) and is given back only by builder-tree-drop.
decisions.why: This narrows T245's cache budget, whose 100 GB and idle-tree eviction are the session's design, not the GM's words. Applying the budget literally would defeat T285's purpose: it would empty each free pool tree between builders, so the next handout would be cold while called warm. The GM's own words of 2026-11-22 ('your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken') support keeping the cache. His 'without us realizing it' still holds because the pool's share is bounded and visible in make builder-trees. Aside: the block does not say whether the low-free-space trigger shares choose. If it does, the pool is exempt there too, which is the same reasoning but worth one sentence in the block.

The clones directory is where every builder tree lives (the pool's own trees, the hand trees of the mistake, -t269/-t270/-t271), so under it the guard reaches exactly the mistake's class. A worktree elsewhere is a scratch tree whose correct behavior is to be made and removed; refusing it would reach work the GM did not ask to stop (UNREQUESTED reach), and a hook cannot tell a scratch tree from a builder's except by where it lands. Taking the bound literally away would defeat no part of the request's purpose that the pool does not already serve.

decisions.id: L1 cp -a into the clones directory
decisions.summary: a tree under the clones directory made by `cp -a` is not a worktree and not read (limit accepted)
decisions.why: Same test as D8a: under the clones directory any tree made by hand is a builder tree of the mistake's class, whatever command made it. 'Not a worktree' is the word-level argument; the purpose ('without the opportunity for this kind of mistake') is that no builder starts in a hand-made cold tree, and a copied tree is cold (the cache is keyed by the tree's name; D6 measured that a moved tree is not warm). The block's own goal (part A item 1, 'the only way to get a builder's tree is the pool') is contradicted by it. None of the three tests is met: it is not impossible to read a cp whose destination is a new directory directly under <mirror>/.clones/, nothing in the request implies it, and the literal reading defeats no stated purpose. A guard that passes bad work is a defect: either refuse it in T285 (same escape, red first), or carry it under 'Found and left?' with a filed task and its order, as T295 is carried.

decisions.id: L2 git clone into the clones directory
decisions.summary: a tree under the clones directory made by `git clone` is not a worktree and not read (limit accepted)
decisions.why: Judged on its own: a `git clone` to <mirror>/.clones/<name> handed to a builder is a fresh, cold, hand-made builder tree in the place builder trees live, which is the mistake the GM asked to have no opportunity for; the registry would not even hold it. The exemption rests on the word 'worktree', not on the request's purpose, and is not impossible to guard (a clone's destination under the clones directory is read from the command like a worktree's). decisions.summary: A slot is the flock of a file slot-<i> under ~/.cache/l7r-build-slots/, signed with its holder, freed when the holder dies; no daemon
decisions.why: This is the synchronization the GM asked for in place of a builder cap.

decisions.summary: L7R_BUILD_SLOTS, default 2, labeled GUESS; it caps compiling cargo calls at once, not builders; 0 means no slot
decisions.why: It caps coinciding compiles, not builders. Extra builders edit, test and run coverage freely and queue only where their compile would coincide, which is the opposite of 'pre-emptively limiting builders'. The 0 switch only turns the mechanism off.

decisions.summary: Poll every 0.5 s (GUESS); a waiter says it waits each minute, naming the holders
decisions.why: These are mechanism parameters, and the waiter's notice makes a wait visible.

decisions.summary: A cargo started by a holder carries L7R_BUILD_SLOT_HELD and a gate run under it takes no slot
decisions.why: Holding a slot for a nested run is physically impossible without deadlock: the inner run would wait on the slot its own parent cargo test holds. Its compiles already sit inside the parent's slot, so nothing goes unsynchronized.

decisions.summary: A slot directory that cannot be made, a slot file that cannot be opened or a flock that cannot start lets the call run without a slot, said on stderr
decisions.why: Synchronization is physically impossible when the lock cannot be had at all. Refusing would turn a throughput control into a red gate, and waiting would hang every tree. A caveat: the block writes the code-1 slot-wait line for a wait that ended without a slot, so a call that fell open with no wait may show only on stderr. Writing that line here too would let the audit's one-a-week reopening see it.

decisions.summary: A waiter past L7R_BUILD_SLOT_CEILING (900 s, GUESS) runs without a slot, said on stderr and written as a slot-wait line of code 1; dev/audits/build-slot.md reopens the count on one such line in a week
decisions.why: In the hung-holder case the block names, holding the rule literally defeats the request's purpose: one hung cargo would stop every tree's checks for good, which is worse than the builder cap the slot replaces. Rejected alternatives were priced: wait without end, or refuse as the run lock does. The block's sentence 'a waiter passes it only when both slots stay held for 900 s on end, which is two holders each longer than the longest compile measured' overclaims, and the claim is unmeasured. Waiters are not served in arrival order. Each 0.5 s poller races the others, and a tree that releases a slot and starts its next compiling cargo call at once tries again immediately. So under sustained contention (four or more builders, cold trees) a turning-over queue can keep one waiter out for 900 s with no holder hung. This is not ruled a defect: such a pass yields one extra compile, three at once, the measured peak level, with no wrong outcome; it is recorded as code 1 and reopens the count. The sentence should be restated to say so. Counting the ceiling only while the slots' holder signatures stay unchanged would confine the pass to a hung holder; that is offered as an option, not required.

decisions.summary: The task line's fourth case (the guard-messages store) is left to 451 T281's builder; T295 does three jobs, and goes wider than the line where the same spelling defect sits in other readers (history guard, make detector, ledger, conflict-marker, gate-write, gm-tree).
decisions.why: No GM words name T295; the task line is the coordinating session's. Handing the guard-messages case to T281's builder is, on the block's own claim (not verified here: the bundle holds no T281 text), an assignment to the task that owns it rather than a defect left unowned; widening a defect fix to every reader with the same defect is what fix-as-we-go asks.

decisions.summary: One shared reader (spelled.rs) names a program by its command word's last path part, past a backslash, quotes, VAR= words and wrappers with their options; the name compared whole; command -v/-V and VAR=/path/git are not runs of the program.
decisions.why: Ends a guard passing bad work (a git by its path or behind a wrapper ran past builder-pool and the history guard), which is the 2026-11-19 'real enforcement and not just instructions' and a defect under XIV; reading invocations and not mentions keeps the project's rule.

decisions.summary: gm-tree's git exemption now also covers a git behind A=1 or timeout 5, which the old first-three-letters test refused.
decisions.why: The exemption is for git commands; refusing the same git command because of how its command word is spelled is a check refusing good work, a defect. It does not open any non-git command.

decisions.summary: The one make detector (make.rs, invoked) reads make by its path, a backslash, or behind command/exec/builtin/sudo (with options, and a wrapper by its path); /tmp/mymake and the like stay other programs.

decisions.summary: Readers that exempt a git command or rule no tree write (claims-file, parked.rs git mv, phase-source, house-style, shell-check) are not changed here; filed in T306, ordered before T302.
decisions.why: None is a tree guard passing a tree write; where an exemption misses a spelling the effect is an extra refusal of a rare spelling. Filed in T306 with an order before T302 (the block's 'lands before T302'), which meets FR-009's why, id and order and fix-as-we-go's 'fixed before the next step', while T306 keeps that order.

decisions.summary: A program run by another (xargs git worktree add, sh -c 'git push -f') is read by no guard of the walk. Filed as T306, lands before T302.
decisions.why: 'Outside three jobs' is not by itself a ground. The ground is that the GM's words and the accepted spec allow a defect to be deferred with a why, a task id and an order (FR-009; fix-as-we-go's 'fixed before the next step's port begins'): the block gives the why (the walk would read another program's argument as a command, a change to what every walk guard sees), names T306 and orders it before T302. decisions.summary: A quoted "git" passes the history guard and discard, two guards T295 itself edits; their quote blanking runs before the pattern. Filed as T306, lands before T302.
decisions.why: This is D1's own class left in guards this task edits, so it is the weakest of the deferrals, and the block's goal and the test names ('however it is spelled') overstate what those two guards now read. Holds only while T306 lands before T302.

decisions.summary: cargo by its path or behind command, exec, sudo or builtin passes make-only and no-poll (FR-008's cargo refusal), their own patterns. Filed as T306, lands before T302.

decisions.summary: A name the shell builds ($GIT, g\it) is read by no guard; T306 may only document it in docs/guards.md as a limit. Filed as T306, lands before T302.
decisions.why: The ground is impossibility, not scheduling: a static reader of the command text cannot know what $GIT expands to without running the shell. Saying so in docs/guards.md, as T306 is to, is the honest answer.
