decisions.why: FR-007 requires the refusal to name the crate-scoped checks for the task's crates, so the crate list is required, not optional; the GM's 2026-11-23 hook-length words ask for fewer tokens with no loss of fidelity, which keeping the shortened measured words honors; FR-012's two-word escape is met. decisions.summary: Found-and-left items outside the task's subject: pool trees lacking the magistracy sheets (T159), a land test failing once under load (T304), the per-task bundle path shared between clone and builder tree (T288); each with why, task id and order before T302.
decisions.why: Defects in other crates or in make decide's bundle key, not part of what T295 fixes; each is filed and ordered before T302, which satisfies fix-as-we-go and FR-009's three parts. T288's case does not make D3 worse than before: a bundle rebuilt from the clone moves the hold to the clone, which was the old behavior.

### T309 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The cause is put down to the clock: three fixture transcripts are written in one coarse tick, so the sort ties some of the time. The task line had guessed the live transcripts.
decisions.why: The diagnosis is measured (probe 41 of 41, ties in 300 of 300 rounds, red every run once the times are set apart). Fixing the flaky gate verdict the task names is exactly the defect at hand.

decisions.why: This makes the gate's coverage verdict repeatable, which is the task. Keeping the tie-break or cutting it is a design choice, not a fidelity question. The test claims no more than it shows.

decisions.summary: In a test build, transcripts_base and marks::reply_in read the fixture's TRANSCRIPTS or the empty path, never ~/.claude/projects. The binary is unchanged.
decisions.why: This closes the crate's tests to machine state, the same class of nondeterminism as the red. No behavior of the shipped binary changes.

decisions.summary: close_in(root, args) carries the work. The test runs it on a scratch tree, with GUARD_LOG_DIR set to the test binary's own directory.
decisions.why: It fixes a found defect: a test reading the live tree's check state and writing CHECK_CLOSED escapes to the live guard log. That breaks the standing rule that a test's guard log is never the live one (451 T94/T207).

decisions.id: D5 not changed: two cli wrapper calls
decisions.summary: arbiter::cli(['bogus']) and cli(['bundle','--check-ask','x']) still run on the process's directory and environment.
decisions.why: Both answer before reading a file. The empty-HOME run shows nothing read or written, so no wrong outcome is left.

decisions.summary: Green is builder-checks plus a clean cover run on the live HOME and an empty one. Red is set down and ruled through arbiter-ask. Budget is one landing. Not performance work.
decisions.why: These are the task's own exits and classification. Nothing narrows what was asked.

decisions.id: D7 the 2,229 test-written guard-log entries left
decisions.summary: The section heads 'Found and left?' with 'none', then leaves the 2,229 CHECK_CLOSED 'nothing to close here' entries the test already wrote to ~/.claude/guard-log, because 'nothing here deletes from the live log'.
decisions.why: This rests on the plan's own step 12, which says make audit and make guard-log GUARD=checks count these entries as escapes. By the plan's own words, then, those tools report about 2,229 escapes that no session made. That is a tool answering wrongly, a defect, not a mere difference. The figures SC-005/SC-006 read off the escape log depend on those counts. Fixing it is not physically impossible. Nothing in request.md or the spec carves out the guard log. Fixing it would not defeat the task's purpose. 'Nothing here deletes from the live log' describes the task's reach; it is not a reason. FR-009 lets a deferred defect stand only with the reason it is not fixed here, a filed task id and its order ('lands before ...'), and the section gives none of the three. It also labels the item 'none', which hides it from that check. The section must either remedy the 2,229 entries' effect on those counts in this task, or record it as a found-and-left defect with all three of FR-009's parts.

decisions.summary: no command that reads a builder's report; the builder files what it finds itself with the existing make task-add, at the find
decisions.why: The report-reading command is the task line's design, not the GM's: no GM words in request.md and no requirement in spec-index.md name a command over a report or candidates file (grepped for candidate/report/file). The replacement serves the task's purpose more fully - an id exists before the plan section, which FR-009's deferral refusal needs in round 1 - and leaves nothing the task line asked for undone; a refused filing is reported as NOT filed with the refusal, not dropped.

decisions.summary: make task-add unchanged; the cross-tree id allotment (451 T255's shared task-ids.txt under the common-dir flock) measured already safe, the test kept as the record
decisions.why: The brief asked for the allotment to be safe across trees; it was measured (2026-11-26, a new test, green on the old code) and the existing mechanism kept. Nothing asked for is left out.

decisions.summary: make carry keeps both sides' additions by block: tasks.md blocks (a list line with its continuations) kept ours-then-theirs, plan.md whole ### T<n> sections kept, a section written differently by both sides stops
decisions.why: A defect found in this task (a second tree's filed task stopped on plan.md, or lost its research line) that the approach cannot work without; fixed here, red-first on each fault, T292's stop-on-the-rest kept. Fixing a found defect in the task is what the project's rules ask.

decisions.summary: the brief and report-format words: FILE what you find, CANDIDATES as filed: T<n> or NOT filed: <refusal>, the 'do not file tasks' brief instruction withdrawn in the brief file; no guard change
decisions.why: Words that carry Decision 1; the absence of the instruction in the repository and of any guard refusing a builder's task-add are labeled observations with their method. The GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions' (2026-11-19) was said of the six approved improvements and four data ideas, not this task, and the mechanical backstop for the costly case (a deferral with no filed id) is FR-009's existing make decide refusal.

decisions.summary: nothing found and left; the carry's line-by-line fault fixed here
decisions.why: The NOT filed path is a runtime outcome of a future builder's report, not an item this task finds and leaves.

decisions.summary: the task is classed not performance work because 'no check, gate, engine or landing runs faster', although it removes a filing by hand and blocked plan-review rounds
decisions.why: The plan's test (a tool runs faster) is narrower than the GM's. On 2026-11-19 he approved six improvements 'ranked by minutes they'd have saved', item 4 being 'Fewer plan re-rounds: about 10 min', which makes no tool faster; on 2026-11-20 he asked to 'prioritize those remaining improvement fixes ... doing those first makes everything after them faster' and 'in general priotitize performance improvements going forward', and counted measurement work as performance 'even if the task itself doesn't improve performance'. The plan's reading would exclude his own approved item 4; T289's stated payoff (six round-1 BLOCKs and four unfiled candidates in one day, removed) is of exactly that class. FR-013's full definition is cut at [...] in this bundle and was not read; if it defines performance work as only a faster tool, that definition is itself narrower than these words. Fix: answer yes, as process-time work that removes re-rounds and hand filing, and carry what FR-013 and the register (451 T259) owe such work.

decisions.why: The GM asked for 'the test that fails under load being fixed'; when the failing case is unknowable, fixing each case reproduced red under load is the request itself, not an addition.

decisions.summary: Case 6's run holds the lock while a gate file stands, released only once two timers have logged the deferral and the winner has started; the check asks 2 deferrals instead of 1; record waits 12 s to 90 s upper bounds; the sleep 0.3 before the overlap check removed; stand-in sleeps 0.3 s after the gate.
decisions.why: Replaces a timing-dependent contention (red 8 of 8 under a 1.0 s stall on HEAD) with a condition, which is the fix asked for; the assertion is strengthened, not weakened, and the case still goes red on a guard that takes no lock (measured).

decisions.why: Same defect class as the task line's (a test whose subject depends on ignored files on disk), found by the census the task asked for; making a check's subject independent of the tree is the fix itself, not unrequested scope. Test-only.

decisions.summary: page/held.rs (a cfg(test) module): outcomes takes (path, text) and reads no sheet; the path still names the page and finds its notes.
decisions.why: The mechanism the end-to-end fix needs; test-only, no drawn or shipped behavior changes.

decisions.why: Not a narrowing of 451's request or spec, neither of which carries 449 FR-008; weighed against it anyway: a fixture cannot see a spec change (the plan's red-on-a-real-defect run shows the old disk-reading test could not), a skip drops the check, and reading the disk is the defect, so composing is the only form that keeps the check doing its job and obeys 449 T211/T252; the crate's standing composing tests stand at 0.27 s and 0.40 s under the same load, and the timings were taken at load ~250 with no quiet-machine figure, so the over-the-bar state is not established. A test some tenths of a second slower is not a wrong outcome (constitution XIV's defect definition), so nothing known is left.

### T304 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: make carry treats a failed pick or failed --continue that leaves CHERRY_PICK_HEAD with nothing unmerged and nothing staged as an empty pick: git cherry-pick --skip, then the END verification (nothing in progress/unmerged/staged, non-spec files in HEAD), exit 0. A pick that never started, or a continue a hook refused, still stops.
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome (a second carry of a carried commit stopped with a pick standing, which make land refuses), as constitution XIV and fix-as-we-go require. The carry still ends verified, never assumed (T292); the stop cases that hold real unfinished work are kept and pinned. Nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The clean-carry test ends at its first carry; three tests replace its second half (the clone given its own commit so the pick sha differs; history reached by fast-forward; the kept-equal-ours continue door), red first with skipped_empty off.
decisions.why: Makes the test exercise the case that happens in a real clone rather than the same-second sha collision; enforcement of the fix, not new scope.

decisions.id: D3 GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 on every asked program
decisions.summary: shared::tool's three askers start their program through command, which sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 for every program a guard asks (git and the scripts/gate it runs, which inherit it); locks a command needs are still taken. The per-call --no-optional-locks flag was priced and rejected because it reaches neither the scripts nor the gate.
decisions.why: Carries the brief's instruction (make the hooks' read-only git calls take no optional locks) at the one place every such call passes through. Reaching the scripts and gate a guard asks is reaching the hooks' own calls by the route they take, not a new behavior: only optional locks are dropped, the cost (a stale entry re-read by each such status) is stated.

decisions.id: D4 direct git spawns read and left
decisions.summary: The guard crates' direct Command::new("git") calls (rev-parse, for-each-ref, worktree remove, a tree-to-tree diff, a suite tool's own tree) are left, none refreshing an index.
decisions.why: None of the listed verbs writes an index refresh, so leaving them leaves no part of the lock fix undone. (Its count is noted in the report: the sentence says five calls and lists six files and about eight verbs.)

decisions.summary: The hooks-test suite stamps, gate-green-<area> stamps and semantic-id-cache-2.json (single-valued in the common git dir, overwritten by every worktree; a suite reruns though its tree last passed) are left to a later builder as T304's remainder, before T302; this landing does not tick T304.
decisions.why: Not dropped: the work stays in T304, which this landing does not tick, ordered before T302 with why it is not fixed here (FR-009's three parts). Its visible effect is reruns (time), not a false pass, and it is to be measured before it changes.

decisions.id: D6 guards' git diff lock left as remainder
decisions.summary: The guards' git diff calls against a work tree (delta_crates, changed_lines, stages_ledger, conflict_marker_hooks) still take index.lock where a stale entry stands (142 of 200 with the variable); left as T304's remainder, lands before T302.

The unmeasured premise that none reaches the session clone from a builder's tree carries nothing here and must not be used to tick T304 without that measurement or the fix.

decisions.summary: Lands before T302; builder-checks for the two crates green in the builder's tree; full gate and coverage at landing; red recorded and set down, a can't-be-done claim through make arbiter-ask.

blocks: ### T298 (the task line's count, observed 2026-11-26, method: the day's report as the coordinating session read it: a day's task time report was 2,294 lines in 38 per-task tables with no table of the window, the GM had to remember the period to ask for, and a batch landing's gate was booked to whichever of its tasks the mark or the command line named)
### T298 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The report opens with one table of the window (minutes, blocking, each as a percentage of the working time) and one line per landed task; builder minutes are the builder's event-log span.
decisions.why: This is how the report is laid out. It keeps T243's percentages of working time ((i)) and the breakdown the GM asked for. The table and the lines are the coordinating session's task-line words, and they narrow nothing he asked.

decisions.summary: Every make land is a batch keyed (feature, 'second tier: <tasks>'), owned by no task, with one category in the window table and its own section of one line per batch.
decisions.why: This is the GM's second message nearly word for word: 'move batched landing stuff that happens as the second tier of checks into its own separate category rather than counting it against any individual task.' Under the two-tier trial a single-task make land is also the second tier, so keying every landing as a batch matches his words.

decisions.summary: A task's own table ends at its make carry, found through the pool's log. With no carry found it ends where the batch's first attempt starts, a labeled GUESS knob (Batch::from).
decisions.why: This puts the GM's second message into effect: the second tier's time is not counted against a task. The fallback is a stated default of the kind (l) allows ('it doesn't have to be 100% exact'), and it is labeled where it is used.

decisions.summary: GUESS defaults for the second tier's blocking. A gate blocks nothing while any task's own blocking work is in flight. It blocks the batch (never a task) (a) when the session waits on it alone, (b) when it runs in the foreground, and (c) through a repair. A builder dispatched with Blocks: none leaves the gate waited on alone.
decisions.why: Each part was judged on its own. (c) A repair stops the batch from landing until the repair is done, which is (l)'s 'waiting on it to be done before it can be started' exactly. (b) A foreground run holds the session's next step by construction. (a) This is the weakest part: the T303 T305 batch had one green run and no repair, yet 3.9 of its 4.9 min books as blocking, while the GM said 'new tasks beginning is not something that blocks on it.' His third message, though, is an expectation that ends in 'Right?', not a rule that the line must read zero. (l) allows stated defaults at about 90% accuracy. Building his expected answer into the default would rig the instrument to agree with him and defeat its purpose, which is to find where the bottlenecks are. The plan calls the rule a knob and not a target, says what most of the line rests on, and names it the first knob to turn. The first measurement (24.8 of 27.9 min blocking) runs against his expectation and rests on default (a). That is a difference to report, not a defect.

decisions.summary: When a batch's own landing run is in flight, a wait is booked to that run, whatever else in flight ends later. This moves 12.1 min out of wait loops.
decisions.why: This fixes a wrong outcome as it was found. A builder's leftover loop was booked as the cause of a session's wait on a gate. Minutes are unchanged by the fix.

decisions.summary: The task line's four booking faults, and a fifth target name found: a main session's background command under the mark alone belongs to no task; the session's own quick or done goes to the batch whose span holds it; the builder-* targets and make carry get named categories; a carry belongs to the carried task. prewarm is left to T316.
decisions.why: These are the task line's own items, each a stated default. The fifth target (make builder-trees) is the same fault class, fixed as it was found.

decisions.summary: SINCE=last reads the greatest 'until' from an append-only l7r-events/task-time-asked.log. Only a SINCE=last run writes the marker, after its report. With no marker the window is 24 hours and the report says so. The window used is stated on the report's first line.
decisions.why: This is the GM's first message: 'keep track of whenever I last asked, so that I don't have to remember the period.' Only SINCE=last runs write the marker so that the session's own measuring runs, such as this task's --since runs, do not move it. That serves his purpose. A gap is noted to the caller and not ruled: if he names a period himself, that ask is not recorded.

decisions.summary: A carry held behind a running gate and another run's wait for a build slot are not attributed to the gate, and neither is a carried task that no make land has named yet. Two of the three signals the task line names read zero. Filed as T319, lands before T302.
decisions.why: All of the GM's own words are delivered: a category of its own, never counted against a task, its blocking on a line of its own. The three signals appear only in the coordinating session's relay, which request.md marks as 'the coordinating session's, not his'. The missing two cannot be attributed from this report's inputs, because no log line records a carry's refusal or a slot's holder. The deferral takes FR-009's form: why, the filed id, and 'lands before T302', and T302 is the comparison that reads this line. It does not defeat the purpose: the line already reads well above zero, so it is not hiding a bottleneck behind a forced zero.

decisions.summary: The shared event-log reader keeps one start and one stop per agent, so a resumed builder's later spans are dropped and builder minutes read low (8.8 of T289's 13.7). Filed as T324, lands before T302.
decisions.why: None of the GM's three messages, and no part of the T243 request, asks for builder minutes per task. The column is the session's own addition, and the plan states its shortfall where it introduces the column. The defect is in a shared reader that predates this task, and the deferral takes FR-009's form (why, filed id, lands before T302). It narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Wait loops are still 25.6 min of the window's blocking in tasks' own tables. Whether those loops held tasks up must be measured loop by loop first. Filed as T328, lands before T302.
decisions.why: This is a suspicion still to be measured, not a known wrong outcome. The defect that was established, inside a batch, is fixed in this task. It narrows nothing in the T298 request.

decisions.summary: T298 lands before the before-and-after comparison of two-tier checking, which it does not make. The green exit is make builder-checks in the builder's tree, with the full gate at landing. T316 extends columns::category afterwards.
decisions.why: This is ordering and the two-tier trial's exits as docs/process-decisions.md records them. Nothing the GM asked is left out.

decisions.summary: The category names are split out of book.rs into book/cats.rs because book.rs passed the file-scale bar.
decisions.why: This is code layout and carries no fidelity content.

blocks: ### T316 (a pool tree is warm for what it last built, and the commits others landed since are compiled by the builder's first test run, after a median 4.6 to 5.7 minutes of reading in which the tree compiles nothing, measured 2026-11-26 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-26/split-reproduction`))
### T316 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.id: D1 detached pre-warm at a warm handout
decisions.summary: A warm handout starts, detached, `l7r-gate rust prewarm --since <commit>` so the moved crates' test builds compile while the builder reads.
decisions.why: It serves the request: 2026-11-19 ('how much time are we spending on recompiling things? ... efficiency improvements'), 2026-11-20 ('prioritize performance improvements'), and FR-013, whose performance work covers 'the builders' loop'. T316's line and the GM's 2026-11-26 question it is said to carry are not in the bundle, so this is grounded in request.md and FR-013 alone.

decisions.id: D2 measured from the tree's last handout (prewarm-base), not its HEAD
decisions.summary: The base commit is kept in the tree's git directory at each handout, because a release brings the tree to HEAD and the brief's sketch (since the tree's previous HEAD) would then see nothing moved.
decisions.why: It differs from the brief's sketch, but the brief is not in the bundle and is not the GM's words. It widens what is warmed rather than narrowing it, and without it the mechanism could not reach the case it names after a release. Grounded in the same request.md lines as D1.

decisions.id: D3 a cold tree's first handout starts nothing
decisions.summary: A tree whose whole cache is cold records its base and starts no pre-warm; a tree with no base on record but a warm cache is measured from where it stood before the handout.
decisions.why: A cold tree has no warm cache to bring up to date, so pre-warming it would be a full build that nothing in request.md asks for, and its coldness is already reported. Aside, not a ruling: the summary table's first row says none starts 'for a tree with no handout on record', while the prose says such a tree is measured from where it stood before the handout. Every existing pool tree has no record at landing, so both statements cannot hold. Correct the one the pinning test does not match.

decisions.id: D4 which crates, and in what order
decisions.summary: It starts only when a file under rust/ or .cargo/ changed. It builds each crate whose build reads a changed file, found by Kept::reads_any over Reads::Source, with the fewest dependencies first.
decisions.why: This is the mechanism of D1 and adds no scope.

decisions.id: D5 the same build as a real run's, nothing kept
decisions.summary: It runs one `cargo test --no-run` per crate through cargo_call (now shared with cargo_in), using the tree's own target dir and with the handout's environment taken out. It keeps no result.
decisions.why: Only a build identical to the real run's is found fresh by that run, which is what makes it save time (measured: 0.1 s against 7.7 s). Keeping no result means no test result is recorded that a real run did not produce.

decisions.id: D6 yields its slot: free_now, POLL 0.5 s, ended by a real run in its tree, pre-empted by any tree's waiter, a new waiting-<pid>-<n> mark
decisions.summary: It takes a slot only when one is free right then, and is ended by a real run in its tree. It kills its cargo for a waiter in any tree and rebuilds after. slot.rs gains a waiting marker so that waiters can be seen.
decisions.why: A pre-warm that delays real work would defeat the request's purpose (2026-11-20, 'doing those first makes everything after them faster'). The GM chose synchronization over a builder cap for exactly this kind of contention (2026-11-26, T284: 'wouldn't it be better to address that with some synchronization'). The waiting mark is the least this needs. The brief's wording is not in the bundle.

decisions.id: D7 the pre-warm runs during the rollout, while other trees' waiters are unseen
decisions.summary: Trees still running the old slot code leave no waiting mark. During the 402 s pre-warm, two real runs of such trees waited 39.3 s and 25.2 s on a slot it held. The plan accepts this until every tree carries the new code, and the yield to such waiters is pinned only by its test.
decisions.why: Seeing an old tree's waiter is impossible, but not holding a slot against one is not: the pre-warm could stay off or take no slot while any pool tree runs the old slot code, for example by checking each tree's HEAD for the marking commit or by defaulting to off until the rollout ends. So the rule is not physically impossible. Nothing in request.md implies leaving it, and honoring it defeats no purpose; it only delays a gain of a few seconds per handout. The measured cost runs against the request's purpose: 64.5 s of other trees' real-run waiting during one pre-warm. The plan names this as the mechanism's own falsifier ('a pre-warm would hold one of the machine's two slots through a whole build while another tree's real run waited'). Shipping it while that falsifier is observed to hold carries a known wrong outcome forward. Required: keep the pre-warm from holding a slot while any tree that could wait runs the pre-mark slot code, or show that the window is empty.

decisions.id: D8 it fails nothing; one per tree; CEILING_S 900 s GUESS; L7R_PREWARM=0 off
decisions.summary: It runs detached in its own process group, its output goes to prewarm.log, it exits 0 whatever happens, it holds a per-tree lock, and it has a ceiling knob and an off switch.
decisions.why: A speed-up that could fail or stall a handout would defeat its purpose. The ceiling and poll interval are labeled GUESS. The 2026-11-19 approval's 'real enforcement' concerns refusals, and this task adds none.

decisions.id: D9 booked apart; task-time shows no prewarm category until T317
decisions.summary: Each cargo call writes a `prewarm` Phase line that is booked to no call. The make task-time category is filed as T317, which lands before T302.
decisions.why: The seconds are measured (2026-11-22: 'we want everything measured so we know where our time goes, especially for compiling'), since the Phase lines are in the event log. Booking them to no call keeps them out of a builder's blocking compile: nothing waits on a pre-warm, and under the GM's definition (2026-11-25, (l)) a minute blocks only when something waits on it. Breaking down its minutes by task is the readers' work. It is filed as T317 with an id and an order, which is what (j) asks ('automatically gets broken down in the future'). The plan says the report does not show them, so nothing is silently booked as 'other' ((c)).

decisions.id: D10 the lint build is not warmed (T318)
decisions.summary: Clippy's artifacts are a separate build, so the first builder-checks lint still compiles what moved (4.8 s for land). This is filed as T318, which lands before T302.
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md asks for the lint to be pre-warmed, and the work is filed with an order and a measured reason to size it first. The plan's premise, that T316's line asks for the test builds only, could not be checked: that line is not in the bundle.

decisions.id: D11 the one real-run test failure seen during the live yield runs is left unexplained, unlisted and unfiled
decisions.summary: One of the nine real `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land FRESH=1` runs started beside a pre-warm failed in its tests (code 101, 1.7 s in, build green) and passed when re-run. Its output was not kept, and seven later tries did not repeat it. The plan reports this inside the Approach and moves on. It is not in 'Found and left?', and no task is filed.
decisions.why: A test that fails on good work is a wrong outcome (constitution XIV v2.36.0: a check that refuses good work). The GM ruled on this case the same day: 'I agree with prioritizing the test that fails under load being fixed' (2026-11-26, T104). Fix-as-we-go asks that a step's known defects be fixed, or at the least filed with an order. This failure was seen while the new mechanism ran in the same tree (a cargo killed mid-build, a real run starting beside it), so the plan cannot rule this mechanism out as its cause. None of the three grounds holds: recording or filing it is not impossible, the GM's words do not imply leaving it, and doing so defeats no purpose. Required: either show the failure is not this mechanism's and not a defect (for example, identify the test and an existing task that covers it), or list it under 'Found and left?' with its visible effect, why it is not fixed here, a filed task id and 'lands before ...'.

decisions.id: D12 the record and the [perf] tag
decisions.summary: dev/audits/builder-prewarm.md with its measurement, falsifier and cost; the rows in rust/gate/CLAUDE.md; a help line; the task tagged as performance work under FR-013.
decisions.why: The audit-register entry follows the GM's 2026-11-25 rule ('documenting the logic behind it, the measurements that we took, and ... what we would look at that would falsify'). The [perf] tag is FR-013's own definition.

decisions.id: D13 new files: prewarm.log, prewarm-base, prewarm.lock, waiting-<pid>-<n>
decisions.summary: Small files in the tree's git directory, its target directory and beside the slot files. The builds go into the tree's existing target directory.
decisions.why: Weighed against the GM's 2026-11-25 disk words (T245, T246): no new build cache is created, since the pre-warm fills the tree's existing target, and the files are a log, a commit id, a lock and a mark of a live wait. They live inside places the disk audit already covers. Nothing here narrows or departs from those words.

blocks: ### T316 (a pool tree is warm for what it last built, and the commits others landed since are compiled by the builder's first test run, after a median 4.6 to 5.7 minutes of reading in which the tree compiles nothing, measured 2026-11-26 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-26/split-reproduction`))
### T316 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: a warm handout starts, detached, the test builds of the crates whose build moved, so they compile while the builder reads
decisions.why: This is the GM's question of 2026-11-26 ('would it make sense to begin compiling immediately within a work tree builder?') answered in the form T316's line records; measured first, as the project requires.

decisions.id: D2 measured from the tree's last handout (prewarm-base)
decisions.summary: the moved range starts at the commit the tree was last handed out at, not its HEAD; a tree with none on record from where it stood before the handout; a cold tree's first handout starts nothing
decisions.why: Departs from the brief's sketch, not from the GM: a release brings the tree to HEAD, so a HEAD-based range would find nothing moved and defeat the request's purpose. The base is the one that makes 'compile what others landed' happen. A cold tree has nothing warm to extend, and the handout already reports it cold.

decisions.summary: only commits touching rust/ or .cargo/ start anything; each crate whose build reads a changed file, through Kept::reads_any, fewest dependencies first
decisions.why: This picks out the crates the request is about. Building them in dependency order is how the mechanism works and narrows nothing.

decisions.id: D4 the same build as a real run's
decisions.summary: cargo test --no-run per crate through cargo_call (now shared with cargo_in), the tree's own target dir; nothing run, no result kept
decisions.why: A pre-warm only helps if its build is the one a real run then finds fresh. Measured: 7.7 s to 0.1 s for the first test build after the core crate moved. Keeping no result keeps a kept result a real run's alone, so the gate is untouched.

decisions.summary: it takes a slot only when a second is free beside it, never queues, kills its cargo group and rebuilds later once none is spare; builds nothing at L7R_BUILD_SLOTS=1, builds freely at 0
decisions.why: This narrows 'begin compiling immediately' to when a slot is spare, which on the two-slot machine means both slots free, and it covers two cases. (a) Two or more slots: the ruling rests on the GM's T284 words ('address that with some synchronization rather than pre-emptively limiting builders'). Those words make real compiles of any tree the thing the slots serve, and a pre-warm holding the last free slot would make a real compile wait behind speculative work. The block shows the yield live against a slot held by hand, but a real compile of another tree starting beside a pre-warm is shown only by the test. How often a handout finds a spare slot is not measured. The earlier waiter's-mark form was measured holding a slot while two real runs waited 39.3 s and 25.2 s, and was replaced. (b) One slot (L7R_BUILD_SLOTS=1): the pre-warm builds nothing. Its only slot would be the one every real compile needs, so building would break the same T284 synchronization. This is a knob setting, not this machine's two slots.

decisions.id: D6 ended by a real run in its tree
decisions.summary: a live member of the tree's run lock ends the pre-warm
decisions.why: The builder's own run takes over the build. The pre-warm exists to serve that run, so it gives way to it. Measured live nine times.

decisions.summary: never waited on by the handout, own process group, logged to prewarm.log, exits 0, one per tree, ceiling 900 s (GUESS, L7R_PREWARM_CEILING), POLL 0.5 s (GUESS), off at L7R_PREWARM=0
decisions.why: These are the safety limits of a speculative background build. The knobs are labeled GUESS and recorded in the audit register (the GM's T259 register asks for this). Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.id: D8 booked apart; task-time category deferred to T317
decisions.summary: each cargo call writes a prewarm Phase line booked to no call; make task-time does not yet show it as a category, filed T317, lands before T302
decisions.why: The GM asked that everything be measured (2026-11-22) and that the breakdown name every minute (2026-11-25 (c)). The seconds ARE measured, one Phase line per cargo call in the event log. Booking them to no call is correct, because a detached run is no builder call's compile, and charging it to one would misstate the breakdown. Only the report's reading of them by task is deferred. That is the measure crate's readers' work, filed under FR-009's form with its order before T302. The measuring the GM asked for is not removed.

decisions.id: D9 the lint's build not warmed; T318
decisions.summary: only the test build is warmed; clippy's build (4.8 s for land on the measured handout) is filed as T318, lands before T302
decisions.why: The GM's word is 'compiling', and the lint compiles too, so this narrows it. It is a sequencing, not a carve-out. It is filed with its order before T302 and kept in scope, and the stated reason is measured: a second build per crate doubles how long the pre-warm holds a slot, which runs into the T284 synchronization the GM asked for. Measuring first is the project's rule. Leaving it is not a wrong outcome, since the first lint compiles as it did before this task.

decisions.id: D10 one red test run in nine; T329
decisions.summary: one of nine real runs that ended a pre-warm failed in its tests (code 101, build green) and passed on rerun; its output was not kept and eight further tries did not repeat it; filed T329, lands before T302
decisions.why: A possible red run on good work would be a defect, so leaving it needs a ruling. The cause is not known: the block names the killed cargo, the guard's rebuild under the suite and the land suite itself, and none is excluded. The ground is impossibility. Fixing needs a cause, and there is none to act on: the output was not kept, and eight further tries, three by the same recipe, did not reproduce it. What can be done now is to reproduce it with its output kept, and that is the filed T329. It carries its order before T302, so under the FIX AS WE GO rule and the GM's T104 priority on tests that fail good work, it is fixed before the work moves on, not left.

decisions.id: D11 a pre-warm ended early leaves crates unbuilt; T330
decisions.summary: prewarm-base is written when the pre-warm starts, so crates a cut-short pre-warm never built are not counted at the next handout; filed T330, lands before T302
decisions.why: In one case a builder's first run still compiles crates others moved, so this narrows the request's purpose. The block states, by its mechanism, that this is no worse than no pre-warm: those crates are compiled by the builder's own run, as before this task. That is a smaller gain, not a wrong outcome. The fix (writing the base when a pre-warm finishes) is named and filed under FR-009's form with its order before T302.

decisions.summary: dev/audits/builder-prewarm.md (measurement, falsifier, cost), rustc/task rows of rust/gate/CLAUDE.md, builder-tree help; tagged [perf] under FR-013; performance-checklist not applied (not engine speed); exits by the first tier here and the full gate in the clone
decisions.why: The audit entry is what the GM's T259 register asks for. The [perf] tag is FR-013's definition (it makes the builders' loop faster). The exits are the project's two tiers.

blocks: ### T308 (the plan review's later rounds, one part of the task: of feature 451's 135 plan review rounds from 2026-11-24 to 26, 56 were not the first for their task, 169 minutes of the 373 (observed 2026-11-26, method: `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/plan-review-rounds/t308-class.py` over the reviews' transcripts))
### T308 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: This landing builds only T308's ALSO on the plan review's later rounds; the two tiers built into tooling, the trial's measurement and the coverage run are T308's remainder, still open, and the task is not ticked from this landing.

decisions.summary: Replayed over 77 tasks, the rule refuses 11. 6 are true, 3 are the replay's artifact, and 2 (T241, T235) are refusals that no review raised. The 2 are accepted, cured by one edit each.

The GM's T233 section (2026-11-24) says a ruling attributed to him names his recorded words: 'I never made a ruling that ... That was never at any point something that I said'. Its audit counted 74 of 180 such attributions as the defect. A quote with no record behind it is that defect, whether or not a review happened to raise it. So refusing it enforces the GM's own standing rule, and the cure is to record the words or correct the line. This is not a check refusing correct work under constitution XIV, so it needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: The figure lint reads a k/K/M-suffixed numeral and a rounded figure with a unit ('20-odd minutes') as figures. A threshold's suffixed numeral ('past 300k tokens') stays a limit.

decisions.why: It serves the section's goal that 'a builder knows before it dispatches which edits will cost it another round'. A test found the earlier wording false, and it was made true. It describes a rule the plan gate already enforces, so there is no enforcement to add (the GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions', 2026-11-19, is not engaged).

The convergence rules (2026-11-23), that only a claim-changing edit triggers review, govern page and pop-up cascades. The plan gate already applies that idea to committed sections, and T337 extends it on schedule. The 'fix all known bugs in each step' rule (2026-11-18) is about port steps, and the order 'before T302' honors it anyway. So this is not a narrowing that needs a ruling.

decisions.summary: T282 built in the same landing: the quoted line of the two refusals masked in the message key, anchored on the two heads so no other key moves

### T299, T282 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A quoted or backticked phrase that is the subject of 'does/did ask you' is blanked with its verb before spans are blanked; the session's own 'I do ask you' still fires.
decisions.why: T282: a report describing an ask's wording was read as an ask. Removing a statement the detector misread serves the GM's 2026-11-26 words ('I would prefer not to see these messages about false positives') and FR-002's narrow detector. The rule is bounded by the span, and the true-ask twin is pinned. Nothing FR-002 or amendment 1 owes the filter is exempted.

decisions.summary: The '?' rule skips a last sentence running from 'asks:'/'asks whether'/'asks if' to its '?' with no you/your and no other '?' on the line.
decisions.why: It removes the check-described-by-its-question false firing from the corpus. Four twins that put something to him still fire and are pinned, including a reported question addressed to 'you' and a second question on the line. Only statements leave the detector's reach.

decisions.summary: The '?' rule skips items of a 2+ item all-'?' list under a lead-in naming a checklist, or naming what something has/asks/holds/lists/poses/carries/answers, when the lead-in names neither the GM nor the session.
decisions.why: It removes the listed-checklist false firing. Lists put to him all still fire and are pinned: 'Two questions for you:', 'Open questions:', 'I have two questions...', a mixed list, a single item, no lead-in, and question-word items with suite case 9 kept. This is precision on statements and does not narrow FR-002's asks.

decisions.summary: 'waiting (on|for) you' is a measurement when a time count or share is the past-tense subject of was/were and the clause ends or goes on to another figure.
decisions.why: It removes the two time-breakdown figure firings. Work put to him ('Two hours of review are waiting on you', 'waiting on your budget answer', present tense, count of things) still fires and is pinned in the Rust test. It is bounded on both sides.

decisions.summary: 'with waiting on you kept/counted/... separate/apart/...' names a breakdown category.
decisions.why: It removes the 'Blocking minutes, with waiting on you kept separate:' firing. The twins 'Two tasks are waiting on you, kept separate below.' and 'with waiting on you: the budget's words.' still fire. It reaches statements only.

decisions.summary: STATED's 'needs your words' becomes 'words?' so 'What needs your word: ...' is caught; pinned in both suites.
decisions.why: This is a widening: a true ask HEAD's guard passed (a check passing bad work, a defect). Fixing it enforces FR-002 and narrows nothing. It was measured on both corpora: no T235 firing changes, and one already-firing message's quoted line moves.

decisions.summary: Both refusals gain 'If the line puts nothing to him (offers him nothing), go on and say nothing of this to him.'; reviewed by message-check.
decisions.why: This sentence directly carries 'I just don't want to see the explanation of the false positives reach me'. FR-002's obligation attaches only to a message that asks or puts a decision to him, and amendment 1 adds offers. A line that puts nothing to him owed the filter nothing, so 'go on' restates FR-002's scope and is no carve-out from it. The GM's words take as given that sessions recognize false firings; what he struck is their explanation reaching him. Goal item 1 keeps every true ask refused until filtered. The new wording went to message-check (T170).

decisions.summary: The restated morning offer still fires; recognizing an ad-hoc escalation-check's kept verdict needs a new record and is filed as T335, landing before T302.
decisions.why: Under FR-002 the firing is arguably not false. The GM wrote after the 08:10Z ad-hoc check, so 'no escalation-check dispatched since his last message' holds. The restatement is an offer (amendment 1) in new words, and no gm-review.jsonl row records it as kept. Read most harshly as a residual false firing, it is one of 13, which 'I am okay with some number of false positives' covers. It is filed with an id, an order and the reason it is not fixed here (FR-009).

decisions.summary: The GM's question is answered with the measured rate, 33% before and 8% after on the 28 firings with no T lost, against 'under about one false firing in five'.
decisions.why: It answers 'it probably is worth asking whether the number of false positives is within ... an acceptable range' with numbers he can judge. The one-in-five threshold comes from the coordinating session's brief, not from the GM. The plan names it as 'the brief's aim' and does not attribute it to him, so the range stays his to accept. The plan also states that a firings-only corpus cannot show a newly dropped ask, and points to the pinned bounds instead.

decisions.summary: suite_tools::messages masks the quoted second line after a 'QUESTION UNFILTERED:'/'OFFER UNFILTERED:' head, so each refused suite case is not a new guard message.
decisions.why: T282's defect: each refused suite case created a new message key to review. The mask covers only the quoted user text under the two heads. The refusals' own wording is still keyed, so a change to it is still reviewed (451 T170), and no other message's key moves. A red-with-the-mask-off test pins it.

decisions.summary: A rust-lld link failure after the pool tree's pre-warm is filed as T336, landing before T302, to be reproduced first.
decisions.why: This build-tooling defect lies outside this section's request (T316's pre-warm). It is filed with an id, an order and the reason it is not fixed here, so nothing asked of T299 or T282 is left undone.
