blocks: ### T293 (the GM asked on 2026-11-26 whether the tooling shows where a task's time is going while it is in progress, his words in `request.md` under "2026-11-26: a live view of the tasks in flight (451 T293)"; it did not: `make task-time` books a task's categories when it lands)
### T293 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: a new read-only make task-progress showing held trees' builders, landings in flight, page sessions, review agents, free trees and staged tasks; no booking rule and no make task-time output changed
decisions.why: The GM asked (request.md, 2026-11-26, 451 T293) that 'we should be able to see while a task is in progress where the time is going'. A read-only view in the landed report's own categories does exactly that and changes nothing he did not ask to change.

decisions.summary: the code is a submodule of task_time with its own subcommand
decisions.why: Where code lives. No request text bears on it.

decisions.summary: a builder's minutes come from the landed report's booking run over its family alone, summed over every key by category
decisions.why: It shows where the time is going in the same categories the task time breakdown (T243) uses, with no second booking that could drift from it.

decisions.summary: one block per held pool tree, then one per running builder no tree is held for
decisions.why: It shows the tasks in progress, including a builder that has stopped while it waits on its plan review. The method is labeled an observation with its method.

decisions.summary: RUNNING is two tests (no stop or own lines after it, and named inflight by the latest Stop or later than it)
decisions.why: It decides which work is in progress. The measured case is labeled. A Stop that predates the field is taken as running, so the view shows more rather than less.

decisions.summary: the step now is the open make run with its last finished phase; the phase running now sits in the run's category until its line lands, and the header says so
decisions.why: It departs from the coordinating session's task line, not from the GM's words, which ask where the time is going and never ask for the open phase. The running phase's minutes are still shown, in their run's category, so no time drops out of the view, and the output states its limit. The plan's reason for adding no start marker is a cost reason, but no ruling is owed because nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: an open call is closed at the moment of the view by a line made in memory, never written
decisions.why: Mechanism. It lets the existing booking count in-progress time, which is what the request asks to see.

decisions.summary: the model turn open now is a row of its own, its tool not yet known
decisions.why: The open turn's time is named rather than dropped, consistent with the breakdown's rule that every minute is named (T243 amendment (c)).

decisions.summary: context is read live from the transcript by the context-cap guard's reader, else from the stop line's ctx, else said to be not known, each figure naming its source
decisions.why: It is extra information about a task in progress, with its sources stated. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: a pool tree's Phase lines are re-tasked from builder-pool.log, and runs are tied by clone (a workaround for the open T332)
decisions.why: It makes the view assign time to the right task where the shared writer would mislabel it. The workaround is stated openly and the writer's defect is filed as T332.

decisions.summary: a resumed builder is shown RUNNING on the in-flight test alone, its minutes headed AT LEAST (a workaround for the open T324)
decisions.why: The view states a floor and says that it is a floor, and that the builder may have stopped again. That matches the GM's 'broad understanding of where our time goes' and 'doesn't have to be 100% exact' (T243 (l)). The event-log reader's limit is shared with every report and is filed as T324, landing before T22.

decisions.summary: a landing in flight is an open session make land run that passes the in-flight test; its tasks come from tiers::batches, its phase is the last finished land Phase, its minutes are the same booking
decisions.why: It shows a landing in progress and where its time is going. The fallback names the landing by its call's task rather than dropping it.

decisions.summary: staged is each task's latest carry with no landed batch after it and no landing in flight
decisions.why: Part of what is in progress. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: a page session is one line (the run log since the read-back without ALL DONE, the brief it is in, how many briefs have ended) with no minutes by category; the categories are deferred to T350, filed to land before T22
decisions.why: Of all request.md's text, only the coordinating session's task line puts page sessions, broken down like a builder, in this view (request.md line 355: 'what it lists' is the session's). The GM's words ask where a task in progress spends its time. In the landed breakdown, a page session is one category of a task's time ('research and page sessions', T243), not a family broken down by category. So one line showing that a page session is running and how far it has got gives at least the granularity the GM's existing breakdown gives. The deferral departs from the session's own line, not from the GM's request. The build-cost reason given would not carry a narrowing, but no ruling is owed. The fuller breakdown is filed (T350) with an order.

decisions.summary: the read-back is the earliest held tree's take or BACK_H (GUESS 2.0 h, a knob), whichever is earlier; AT= gives a past moment
decisions.why: A labeled GUESS knob with an override. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: the minutes shown are machine minutes; blocking minutes are not shown in the live view; the header says a block's minutes can pass its clock
decisions.why: The GM's T293 words ask 'where the time is going'. In T243 he separated that (the minutes and percentage spent doing a thing) from the minutes spent blocking on it. The live view answers the first. Blocking stays in the landed make task-time, which T293 leaves untouched, so nothing the GM was given is taken away. The header states the limit.

decisions.summary: landings() kept the earliest of two carries on a held tree's block; it now keeps the latest, pinned by a test that was red before the fix
decisions.why: It fixes a wrong outcome in this command's own build half, found by its test. That is fix-as-we-go and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: the Makefile's .PHONY line ran task-progress and land-batch together; it is split so both are phony
decisions.why: A defect fix in the build half's own edit.

decisions.summary: a resumed builder's later start and stop lines are not read (the shared event-log reader); filed T324, lands before T22
decisions.why: A defect of the shared reader that every report uses, not of this command's new code. The view says so on its output. It carries a reason, a filed id and an order (FR-009).

decisions.summary: a Phase line written from a pool tree can name another task; this view re-tasks it, make task-time does not; filed T332, lands before T22
decisions.why: The defect belongs to the build tools' writer and the landed report. This view works around it in the open. Filed with a reason and an order.

decisions.summary: make task-time books the gap between a builder's stop and its resumed next line as the builder's model turn; filed T345, lands before T22
decisions.why: A defect of the landed report, outside this read-only view's scope, found and filed with a reason and an order. T293 changes no booking, as its approach states.

decisions.summary: a carry is booked to the task that took the tree in the carry's last second, so the staged list can name the wrong task (seen: T308 for T301's carry); filed T346, lands before T22
decisions.why: A wrong-outcome defect in the shared tiers::carries booking, which the landed batch tables also use. It is not new behavior of this view. Fixing it changes make task-time's tables, which belongs to a task of its own. It is filed with a reason and an order, and it lands inside the feature.

decisions.summary: a compound command is named by its first make target alone (book::run_cat, shared with the landed report); filed T348, lands before T22
decisions.why: Shared naming behavior of the landed report, which the view inherits. Within the GM's 'broad understanding ... doesn't have to be 100% exact' (T243 (l)). Filed with a reason and an order.

decisions.summary: a page session has no minutes by category; filed T350, lands before T22
decisions.why: See T293-D13. It departs from the coordinating session's line, not from the GM's words. Filed with a reason and an order.

decisions.summary: a builder's background run whose shell died silently stays listed as in the background, and one ending during the read is dropped from its builder's line; filed T349, lands before T22
decisions.why: An edge case of this view's own output with no in-flight list to test against. It is transient or rare, and the run is still shown or ends within seconds. It does not misstate where a task's time has gone in its categories, and it sits within the GM's 90%-correct tolerance (T243 (l)). Filed with a reason and an order.

blocks: ### T315 (the GM, 2026-11-26, on 451 T305's repeated slow test runs: why more of a builder's test run could not be cached, T301 part 1 having answered the compile side and T316 having timed one run of `rust/gate/crates/land` on a heavily loaded machine)
### T315 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: T315 is a measurement, no code changed: it answers the GM's why with build/link/test splits, write counts and priced levers
decisions.why: The GM's words (request.md, 2026-11-26, T315) ask why more of the compilation could not be cached. A measurement that answers why is the request itself; it builds nothing he did not ask for.

decisions.summary: The answer: the slow runs were build, not tests; the build is cached as far as it can be; the first build after a handout is T316's; a build-slot wait (T347) is the largest single cost; the 4-to-8 s gap in T305's builds is left unsplit because the log cannot tell edits from first builds
decisions.why: It answers his sentence about compilation directly. T305's own 5.4-8.0 s builds are not fully explained: the slot wait came later (T284), and the plan says openly that the gap is not split. That is a stated limit on an answer, not a narrowing of the question.

decisions.summary: No load generator and no suite copies run together (the brief, the host freeze, feature 460); one run at a time; nothing T301 part 1 or T316 measured is measured again
decisions.why: These are limits on how the measurement is taken. They do not narrow the question. Where the limit leaves something unmeasured (T342's saving under load), the plan files a task whose first step is that measurement, rather than claiming a result.

decisions.summary: TMPDIR on /dev/shm: NO task for time (estimated at most about 0.3 s; /dev/shm is noexec)
decisions.why: A lever priced and declined. The GM asked why, not for this lever. It also reports the size feature 460 asked for.

decisions.summary: git init with an empty template: NO task
decisions.why: Priced, under 0.02 s of wall a run. The GM did not ask for it.

decisions.summary: A shared fixture repository copied per test: NO task
decisions.why: Priced at 0.04 to 0.13 s of wall a run. The GM did not ask for it.

decisions.summary: Test thread count: NO task
decisions.why: Measured: 44 threads are no faster than 22. The GM did not ask for it.

decisions.summary: A faster linker: NO task
decisions.why: The link is already rust-lld and under 0.25 s. The GM did not ask for it.

decisions.summary: A check-only pass before the test build: NO task
decisions.why: Cited from T301 part 1's measurement. It saves nothing on a run that compiles.

decisions.summary: Splitting a large crate: NO task (about 1 s a run)
decisions.why: A cost judgment on a lever the GM did not ask for. Design and cost are not fidelity findings.

decisions.summary: rust/guard/shared's 8.06 s real-time waiting test: deferred to T339, lands before T302
decisions.why: A defect deferred under FR-009's form: why it is not fixed here (a stepped clock with its own proof), the filed id and its order are all stated.

decisions.summary: Orphaned sleep 5 processes hold rust/guard's output pipe open, 3.2 s a run: deferred to T340, lands before T302
decisions.why: FR-009's form: why (the tests that start them are not found), the id and the order are all stated.

decisions.summary: The checks' tool spends 2.0 s before an edited guard crate's build: deferred to T341, lands before T302
decisions.why: FR-009's form: why (where the time goes is unmeasured; perf and strace are refused), the id and the order are all stated.

decisions.summary: The checks' tool cannot run part of a crate's tests: deferred to T342, measurement first, lands before T302
decisions.why: FR-009's form: why (the saving under load must be measured first, and it is a new option of a command), the id and the order are all stated.

decisions.summary: The pool tree's Phase lines all carry task T285, so make task-time misbooks: deferred to T344, lands before T302
decisions.why: FR-009's form: why (builder-tree's and the log's code, outside a measurement), the id and the order are all stated. Booking time correctly serves the feature's own request that everything be measured.

decisions.summary: A builder's test build waits up to 57 s for one of two build slots: deferred to T347, lands before T302
decisions.why: FR-009's form: why (the slot count is T284's knob, retuned from a measurement), the id and the order are all stated.

decisions.summary: /dev/shm being noexec and 62.5 MB: not a defect, not filed
decisions.why: No wrong outcome: nothing uses /dev/shm. It is reported to feature 460 as the measurement that feature asked for.

decisions.summary: One land test phase rebuilt l7r-gate inside it (3.1 s once): not a defect, not filed
decisions.why: The rebuild happens once whichever command comes first, so the seconds move and are not added. Tests that read the machine's live state are already 451 T312's and T143's.

decisions.summary: The one landing includes feature 460's one pointer line to these measurements
decisions.why: A pointer, not behavior. The size figures are ones the block says 460 asked for first.

decisions.summary: The 'Performance work?' line answers 'no: a measurement', with the perf work booked only to the filed tasks
decisions.why: This contradicts the GM's verbatim words (request.md, 2026-11-20, on measurement work): 'I would also like for this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first ... even if the task itself doesn't improve performance.' The block's reason ('a measurement'; the speed-ups belong to the filed tasks) is exactly the argument he answered. Nothing in the bundle shows the field asks anything other than FR-013's class: the block does not cite FR-013, and its text in spec-index.md is cut. Two ways to clear it: answer 'yes: a measurement task, counted as performance (the GM 2026-11-20)', or cite FR-013 so its full text shows that this field means something other than FR-013's class.

blocks: ### T315 (the GM, 2026-11-26, on 451 T305's repeated slow test runs: why more of a builder's test run could not be cached, T301 part 1 having answered the compile side and T316 having timed one run of `rust/gate/crates/land` on a heavily loaded machine)
### T315 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: T315 is a measurement only: no code changed, scripts and raw results kept in dev/measurements/2026-11-26/test-run-split/.
decisions.why: The GM's words (request.md, 2026-11-26, T315) are a why-question: 'more of the compilation was not able to be cached'. Measuring and answering it is what was asked; his 2026-11-20 words make a measurement task a performance task in its own right.

decisions.summary: Answers the caching question: the build is cached as far as it can be, a one-line edit rebuilds in 1-3 s (rustc start, incremental cache read and binary rewrite, not the edit; probe-link and e2 rows); T305's slow runs were builds (first build after a handout, load) and now a build-slot queue, not tests.
decisions.why: Directly answers his words about compilation caching with this task's own measurements (probe-link rows, e2 rows, body-edit.sh, T305's own event-log Phase lines). The compile-cache ceiling also cites T301 part 1, which is not in the bundle and was not checked here; the block's own figures carry the answer without it.

decisions.summary: The recorded build medians (3-8x a one-line edit alone) are not split into own-edit, first-build-after-landings and beside-other-builds, because the event log does not record which.
decisions.why: A stated limit of the data, labeled as such, not a narrowing of the question: the answer to 'why not cached' still stands on the alone measurements and T305's own lines, and the first-build cause is T316's subject (already a GM-asked task).

decisions.summary: No load generator and no concurrent copies of a suite (the brief, after the host freeze, feature 460); one run at a time; nothing T301 part 1 or T316 measured is re-measured.
decisions.why: Tested against purpose: T305's runs were under load, and the block still covers loaded behavior from T305's own event-log Phase lines, the 2026-11-25/26 phase history (57-104 lines a crate) and body-edit.sh at load 25-28 beside real builders. Not re-measuring prior tasks' figures narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: The section also splits the tests' own run (which tests start git or programs, what a run writes, sampled TMPDIR peaks) per the brief's part 2 and gives feature 460 its /dev/shm size figure.
decisions.why: Widens, does not narrow: measurement only, no behavior added, and it serves the GM's question of where T305's repeated test runs spent their seconds. Feature 460's figure is that feature's own ask, recorded as one pointer line.

decisions.summary: Seven levers priced and given NO task: /dev/shm TMPDIR, empty git template, shared fixture repository, thread count, faster linker, check-only pass, smaller crate.
decisions.why: Each priced by a labeled measurement or a citation and found worth under about 1 s a run; none is a defect (no wrong outcome), so declining to build them leaves nothing the GM asked undone.

decisions.summary: Running only the tests a change reaches filed as T342, first step a measurement of its saving under load.
decisions.why: A new option of a command, out of a measurement's brief; filed with reason, id and order ('lands before T302'), the FR-009 form.

decisions.summary: rust/guard/shared's idle test waits 8.06 s of real time, the suite's whole wall; filed as T339, lands before T302.
decisions.why: A speed cost in test code, not a wrong outcome; the measurement builder was not briefed to change test code and the fix needs its own red-first proof. FR-009 form complete: why, id, order. T302 itself not checked (outside the bundle).

decisions.summary: rust/guard tests leave sleep 5 processes holding the output pipe 3.2 s past the binary's exit; filed as T340, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Leftover processes are arguably a defect; deferred with why (the tests that start them not yet found, the pin belongs with the fix), id and order, per FR-009. A measurement task carrying it to a filed, ordered task is within; no GM words require a measurement task to fix what it finds.

decisions.summary: The checks' tool spends 2.0 s on one thread before an edited guard crate's build; filed as T341, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Speed cost whose site is unmeasured (perf and strace refused); FR-009 form complete.

decisions.summary: Every Phase line of the pool tree since 14:00 UTC carries task T285, so make task-time books T284/T305/T104/T316/T315's seconds to T285; filed as T344, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Unlike the others this is a wrong outcome (time booked to the wrong task), a true defect in builder-tree and the event log, outside this measurement's brief. It is not left: it is filed with why, id and an order that lands it before the next work (FR-009). Within.

decisions.summary: A builder's build waits up to 57.3 s for one of two build slots (451 T284); filed as T347 to retune the slot count from a measurement, lands before T302.
decisions.why: The slot is T284's GM-asked synchronization; retuning its count is a knob change needing its own measurement. FR-009 form complete.

decisions.summary: /dev/shm being noexec and 62.5 MB, and a land test run rebuilding l7r-gate inside its test phase once, are recorded as not defects and not filed.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome: /dev/shm is unused, and the rebuild moves seconds rather than adding them; tests reading live machine state are cited to 451 T312 and T143 (not checked, outside the bundle). Constitution XIV: a difference that works is not a defect.

decisions.summary: T315 counted as performance work for scheduling.
decisions.why: The GM's own words, 2026-11-20: 'I would also like for this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first.'

blocks: ### T274 (the number of builders at once is certified against the container's memory limit from samples, and on 2026-11-26 those samples were a shell loop the coordinating session started by hand, so the three- and four-at-once comment batches ran unsampled (`docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once"))
### T274 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: Samples written to l7r-events/samples/mem-samples.jsonl, not the brief's l7r-events/mem-samples.jsonl; as a consequence state-sync's commit (which skips non-files) no longer carries the samples off the container
decisions.why: The GM's words say nothing about where samples live; the task line's 'into the tree's l7r-events' holds. The move avoids a stated wrong outcome at the brief's path (the launch lookup reading the samples first, the cohort report calling an idle clone active). The samples not reaching the tooling-state repo narrows nothing the GM asked: his T258 words name record-check answers and event logs, and the sampler's data is neither.

decisions.summary: Sampler is a module of the measure crate; task crate gains no dependency, runs the gate binary
decisions.why: Code placement; nothing asked settles it.

decisions.summary: The sampler writes and re-reads its own pid file; two starts converge on one; stop is file removal; duplicated line possible for one interval
decisions.why: Implements 'one sampler a clone' from the brief; the duplicate-line cost is stated.

decisions.summary: Alive is pid plus start time; a zombie is dead
decisions.why: Liveness mechanism; nothing asked settles it.

decisions.summary: Detached via setsid, streams on /dev/null, inherited descriptors close-on-exec
decisions.why: Implements 'detached' and 'never failing a handout' (a handout must not hang on a pipe or hold a build slot).

decisions.summary: A second start exits 0
decisions.why: Follows from one sampler a clone and a start at every handout.

decisions.summary: Sampler ends at MAX_BYTES (4 MiB); next start moves the file to mem-samples.1.jsonl; report reads both
decisions.why: The brief's size bound, kept literal (the sampler ends); the rotation keeps the handout's start from silently ending sampling for good. Arithmetic re-done: 4,194,304/277 bytes x 10 s = 42 h.

decisions.summary: Each line carries max, cores, peak; report checks the sampled peak against memory.peak on every report
decisions.why: Serves the audit-register entry's falsifier, which the GM's T259 words ask for ('what we would look at that would falsify').

decisions.summary: Median = middle sample (mean of middle two), p95 = nearest rank, labeled CONVENTION
decisions.why: Statistic convention chosen to reproduce the recorded figures; nothing asked settles it.

decisions.summary: Stall and OOM rises booked to the later sample's row; pairs >120 s apart (GAP_S, GUESS) or with a fallen counter booked to no row, counted as gaps
decisions.why: Report arithmetic; the knob is labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: Report rows are pool trees HELD, caveat printed; rows by trees at work deferred to T351, lands before T302
decisions.why: The brief asks for a report by the count of builders, and a held tree is a builder's; the limit that a held-tree row cannot certify N builders compiling is stated and filed in the found-and-left form. The bundle does not show what T302 is; the deferral is sound only if T302 (or whatever certifies three and four builders) reads the report after T351 lands, which the ordering claims and the bundle cannot confirm. Not blocking.

decisions.summary: CPU stall read from /proc/pressure/cpu (the brief's file), possibly the host's, not compared to the cgroup's cpu.pressure
decisions.why: The brief's choice, its unmeasured limit stated honestly.

decisions.summary: Knobs L7R_MEM_MARGIN_GIB 7 (GUESS), L7R_SAMPLE_MAX_H 12 (GUESS), L7R_SAMPLE_S 10 (the hand loop's interval)
decisions.why: Values for the brief's ten-second interval and bounds; guesses labeled where they stand and in the audit entry.

decisions.summary: builder-tree asks for the sampler after any handout exiting 0, including 'already holds it', and waits for the start's line
decisions.why: Implements 'started by make builder-tree'.

decisions.summary: A sampler start failure is a line, never the handout's exit code
decisions.why: The brief's 'never failing a handout', literally.

decisions.summary: L7R_SAMPLER=0 asks for no sampler
decisions.why: An opt-out switch that refuses, blocks or rewrites nothing; with it unset the sampler starts at every handout as the brief asks, and the GM's words do not speak to it.

decisions.summary: On a cold handout the start comes after the new tree's guard build, so a clone's first guard compile (or the first after a sampler ended) goes unsampled
decisions.why: Neither the GM's words nor the brief as relayed settle when in the handout the start falls; the gap is stated. Read against the block's own goal ('whenever builders hold pool trees') it is a small hole that falls on the first compile of a batch, the one least likely to coincide with another; worth closing by starting before the guard build, but not a narrowing of anything asked.

decisions.summary: Sampler writes no Phase or event-log line; task-time shown not to break with the folder present
decisions.why: Keeps the task time breakdown's booking as it is; the GM's breakdown words are not narrowed.

decisions.summary: Samples folder made once at loop start; an append never recreates it
decisions.why: Mechanism for a sampler whose clone was deleted; nothing asked settles it.

decisions.summary: sampler_words split out of Env::live as its own function so its lines are tested regardless of the test runner's environment
decisions.why: Serves the brief's 100% line coverage of new Rust.

decisions.summary: No signal handler (a bare TERM leaves the pid file, the next start replaces it); no test starts the real detached binary (a stand-in shell does; real path run by hand twice); no-inherited-descriptor shown once by a pipe
decisions.why: The brief asks for tests with 100% line coverage of new Rust, which the cover step reports clean; a bare-TERM kill is recovered at the next start, so no wrong outcome is left.

decisions.summary: Audit entry dev/audits/memory-sampler.md; one line of builder-brief.md retiring the hand loop; process-decisions, CLAUDE.md, efficiency-tooling rows; slot-coincide.py reads the JSON lines
decisions.why: The audit entry is the brief's and the GM's T259 register. Retiring the hand loop follows from the sampler replacing it, the task line's own premise.

decisions.summary: Green is builder-checks over the two crates plus their cover step (first tier); the full gate runs once in the clone over the batch
decisions.why: The two-tier arrangement the GM's T308 words ask for; the brief's coverage is met by crate-checks.

decisions.summary: 'Performance work? no: a measurement tool; it makes nothing faster.'
decisions.why: The GM, 2026-11-20 (request.md): 'I would also like for this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first ... it should be counted as such even if the task itself doesn't improve performance.' T274 is a measurement task in that sense (it measures the machine to certify the builder count, a throughput lever), and the block's stated reason, 'it makes nothing faster', is the exact reason the GM ruled out. The bundle does not show that the field means anything other than FR-013's class (FR-013 and SC-006 use the same words, 'performance work'), and it bears on how T351, this task's deferral, is scheduled. None of the three tests holds: nothing makes the GM's classification impossible, nothing in his words implies an exception, and the literal reading defeats nothing. Fix: 'Performance work? yes: a measurement task, counted as performance work by the GM's words of 2026-11-20; it makes nothing faster itself.'

blocks: ### T274 (the number of builders at once is certified against the container's memory limit from samples, and on 2026-11-26 those samples were a shell loop the coordinating session started by hand, so the three- and four-at-once comment batches ran unsampled (`docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once"))
### T274 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: samples under l7r-events/samples/ rather than the brief's l7r-events/mem-samples.jsonl; a consequence disclosed: state-push skips the folder, so samples stay on the container
decisions.why: The path is the coordinating session's brief, not the GM's words (the bundle holds neither the task line nor the brief, so this was judged against request.md and the spec only). The task line's 'into the tree's l7r-events' holds. The GM's tooling-state repository (2026-11-25) is for 'record-check answers and event logs'; samples are neither, and no GM sentence asks for memory samples to be kept off the container. The reason (readers that take every .jsonl there as a feature log) was read from code and labeled as such.

decisions.summary: a module of the measure crate; task gains no dependency
decisions.why: Placement; nothing the GM asked turns on it.

decisions.summary: the sampler writes and re-reads its own pid file; two starts converge on one; stop is a file removal
decisions.why: Mechanism for the one-a-clone constraint; its one cost (a duplicated line for at most one interval) is stated.

decisions.summary: alive is pid plus start time; a zombie is dead
decisions.why: Mechanism.

decisions.summary: setsid, null streams, inherited descriptors close-on-exec
decisions.why: Serves 'never failing a handout' (no handout waits on a pipe or holds a build slot's flock); measured once, labeled.

decisions.summary: a second start exits 0
decisions.why: Mechanism for asking at every handout.

decisions.summary: ends at a 4 MiB bound; the next start moves the file to mem-samples.1.jsonl, keeping at most two files
decisions.why: Bounded in size as the brief says, and bounded on disk in line with the GM's 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-25 words on cleaning up after ourselves. The rotation keeps sampling from stopping silently. Figures checked: 18,036/65 = 277 B a line, 4 MiB / 277 B x 10 s = about 42 h, 4,320 lines about 1.2 MB.

decisions.summary: each line carries max, cores and peak; the report checks itself against memory.peak
decisions.why: Gives the audit entry its falsifier, which the GM asked for in the register (2026-11-25: 'what we would look at that would falsify').

decisions.summary: median and nearest-rank 95th percentile, labeled CONVENTION
decisions.why: Chosen to reproduce the recorded hand-log figures; labeled, as the 2026-11-23 talk on labels asks.

decisions.summary: stall and OOM rises booked between consecutive samples; GAP_S 120 s, a GUESS knob
decisions.why: Arithmetic of the report, with its knob labeled.

decisions.summary: the report's rows are pool trees HELD, not builders compiling; refinement deferred as T351, lands before T302
decisions.why: This narrows the purpose in the heading (certifying the builder count against memory): the block itself says a row for N trees held cannot certify N builders compiling and reads low on memory. Ruled on purpose, not wording. (1) The purpose the task exists for, samples taken without a hand-started loop so a three- or four-at-once batch is never unsampled again, is delivered in full. (2) What is deferred is how stored samples are attributed to rows. The fix named is a join with the event log's Phase lines, so a later reader can re-book the same stored samples; nothing is lost at sampling time. (3) The report prints the caveat and its rustc column, so no row silently claims to certify a compiling count. (4) The deferral has the form FR-009 asks for (why it is not fixed here, a filed id T351, an order 'lands before T302'), the GM-approved form for a deferral. Not verifiable from the bundle: what T302 is, whether T351 is an open unticked task, and whether the samples outlive T351's landing given D7's two-file rotation (about 84 h) and D1's samples staying on the container. make decide's open-task test covers the second.

decisions.summary: CPU stall read from /proc/pressure/cpu, which may be the host's and not the cgroup's; not compared
decisions.why: The brief names that file, and the certification is against memory, not CPU stall. The premise is unmeasured but stated plainly, and it is not a defect of the memory figures the task certifies. Noted for the audit entry rather than ruled.

decisions.summary: knobs: L7R_MEM_MARGIN_GIB 7 (GUESS), L7R_SAMPLE_MAX_H 12 (GUESS), L7R_SAMPLE_S 10 (the hand loop's interval)
decisions.why: Bounded in hours as the brief says; each guess is labeled beside its constant, in the help and in the audit entry.

decisions.summary: asks after any handout that exits 0; a sampler failure is a line, never the exit code; L7R_SAMPLER=0 opts out; a cold handout's guard compile runs before the start, so on a clone's first handout it goes unsampled
decisions.why: 'Never failing a handout' is the constraint. The goal is sampling while builders HOLD trees, and during a cold handout's guard build no builder holds that tree yet. The unsampled first compile is stated. It is a gap in a reading, not a wrong outcome of the memory certification at N concurrent builders: on the first handout of a clone no sampler-covered batch is yet running.

decisions.summary: the sampler writes no Phase line and no event-log line
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-22 'we want everything measured so we know where our time goes' is about the time a task's work takes. A background monitor spends no task's time; its cost is measured separately (0.9 ms a sample, 7.2 MiB resident).

decisions.summary: the samples folder is made once at loop start, never on append
decisions.why: Keeps a deleted clone from being recreated, which serves the GM's clean-up words of 2026-11-25.

decisions.summary: sampler_words split out as its own function so its test does not depend on the test runner's environment
decisions.why: Testability, serving the brief's 100% line coverage.

decisions.summary: not built: no signal handler (a bare TERM leaves a stale pid file, which the next start replaces), and no test starts the real detached binary (a stand-in shell instead, the real path run by hand twice)
decisions.why: Both are stated. The stale pid file is recovered by the next start (pinned by a test), so no wrong outcome is left. Coverage of new Rust is clean, which is what the brief asks of the tests.

decisions.summary: baseline read over the three kept hand logs, where the brief said four
decisions.why: An observation of what the directory holds, not a choice to leave one out. Two of the three reproduce the decision record's figures.

decisions.summary: exits: first-tier builder-checks and crate-checks here; the full gate runs once over the batch in the clone
decisions.why: The GM's two-tier ruling of 2026-11-26 (T308).

decisions.summary: counted as performance work; order after T285 and T316, before T351
decisions.why: The GM, 2026-11-20: 'this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task'; FR-013.

blocks: ### T334 (the coordinating session's own briefs of 2026-11-26 broke the sizing rules of `scripts/container/builder-brief.md` five times with nothing refusing - T285, T298, T316 and T308 each reached the 300k cap, T315 ended at 308k - and carried no STOP POINT line; the GM asked that day whether the instructions were in the right place)
### T334 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The standing part of a builder's brief is printed by a command that sizes the brief first. A PreToolUse guard refuses a builder's dispatch that does not open with the command's marker. builder-brief.md keeps each rule with its incident.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 2026-11-26 question ('putting the instructions in the right place') answered with the 2026-11-19 standard ('real enforcement and not just instructions') and T285's ('not rely on you remembering'). The instructions move into tooling that prints them, and a dispatch without them is refused.

decisions.summary: The kinds are named fix|measurement|build-half|closing-half, not the task line's fix|measurement|mechanism-build|closing.
decisions.why: Only the name changes; the set of kinds and what each does are the same. The task line's kind names are the coordinating session's, not the GM's.

decisions.summary: An unsplit mechanism is refused by the command, not by the PreToolUse guard. Only a hand-edited marker evades it.
decisions.why: The refusal still fires on the only route that makes a marker, and the guard refuses any builder's dispatch without one. The gap left is a forged marker, which is deliberate circumvention rather than the forgetting the GM's words target. The cost reason given is not needed to place this within scope.

decisions.summary: A task is recognized as a mechanism by mechanism(): phrases on its tasks.md line, or a make target with a hyphen that the Makefile does not define.
decisions.why: This is how the sizing rule 'a mechanism as two builders' is detected. It reads the task's own line, not the caller's words.

decisions.summary: The escape SIZING_OK="<reason>" passes the mechanism refusal and is logged.
decisions.why: It is the project's escape pattern (FR-012: a reason, recorded). It covers a line that names a guard the task only repairs, which would otherwise be refused as correct work.

decisions.summary: A builder's dispatch is an ad-hoc Agent call whose prompt names a pool-registry path or carries a marker. This is narrower than spec D8's 'no defined agent' definition, so an ad-hoc builder working in the session clone with no pool tree passes unchecked (filed as T353, lands before T302).
decisions.why: Spec D8 defines a builder for the context cap, where reading every ad-hoc agent costs nothing. This guard demands a marker. On the replay day, applying D8's definition here would refuse the 17 ad-hoc dispatches that named no pool tree, measuring agents among them (observed 2026-11-26, the block's replay). That is a guard firing on correct work, and it defeats the purpose of real enforcement by teaching bypass (root CLAUDE.md). The prose cannot tell a reader from an editor, so the literal rule cannot be met without that cost. The leftover is filed with its reason and ordered before T302 (FR-009's form), so the feature still owes it.

decisions.summary: Defined agents, Explore and Plan are never a builder's dispatch.
decisions.why: Spec FR-006 and D8 exclude defined review agents from 'builder' too, and Explore and Plan do not build.

decisions.summary: A prompt opening 'Run the claims round' is exempt, as split.rs reads it.
decisions.why: The claims round was split off from the builders by the GM's 2026-11-25 'sounds good please do that ASAP'. It is not a code builder, and the exemption matches the existing split.rs reading.

decisions.summary: The marker and the escape count only on a line of their own. A pasted '<' placeholder is no reason.
decisions.why: This is a parsing convention that stops a mention in prose from passing as a marker or an escape. It is stricter, not narrower.

decisions.summary: The escape is checked after the 'is this a builder's dispatch' test and before every refusal, so every escape taken is logged.
decisions.why: It is an ordering convention that keeps the escape log truthful. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: KIND=measurement requires MEASURES.
decisions.why: It is stricter than the brief. It makes the measurement bound fire for T315's case, which is one of the motivating incidents.

decisions.summary: A bundle T=a,b is briefed as one builder on one tree, with the marker naming both. A mechanism among the tasks still refuses KIND=fix, and the guard holds the tree to every task named.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-22 bundling words ('small defects can be bundled together and worked at the same time') and builder-brief.md's 'one task or one bundle' both allow it. Refusing bundles, or escaping every one, would refuse correct work.

decisions.summary: Every sizing refusal runs before the pool's handout, so a refused brief holds no tree.
decisions.why: It is an ordering convention and is pinned by a test.

decisions.summary: JOBS_MAX is 3 (the sizing rule's own limit). MEASURES_MAX is 6, a GUESS knob. Both are listed in the audit register's covers.
decisions.why: JOBS_MAX follows the written rule. MEASURES_MAX is a labeled knob sitting under T315's observed seven, and it is registered for audit as the GM's 2026-11-25 register words ask.

decisions.summary: The measurement rule reads only lines opening 'Job|Part|Step <n>' that hold a fixed edit word, not every sentence. It misses T316's numbered list and is labeled GUESS; the T316/T308 shape is filed as T354, which lands before T302.
decisions.why: Taken literally, 'names a source edit' would require reading every prose sentence for an edit, and that would refuse correct measurement briefs. That is a guard firing on good work, which defeats the purpose by teaching bypass. The narrow form, what it misses and its false positive are stated at the guard's head and under Found and left. The detector was not tuned to fit the five incidents (the anti-overfit rule).

decisions.summary: Sizing reads the caller's declared KIND, JOBS and MEASURES. Only the mechanism test reads tasks.md independently. Item 4 says that even with a truthful caller, the sizing misses two of the five motivating briefs (T316 and T308).
decisions.why: Judged against the purpose (real enforcement, not reliance on remembering). The command runs before the brief's text exists (D8), so it cannot count jobs from that text, and forcing a declaration that is then checked removes the forgetting the GM named. T285 (by the task's line), T298 and T315 are caught (observed 2026-11-26, the block's replay2). The two misses are the measurement-plus-build shape. The block says the rule for that shape (refuse JOBS>1 on a measurement outright) is not yet settled, and adopting it from five briefs risks refusing correct work. It is filed as T354 and ordered before T302, so the feature still owes it before the next step.

decisions.summary: The block stays under 2,000 characters and quotes no rule text. Every kind's block carries a 'STOP POINT (' line.
decisions.why: This keeps agent-prefix-hooks from refusing the block, and the incident's missing STOP POINT line is now always present.

decisions.summary: The build half's handoff is <git common dir>/l7r-handoffs/<task>-build.md. A closing half asked for before that file exists gets a note on stderr, not a refusal.
decisions.why: The path is a naming convention. Not refusing is right because of the known T352 case: a capped build half writes <task>-<aid>.md, so a refusal would block a legitimate closing half.

decisions.summary: A build half that reaches the context cap cannot write <task>-build.md, so the closing half's block names a file that does not exist. Filed as T352, lands before T302.
decisions.why: This is a defect left (a block naming a missing file), but it is not carried past the next step: it carries FR-009's reason, a filed id and an order, and the command reports it on stderr when it occurs. The decisive ground is that ordering, not the 'another guard's rule' cost reason. The leftover stays inside this feature's own delivery.

decisions.summary: A builder sent from a Workflow script's agent() call bypasses the guard. Filed as T360, lands before T302.
decisions.why: No builder was sent that way on the replay day; all 56 builder dispatches went through the Agent tool (observed 2026-11-26). Closing the gap means routing workflow_hooks' agent() through this guard's verdict. It is filed with a reason, an id and an order before T302, so the feature does not drop it; only the sequencing changes.

decisions.summary: The guard rule 'marker names a tree the pool does not hold for its task' was not replayed, because the day's holders cannot be recovered.
decisions.why: This is a limit on the evidence, not on scope. The rule is built and pinned by a_marker_is_held_to_its_kind_its_jobs_and_the_pool.

decisions.summary: The section calls the task performance work by FR-013's test (the builders' loop is faster), adds no [perf] tag, and leaves the tag to the coordinating session.
decisions.why: FR-013 names 'the builders' loop faster' as performance work. Leaving the tag to the coordinating session changes nothing the GM asked.

blocks: ### T339 (451 T315's measurement of 2026-11-26: most of every run of `rust/guard/shared`'s suite is one test of the idle check waiting real seconds, and two more wait a second each)
### T339 Approach (checklist part A)
### T339 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: Of the brief's two routes, a clock the test drives is taken over knobs in fractions or milliseconds
decisions.why: Both routes are the brief's own; the reasons given (a constant second past a crossing, a whole-number bound printed in the notice, waits left open to load) keep the production path and every guard message unchanged. It serves FR-013 (the builders' loop faster) and the GM's T104 words on the test that fails under load. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Procs gains now() and sleep() with default bodies (Instant::now, thread::sleep); the check's four clock uses go through them; Blind and the guard crate's Ctx define neither, so production makes the same calls; stalls::stalled's SystemTime read unchanged; no file outside rust/guard/shared changes
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for the chosen route. The production behavior, its looks, budget and hand-on (451 T193/T201) are unchanged, and the plan states that and pins it (Blind's clock tested against the machine's).

decisions.summary: The tests' Table notes each wait, advances a stand-in time, runs a meanwhile (it backdates the builder's transcript, appends turns), and fails past 50 waits
decisions.why: A test fixture that makes the idle tests independent of load and turns a check that never stops looking into a red test, not a hang. It is enforcement of the existing behavior, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: The idle tests are rewritten to exact counts of looks and waits; the old budget-of-one case is kept as budget zero; the crossing case uses the shipped ten-minute bound in place of two seconds; the reply-during-wait test has no thread or timing
decisions.why: Every behavior the old tests proved is still proved, more strictly: exact counts in place of elapsed wall time, and the five breaks of idle.rs each turn a test red, measured 2026-11-26. The ten-minute bound is the shipped value, so it narrows no coverage, and the plan gives the reason (the real-clock read of the transcript). The old one-second case's meaning is kept as budget zero.

decisions.summary: The spelling test's text goes from 50,000 to 40,000 repeats (LONG_TEXT, a CONVENTION knob), 8% past the old million-step limit, with the test's own assertion proving the limit fires; CPU_BOUND_NS is not moved
decisions.why: What the test pins (451 T81, 449 T185) is that the text is past the old limit, and its own assertion still proves that on every run. Cutting a test's own text length changes no behavior and no claim. Leaving the bound alone loosens nothing.

decisions.summary: The next slowest tests (the context test at 1.57 s, two at 0.47 s) are read and left; the context test is real work, not a wait; nothing filed
decisions.why: The task is the waits T315 measured, and the brief bounds the read. Slow work that gives correct results is not a defect (a wrong outcome) under constitution XIV, so leaving it defers no known defect. No GM request asks for every test in the crate to be shortened.

decisions.summary: Green is builder-checks and crate-checks in the builder's tree, with the full gate at the landing; red is recorded and set down, and a claim of cannot-be-done goes through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: This follows the two-tier checking the GM asked for (451 T308): the full rigor is at the landing's gate. It skips no check.

decisions.summary: The task is classed [perf] under FR-013, as builders'-loop speed
decisions.why: FR-013 names 'the builders' loop faster' as performance work in words, and this task cuts the shared guard crate's test run from about 8.3 s to about 2.9 s, measured 2026-11-26.

blocks: ### T336 (a pool tree's first test build after its pre-warm failed to link, `rust-lld: undefined hidden symbol`, twice on code that was right (2026-11-26, `diagram-backlog-t270`, found by 451 T299's builder); the cause is proved by the measurement under `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/prewarm-link/`: a test build killed past rustc's front end, as the pre-warm's cut killed it)
### T336 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The pre-warm never cuts a crate in flight: a real run, the last slot taken or the ceiling passing mid-crate is noted and the crate runs to its end, slot held; End::Cut and code 130 go
decisions.why: Fixes a measured wrong outcome (a test build red on right code, 29 of 54 cut tries vs 0 of 20 uncut) in T316's mechanism. The GM's T316 words ask only whether to begin compiling at once; the cut was T316's design, not his. Holding the slot until the crate ends is synchronization, as his T284 words prefer. Nothing he asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: On no spare slot the pre-warm WAITS at the loop head rather than ending, departing from the brief's sentence, stated
decisions.why: The brief is the coordinating session's, not the GM's; the behavior is T316's as built and keeps the pre-warm doing what the GM's T316 question is for (compile ahead). Stated openly, nothing of request.md or the spec narrowed.

decisions.summary: A real run may wait on cargo's lock, and another tree's compile in the slot queue, for the rest of one crate (median 2.0 s, p90 13.0 s, max 82.7 s, measured 2026-11-26); alternatives priced and rejected; reopening bounds GUESS 90 s / one in ten past 13 s
decisions.why: A design tradeoff chosen on a labeled measurement; no GM words promise a real run pre-empts a pre-warm within a poll - that was T316's promise. Not a fidelity matter.

decisions.why: D5 requires tasks split as D16 splits them. D7 and D11 define landed on the end line.

decisions.summary: Each phase line carries the first task landed as task; end carries every id asked
decisions.why: A run of several tasks cannot be divided between them. D5 puts the full list on end, which is where D7, D10 and D11 read a landing, and every second is still booked.

decisions.summary: main's own refusals (no NOTE=, no feature directory) write an end for the tasks they name; a usage refusal that names no task writes none
decisions.why: D5 defines end by 'the task ids it was asked to land'. A usage refusal was asked to land nothing, so D5 owes no line for it.

decisions.summary: landed is true when the push went out (exit 0, or 3 MERGED). D7's rework, D10's and D11's landing, T13, T14 and the data model's Landing read landed, restated with this task
decisions.why: D7 and D11 in the accepted spec say exactly this. The restatement brings the other tasks into line with the spec and does not widen it.

decisions.summary: append_row_for(root, feature, row) beside append_row in the held writer (make guard-edit) files a line in the feature its word names, before T26's chain. A blank word or one naming no feature leaves the chain as it was, and T05's callers are unchanged
decisions.why: FR-005's readers read per feature. Without this, a landing of a task never started in the clone would be filed under fallback, where T13 and T14 would not find its end. It reaches only the new callers and adds no behavior beyond what the requested lines need.

decisions.summary: make is the outermost make's first goal, read from /proc as T05's lines read theirs; land when no make is above
decisions.why: This is T05's row form applied to this source.

decisions.summary: A landing stopped (make land-stop, TERM) before its push went out writes no line past its last finished step and reads as open, never as refused
decisions.why: A stop is not a refusal, and a landing stopped before its push did not land. Reading it as open answers D7, D10 and D11 correctly. The running step's split is lost, but FR-002 still books the run's span.

decisions.summary: A landing stopped in the push's tail (after-push) already has its end written, landed true
decisions.why: This closes the previous round's NOT LEGITIMATE finding. The end at the push now carries landed true before the tail starts, so D10 and D11 read the task as landed, and red-first cases cover a tail that raises after the push.

decisions.summary: One window stays open. A stop while sync-with-main.sh done runs, after the remote took the push but before the script reports it, writes no end. The section points to the push's tick commit on main as the record
decisions.why: Last round's exception rested on implementation awkwardness ('no signal handler's work'). This one rests on knowledge: until the push command reports, the landing process does not hold the fact that the remote took the push, so no writer in the landing can record landed true in that interval. A pre-push guess would write a false landed whenever the push then fails. The rule is impossible here, not merely awkward, and the section has already shrunk the gap to that interval. The tick commit on main is not what makes this legitimate: D10 and D11 as cited read the end line, not main. The real outcome in the window is that the landing reads as open, never as refused. D7's rework count therefore stays right, D10 misses a resume of that task's builder, and D11 keeps that task's static count unreset. That is one rare interleaving (a manual stop during the push itself), with the outcome confined to that one task. This is the one case the previous round's requirement ('once a landing's push has gone out, a later stop must not leave it reading as unlanded') cannot reach. The ruling covers only the interval before the script reports the push went out. The block also says 'before the script exits'. If sync-with-main.sh reports success and then goes on working before it exits, that stretch is not unknowable: end must be written when the report comes, and an end held until the exit would be outside this ruling.

decisions.summary: T18 carries only D16's first half (land.rs splits T= on commas and whitespace); task-add's quick check is left to another task
decisions.why: Splitting FR-011 between tasks narrows nothing about the feature. The request's improvement 6 ('Accept commas in T=') is carried whole here. The task-add half is not in this bundle, so whether it is planned elsewhere is for that task's own review.

decisions.summary: The change goes in rust/gate/crates/land/src/land.rs and make land's help text
decisions.why: Where the T= parser lives, plus documenting the accepted form. Both serve 'Accept commas in T='.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests: T="T1,T2" and T="T1, T2" each land both tasks in the land tests' fake world
decisions.why: D16 splits on commas and whitespace, so both forms are what FR-011 asks for. A test that fails only when commas are not accepted is enforcement of the request ('real enforcement'), not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Ordered after T17
decisions.why: Sequencing among the approved improvement fixes, which the GM put first on 2026-11-20. Nothing is deferred behind non-improvement work.

decisions.summary: Item 12 counts a comma list refused as one unknown task as a defect (valid input refused); found-and-left none; no map, no pool manifests
decisions.why: Matches the request's framing of the comma refusal as something to fix. Nothing is left unfixed.

decisions.summary: 'Performance work? no'
decisions.why: The label leaves nothing out and changes nothing in FR-011. The task is still placed among the six improvements the GM put first (order after T17). See the note on SC-006 in the reply.

decisions.summary: The guard's consulted::context gains context_from(root, var) with the environment handed in; context delegates to it with the guard's own var, so other callers are unchanged.
decisions.why: An implementation choice for repairing a test that read the real environment (make static red on the bundle crate's coverage with SPECIFY_FEATURE exported). It changes no behavior the request or spec settles; the existing entry point keeps its behavior.

decisions.why: Test-only seam so the test, not the builder's shell, decides the branch; the binary still reads the process environment. Nothing in request.md or the spec is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The test at helpers/tests.rs asserts the one outcome it means (code 1 and the exact AttributeError on a [1] pointer), then names SPECIFY_FEATURE in its own map and asserts the pointer skipped (code 0); red first with SPECIFY_FEATURE exported.
decisions.why: Makes the test assert exactly rather than depend on the environment; tightens a check, narrows nothing asked. Red-first runs carry dated methods.

decisions.summary: Constraint: no process-environment mutation in a test (it races other tests on the thread pool); 100% line coverage of each crate by its own tests kept.
decisions.why: A constraint on how the fix is made, not a reduction of any requested outcome.

decisions.summary: Lands before T08 (T03's plan review); independent of the land crate's work.
decisions.why: Ordering of a blocker repair (make static red stops landings); the spec does not settle T24's position and nothing requested is deferred by it.

decisions.summary: The sweep's other either-outcome tests (arbiter/tests.rs:579, gate/src/lib.rs:309, record/tests.rs:301, measure/spec/tests.rs:54, owed/.../answer_modes.rs:149) and modal.rs:866's raw CHECK_ORDER_OK read are named in the report, outside T24's edit scope, not filed.
decisions.why: Neither request.md nor the spec asks for these tests to be changed, and the plan states, with a measured probe for CHECK_ORDER_OK (78 of 78 exported, 2026-11-20), that none reads SPECIFY_FEATURE or flips with this task's defect. No wrong outcome is shown for them here, so leaving them is not a defect deferred and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: make set-down removes the clone's active-task mark once the set-down row is written, when the mark names the set-down feature, and says so in its reply; the next task-start writes it again
decisions.why: Fixes a defect in the sense of constitution XIV (a tool refusing valid work: a set-down feature's stale mark held every push touching its specs and refused T06's landing). It removes friction from the landings this feature exists to speed up (request 2026-11-20: prioritize the improvement fixes and performance work), and it matches FR-013's own reading that a set-down feature holds no started task. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: A refused set-down, another feature's mark, or a mark that cannot be read or names no feature is left as it stands and fails nothing
decisions.why: None of these cases is the defect. Clearing another feature's mark, or clearing the mark after a refused set-down, would be wrong. Leaving an unreadable mark as it is does not take back any part of the stated goal: a set-down feature no longer holds pushes through its own mark.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf] in FR-013's sense (it makes the landings faster), not filed with PERF=1 because it touches no engine stage's counted operations or time
decisions.why: FR-013 defines performance work to include a task that makes the landings faster. A stale mark cost a refused landing and reverted ticks. The PERF=1 distinction follows FR-013's two routes as written.

decisions.summary: Red-first test, 100% line coverage of the task crate, the clear deleted to show the test turns red, a scratch-repo replay of the incident, and the usual green exits
decisions.why: Verification that the fix does what it says. It is not new behavior.

decisions.summary: One reader performance(id, title, plan): the [perf] tag among the bracketed tags right after a task's id (not a quoted [perf] in prose), or PERF=1's '### T<n> Performance checklist' heading.
decisions.why: FR-013 defines performance work as a task filed with PERF=1 or tagged [perf] on its line; the reader recognizes exactly those two marks.

decisions.summary: The Stop hook's active test comes out of verdict() as active() (open box but the GM's, not set down since the last task-start, not closed by status) and is shared by task-start.
decisions.why: FR-013 defines an active feature as exactly the Stop hook's own test in set_down_hooks.rs; sharing one function is how that definition is honored.

decisions.summary: next_performance(root, git dir, prefer) picks the open performance task: the feature being started first (counted active even if set down, since its start ends that), then each other feature started in this clone, latest start first; both the Stop hook and task-start ask this one picker.
decisions.why: FR-013: task-start refuses while an open performance task exists in any active feature, and the Stop hook names one before any other. The active set is the Stop hook's own test (which reads this clone's start log); counting the feature being started as active widens, not narrows, the refusal; one picker for both keeps the hook from naming a task the start refuses.

decisions.summary: task_start.rs perf_first reads PERF_LATER_OK first (reason of two words or more, refused short, recorded in the guard log under perf-first), then refuses a non-performance task naming the picked task and its make task-start F= T= command.
decisions.why: FR-013 (refusal naming the task and the command to start it, an escape of a reason) and FR-012 (two-word recorded escape, message naming the compliant command, red-first test with the check deleted - the reds, greens and deleted-check reds are recorded).

decisions.summary: Specs read under the clone's toplevel where resolve_feature found the feature, never L7R_GATE_TREE.
decisions.why: An implementation choice of where to read the tasks FR-013's test reads; it removes no case FR-013 covers.

Left untagged, each with its reason: 451 T07-T11, T22, T24; 444 T24, T25, T28, T29, T31-T33, T35, T39, T42; 449's listed open boxes; 417 (engine deleted); every box of the 20 closed features.

No performance-improving task is shown left out.
