decisions.summary: On a build error holding `undefined hidden symbol`, drop only the incremental session holding each `.rcgu.o` unit the linker names and that crate's `.fingerprint/<crate>-<meta>`, under cargo's own lock, print what was dropped, and rebuild once incrementally
decisions.why: This is the task line's own remedy, 'dropping that crate's incremental session', as the block quotes it. The fingerprint drop is what makes the heal work: 449 T244 cleared sessions but not fingerprints, cargo kept the broken rlib as fresh, and the scratch copy showed a stale rlib behind an out-of-date fingerprint recompiled and linked clean (e2e.log, 8.3 s). Its reach is no wider than the directories the linker names.

decisions.summary: A link error that names no unit rebuilds once with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; a second failure is refused as before, with the cargo text
decisions.why: A bounded fallback inside the same goal: a gate command that failed on stale link state runs on a freshly linked tool. It adds no behavior beyond one retry and keeps the existing refusal afterwards. In this path the stale incremental set is left as it is (the block's own finding is that a CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 set is separate), so goal 1's 'next incremental build links with no retry' is guaranteed only for the named-unit path. That is a limit of a fallback for unrecognised failures and no narrowing of the task.

decisions.summary: An uncompiling file is still refused with no retry (T41 kept); only the link-error text triggers a retry
decisions.why: Keeps existing, separately approved behavior that T142's line does not ask to change; the detection is limited to rust-lld's own spelling.

decisions.summary: Always-non-incremental and `lto = "off"` rejected: T95's incremental tool profile and default ThinLTO kept
decisions.why: Leaves T95's measured, GM-asked profile as it is. The alternative was measured to cost 83-116 s per rebuild of the core crates against about 5 s (time.sh, measured 2026-11-22), which works against the feature's performance purpose. Keeping an approved profile is no narrowing.

decisions.summary: Show the rust-lld lines and a line naming what was dropped, not the full link command line
decisions.why: Presentation of the refusal and the heal. It serves the defect statement in Approach item 12, where a wall of linker text is the symptom.

decisions.summary: Change only scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh, its hook test and this section; the real cache is never removed by hand; red-first test (FR-012)
decisions.why: Matches T142's line and FR-012's red-first requirement (13 FAIL lines on HEAD's launcher, then green, measured 2026-11-22).

decisions.summary: The same stale-link exposure in scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh (l7r_guard, same incremental tool profile, l7r_shared units that failed l7r-rust twice) and in make rust-test's dev-profile builds is deferred to T146, which lands before T98
decisions.why: The fix stops at the gate launcher although the same defect class is known in two other builds, so this is a narrowing, and it is a defect left rather than a difference. It is legitimate because the defect is not left: it is filed as T146 with a stated order (before T98, whose occupancy measurement a stalled build would skew). It also states why it is not fixed here (T142's line is the gate launcher's failure, and the guard fails open to its last good binary rather than refusing every gate command). FR-009 asks for exactly those three things: a reason, a filed id and an order. Nothing the GM asked is excepted: the request does not name this defect, and the GM's 2026-11-22 words favour filing small defects and bundling them over widening one task. One caution for T146: these two instances came from a scan of transcripts for link failures, which finds builds that FAILED, not every build exposed. T146's census should be drawn from the launchers that build with CARGO_INCREMENTAL or the tool or dev profile, for example a grep over scripts/ and the Makefiles, and not from this list.

decisions.summary: make task-start, make closing-checks and make decide take T=a,b,c as make land already does; a bundle gets one section and one verdict that counts for each task.
decisions.why: This is how the GM's 2026-11-22 request is carried out: bundle the open small tasks and work them at the same time, which he approved with 'so let's do that then'.

decisions.summary: active-task names the first member as task and every member as tasks. Each member's start is logged, the first member's last, so it is the task in force. All of a bundle's refusals are checked before anything is written.
decisions.why: This is how a bundle is started. A single task's flow is unchanged (Approach 1, 12).

decisions.summary: A member is refused when its box is not open, when it is a phase task (a parked stage's task included) or when its feature is held. The plan has no size test, so which tasks to bundle is the caller's choice.
decisions.why: The GM's words leave it to the session to look at the open tasks and pick the tiny ones, so leaving out a size test narrows nothing. A phase task is a stage of a staged plan, not one of the small defects the GM asked to bundle. A held feature or a closed box cannot be started alone either.

decisions.summary: Performance-first is checked for each member. A member that is not performance work is refused while an open performance task waits, unless that waiting task is a member of the same bundle. A performance task waiting outside the bundle still causes the refusal, with the same escape a single start has.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-013's literal start refusal. The GM's own words imply it: look at 'what set of tasks is currently open' and work them 'at the same time'. If the exception were refused, the performance member would have to go alone first, and every member would pay the fixed cost again, which is exactly what bundling exists to stop. It leaves FR-013's purpose intact, which is that performance work comes first and makes everything after it faster. The block says members are 'started, closed and landed together' and 'the landing ticks every member'. So a member that is not performance work can never land ahead of the performance member it shares a bundle with, and the end-to-end pin (land/tests/bundle.rs) lands the bundle as one unit. Counting each member as started for land-alone (T101) only lets the bundle land apart from other tasks. It does not let one member land apart from its own bundle. Any performance task outside the bundle still blocks as before.

decisions.id: D5 FR-006 bundle as the task
decisions.summary: One builder serves one bundle. The resume refusal after landing still fires because the landing ticks every member, whichever member's id the guard reads. The context-cap guard is unchanged.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-006's 'serves one task'. The GM's words call for it: working the tiny tasks 'at the same time' with one builder is how the builder's reading-in cost is paid once, and that cost is one of the fixed costs bundling exists to cut. FR-006's purpose is to keep builder contexts small, and that is still enforced without change. The context threshold guard is untouched, and resuming a builder after its bundle lands is still refused, since every member is ticked. This ruling does not rest on the members being small: a large bundle reaches the same context cap as a large task.

decisions.summary: The event log files a T=a,b,c command under the first member, so the static-runs guard and the plan-round tripwire count a bundle once. PLAN_ROUND_CAP and STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK are unchanged.
decisions.why: A bundle gets the same allowance one task gets, which is tighter than n tasks would get, not a carve-out from FR-007 or the round cap.

decisions.summary: make where-time reports a bundle's time under its first member (performance checklist 5). The other members carry no time of their own.
decisions.why: One builder's minute, one closing run and one review round in a bundle belong to the bundle, not to any one member. No per-member split could be true. The time is kept whole, so the categories (tests, compile, gate, land, review) and the totals the retrospective tooling exists to show are intact. This is a difference in how the time is reported, not a wrong answer from the tool.

decisions.summary: A heading that opens with a list of task ids followed by (bundle), Approach, part B or Performance checklist belongs to every listed task. Any other list heading still belongs to its first task, which keeps feature 405's 15 existing headings as they were. The search space is stated: a grep of specs/*/plan*.md.
decisions.why: The bundle section needs this, and the plan does not change how past plans are read.

decisions.summary: make decide T=a,b,c is refused while a member's section is not the first member's, or while T= differs from the heading's list, and the refusal names the fix. The lint runs once and the checklist once per member. One MODE 4 prompt asks the reviewer to judge every task in the bundle.
decisions.why: The bundle's single review, which the request implies.

decisions.id: D10 the verdict, tick and push
decisions.summary: record-task on the first member writes the same entry under each listed member that shares the section. owed_for and judge_in treat a block as in scope when any of the tasks sharing it is. The Approach gate and the plan-round count read the bundle heading for each member.
decisions.why: One verdict that counts for each member, as the bundle needs.

decisions.summary: The split in make closing-checks T=a,b,c takes a set of tasks, and the members' edit lines count as the caller's.
decisions.why: One set of closing runs per bundle, which is the fixed cost the GM asked to pay once.

decisions.summary: T141 is classed as performance work under FR-013 because it makes the builders' loop faster.
decisions.why: FR-013 defines performance work to include a task that makes the builders' loop faster, and the GM asked on 2026-11-20 for performance improvements to come first.

decisions.summary: The fixed cost is measured first, and each figure carries the date it was observed and its method. The tests go red before the change, the expected saving is marked GUESS, and the after-measurement waits for the first real bundles.
decisions.why: This is ordering and evidence, and it narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: A ledger refusal (--refuse or --landing) leaves out a MODE 4 pass whose subject names a feature present here and a task ticked in neither tasks file and not among the landing's tasks; it names them on stdout. Block reviews, ticked tasks', absent features' and every other pass still refuse.
decisions.why: This is the fix the task names in its heading (a landing refused on another task's open plan-review passes) and serves the request's rework clause (refused landings, improvement 6 'smaller landing fixes'). The left-out pass is not dropped: it refuses at its own task's landing and push, where that task is in the landed set or ticked. The bundle holds the heading, not T147's task line verbatim; judged against request.md and the spec.

decisions.id: reach: the rule in the set all three refusals read
decisions.summary: The rule sits in the one owed set the first pass, the push's ledger-owed --refuse row and make land-tooling read, so all three leave another open task's plan review out.
decisions.why: Same deferral as the rule. Each left-out pass still refuses at its own task's push, because that task is ticked by then (the plan says so explicitly). Enforcement moves to the landing that can answer it and is not lost, so 385 T72's 'plan reviews written by every push route' still holds for each task's own reviews.

decisions.summary: A task id in neither tasks.md nor tasks-done.md counts as open, so its pass is left out.
decisions.why: A design detail of the fix with a stated, measured-against-history reason: land-alone commits a task's own lines only (de7ecc7de4), so another task's line can be absent at the landing worktree's HEAD. It removes no requested behavior.

decisions.summary: A feature's landing still writes every pass traced to it, another open task's plan review included, and --write-plan-reviews still writes any recorded one; 'left to that task's landing' governs refusal, not writing.
decisions.why: Measurement corrected the heading's premise ('which only that task's landing writes'). Keeping the earliest write route changes nothing asked and narrows nothing: more rows get written, none fewer.

decisions.id: no escape added at the first pass
decisions.summary: cheap.rs asks --refuse --landing <feature> --tasks <ids>; LEDGER_ROWS_OK stays at the push and make land-tooling only.
decisions.why: The heading's second half is answered by removing the refusal the landing could not answer, rather than by adding a way past it. By the plan's own defect test (checklist item 12: a landing refused that its own work could not answer), the refusals left are the other passes. Its own session clears them with the named make ledger-owed WRITE= and a commit. The '70 still owed with the clone's 46 uncommitted rows added' sentence shows they are rows the session itself has not yet written, not rows a landing cannot reach. With no wrong outcome left there is no defect left (constitution XIV v2.36.0), and adding no bypass fits the GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions'. FR-012's escape rule covers FR-006 to 009, 011 and 013, not this ledger refusal that predates the feature.

decisions.id: found and left: the 86-133 untied passes
decisions.summary: The passes no subject ties to a feature (impl-drift DECIDE_OK dispatches, workflow units, modal and record checks) refuse every landing until the session writes and commits their rows; called working as designed, not filed.
decisions.why: Rises or falls with the escape decision, on the same reading. These are passes the landing's session ran and can write itself with the remedy the refusal names, so they are a refusal the landing's own work can answer, not a defect deferred. FR-009's deferral form is therefore not owed.

decisions.summary: rows.rs gains wave_transcript to find <session>/subagents/workflows/<run>/agent-<id>.jsonl; session_of names a wave unit's session as the directory above subagents/workflows/<run>/; filled_row takes a wave unit's reply and label from its run's journal.jsonl result line and fills the same cells a hand-dispatched pass gets.
decisions.why: This is the task line itself: a session's make ledger-owed WRITE= must trace and write the check-wave units it ran so they stop refusing every landing. The mechanism follows from the measured transcript and journal layout; nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A wave pass's verdict cell is read from its reply by verdict_of, as a hand-dispatched pass's is, not from the journal's verdict field; an all-IN-STEP impl-drift reply therefore reads 'findings' exactly as the session's hand-dispatched impl-drift rows already do.
decisions.why: Within the task: the task line is the trace, and choosing which source fills the verdict cell, the same reading verdict_of already gives every hand-dispatched pass, narrows nothing asked. Whether an all-IN-STEP impl-drift reply reading 'findings' is a wrong outcome: the bundle shows none. The plan's own constraint is that a row answers a pass by its check and cost cells (feature 371), and nothing in the bundle shows a consumer of the verdict cell that would refuse, let through or misreport work because of it. It is a pre-existing reading of verdict_of shared by the hand-dispatched rows, not introduced here; on what the bundle shows it is a difference, not a defect left (constitution XIV), so it needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: settle::settled / cost::subagent_files are not taught the wave directory, so a wave pass keeps the hook's logged cost cells rather than cells recomputed from its finished transcript; the size of any difference was not measured.
decisions.why: Wave passes' costing is left unlike hand-dispatched passes' (the hook's logged cells kept, not recomputed). Applying the fuller treatment would defeat the task's own stated purpose, concretely: by the plan's constraint a row answers a pass by its check and cost cells (feature 371), so recomputing the cells of the ~342 wave passes already answered (377 logged, 35 owed, measured 2026-11-22 by grep -c) would make those rows answer nothing and put the passes back on the owed list, refusing landings again - the exact failure T151 exists to end. The plan states the unmeasured size of the gap openly rather than claiming it is nil.

decisions.summary: The fix's binary runs make ledger-owed WRITE= with the session's earlier rows' full text, writing 41 rows (the 35 impl-drift units and 6 later passes), with the 40 plan reviews refused as their landings' own per 451 T105; after, only 40 MODE 4 plan reviews are owed.
decisions.why: Carrying out the task's goal under an existing rule (451 T105); the WRITE= text names where every check's verdict is recorded, so applying it to the 6 later passes asserts nothing false. Nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Red-first pins in ledger_passes/tests.rs (a wave unit written for its own session from the journal, another session's unit left owed) and rows/tests.rs (text result, structured result without text, no result, no agent), shown red before the fix; then crate tests, lint, cover, closing checks.
decisions.why: Tests whose only effect is to make the requested fix happen and keep happening; enforcement of the task, not added scope.

decisions.summary: transcript( callers under rust/gate/crates/reviews found by grep; trace.rs unit_prompt already walks the wave directory and is unchanged; cost::transcript itself is not changed.
decisions.why: The enumeration states its search space; because the fix adds wave_transcript in rows.rs rather than changing cost::transcript, callers of cost::transcript outside that crate are not affected. No narrowing.

decisions.summary: The plan declares no defect found and left.
decisions.why: Consistent with the rulings above: the verdict-cell reading is shown by the bundle to be a difference with no wrong outcome, and the cost-cell limitation is a stated, purpose-justified choice, not a defect shown. Nothing else in the block is left.

decisions.summary: T151 is declared not performance work for FR-013's scheduling.
decisions.why: The task repairs the review ledger's tracing of check-wave passes to their session so landings stop being refused; it neither improves a measured time nor is the time-measurement work the GM asked on 2026-11-20 to count as performance. The declaration takes nothing from FR-013.

decisions.summary: One Phase line form (phase_row in event_log_hooks.rs) built in one place, every writer appending through append_row_with, the hooks' writer; the make target read one way via shared::make::outermost_goal
decisions.why: FR-003/D4 name the hooks' line writer as the one writer; a shared form is how every step the GM named gets measured the same way.

decisions.summary: A step's line is written in process where a Rust tool already runs it, otherwise through one shell door (l7r-gate measure event-log phase)
decisions.why: A mechanism choice for 'we want everything measured'; it drops no step.

decisions.summary: hookrun.sh leaves each job's span and make hooks-test hands them to the door in one call, so closing-checks and make done write theirs too
decisions.why: Directly the GM's 2026-11-22 words: 'make the hook suites measure their time so they won't be missing'.

decisions.summary: make map's generate/render/page cut at each staged artifact's mtime, a CACHED hit its own line, rather than the engines timing themselves
decisions.why: Map generation is measured, as the GM asked ('especially ... generating maps'), with its steps split; how the cut is taken is method, not scope. The plan labels the reading and the reason (engine self-timing would move every map's engine id).

decisions.summary: measure runstats phase|phase-pre, already called per gate phase by make done, writes the Phase line in process
decisions.why: Measures the gate's seeds, counters, preflight, reference etc., which the task names as invisible; no process added.

decisions.summary: make record, quick, preflight, cohort timed whole by the Makefile's TIMED macro (quick's checks moved to _quick)
decisions.why: Brings these targets into the phase record; 'everything measured'.

decisions.summary: Page sessions write write/check lines from the runner, booked under their task directly since no Bash run holds them
decisions.why: Detached work that was invisible is now measured and attributed rather than left loose.

decisions.summary: where_time/columns.rs books each phase to compile, hook suites, map generation, tests, gate, docs or review; containers book none; Split carves categories in a fixed order so parallel suites count once; both tables gain hook suites and map generation columns; a session-less test phase is now counted loose
decisions.why: The GM asked to know where time goes, 'especially for compiling, running tests, and generating maps'; the new columns and no-double-count carving serve exactly that.

decisions.summary: lint (clippy) and format (rustfmt) phases booked to no phase category; their seconds stay in the holding run's own bucket as before; a lint's own build line still booked to compile
decisions.why: Narrows the split the readers give, not the measurement: the lines are written and the seconds remain counted in the run's FR-001 bucket, so nothing is invisible. Splitting clippy into compile vs tests is not possible without a seam inside one process, and rustfmt is neither, so booking either to compile or tests would misstate the very categories the GM wants to read; the literal alternative defeats the request's purpose (accurate knowledge of where time goes).

decisions.summary: Lines verified by real runs in the clone for map, cohort, record, quick, page session and hook suites; make preflight and make done's gate phases shown by unit tests (runstats/tests.rs) alone until a make done runs
decisions.why: The writers for those steps are implemented as asked; this is how their working is shown, not a reduction of what is measured, and the plan states it plainly rather than claiming a run.

decisions.summary: Measurement overhead kept negligible (one door call per hooks-test, none added for gate phases, one in-process append per map step); the pool crate edit moves Mode A maps' build id so each is redrawn once to the same rules
decisions.why: Consequences of measuring map steps, stated and measured; no map behavior changed.

decisions.summary: T147's left rule widened from plan reviews to every non-plan-review pass, read by a new left/whose.rs, through the one owed set the first pass, the push's row and make land-tooling all read
decisions.why: The task line names a landing refused on other started tasks' record and pop-up check passes. Widening to every non-plan-review pass does not drop a row: each left pass is still owed by its own task's landing or session, and the refusal stays on everything not attributable to another started, unticked task. No GM clause or FR touches the ledger refusal, so this narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Whose a pass is: first source naming a task, in own.rs's order - own words (logged subject, check-bundle -t<n> suffix, meta description), then builder (parentAgentId's brief), then page session (index.txt brief's feature and first-line task, else file name); prompt bodies never read
decisions.why: A design of the attribution the task needs, grounded in a dated measurement (25 of 26 named by page session, 1 by builder) and in the measured fact that prompt bodies name unrelated tasks. Implements the task; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A bare task id takes the feature that started it (event_log_hooks::started); a number names its unique specs/<n>-*
decisions.why: Resolution detail needed to attribute a pass; carries no carve-out from the task line.

decisions.summary: A pass is left only where its task is STARTED (task-starts.jsonl), not merely open
decisions.why: The task line itself says 'other started tasks''. An open task nobody started has no landing or session coming to write the row, so leaving its pass would lose the row.

decisions.summary: A pass of a ticked task (in tasks.md or tasks-done.md) still refuses, though task-starts.jsonl records it as started
decisions.why: The task line's 'started tasks' are tasks whose own landings and sessions will write their rows; a ticked task's landing has already happened, so leaving its pass would leave the row unwritten forever, defeating the ledger. task-starts.jsonl keeps every landed task's start (740 rows), so 'started' alone would leave almost everything. No known instance is left: the after-measurement refuses 3 passes, all the landing's own. A hypothetical refusal is not a known defect left.

decisions.summary: A pass naming a task never started still refuses
decisions.why: Outside the task line (not a started task), no landing or session is coming to write it, and the after-measurement shows no such pass in today's owed set: no known defect left.

decisions.summary: A pass whose every source names no task still refuses every landing until its session writes its row (found and left, judged working as designed, not filed)
decisions.why: Not a pass of another started task, so outside the task line; no landing can know whose it is, and leaving it would let an unattributable pass escape the ledger. None of the 26 measured owed passes named nothing (all were attributed), and the after-measurement's 3 refusals are the landing's own, so no known instance is left unfixed.

decisions.summary: The landing's own passes, by any source, bare or with its feature, still refuse with make ledger-owed WRITE= named
decisions.why: The task line is about OTHER tasks' passes; the landing's own are writable by WRITE= as the landing session's, so refusing them is the existing behavior the task leaves intact.

decisions.summary: Plan-review passes keep T147's rule unchanged
decisions.why: The task line names record and pop-up check passes; plan reviews are T147's already-settled case.

decisions.summary: 449 T258's own.rs is not reused as code (it lives in l7r_guard, which no gate crate may name per check guard-deps); whose.rs reads the same sources after the fact from l7r_shared, regexes copied; no guard source edited
decisions.why: Implementation choice forced by the T66 crate rule; same sources and order, no change to what the task delivers.

decisions.summary: Transcripts listed once per refusal (settle::Transcripts made pub(super) and shared), only for passes whose subject names no task
decisions.why: Cost choice inside the task; attribution unchanged.

decisions.summary: note() reworded to 'the passes of N open task(s) left to their own landings and sessions (451 T147, T157), which write their rows'; T147's pins follow
decisions.why: Message follows the widened rule; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The heading's note that LEDGER_ROWS_OK does not reach the first pass is not addressed; the escape's reach stays as it is (unlabeled by the author)
decisions.why: The task line's subject is the landing refused on other tasks' passes; the escape's reach is given as why that refusal had no way out. Once the first pass refuses only passes the running session can write (WRITE=), the way out exists, and the after-measurement shows the observed refusal cleared. No request clause or FR asks for the escape to reach the first pass, and no remaining refusal without a remedy is known.

decisions.summary: Two pins (left/tests.rs reading test, land inproc.rs first-pass test), each shown red with clues.left_to stubbed
decisions.why: Enforcement of the task's own behavior (FR-012's red-first practice); serves the task, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: T98 is a measurement of builder-slot occupancy under T88's rolling dispatch; no engine or hook code changes and L7R_BUILDERS stays at 3.
decisions.why: A measurement task of the builders' loop, counted as performance work by FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 words on measurement tasks; the measurement finds no wrong outcome to fix, so leaving the constant and code as they are narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The night window runs from T88's landing (2026-11-21T18:40:16Z) to the last night builder's end (07:06Z), 745 minutes, and leaves out the 3-hour builder-free gap before T147.
decisions.why: Chosen by the same rule as T88's before window (the builders' day, first start to last end); the before is reproduced to the minute by the same script, so before and after are one method.

decisions.summary: Occupancy is reported both for 451's builders alone (the before's method) and for every feature's builders (what the Stop hook counts).
decisions.why: Reports more, hides nothing; the before has no 449 builder so its row is the same in both readings.

decisions.summary: The replay's independent-task rule (a line naming no file a running task edits) is kept although it does not read 'after T<n>' and so over-reports for the 449-slot minutes.
decisions.why: Kept so before and after are one method, and the over-report is disclosed with its cause; a difference of method that is stated, not a defect left.

decisions.summary: The stretches below three are attributed to a recorded choice to give the slot to 449 when no 451 task could start, to landings, and to 30-80 s dispatch latency; the Stop hook's count is found correct for the window, and nothing is fixed.
decisions.why: Each cause is named with its source; none is a wrong outcome (the weekly cap and T156's miscount are each ruled out with evidence), so there is no known defect carried past this task.

decisions.summary: T98 runs after T88 and a full day, and before T22.
decisions.why: Ordering inside the feature's own task list; narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: builder_brief reads the feature number and every task id before the description's first colon, words between allowed; a range T289-T300 is each member at its first id's width; a backwards, lettered or wider-than-SPAN range reads as its two ends.
decisions.why: A defect fix in this feature's rolling-dispatch tooling (451 T88, the bundling the GM asked for 2026-11-22, T141): the Stop hook miscounted five live builders. Fixing a known bug as found is the standing rule; a malformed range kept to its two ends is the prior behavior, not a narrowing of anything asked.

decisions.summary: A running agent whose description names a landing before its colon, or whose prompt's first line runs make land (not land-tooling/land-stop), is a lander; free_slot names no task-start while one runs. A landing brief naming neither reads as no lander, failing toward a visibly named start.
decisions.why: Carries the arbiter's ruling ask:set-down-449-mid-landing (no task-start while a landing runs) into the hook. The residual case (an unrecognizable landing brief) is backed by (c)'s process check for any landing actually running in the clone, and fails toward a named start the session can see rather than a hidden hold; the ruling binds the session's conduct, which a named suggestion does not override. No requested behavior is cut.

decisions.summary: A landing process in this clone or its -land worktree (l7r-gate land without --stop, or land-alone.sh), found by walking /proc (L7R_PROC_ROOT in tests), also holds the slots; the few lines of the land crate's landing_pids shape are re-read here rather than imported.
decisions.why: Same ruling, enforced on the process rather than the brief; where the code lives is design, not fidelity.

decisions.summary: next_independent skips a running builder's own tasks, including bundle members never task-started, so none is named the next start.
decisions.why: A defect found while testing and fixed in the task (fix as we go); it makes the hook's start-next correct for the bundles the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: SPAN = 200, a CONVENTION past the widest bundle seen (twelve).
decisions.why: A labeled convention bounding range expansion; it narrows nothing asked, and a range beyond it keeps the old two-ends reading.

decisions.summary: Green on make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared, its cover, lint, format and the hook suite; red recorded and the task set down, a cannot-be-done claim ruled through make arbiter-ask; red-first tests for the three new cases.
decisions.why: Verification of the fix itself; enforcement of the requested behavior, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Nothing left: the one defect found (range members named as next start) is fixed here.
decisions.why: No defect is deferred.

decisions.summary: Every rule lives in the existing scratch-sweep guard, so the cache has one cleaner.
decisions.why: Where the cleanup lives is how it is built, not how much of it there is. It serves 'clean up after ourselves in terms of the file system' and drops nothing.

decisions.summary: make done, make land and make closing-checks refuse below L7R_DISK_FLOOR_GB (15, GUESS) free. The refusal names the largest build directories, what cache-clean would free, the scratch worktrees and the DISK_OK escape, which is recorded.
decisions.why: This is the 'without us realizing it' half of the GM's words, enforced: a gate stops before the disk fills. The recorded escape is the project's standing guard rule. 15 is a knob marked GUESS, and the 4.56/24.77/31 GB figures that back it each carry a date and a method.

decisions.summary: make cache-clean [DRY=1] [HOURS=n] takes the cache's share of the sweep once idle past 12 h (GUESS). It is refused while any cargo/rustc/clippy/llvm-cov process runs, and a build directory a live process or a live run member holds is kept whole.
decisions.why: This is the cleanup the GM asked for. Not deleting under a running build is a physical constraint: deleting there would corrupt it and force the cold rebuild the GM's 'reusing the same build cache' point warns against. The floor still catches a machine that is never idle. The machine-wide refusal is broader than the per-target in_use check strictly needs, but that is a design choice and not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: A build directory is live when its name belongs to a clone, the mirror, a clone's -land/-tooling/-land-tooling, or a registered worktree whose tree exists. Because four worktrees share 'wt', its cache stays while any of them exists.
decisions.why: This fixes a measured defect, the old rule judging 'wt' dead, and keeps the cache that live work reuses, which is the GM's stated intention.

decisions.summary: A build directory goes whole only when no code path builds into its name AND every tree its dep-info names is gone. One with no dep-info cannot be proven dead and is kept. rc, clone and tree are kept; head is taken.
decisions.why: It narrows the cleanup: some directories that may be dead are kept. The GM's own words imply the exception: 'your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken... you have correctly understood my intention'. The measured case shows what the literal reading would do. Presumed-dead deletion would have taken rc (11 GB, a live scratch clone's checks target) plus clone and tree, which current code builds into, and that is the cold-rebuild cost the GM accepted as a reason. The purpose ('not have 30 gigs... eaten without us realizing it') is still met for what is kept, because the floor refuses and names the largest build directories, live or dead. The exception covers three cases, ruled separately: (a) a name a code path builds into is reused by construction, so legitimate; (b) a tree its dep-info names still exists is live by evidence, so legitimate; (c) no dep-info, so nothing to prove from, kept and surfaced by the floor's listing, legitimate on the same 'no loss of the cache' ground and bounded by the floor.

decisions.summary: Keep each crate's newest SIXTEEN variants, not four, restating the task line's 'the newest per crate' as a count. KEPT 4 -> 16.
decisions.why: It keeps more than the task line's literal 'newest' would. Applied literally, that rule defeats the purpose the GM endorsed, reusing the build cache. It was measured: one landing gate touched 13 live l7r_mode_a variants, so keeping one or four takes variants a live build is using and forces rebuilds. The size budget still takes every variant past sixteen when the cache is over 100 GB, and the floor still refuses, so the GM's 'without us realizing it' purpose is not gutted. The task line is the session's wording, not the GM's; the GM's words do not fix a count.

decisions.summary: Past L7R_CACHE_BUDGET_GB (100, GUESS), the cleanup and the day's sweep take every dead tree's directory and every variant past sixteen, whatever its age. They never take one in use and never run while a build runs.
decisions.why: This adds cleanup in service of the request. The 100 GB knob is marked GUESS and is backed by dated du figures.

decisions.summary: The day's sweep removes this uid's /tmp/t<N>... and /tmp/tmp.* idle past 24 h (GUESS), and session task outputs idle past 24 h, a live session's included. A held-open output, and an entry holding a registered worktree, stay.
decisions.why: This is file-system cleanup the GM asked for. Keeping files that are held open or that hold a worktree prevents breaking live work; it is not a carve-out from 'clean up'. The 24 h split carries the host's dated measurement.

decisions.summary: A session's first prompt starts the sweep. The plan hooks it on the same UserPromptSubmit event that clone-sync uses, but from the sweep's own guard rather than from a call inside clone_sync_hooks. The plan labels this a deviation from the task line's '(the clone-sync prompt hook)'.
decisions.why: Ruled as the plan asks. It narrows nothing: the trigger is the same (a session's first prompt), the effect is the same (the sweep starts however recent the day's sweep was), and only the file the call sits in differs. No case the task line covers goes unswept, so it is not an exception and needs no ruling. Keeping the period, lock and detached start in one place is a placement choice. The GM asked for the cleanup, not for its host module.

decisions.summary: After a successful make land, the landed tasks' /tmp/t<N>* are removed. When another feature started a task of the same number within the day, removal is left to the 24 h age rule, and the plan says so.
decisions.why: The cleanup still happens, by the age rule within a day, so nothing is left uncleaned. Removing at once would delete another feature's live scratch (measured: 449 T158 and 451 T158 share /tmp/t158), which is destroying work, not cleaning up after ourselves.

decisions.summary: A scratch worktree is removed only when it is idle 24 h, not held, its HEAD is on a ref, and git worktree remove takes it without --force. Every other worktree is named with its idle hours, its build directory and the --force command, not removed. The plan labels this decision.
decisions.why: It narrows the cleanup: dirty or ref-less idle worktrees, and their build directories, which stay live through the registered-name rule, are named rather than removed. Removing a worktree with uncommitted files or a commit no ref holds destroys work that cannot be recovered. 'Clean up after ourselves' does not reach that, and the plan records that it cannot tell which task made a worktree, so it cannot tell whether anyone still wants it. The earlier review's concern, 'naming is an instruction, not the cleanup', is answered two ways. Every worktree that can be removed without loss now is removed. And the rest is not left to an instruction: the floor refuses done/land/closing-checks and names them, so 'without us realizing it' holds as real enforcement.

decisions.summary: The scratch-sweep guard's unit tests now use fixture paths for the cache, clones, mirror and /tmp, not the machine's real ones. This fixes the real worktree /tmp/t216/wt that a test removed.
decisions.why: This fixes a defect found in the task, an instance of the cleanup reaching real data. It is fixed here and not deferred.

decisions.summary: The clone's guard build link failure was fixed by hand (tool-profile artifacts and incremental sessions removed, rebuilt). No rule is added because its cause is not proven.
decisions.why: The defect, a build that fails, is fixed in this task. Adding no rule for an unproven cause is not a defect left unfixed.

decisions.summary: The task is classed 'Performance work? no' (disk hygiene); the gate's cost is one df.
decisions.why: The GM's words on T158 ask for cleanup and do not call it performance or measurement work. Classing it this way narrows nothing T158 was asked to do.

decisions.summary: The trial's verdict: do not build. The gate (make done / make land) runs no plain `rust test` build; coverage already answers for the plain run (449 T111 keep_tests, 451 T57 unit_tests_only), so the candidate saves 0 min.
decisions.why: The task was a trial (measure first) on whether a plain test build could be dropped where coverage runs the same tests. Finding it already dropped and saying so is the green exit, measured by recipe reads and Phase lines with no build line under done/land but the counting crates'. It answers the GM's 'how much time are we spending on recompiling things' and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The counting build (test-counters on pool, phases, mode_a) is kept, not dropped: it runs 13 tests the default build does not and is the counters-inert check's job.
decisions.why: The candidate was to drop a build where coverage runs the SAME tests. The counting build does not run the same tests (counted 59/54, 339/335, 134/130), so it is outside the candidate by its own terms. Keeping it keeps an existing check working and does not narrow what was asked.

decisions.summary: The builders' own `make rust-test` builds (61.1 of the window's 75.7 build machine-minutes) are outside the gate; whether they could share the coverage build is not measured here and nothing is proposed.
decisions.why: T154's question is the gate's build. Stating where the rest of the build time sits, and declining to propose a change on an unmeasured premise, keeps to the trial form and to the measure-first rule. The time is already measured by the Phase lines (FR-003), so 'everything measured' is not narrowed. Whether to file a follow-up on builder builds is scheduling, not a fidelity question for this section.

decisions.summary: The task line's 78 / 54 machine-minutes and this window's 122 / 121 are given side by side, not reconciled, because the task line's method is not recorded.
decisions.why: A presentation choice about a premise that does not decide the verdict (the verdict rests on the recipes read and on no plain build Phase line in the gate). Both figures carry a date and a method or say that none is recorded. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The cold run used `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust <step>` in the gate's order in a detached worktree, not `make done`, so that the trial commits no run record.
decisions.why: A choice of measuring method that keeps the trial from committing. It measures the same phases, and the worktree and its 19 GB target directory were removed afterwards. Not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: A fresh tree's coverage run is red on rust/mode_a (armory test reads two .gitignored generated SVGs, NotFound). Not fixed here; filed as T159, ordered to land before T148.
decisions.why: This is a defect (a check that refuses good work in a new tree), so leaving it unfixed in this task is a narrowing and is ruled on. It is legitimate: the section is a trial that changes no code, the defect is not dropped but filed as T159 with a stated reason and a stated order ('lands before T148', the first task that builds in fresh trees, so the defect cannot bite before it is fixed), which meets FR-009's form. Fix-as-we-go asks that a step's known defects be fixed before the next step begins, and that order does exactly that.

decisions.summary: T155 is run as a trial: measure a landing's duplicate build and two candidates (sccache, building at the clone's path), no code changed.
decisions.why: Measuring where the time goes is performance work by FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-22 words ('we want everything measured so we know where our time goes, especially for compiling'). Measuring before building narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Verdict (a): no content-keyed compilation cache is built, because it hit 0 times across the two paths, coverage units are uncacheable under it, and 0.13 has no base-directory option.
decisions.why: The task's own goal (Approach item 1: a landing compiles nothing the clone already compiled) is left unmet by this candidate, so it is a narrowing; but the candidate is measured to be physically unable to deliver: 0 hits at the second path, every coverage unit 'multiple input files', and even with a base-directory option the ceiling is rlibs only, bought with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 in every builder's loop, which would slow the loop the GM asked to speed. Physically impossible as it stands, not merely awkward.

decisions.summary: Verdict (b): the landing is not built at the clone's path in the clone's target directory, because mtime freshness across two trees reuses the clone's build of a different copy - a red tree passed cover clean.
decisions.why: Adjudicated separately from (a). Building it would defeat the request's own purpose: the GM asked for performance improvements and for enforcement that is real, and a landing whose tests run the clone builders' code instead of the commit's is a check that passes bad work - a defect, measured on a deliberate hazard (red probe passes at the clone's path, fails in its own directory). The saving it offers is exactly the units it can reuse wrongly. Refusing a change that weakens the gate is not carving out a case contrary to what was asked.

decisions.summary: The residual duplicate (the l7r-rust tool binary rebuilt per target directory, 0.66 min on pair 1 when a gate crate moved; pair 2's 5.15 ceiling, partly the setup's hand edit) is judged too little and too narrow for a follow-up; none is proposed.
decisions.why: It leaves a measured cost, not a defect: no map reads wrong, no check passes bad work or refuses good work. FR-013 orders performance work first; it does not oblige filing every measured residue, and the GM's request asks for numbers to decide on, which this trial gives with methods. The 5.15 is reachable only through sccache with an option it lacks plus incremental off everywhere (D2a), so it is not an open route. The figures are recorded, so the call can be revisited.

decisions.summary: pool's maps::tests::the_launcher_runs_the_gate_script failing 'Text file busy' under load is left unfixed in this trial, filed as T160, to land before T148.
decisions.why: A defect (a gate red on a test that is not broken) found by the trial, deferred in FR-009's own form: why not here (a trial changes no engine code), its filed id (T160) and its order ('lands before T148', the task whose side-by-side gates would raise the race). FR-009 is the spec's provision for exactly this; nothing in the request requires a measurement task to fix a defect it stumbled on in another crate.

decisions.summary: Constraints: the trial form, FR-013, kept results keyed by contents and seeded by land-alone.sh, constitution XIII, and 'a copied cache is no answer' attributed to the GM's 2026-11-22 words.
decisions.why: The constraint decides nothing here: no candidate examined or excluded is a copied cache, and the heading's own premise (fingerprints carry absolute paths) makes a copied target directory moot. Note for the author: 'a copied cache is no answer' is a reading of the GM accepting the session's unquoted points ('your points about reusing the same build cache ... are well taken'), not his words; labeling it G overstates it, but it narrows nothing in this section.

decisions.summary: After 451 T154, before any build follow-up (none proposed); green exit = measurement recorded with its verdict; red exit = set down with an arbiter-ask; budget one landing.
decisions.why: Ordering and exits of a measurement task; nothing the request or spec constrains is narrowed.

decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-22 purpose is that disk is not eaten 'without us realizing it'; the large artifacts (target directories, cache) were removed and checked, and the package left is recorded, so it does not gut that purpose. Measured against the request, it serves the purpose of a per-task breakdown: with several builders in one clone the mark booked one builder's edits to another task and refused a CLEAR landing, and a line left unbooked is honest where a wrong booking corrupts both the breakdown and land-alone's split. Two new rungs (the builder reading and the page-session brief) keep correct bookings coming in, so the request's per-task attribution is not narrowed.

decisions.summary: make verify T= runs the bundle's own files in a separate review tree so other builders' edits in the clone cannot turn its gate red, void its verdicts or hide a stale engine; classed performance work
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work making the builders' loop or the gate faster as performance work; the observed T312/T289 incidents (gate reruns, seven voided reviews, hours waiting on a stale engine) are time lost in the loop of the bundled work the GM asked for (2026-11-22, T141). All four harms in the header (red/tree-moved gate, voided verdicts, stale-engine wait, silently dropped units) are each answered by the Approach.

decisions.summary: the bundle's files are taken by land-alone's split, read from scripts/land-alone.sh, not re-implemented
decisions.why: an implementation choice inside the task; narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: temporary commit on HEAD through a scratch index; clone HEAD and index untouched
decisions.why: mechanism of the task; serves the goal that the review stands on the bundle's own work.

decisions.summary: one review tree per clone (<clone>-review) with its own cargo target and its own .gencache, added once then reset each run and kept, never piled up (9.3 GB, 64-67 GB free throughout, measured 2026-11-22)
decisions.why: the GM's 2026-11-22 purpose is that disk is not eaten 'without us realizing it'; the tree is bounded to one per clone, reused rather than multiplied, its size measured and stated, and T158's floor and cleanup named as a constraint. Keeping it is what makes the warm gate about a minute rather than a cold build, so keeping is the reuse the GM endorsed, not a departure.

decisions.summary: the review tree does not share the landing target
decisions.why: it stands against the GM's 2026-11-22 'your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken' (the session's points themselves are not quoted in the bundle). Ground: measured on a scratch copy, cargo judged l7r_guard Fresh across worktrees whose pair_hooks/review.rs and state.rs differ, so a shared target makes the gate judge other code - applying reuse here would defeat the gate's own purpose and the GM's 2026-11-22 cleanup aim is still met by bounding the tree to one. Reuse is kept where it is sound: the content-keyed rust-checks and hooks-test results are seeded from the clone.

decisions.summary: the clone's 6.2 GB .gencache is no longer seeded into the review tree; the tree keeps its own across resets
decisions.why: also against 'reusing the same build cache' (the session's points not quoted in the bundle). Ground: impossibility, observed - entries are keyed by the engine binary's build id, which embeds the tree's source path, so ids never match across trees; of 31,067 seeded entries none served a map. Removing it removes 19.2 s and 6.2 GB of work that reused nothing, which serves both the cleanup and performance requests.

decisions.summary: reviews prereq and the pair guard judge a snapshotted unit by the review tree's record (gate at its key), every other unit by the clone's stamp as before; agent files read review-paired-gate UNIT=
decisions.why: keeps the review paired with the gate (feature 151) while judging the bundle's own tree; the agent-file fix closes the path by which the incident would recur. Note: the search for bare review-paired-gate callers is stated as grep -rn over .claude/agents, rust/, scripts/ - the Makefile, docs/, tests/, CLAUDE.md and the rest of .claude/ are not shown as searched; a reach gap in the enumeration, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: reviews owed names a map not current with its stale engine and the units it hides (owed/hidden.rs)
decisions.why: answers the T289 harm (a stale engine waited on and new-element units dropped without a word).

decisions.summary: bare make verify refused, naming T=; REVIEW_TREE_OK= escape
decisions.why: a refusal naming the compliant command with a reason escape per the project's guard rules; T= kept working for the 449 sheet bundle.

decisions.summary: after T160/T161, before the 449 sheet bundle's make verify T=
decisions.why: dependency order; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: engine_freeze_hooks still holds engine edits during a snapshotted review; not changed here, filed T165, lands before T154
decisions.why: T164 does not make the freeze worse: the freeze's existing hold becomes unnecessary for snapshotted reviews only, a cost and not a wrong verdict, and changing a guard's rule needs its own measurement (a review beside an engine edit keeping its verdict). FR-009's three parts are present: why not here, filed id T165, and its order 'lands before T154'. Deferral to a filed, ordered performance task narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: the review tree's make done writes the shared gate-green stamps; left as is and the claim restated
decisions.why: each stamp is a content key compared with HEAD's key at push, so an overwritten stamp is a missed reuse at most, never a wrong pass - a difference, not a defect (constitution XIV), and restating the claim is the prescribed handling.

decisions.summary: review-tree.sh gains # TOOL_RECORD: naming its record file and the event log
decisions.why: the GM 2026-11-22: 'we want everything measured so we know where our time goes'.

decisions.summary: red-first run in the review tree at HEAD with only test files over it, reusing its warm target rather than a third cold build
decisions.why: a method choice for the red-first evidence; the red results are recorded.

decisions.summary: Fix gate-write refusing a make behind more than 120 characters of VAR=value prefixes as a shell write of '.' while a gate runs.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T171's section as it stands
No time-window matcher ties a detached run (no harness ancestor, no launch line) to a builder; such a run still refuses the Stop.
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md or the spec asks for detached runs to be attributed by timing. A run with no pid ancestry and no launch line cannot be tied to a builder except by a guess. The class the matcher would serve was measured as gone: 8 detached verify-gate refusals before T164, none after, and 1 refusal since T164, which was the race fix 1 fixes (dated and with its method). FR-008 (spec-index) refuses any other backgrounded make or cargo run. Leaving these runs refused keeps the guard's existing behavior and narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: An unnamed depth-1 agent holds a builder slot only if its type is general-purpose; typed check agents (round-arbiter, spec-fidelity) take no slot.
decisions.why: This narrows the task line's words ('an agent whose description names no task still counts as a builder'). The exception is already implied by the accepted spec: FR-006 defines a builder as 'an agent dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent'. The block should have cited FR-006; it cites only T88. The purpose test also holds. Fix 2 exists so the slot count sees the builders it missed. Counting a round arbiter as a builder would read three builders running while a builder slot was free, and let the turn end over the empty slot that T88's rolling dispatch exists to fill. The rule's reach past the two types named (every other non-general-purpose type) rests on the measurement: on the 69 slot refusals, the unnamed running depth-1 agents were general-purpose 37 times and round-arbiter 11 times, and no other type appeared (dated, /tmp/t171/slots.py).

decisions.summary: Only agents at spawnDepth 1 (dispatched by the session itself) are counted as unnamed builders; a builder's own sub-agents take no slot.
decisions.why: A builder is an agent the session dispatched: FR-006's 'an agent dispatched with a task's brief', and the block's T88 reading. A depth-2 agent works inside its builder's slot. Counting it separately would overcount and refuse nothing wrongly removed. This narrows nothing in the request or the spec.

decisions.summary: A run whose launch line names another session is Status::Session; this session's turn closes and the context line names the owning session.
decisions.why: The guard's job is that a session does not end its turn over a run it started. A refusal over another session's run is a wrong outcome (block item 12), and fixing it serves FR-013's faster builders' loop. The run is still named in the context line, and nothing in request.md or the spec asks that a session be held over another's run.

decisions.summary: still_running follows an unnamed agent up parentAgentId at most HOPS=4, a labeled CONVENTION; a sub-agent's run is waited on while it runs and judged detached once it stops.

decisions.summary: Procs::gone drops a pid whose stat is gone or a zombie's, so a run that ended while /proc was read is no run.
decisions.why: This fixes a measured defect: 2 refusals with 'output in (no file)', dated, with their method. A wrong refusal is removed and no watched run is released.

decisions.summary: An unchanged refusal is said in full once, then as one line 'still: <first 8 words> - unchanged since HH:MM' that is still exit 2. It is said in full again on a changed text, on a block back after a passing Stop, with no session id, or when the record cannot be read or written.
decisions.why: This serves the GM's 2026-11-23 ask: 'could we accomplish the same thing with no loss of fidelity and fewer tokens?' The repeat is still a refusal, so it does the same thing. The text appears in full whenever it differs from what this session was last told, and on every failure path. The repeat stands only while that same full text was already said to this session in this block, and the block measures a 32% cut in the Stop blocks' characters. On what the block states, no fidelity is lost.

decisions.summary: The one-line repeat carries the refusal's first 8 words, a labeled CONVENTION.
decisions.why: This is the form of the summary line, labeled with its reason. It narrows nothing the request or the spec asks for.

decisions.summary: Measure which guard messages cost most (count x length), shorten the top ones keeping every fix command and escape, and hold every suite-rendered message to a budget and a content-keyed review instead of a per-hook comment

A budget check plus a content-keyed review enforces the same thing mechanically and cannot drift from the text the way a comment can. Every new or changed wording is held to it.

decisions.summary: Mid-task notice in full once, then a 53-character line while unchanged; said in full again after a sync, a failed refresh or a SessionStart

decisions.summary: Seven rewrite notices say what was done and what to do; the history moves to the code comment
decisions.why: Fewer tokens. The actionable content is kept.

decisions.summary: Notice trimmed from 278 to 248 characters
decisions.why: Fewer tokens.

decisions.why: This is the subagent review the GM asked for. Declining one cut keeps a piece of information the reader needs (no loss of fidelity), and the reviewer later passed it.

decisions.summary: NOTICE_BUDGET 900 and REFUSE_BUDGET 1,800, labeled GUESS and set from the longest rendered wordings rounded up

decisions.summary: Classed as performance work under FR-013

decisions.summary: T165 withdrawn as done by T175: a review naming a review tree holds only edits inside it, one naming none and the rolls hold the clone; nothing built.
decisions.why: T165's ask, as the block quotes it, is to narrow the engine freeze to reviews with no review-tree snapshot (and the rolls). The block shows the snapshot and the prompt line T175 keys on are written under one condition (a non-empty --commit), so T175's rule is that ask; it is backed by a measured live case (449 T383's two reviews kept PASS at the tree's key while five rust/ files were edited, no engine-freeze firing since T175 landed against 20 before it, 2026-11-23) and the engine-freeze suite green. Withdrawing a task whose ask is already met drops nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: review-tree.sh carries its bundle to reviews owed --check-declared by L7R_VERIFY_STARTED, read in place of the clone's shared active-task mark; a gate built before reads the mark as before; no feature dir or no task falls back to the mark's rule.
decisions.why: The measurement restates T166's cause (the shared mark moved by another session's set-down or task-start, not a worktree lacking the mark) and the fix targets that cause, so verify judges the bundle it verifies. The environment-variable route and the fallbacks preserve existing behavior for old gates and undeclared cases; nothing the task asked for is dropped. Pinned red-first by a crate test and a suite case.

decisions.summary: Of the carried bundle, only the FIRST task counts as the started one (a CONVENTION); a declared line naming only the bundle's second task is refused.
decisions.why: The first-task rule already exists: make task-start marks a bundle by its first task, 449 T238 round 2 answers a line naming the started task, and the landing's holding box reads the same. T166 changes WHERE the started task is read from (the carried bundle, not the shared mark), not WHICH task counts; neither request.md nor FR-013 says which of a bundle's tasks answers. The block's 'algorithmically easier' remark is not the ground for this class - the ground is that verify and the landing keep one rule, so verify does not pass what the landing then refuses.

decisions.summary: reviews owed's listing in the review tree reads the active features without the carried bundle; left unfixed.
decisions.why: No wrong outcome is measured: the three review commits observed (36fa41f4cc, 48103d14e6, d80ff6a0dd, git show --stat, 2026-11-23) each carry their feature's tasks.md, and the pointer names one feature for all builders. A hypothetical gap with no wrong outcome is not a defect (constitution XIV v2.36.0), so leaving it is not a narrowing and FR-009's defect-deferral form does not reach it.

decisions.summary: test-l7r-guard.sh's locked case times the no-binary path three times and bounds the locked call at three times the slowest, never under the old 1 s (a CONVENTION from CLAUDE.md's calibration loop); the live wrapper untouched.
decisions.why: The goal is a suite that fails only when a call waits on another's build. The bound keeps the 1 s as its floor, so it is no looser idle, and the waiting mutant (flock -w 5) still fails it idle; red 10/10 unfixed and green 10/10 fixed under a pinned load (measured 2026-11-23). The check still catches what it is for; nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T183's section as it stands

Every Stop/SubagentStop answer is classed as (a) must-do-before-stopping or (b) a nudge. The free-slot, open-task and parked-stages answers are (b) and leave the Stop block, and the free slot also gets no notice. QUESTION/OFFER UNFILTERED, kept-unnamed, run-still-going, dispatch-dropped, wakeup and builder-stop stay unchanged.
decisions.why: The approved offer is 'Stop hooks block only for what the session must do before stopping'. Each kept block concerns something to settle before stopping: the final message, a run nothing will wake, a dropped dispatch, a stale wakeup, or a builder's own SubagentStop. The (b) blocks are the 'keep working' nudges the GM wanted off the Stop. Unchanged from round 1 except that the free slot now has no notice (see D10).

decisions.summary: The periodic check is a second Stop entry with asyncRewake, where exit 2 wakes the session. It is not a cron.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1. A cron fire always submits a prompt, which would defeat the GM's 'does nothing and adds nothing to the context if we are still active'. asyncRewake is the documented way to stay silent and wake only when idle.

decisions.id: D3 one check per Stop, 300 s wait, 420 s timeout
decisions.summary: Each Stop arms one check that waits L7R_IDLE_CHECK_SECS, a GUESS of 300 s. The check is silent if the transcript gained a user or assistant record since, and the timeout is 420 s.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1. This is the GM's 'every 5 minutes'. Every idle stretch begins at a Stop, and each Stop arms one check.

decisions.id: D4 silent for any background_tasks entry and for a sub-agent stop
decisions.summary: The check is silent at once when background_tasks names a shell, subagent, monitor or workflow, and on a sub-agent's stop.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1. The offer says 'silent while ... waiting on a tracked agent', and each of these tracked runs wakes the session when it ends. The plan prices the long-lived-monitor seam.

decisions.id: D5 feature holds from the newest ask:set-down ruling, read by prose
decisions.summary: A feature is held when its newest ask:set-down-... ruling (continue or accept) says no new, other or further task starts, or sets the feature down. Only a later set-down ruling ends the hold.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1. This carries 'respects binding rulings and set-downs' for feature-wide holds. How the reader classes one particular ruling on record is ruled separately as D11.

decisions.summary: A task the newest set-down ruling holds by name, through its do-not-start clause, is never the idle check's next task. A range counts each member. With only held tasks open the check is silent, and a later set-down ruling ends the hold. This is holds::named, pinned in tests/idle.rs. make task-start's picker does not read it.
decisions.why: Round 1's cure is applied as asked. The held task can no longer be named as 'the next', and a feature whose only open tasks are held stays silent. That carries 'respects binding rulings' for named tasks. Leaving task-start alone adds no refusal the GM did not ask for. The rule that a task named elsewhere in a ruling is not held is right in general: the 451 and 449-rows rulings name the tasks to go on with. Whether one particular ruling's other clauses hold its tasks or its feature is D11.

decisions.id: D7 task-start never reads a hold
decisions.summary: Holds silence the nudges only. make task-start's refusal does not consult them.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1. The GM asked for the nudges to respect rulings, not for a new task-start refusal.

decisions.id: D8 findings guard on the session's own dispatch, once
decisions.summary: FINDINGS UNFILTERED arms only on a review the main session dispatched. It is silent while that review is out and fires once after it returns.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1. This is the approved offer word for word.

decisions.id: D9 open-task nudge once while unchanged
decisions.summary: The open-task words are said only when the session is idle with nothing tracked and no ruling or set-down holding, and only once while the state is unchanged. They name the next task in FR-013's performance-first order.
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1. This matches 'speaks only when it is idle with actionable work and respects binding rulings and set-downs'.

decisions.id: D10 free slot named by nothing while builders run
decisions.summary: The free-slot nudge is removed entirely: no Stop block and no report-back notice. A freed slot goes unnamed until the session is idle with nothing tracked running, when the open-task block names the next task. This retires 451 T88's rolling-dispatch block, L7R_BUILDERS and the busy-file reading, and the occupancy cost is recorded as unmeasured.
decisions.why: Round 1's cure is applied. The inventory row, the after-row, the performance checklist and the Accepted limitation all say no block and no notice. This is the approved offer's own silence 'while ... waiting on a tracked agent' and the GM's 'adds nothing to the context if we are still active'. Retiring T88's nudge follows from that, and no requirement in spec-cited.md or spec-index.md carries a rolling dispatch or a builder count (a grep for slot, rolling and BUILDERS finds none). The lower occupancy is a cost recorded honestly, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.id: D11 the 449-pilot ruling's set-down and T171 read as no hold
decisions.summary: The Holds paragraph pins ask:set-down-449-pilot as 'the named-task hold'. It is not among the 6 feature holds, it holds only T150-T158, and T171 is never held ('never a task named elsewhere in the ruling (its T171)').
decisions.why: That ruling's what says, in item 2, 'Leave T171 open as filed' (its why: 'leaving the line as it is for a few hours costs nothing'). Item 4 says 'Then set down. The work resumes from the GM's reply to the pilot report and to the for_gm question below.' Item 4 sets the feature down until the GM replies, and the plan's own hold test in D5 is 'or sets the feature down'. As the paragraph is written and pinned, with this ruling newest and T171 or any other 449 task open, the idle check would say 'start' a task the ruling held. That is round 1's D6 failure one task over, against the approved 'respects binding rulings and set-downs'. No route makes it legitimate. Reading item 4 is not impossible, since the reader already matches 'sets the feature down'. Nothing in the GM's words implies a set-down clause be ignored. And honoring it defeats nothing: silence is what the request asks for. The ruling is no longer 449's newest, since the 2026-11-23 rows ruling supersedes it, so this costs nothing today. But it is the pinned reading of a set-down ruling on record, and a ruling of the same shape would be misread. Cure, either: (1) count this ruling among the feature holds by its item 4 'Then set down' and pin it that way in tests/idle.rs, which also keeps T171 from being named; or (2) state in the Holds paragraph why item 4 does not set the feature down and why item 2's 'Leave T171 open as filed' does not hold T171. Do not change the general rule about tasks named elsewhere, which (2) does not ask for.

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: measure first (the replay over the clone's check state, replies and event logs) before the rules
decisions.why: Measurement before a rule is how the GM asked for this work to go (the convergence talk opens 'let's talk about that before we do literally anything else'). The replay's arithmetic holds (115+103+499+829=1546; 35+34+31+11+2+2=115; 17+8=25; 115-31=84), and it is labeled as a floor with its date and method.

decisions.summary: T188: the category rule applies per EDIT, not per reply. In a mixed round the wording EDITs (and GLOSSARY) go first, fingerprints are read (mid), then the factual ones. Only a unit that wording alone moved settles
decisions.why: This carries 'only factual findings cascade' as stated: a unit that a factual EDIT moved still re-owes. A per-reply rule would either skip factual changes or re-owe wording, and both would break the GM's rule.

decisions.summary: T188: an EDIT whose check or category is not given is factual, and a reply naming no check settles as before
decisions.why: A fail-safe default: a mislabel costs a round and never skips a factual review, which keeps what the GM's rule protects (factual inaccuracies still cascade).

decisions.summary: T188: the wording classes (never re-owe): modal-form, record-format (VOCABULARY, SESSION NOTE, HISTORY), record-style, intro-check
decisions.why: These are the GM's 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies'. modal-form's contract already says a replacement only rewords, and the others are presentation or the order of words. A claim that one of them changes is not part of this table: it is factual by the untold/factual side, and each check's own contract binds it.

decisions.summary: T188: a modal-depiction LINKS EDIT (a pointer to a drawing page) is wording and does not cascade
decisions.why: Judged on its own, apart from the style checks. The GM's own words on splits cover it: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page ... nothing needs to cascade'. A pointer to a drawing states no fact. What a statement rests on (REFERENCES) and what a drawing shows (COVERAGE, TRUTH) stay factual, so the seam is drawn on the fact line.

decisions.summary: T188: factual (may cascade): modal-research ACCURACY/REFERENCES/GAPS, modal-depiction COVERAGE/TRUTH, quote-check, source-reader, translation-check, entry-drift
decisions.why: These are the 'factual inaccuracies' the GM said cascading is for. Putting GAPS (a statement added) on the factual side is conservative.

decisions.summary: T188: quote-check's units stay on settle_quotes, which re-owes a unit whose quoted words changed, whoever changed them (a wording EDIT included)
decisions.why: A wording EDIT can still re-owe quote-check here, so this is a carve-out from 'wording never re-owes'. It is implied by the GM's own approved sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review': changed quoted words change the claim about what a source says, which is a factual matter. A unit whose quoted words and claim held is already settled, so the GM's purpose (no rounds that fix nothing) is kept.

decisions.summary: T188: no change for building-review (error/questionable/nitpick/outside) or impl-drift (IN-STEP/DRIFTED/MISLABELED)
decisions.why: Taken one check at a time. Neither applies EDITs through make apply-edits. building-review is re-owed by the sheet's own fingerprint, and impl-drift by the code's and claims' fingerprints. A record or pop-up wording EDIT, the cascade the GM described ('a page edit re-owes checks on every pop-up citing it'), moves neither fingerprint, so the rule has nothing there to act on. The plan does not narrow the rule here: the cascade it targets does not pass through these checks.

decisions.summary: T188: only modal-depiction's contract gains a category in its EDIT header; every other check is one class throughout
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for telling modal-depiction's mixed classes apart. For every other check, the check's name already says its class.

decisions.summary: T189: a later round's bundle gains 'The change since round <n>', which pairs every changed run of lines since what the last round was bundled (EDITs and hand edits alike). The instruction is to judge only whether the change made something wrong, and the whole unit stays for context
decisions.why: This is 're-reviews scoped to the change'. Including hand edits makes the pairing complete rather than narrow. The scope reaches the reviewer as an instruction: what a reviewer judges cannot be enforced mechanically, and the 11-19 'real enforcement' approval was about the six improvements' guards. The mechanical part, the paired change in the bundle, is built.

decisions.summary: T189: a subject whose last round was bundled before the keeping gets no change section and reads the whole unit unscoped, as before
decisions.why: A transitional carve-out from 'scoped to the change'. What such a round was handed was never kept (the plan's premise: the bundle is overwritten on regeneration, and uncommitted EDITs and hand edits are not in git), so 'every change since the last round' cannot be paired for it. Telling a reviewer to judge ONLY a pairing that might miss a change would let an unpaired claim change through unreviewed, which defeats the GM's sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. The carve-out ends by itself: that round writes the kept bundle, so each subject is scoped from its next round on.

decisions.summary: T190: apply_edits/settled.rs refuses, before applying anything, an EDIT whose new text is an earlier round's EDIT's old text and whose old text is that EDIT's new text
decisions.why: This is 'settled choices stay settled' for the review rounds' oscillation that the GM raised under 'On oscillation and review scope'. It is a real refusal with a red-first test (the refusal off: failed).

decisions.summary: T190: the refusal uses the exact put-back test; the looser near_reversal (two content words back) stays a mark
decisions.why: Measured on 2026-11-23 over 1,670 EDITs: 3 were exact put-backs, and the loose test named 17 more that read as factual rounds widening a sentence. Refusing on the loose test would block factual corrections, which defeats the purpose the GM gave ('we are only interested in factual inaccuracies'). The near cases remain visible as marks.

decisions.summary: T190: a put-back is let through only when its finding carries 'REVERSES round <n>:' and an 'evidence:' quoting the words or naming the page, and its check's category is factual. A wording put-back has no way through
decisions.why: An exception to 'settled choices stay settled', taken on its own. Refusing every put-back of a settled fact would lock in a factual error that an earlier round introduced, which defeats the GM's stated purpose (fixing real flaws, factual inaccuracies). Requiring the stated error and its evidence keeps settled wording settled and allows no escape for style. FR-012's escape requirement covers the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, not this one, so leaving wording without an escape conflicts with no requirement.

decisions.summary: T190 (found and left): no refusal on the Edit tool for hand put-backs
decisions.why: Judged on the replay alone, case by case, not on the cited reversal:<file> rulings, which the bundle does not carry. In 24 of the 25 measured Edit-tool A->B->A put-backs a builder was revising its own code with no round between: nothing was settled. In the 1 (no_poll_hooks.rs) spec-fidelity replies came between, but no check's EDIT was involved: a spec review settles no code wording. The GM's rule sits under 'oscillation and review scope', that is, rounds undoing rounds, and that is refused at apply-edits. A hand edit of a record page is not a round's choice, and T189 still hands it to the next round as a paired change to judge.

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: filed as [perf] tasks; the saving is stated as a floor of 84 of 115 wording-only later rounds, and the rest is a GUESS to be measured after landing
decisions.why: FR-013 counts the builders' loop and review rounds as performance work. The figures carry their date and method, and the unmeasured part is labeled GUESS.
