decisions.summary: T189: a later round's bundle gains 'The change since round <n>', which pairs every changed run of lines since what the last round was bundled (EDITs and hand edits alike). The instruction is to judge only whether the change made something wrong, and the whole unit stays for context
decisions.why: This is 're-reviews scoped to the change'. Including hand edits makes the pairing complete rather than narrow. The scope reaches the reviewer as an instruction: what a reviewer judges cannot be enforced mechanically, and the 11-19 'real enforcement' approval was about the six improvements' guards. The mechanical part, the paired change in the bundle, is built.

decisions.summary: T189: a subject whose last round was bundled before the keeping gets no change section and reads the whole unit unscoped, as before
decisions.why: A transitional carve-out from 'scoped to the change'. What such a round was handed was never kept (the plan's premise: the bundle is overwritten on regeneration, and uncommitted EDITs and hand edits are not in git), so 'every change since the last round' cannot be paired for it. Telling a reviewer to judge ONLY a pairing that might miss a change would let an unpaired claim change through unreviewed, which defeats the GM's sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. The carve-out ends by itself: that round writes the kept bundle, so each subject is scoped from its next round on.

decisions.summary: T190: apply_edits/settled.rs refuses, before applying anything, an EDIT whose new text is an earlier round's EDIT's old text and whose old text is that EDIT's new text
decisions.why: This is 'settled choices stay settled' for the review rounds' oscillation that the GM raised under 'On oscillation and review scope'. It is a real refusal with a red-first test (the refusal off: failed).

decisions.summary: T190: the refusal uses the exact put-back test; the looser near_reversal (two content words back) stays a mark
decisions.why: Measured on 2026-11-23 over 1,670 EDITs: 3 were exact put-backs, and the loose test named 17 more that read as factual rounds widening a sentence. Refusing on the loose test would block factual corrections, which defeats the purpose the GM gave ('we are only interested in factual inaccuracies'). The near cases remain visible as marks.

decisions.summary: T190: a put-back is let through only when its finding carries 'REVERSES round <n>:' and an 'evidence:' quoting the words or naming the page, and its check's category is factual. A wording put-back has no way through
decisions.why: An exception to 'settled choices stay settled', taken on its own. Refusing every put-back of a settled fact would lock in a factual error that an earlier round introduced, which defeats the GM's stated purpose (fixing real flaws, factual inaccuracies). Requiring the stated error and its evidence keeps settled wording settled and allows no escape for style. FR-012's escape requirement covers the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, not this one, so leaving wording without an escape conflicts with no requirement.

decisions.summary: T190 (found and left): no refusal on the Edit tool for hand put-backs
decisions.why: Judged on the replay alone, case by case, not on the cited reversal:<file> rulings, which the bundle does not carry. In 24 of the 25 measured Edit-tool A->B->A put-backs a builder was revising its own code with no round between: nothing was settled. In the 1 (no_poll_hooks.rs) spec-fidelity replies came between, but no check's EDIT was involved: a spec review settles no code wording. The GM's rule sits under 'oscillation and review scope', that is, rounds undoing rounds, and that is refused at apply-edits. A hand edit of a record page is not a round's choice, and T189 still hands it to the next round as a paired change to judge.

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: filed as [perf] tasks; the saving is stated as a floor of 84 of 115 wording-only later rounds, and the rest is a GUESS to be measured after landing
decisions.why: FR-013 counts the builders' loop and review rounds as performance work. The figures carry their date and method, and the unmeasured part is labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: What the 0009 and 0059 cuts lost is restored into the current text, and each page is split along its topics (0009 to new 0332, 0059 to new 0333), with a pointer sentence where the section stood; notes move with their sentences.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-23 approved 'the 0009/0059 repair' and named splitting into multiple entries so all details are preserved; a split with a pointer is his own route ('as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page').

decisions.summary: Three differences the word diff showed (the canal's 'division works', the 'The Chinese articles ...' clause, the Edo weirs' 'large rivers') are treated as earlier checks' corrections, kept and not restored as losses.
decisions.why: A correction to what the source says is not a size cut; keeping it is 'a size edit never changes a claim' and 'settled choices stay settled' from the seven rules the GM approved.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate check question-size (make quick) refuses a SIZE EDIT (page over its limit at the base, or the removed words would put it back over) that drops a claim-bearing token (number, label, quoted passage, proper name, or a negation/qualifier leaving its block) unless it stands on the page or on a page its split pointer names; it names the split.
decisions.why: Mechanical enforcement of exactly the rule the GM approved ('a size edit never changes a claim'; 'no edit to maintain entry size should ever be substantive'); its refusal reaches only size edits, the thing the rule governs. Delete the rule and the check has nothing to check.

decisions.summary: Only the <a class="moved" href="NNNN-<slug>.html"> form counts as a split pointer (the form T185's triage follows); a plain link is refused; the refusal and the three rule files name the form.
decisions.why: Serves the GM's split condition that the original page directs the reader to the full information; one followable form keeps the guard and the no-cascade triage agreeing on what a split is, and narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: SIZE_EDIT_OK="<why>" lets a correction through, printed with the run; 0097's moved-and-rewritten section is its case.
decisions.why: A correction is not a size edit; the project's guard rules require a recorded escape; it does not let a size cut through without a stated reason on the record.

decisions.summary: A page's own limit lives in research/size-limits.json and is read only with the size-exception agent's INDIVISIBLE verdict, its date and ledger row; the 20,000 global cap is unchanged; a divisible page is split instead.
decisions.why: The GM's own option: an audit-based process with an adversarial subagent check that records a new limit for this specific entry. Splitting first where a page divides loses no detail and the audited limit stays open to the page that cannot be split, so the GM's purpose (never lose information to the cap) holds on both routes.

decisions.summary: The guard's token classes are stated (in the docs) to miss a claim carried only in plain words, a scope word outside the classes and a changed term (6 of 14 of the cuts' losses named, measured 2026-11-23); the classes are not tuned to catch them.
decisions.why: No sentence in the blocks permits a size edit to drop a claim: the goal line states the rule whole ('No research page loses a claim to fit the size cap'), the escape is for a correction, not a cut, and item 7 describes the detector's reach, not what the rule allows. The guard is added enforcement of the rule the GM approved 2026-11-23 (which asked for no guard), its misses stated rather than hidden, and on the real trim commit it refused both 0009 and 0059 (the red row, exit 1). A partial backstop is coverage, not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: The guard's firing on 0097 at cce80ca436 (none, not) is left: both claims stand restated on 0331 and 0097, the second a correction to the range the source names.
decisions.why: Observed with a method (grep of the dropped sentences' words), no claim lost, so no defect is left; a correction is the escape's case.

decisions.summary: Pop-ups whose Entry: names 0009 or 0059 for content now on 0332/0333 are not edited.
decisions.why: The GM's words verbatim: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page ... nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs.'

decisions.summary: 0009's heading still ends 'and after the harvest' though that content is now on 0332; the pointer sentence takes the reader there, and a rename would re-owe every Entry: link.
decisions.why: Not a defect under the GM's split ruling: the page directs the reader to where the full information is; leaving it avoids the very cascade the GM asked to stop.

decisions.summary: The registry entry hrr-agagawa-dento's unstated 'on large rivers' and the glossary term 'true leaf' drafted from general botany are fixed in this task by page session.
decisions.why: Defects found by the task's own checks fixed in the task, as the fix-as-we-go rule asks; nothing deferred.

decisions.summary: Page sessions first, then the guard run over their pages as its green fixture; exits are closing-checks green, the record checks recorded, make question-sizes naming none, or a recorded set-down / arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Sequencing and acceptance of the requested repair and rule; decides nothing about scope.

decisions.summary: T184 is classed as performance work for scheduling: a lossy trim is refused at make quick instead of forcing restoration sessions and re-checks later.
decisions.why: The GM framed the cascade as time cost ('very time consuming to make') and said to fix it 'before we do literally anything else'; FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 words on prioritizing performance work cover it.

decisions.summary: A split's pointer is one marked form, <a class="moved" href="NNNN-<slug>[.drawing].html">, which builds as any question link; only that form is followed and lets a removal count as a move.
decisions.why: The GM's condition is that the source page directs a reader to the new page; the marked link does exactly that (it renders as an ordinary link) and adds only a machine-readable mark so the tool can tell which link is the split's. How the condition is detected is left open by the request.

decisions.id: T185-b plain link not a pointer
decisions.summary: A split whose source carries a plain <a href> to the new page (which does direct a reader) is still counted as a removal and still re-owes.
decisions.why: Narrower than the GM's words, so ruled. Treating every plain link as a split pointer would put every page a pop-up's Entry page links to into that pop-up's reach and fingerprint, so an edit of any linked page would re-owe it - a wider cascade than today, defeating the request's own purpose (stop cascades that fix no real flaw). And no real split is left cascading: the 0009/0059 splits are marked before their re-owed checks run, 0097's checks already ran, and the MANIFEST tells every future splitter the form at no cost to them.

decisions.id: T185-c no link stays a removal
decisions.summary: A move with no pointer at all stays a removal and re-owes.
decisions.why: This is the GM's own 'as long as the original page ... directs a reader to the other page' condition, applied literally.

decisions.summary: A pop-up's checks read the pages its pointers name (fingerprints, owed rows, triage pages, research and depiction bundles), so a later edit of a moved block on its new page re-owes the pop-up.
decisions.why: The approved rule is 'a split is a move', not 'moved text is exempt'; a later claim-changing edit of the moved text still triggers review under 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. Keeps the cascade where it can matter.

decisions.summary: A removed block counts as moved only if it stands verbatim on a reached page; a moved block that was also edited is a removal plus a new block.
decisions.why: The GM's exemption is for what cascades 'simply because a split occurs'; text changed in the move is more than a split. Whether a non-verbatim edit changes a claim is other rules' scope (re-classification, size edits), not narrowed here.

decisions.summary: A block carrying only the pointer (no note mark, no figure, at most POINTER_WORDS=25 words beside the link, a GUESS knob) counts as no claim; a longer one is reviewed as a claim.
decisions.why: The pointer block is what the GM's condition requires and is not a claim, so it owes nothing; the cap only stops new prose riding in under a pointer, and new prose is not something the split rule exempts. The 25 is labeled a GUESS knob.

decisions.summary: The claims triage drops the same moves and pointer blocks.
decisions.why: The GM: 'nothing needs to cascade' covers claim checks as well as pop-up checks.

decisions.summary: Record checks need no change: units.rs indexes blocks and notes across every page, so a verbatim move already owes none (observed on the fixture).
decisions.why: No change needed to satisfy the rule; the premise is stated as an observation on the fixture and the plan's test pins the outcome.

decisions.summary: The new page's new heading and intro owe intro-check and record-format on the new page; not suppressed.
decisions.why: Scoped to the new page's new prose, not a re-owe of any pop-up or claim citing the source page; the split rule exempts the moved text, not new writing.

decisions.summary: T184's 0009 and 0059 splits, linked plainly today, are marked class="moved" before any check they re-owed runs (by T184's builder via the handoff if T184 lands second, by T185's own landing otherwise), confirmed by make modal-triage clearing the citing pop-ups.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the 0009/0059 repair' in the same words; this is that repair, ordered so no needless cascade runs.

decisions.summary: 0097's earlier move to 0331 (plain link) is left unmarked; its re-owed checks have already run.
decisions.why: Nothing it re-owed is open, so no cascade is pending. A later edit of the moved text on 0331 will not be followed from 0097, but that is the state before T185 for every page link, not a wrong outcome T185 leaves or causes, and the request asked to retrofit only 0009/0059. Noted as an aside.

decisions.summary: Lands after T186's change computation, which it extends; marked performance work.
decisions.why: Sequencing; FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 words put performance work first, and a split no longer re-owing every citing pop-up is performance work.

decisions.summary: The change computation moves to triage/change.rs; blocks are paired old with new (exact matches dropped, then tool clears, then difflib ratio >= 0.6, PAIR_RATIO taken from the blind test).
decisions.why: Mechanism for the approved first filter and paired-block triage; it decides how to do what was asked, not what is reviewed.

decisions.summary: A block whose claim words, after removing footnote markers and markup (comments, tags, links, glossary marks already gone), are unchanged or empty is cleared by the tool.
decisions.why: This is the GM's own split, verbatim in request.md: 'straightforward adjustments that never could have plausibly needed this kind of cascade', and his approved rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. An edit that leaves no claim word changed is exactly that case.

decisions.summary: An original-language quotation is NOT taken out of claim words, so a corrected quotation still reaches the triage (round 1's BLOCKED ruling, reversed).
decisions.why: Keeps under review an edit that changes what a page says a source says; it restricts the tool's clearing and narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.id: D4 the first filter's three arms
decisions.summary: change::fires sends a page's change on only where (1) a cited note key is gone, (2) the ECHO rule holds, or (3) a new bold-opened finding is added and the pop-up states a single case; a unit with no firing page is answered 'triage: cleared by the tool', no agent.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the echo check as T186's first filter, the agent triage after it' (request.md, the narrowest check). Arms (1) and (3) only add to what reaches the agent beyond echo alone, and arm (1) keeps rule (C) reachable. Clearing a unit where nothing fires is the approved filter itself.

decisions.summary: The absence arm's phrases leave out 'not recorded' and 'no source' (the coordinator's wording) and keep 'the one case', 'only one case', 'every plan': 56 of 114 pop-ups fire instead of 104, 0 of 17 page-caused corrections missed either way (measured 2026-11-23, the landing replay and score).
decisions.why: The plan calls this a narrowing of the COORDINATOR's wording; that brief is neither the GM's request nor the accepted spec: a grep of request.md, spec-cited.md and spec-index.md for 'not recorded|no source|absence' finds no hit. The GM's words name only the echo check as the first filter, and the absence arm is an addition to it, so trimming the addition narrows nothing he asked. Purpose check: with the two phrases the arm fires on 104 of 114 pop-ups, which would gut the filter the GM approved to end needless cascades; the trimmed form shows no measured miss among the 17 page-caused corrections (the knob is chosen and scored on the same 17, as the green exit and the red exit in the section state).

decisions.summary: The triage MANIFEST shows each changed block OLD, NEW and WORD DIFF, the new and removed blocks, and each pop-up whole once (never cut at 400 characters).
decisions.why: Presentation for the approved agent triage after the filter; showing more, never less.

decisions.summary: modal-triage.md states (A) a fact the pop-up states, (B) a label of one, (C) a passage its references point at removed; the code states none of it; (D) is dropped.
decisions.why: The GM approved the plan in which 'the gap-fill clause [is] dropped' (request.md, the narrowest check); the section names this drop as (D), the GM's later form. Stating the rule in one place adds nothing and removes nothing.

decisions.summary: The rule to name a pop-up when unsure whether a block meets (A)-(C) is kept in modal-triage.md.
decisions.why: Round 2 ruled its drop NOT LEGITIMATE because the GM's approval dropped only the gap-fill clause; keeping it is the status quo that ruling required.

decisions.id: D9 notes and originals outside the fingerprint
decisions.summary: The section states .notes.html and .originals.html never reached a pop-up's checks (fingerprint reads only the Entry: and Drawing: pages), pinned by the replay's first class.
decisions.why: Describes and pins existing behavior; it changes no reach of review.

decisions.summary: record modal-triage replay --edits and --landing, the latter calling the same change::fires.
decisions.why: Verification that the approved filter does what it says (misses no page-caused correction); enforcement of the request, not scope.

decisions.summary: Before T185; T187 waits for the garden fix; green is the landing replay missing none of the 17 page-caused corrections; red narrows the arm that cleared a needed correction.
decisions.why: Sequencing and an exit that measures the GM's own criterion (catch every page-caused correction); nothing narrowed.

decisions.id: D12 comment label changes cleared, left
decisions.summary: An Evidence/Grounds comment's label change is cleared by the tool and was never re-owed on HEAD; not a defect, since each page states the label in visible words the triage sees; T187 (labels are data) is the label rule.
decisions.why: The GM's label question ('should attested versus guess be something that cascades mechanically rather than requiring a review') is answered by the approved rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration', carried by T187 by name. T186 leaves HEAD's behavior on comments as it was, the visible label is still reviewed, and no wrong outcome is left.

decisions.id: D13 claims triage not given T186's clears
decisions.summary: The claims triage gets T185's moves but not T186's tool clears and pairing; its agent still sees every changed block; said in the report.
decisions.why: Scope: the cascade the GM described is a page edit re-owing checks on every pop-up citing it, and his approval for this task names T186's filter on pop-up triage. The claims triage left as it is gives correct outcomes (its agent sees every changed block); a speed gap with correct outcomes is not a defect left (constitution XIV's defect rule), so nothing asked is given up here.

decisions.summary: The 'pond is taken as the office's form' sentence is restated in sheet/garden-pond.md, sheet/garden.md and docs/building-programs.md's inner_garden row (via make building-programs), to a garden's water being a knob; modal-form and modal-research owed on the two pop-ups through make record-owed.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the garden-pond sentence fixed in its three places'; these are the three. Owing the two pop-ups' own checks directly adds review.

decisions.summary: A label becomes data on the page: an empty <span class=item data-item data-label data-guess> inside the item's block (not on its <li>, which style.rs and triage/change.rs match bare), the block's own words held to the tag by items::faults.
decisions.why: This is the GM's approved rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration', answering 'Shouldn't attested versus guess be something that cascades mechanically rather than requiring a review'. Where the span sits and the fact that it is empty are design choices inside that rule, and items::faults enforces it.

decisions.summary: A pop-up's Guesses bullet becomes a reference {NNNN#<id>} that the build fills from the tag and drops while the item is not a GUESS, hooked into about::feature and choices::modal so the page writer, registry dump, Mode A and the modal bundle all read the filled text.
decisions.why: This is the propagation by regeneration the GM approved. A relabel is one edit on the page, and the pop-ups follow it with no review.

decisions.summary: An engine claim may name ...html#<id>, and its class is checked against the tag. For such a claim alone the fingerprint leaves out the class word and the anchors, so a relabel flip owes no impl-drift. An unanchored claim keeps its class in its fingerprint. label_free stops the stale-figure check from reading the flip as a changed constant.
decisions.why: Claims are hand-written comments, so they are checked and told which class to write rather than regenerated. The cascade stays mechanical and owes no review, which is the purpose of the GM's question. The fingerprint exemption reaches only the case the request names, a claim held to a tag. label_free fixes, red first, a false flag the pilot found (TREE_ROOM).

decisions.summary: A registry real-tree test names any pop-up whose About states a GUESS-tagged item of a page it cites without calling it a guess.
decisions.why: Prose in an About section cannot be regenerated, so this test makes sure a label reaches the place regeneration does not. It only fails when the requested label cascade is missing, so it enforces the request and adds no new behavior (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: Tooling plus a pilot on page 0218, sheet/compound-shrine.md and the 4 shrine-tree claims. The remaining untagged record keeps the old review path, and T192 tags it.
decisions.why: This sequences the approved rule across tasks of the same feature and drops nothing: the bulk tagging is filed as T192. Nothing is wrongly cleared in the meantime, because an untagged item is treated as unknown and keeps the review it owes today (constitution XII).

decisions.summary: The 4 shrine-tree claims that cited 0218 as attested are restated as GUESS ...#shrine-tree. The code and the drawing are unchanged.
decisions.why: The label was wrong and the behavior was fine, so the claim is restated, as constitution XIV v2.36.0 directs. This is the uncascaded label the GM asked about, found and fixed.

decisions.summary: docs/building-programs.md's 'shrine in a corner beside a tree' cites 0218 as attested for a GUESS. The fix goes to T192, which lands before T22, because T186's uncommitted edit of that file is in this clone.
decisions.why: The defect is not dropped. It is filed, with a reason and an order (FR-009's form), and it is fixed inside this feature before T22. The GM's fix-as-we-go rule bounds known defects by the next step ('fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step'), not by the task that found them. Keeping a hunk out of another builder's uncommitted file is about the order of landings and does not narrow the request.

decisions.summary: Lands after T186 (the triage's first filter, which clears a referenced relabel) and T185 (whose modal.rs this task edits in guesses() only), and before T192.
decisions.why: Sequencing. Nothing the request asks for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Apply T186's pop-up change filter (clears, echo rule, ABSENCE arm) to the claims triage, so a page or procedure-section edit re-owes only the claims whose text it changed in a claim-bearing way; a generated doc's claims are touched only by rows whose text changed in words they repeat.
decisions.why: The GM's convergence talk approved 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' and 're-reviews scoped to the change' ('Please do all of that'); the observed 73-claims-for-one-row re-owe is the cascade the GM said must be fixed before anything else.

decisions.summary: T186's page_change split in triage/change.rs; blocks_change shared by both triages rather than copied; md_words reads a procedure section's Markdown as page words so markup edits pair equal.
decisions.why: Implementation of D1; the same rule as the pop-ups, which is what the GM approved.

decisions.summary: Each changed page/section paired once, then judged per claim by change::fires with the claim's label and account as reader (question paths left out); no note key is a claim's, so the keys-gone arm never fires.
decisions.why: Applies T186's rule to the claim as its reader; the keys-gone arm not firing is a consequence of claims carrying no note keys, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Add change::echo_rewritten: the echo also read from a rewrite's new side, because a relabel rewrites a fact in words the claim repeats; without it the replay missed one DRIFTED claim.
decisions.why: Widens what is sent to the agent, so it narrows nothing; it keeps factual/label changes cascading as the GM's 'only factual findings cascade' intends.

decisions.summary: A claim whose every text edit is cleared, with no code hunk and nothing forced, is recorded cleared by the tool (record_cleared) with snapshots before skip/all-forced/dispatch paths run on the rest; the dispatch is skipped when nothing is left.
decisions.why: This is the 'cost no agent' outcome the GM asked for; code-hunk and forced claims still go on, and the quotation ruling (an original-language edit is never cleared) is kept.

decisions.summary: The claims-triage contract and MANIFEST form are unchanged; the MANIFEST shows only blocks left after the clears.
decisions.why: Scopes the remaining review to the change, as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: claims triage-replay --out DIR: a read-only replay of each owed claim's fate, used as the red-first and 0-misses measurement over today's landings.
decisions.why: Verification that the requested filter does what was asked (no DRIFTED claim whose drift lay in its own text is dropped); enforcement of the request, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Green exit stated as 0 misses of DRIFTED claims whose drift lay in the text they rest on; the two DRIFTED claims the tool clears are the known 'tax archive strongroom role' (its DRIFTED row kept) and 'main gate posts', reached only by an unrelated cart-gate edit of its section.
decisions.why: Clearing a claim on an edit that does not touch what it rests on is exactly the GM's rule ('the ones that never could have plausibly needed this kind of cascade'); the measure matches the GM's rule rather than narrowing it. Both are named, and the known drift's verdict stands.

decisions.id: D9 left: main gate posts cites no page
decisions.summary: Leave the claims-grammar class (a CONVENTION claim whose figure a page states but which cites no page) to the claims grammar; the one instance was already restated at d4da911203.
decisions.why: Not something this request or T191 asks for (cascade scoping, not citation coverage); its one instance's wrong outcome is already fixed, so no wrong outcome is left by this task. Aside for the GM: worth a filed observation if other such claims are measured.

decisions.summary: PAIR_RATIO and ABSENCE stay T186's; function-word trigrams ('one of the') still count, sending 2 extra claims at the garden landing.
decisions.why: Over-sending two claims to an agent is no wrong outcome; leaving T186's approved rule as it is narrows nothing.

decisions.id: D11 rustfmt fix of T187's file
decisions.summary: Fix formatting only in rust/gate/crates/owed/src/item_relabel.rs, whose rustfmt failure turned the owed crate's make static red.
decisions.why: A tool refusing valid work is a defect fixed as found; formatting only, no behavior change. (It departs from the plan's own 'T187's files untouched' constraint, which is the coordinator's, not the GM's.)

decisions.summary: Classed as performance work: removes agent work before dispatch; no engine code, no map change; not a defect fix.
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM's 'prioritize performance improvements'; the work removed is agent time, the GM's stated cost.

decisions.summary: change::page_change counts a note key as gone only where neither the page now nor any reached block holds it; the MANIFEST keys line follows and is relabeled
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-23: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page ... nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs', and the approved rule 'a split is a move'. A key that moved with its block is not a removal.

decisions.summary: change::echo looks for the nearest new sentence on the page and in the reached sentences, so a sentence moved with an edit is compared with its moved self; the echo rule's wording is unchanged
decisions.why: This applies the approved echo check (T186's first filter) under 'a split is a move' and 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. The edit itself is still compared, so a changed claim still owes its review.

decisions.summary: replay_landing reads each pop-up's pages and their pointers' targets at the commit and its parent, and judges every changed page of that set through the same judged() the bundle uses
decisions.why: The landing replay now gives the same judgment as the bundle, the cascade rules applied the same way at both points. This narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Change.moved_edited pairs a removed block with its closest new block on a reached page at PAIR_RATIO. The block stays owed as the echo reads it but is printed under 'Moved with edits' with OLD/NEW/WORD DIFF. A pair whose claim words are equal (a marker edit) is cleared as a move
decisions.why: The GM's rules: 'a split is a move', 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review', 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration', 're-reviews scoped to the change'. A moved block with an edit is still owed, and is shown to the triage as an edit rather than a deletion. Only an edit that leaves the claim words equal is cleared.

decisions.summary: 'Reached' means all the pages the unit reads (the pop-up's own pages and their pointers' targets, modals::followed), wider than the source page's pointer targets only where a key or sentence sits on another page of the pop-up's own Entry
decisions.why: The GM's split condition is sufficient, not exclusive. His approved rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' already clears a verbatim move between two pages the pop-up itself reads, because the pop-up's sources still hold the claim. An edited move is still compared and owed. The width was measured, and it matches the set the moves already used. It drops no review of a changed claim.

decisions.summary: The claims triage passes reached_by_pointers, so its echo widens to pointer targets alone; its 167 tests pass unchanged
decisions.why: This is the GM's split condition as he worded it ('the original page ... directs a reader to the other page'), applied to the claims triage. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A moved sentence whose one edit is an inserted gloss fires wherever the pop-up repeats the gloss's neighbors (weir_form--frame on '(seki)'). It is pinned by a test and not special-cased
decisions.why: This keeps the echo rule the GM approved as worded: an insertion's neighbors count as written. The result owes one review more, never one less, so it carves nothing out of what was asked. Whether the gloss changes a claim stays the triage agent's call, as the approved plan (echo check first, agent triage after) says.

decisions.summary: The modal-triage contract's MANIFEST paragraph names the new 'Moved with edits' kind and the keys rule
decisions.why: The triage agent has to read the MANIFEST's new kind correctly for the approved filter to work. This is no new behavior.

decisions.summary: Lands after T185, T186 and T191 and before T184; green when the T184 re-run owes the 9 pop-ups the rules give, red recorded and ruled through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: This is the GM's 'we have to fix that before we move forward' on the cascade, applied to the split that tests the rules first.

decisions.summary: A builder of a still-open task that the session reads as running is STALLED when it has no live work (listed in the Stop's background_tasks, a run or sub-agent its transcript launched, a sub-agent of its own writing within the bound) and its transcript (mtime) has not moved within STALL_SECS.
decisions.why: Anchored in the 2026-11-23 request: a check that is silent while the session is active or waiting on a tracked agent, and speaks only when it is idle with actionable work. A builder with no live work and a silent transcript is not a tracked wait, and it is actionable. The task line and brief the block cites are not in the bundle, so this is not checked against them.

decisions.summary: A builder is the session's own dispatch whose description opens with a feature number.
decisions.why: FR-006's builder is an agent dispatched with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; this is that definition made readable.

decisions.summary: idle_check waits on every main-session Stop, not only one with an empty list, and names stalled builders when the session did not turn.
decisions.why: T184's builder went unnamed because every Stop listed a run except one, which returned at the hold. Waiting on every Stop is what lets the 2026-11-23 check speak when the session is idle with actionable work. It stays silent when the session turns, as T183 does.

decisions.summary: Stalled builders are named ahead of the hold and the open-task block; a hold holds new tasks, not a started builder's wake.
decisions.why: Two cases, ruled separately. (a) A hold on new tasks: the arbiter's ruling says '451 starts no new task', and waking a builder already started on an open task starts none, so the check still respects the binding ruling the 2026-11-23 request names. (b) A set-down of the builder's own task: the block decides nothing to override one. It names only a builder the session reads as still running, with no final notice and its task open in tasks.md, and it gives the wake command as information, not a block that compels it. The block has no explicit exclusion of a set-down task's builder, so that edge is flagged to the caller, not ruled as a narrowing the plan makes.

decisions.summary: Each stalled builder is named once while its last line is unchanged (once key 'stalled <id>').
decisions.why: T183's said-once rule and the GM's 2026-11-23 aim that the check add nothing to the context it need not.

decisions.summary: With no background_tasks list (a harness from before the field), no builder is named.
decisions.why: Without the list the check cannot tell whether a run the builder launched is still live. Naming would break the goal 'one at work is never named' and the GM's silent-while-waiting-on-a-tracked-agent rule, so the general rule is impossible here, not just awkward. It also covers only a harness that lacks the field, not today's case.

decisions.summary: LAUNCHED reads a Monitor's launch result ({taskId, timeoutMs}).
decisions.why: A defect fix in the reading the stall rule depends on: an agent waiting on its own watch was read as having no work (214 results measured).

decisions.summary: The Stop's list is re-read after the wait and at each look. A shell entry is live while a process holds its output file on fd 1 or 2, or while a live process's command line holds its command (its longest quote-free run of at least 12 characters, a CONVENTION) for Monitors, whose stream is a pipe.
decisions.why: The re-read closes the gap where a watch ends after the Stop (the D12 counterfactual) and serves the task's goal directly. The Monitor reading keeps a working builder from being named.

decisions.summary: A shell whose command is too short to tell, a subagent entry, and any entry where /proc cannot be read are kept as listed (live), failing toward silence.
decisions.why: Taken one at a time. A subagent's turn ends with a notice to the session, which wakes it, so that case cannot become T184's unheard stall. With /proc unreadable, liveness cannot be read at all. A command too short to match cannot be told from other processes, and guessing either way would name working builders, which the goal forbids. In each case the rule cannot be applied, not merely applied awkwardly.

decisions.summary: A listed shell whose writer waits on a dead producer (finished_run_hooks' stale_waiters) is no live work and is named with its pid, file and TaskStop <id>.
decisions.why: A defect fix (the gap audit's item 1): a waiter that will never finish is exactly a watch that will never wake its agent, so it is the task's own case.

decisions.summary: The check looks again when a quiet builder crosses the bound, or every RECHECK_SECS (GUESS 60 s) while live work runs, until WAIT_SECS (= STALL_SECS, 600 s). The Idle hook timeout is raised 420 -> 960 s (a CONVENTION pinned by a test).
decisions.why: Needed to name within about ten minutes a builder that goes quiet after the Stop with no Stop after (the gap audit's item 2). The knobs are labeled GUESS or CONVENTION.

decisions.summary: A builder past the context cap is named for a fresh dispatch from its handoff, not a SendMessage; CAP_TOKENS moves to shared::context.
decisions.why: FR-006 refuses a SendMessage that resumes a builder past the threshold, so a notice naming that command would contradict the spec.

decisions.summary: make builder-status [TRANSCRIPT=] says each builder of an open task working or stalled, and each dead-producer waiter, by the idle check's own reading of the last Stop's kept list, re-read now.
decisions.why: An addition. Its only source is the block's quotation of the task line ('the coordinator's status of a builder comes from that probe'), and that line is not in the bundle's request.md. It reads the same state as the idle check and changes no behavior. It narrows nothing, so it carries no ruling, but it is not verified against the GM's words.

decisions.summary: STALL_SECS (L7R_STALL_SECS) is a GUESS of 600 s, about twice the longest measured silence of an agent at work (280.6 s).
decisions.why: A knob labeled GUESS and derived from measured gaps (280.6 s longest), so that a working agent is never named, which the 2026-11-23 request's silent-while-waiting rule requires. The brief the block cites for the GUESS is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: Two builders that had reported done, with an interim notice never followed by a final one, are named once each; telling them apart is left.
decisions.why: Not a defect: neither was working, so the goal 'one at work is never named' holds. Each is named once with its own last line saying it stopped, and an open task whose builder has stopped is something the session can act on. No wrong outcome is left.

decisions.summary: The idle check's words do not reach make guard-messages' corpus. They were judged by message-check on a hand-built bundle and its cuts applied; wiring the corpus is left.
decisions.why: The words the GM asked to have reviewed for brevity and fidelity were reviewed by that same check, so no unjudged output ships. The remaining gap is only that a later edit would not be caught automatically. Under constitution XIV v2.36.0 that is a check's reach with no wrong outcome today, not a defect, and leaving it changes nothing the request asked for.

decisions.summary: A builder whose live work outlasts WAIT_SECS, with the session silent and no later Stop, is not named. Filed as T201, to land before T200.
decisions.why: This is a deferred defect, and it meets FR-009's terms: it states why it is not fixed here, its filed task id and its order. The reason is real, not a matter of cost. The idle check can wake the session only by exiting under the hook entry's timeout, and Claude Code's cap on that timeout is unmeasured. Building a longer wait on a guessed cap risks the hook being killed and losing the case this task does cover. The project's rule is to measure such a number, not assume it. T184's own case, a watch ending within minutes of the Stop, is fixed here.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests in today's shape, the replay against today's real Stops, T184's files untouched, one landing.
decisions.why: Enforces and measures the task's own goal; nothing outside it.

decisions.summary: One shared follower change::follow (modals::followed now calls it), following a split's target split again, each page once; claims reach it through bundle::follow_names and bundle::read_pages
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-23: a split is a move and the original page directs the reader to where the text now stands; following every level is what makes the moved text read where it stands. Reuse rather than a copy is implementation shape.

decisions.summary: read_pages (cited pages plus their pointers' targets) used wherever a claim's research is fingerprinted or snapshotted (index::current, report base comparison, record, triage page maps, bundle units.json and cited questions, impl_check); cited_pages alone kept for the two 'names no question file' refusals; a page with no pointer reads as itself so no unsplit claim moves
decisions.why: Serves 'a split is a move' and 're-reviews scoped to the change': a claim is judged against the text where it stands, so an edit on the target re-owes it. The refusals keep checking the citation as written, which is what they refuse on.

decisions.summary: research_why reads a rest standing verbatim on a pointer-reached page as standing, so a pure split is owed triage that claims triage clears mechanically with no dispatch (feature 432's clear_page_moves), recording the target; only a claim-bearing edit left after the tool's clears reaches an agent
decisions.why: Directly the GM's 'nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs' and the approved rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'.

decisions.summary: Moved::shown lists moved_edited blocks under 'Moved with edits' with OLD, NEW and word diff instead of as removed, rendering shared with the pop-ups'; claims-triage contract names the kind
decisions.why: A split is a move: a moved block shown as removed sent claims to impl-drift; showing it as a move with its edit scopes the review to the change, as approved.

decisions.summary: marks::subject_files follows its files' pointers (a q: subject takes the target's notes and originals); earlier::pairs_since diffs a newly bundled target against the then-text of the pages pointing to it, no deletions shown, so a verbatim move is no change and a restatement pairs with its old self
decisions.why: The approved rule 're-reviews scoped to the change' and 'a split is a move': a later round sees only what changed on the page where it now stands.

decisions.summary: Left: a claim whose index row predates the following, cited page unchanged, is forced through one triage/impl-drift run when a target it never snapshotted changes
decisions.why: It leaves a path where a non-claim edit can owe a review, against 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. But it is not a defect (no wrong outcome: a conservative extra review, nothing passed or refused wrongly), the case is closed - rows recorded from now on carry the followed pages - and measured empty on the live tree (make claims-owed 2026-11-23, 'no claim is owed', which a pre-following fingerprint on a pointed page would have tripped). Only a defect left is NOT LEGITIMATE.

decisions.summary: T184's and T193's files left untouched; ordered after T185, T191, T194 and beside T184
decisions.why: Coordination among the feature's own tasks; narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Classed as performance work
decisions.why: The convergence work exists to stop reviews that change nothing (the GM 2026-11-23) and FR-013 puts performance work first; removing an impl-drift dispatch per pure split is that.

decisions.summary: The pop-up triage (read_reply) reads the reply whole before record writes anything and refuses a line outside the form, a foreign uid, an empty reply, and NONE beside a TOUCHES line, naming the line and form.
decisions.why: Fixes the fail-open defect the task is filed for (an unread line answered 'triage: untouched' with no word said) in the triage machinery the GM approved on 2026-11-23 (the agent triage after the echo check). A wrong outcome, fixed in the task.

decisions.summary: The claims triage gets the same rules via `refused`, called by `claims triaged` before record_triage so save_index never runs on a refused reply; record_triage is left unchanged for its "" callers (observed, grep of its callers); its now-unreachable unknown-key message is removed.
decisions.why: Same defect on the claims side; leaving record_triage's internal-caller path alone is the scope of the fix, not a narrowing of it, since those callers pass no agent reply. Removing dead code follows from the fix.

decisions.summary: A claim key may hold spaces, so a non-ASCII dash with a later ' - ' reads as an unknown key and is refused.
decisions.why: A consequence of refusing unknown keys whole; it refuses, never records wrongly, so it cannot reintroduce the fail-open path.

decisions.summary: EDIT: unread_edits/EDIT_FORM finds a line shaped as an EDIT header (first word EDIT past bullet, quote or bold, not EDITS) or a <<< fence outside any parsed block; record apply-edits refuses on it before any block is applied or settled.
decisions.why: Fixes the dropped-EDIT defect (audit item 12a) at the point where a block is applied.

decisions.summary: Only record apply-edits refuses; the guard's own readers (round state rounds.rs:856, freeze.rs:88) and the bundles' displays keep the existing parse, on the observation (grep of reply::blocks|categorized( over rust/, each caller read) that apply-edits is the one reader that applies or settles a block.
decisions.why: The defect is an EDIT lost with no one told; every path by which an EDIT takes effect goes through apply-edits, which now refuses the whole reply, so a dropped line in a display or round count cannot become a lost EDIT. The reach is labeled with its search space. Not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: Agent files: modal-triage.md asks for NONE when nothing is touched (an empty reply is now refused); claims-triage.md says a line outside the form is refused.
decisions.why: Keeps the agents' instructions in step with D1/D2 so a correct no-touch reply is not refused.

decisions.summary: Order: before T197's REJUDGE on T184's pop-ups; independent of T198-T200 and T192.
decisions.why: Sequencing only; a re-triage must not run on the fail-open readers.

decisions.summary: Performance work? no - it changes what the readers refuse, not how long anything takes.
decisions.why: Corrected from round 1: the task is neither performance nor measurement work under FR-013, so it does not claim the ordering's priority. The round-1 gloss on FR-013 is struck; item 2 now cites FR-013 only as the ordering constraint.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the empty pop-up reply clearing every unit, and an unknown uid or claim key exiting 0 and clearing the rest, both fixed here (observed, every reader of a triage reply read for its unmatched-line path).
decisions.why: Known defects found by the task are fixed in it, none deferred, as the GM's fix-as-we-go rule asks.

decisions.summary: make quick's _quick recipe gains make-docs --check, mode-a building-programs --check and record check glossary, the three derived files make done's preflight regenerates, so the closing checks fail on a stale one naming its regenerate command
decisions.why: The task's own subject (a red make done on a stale derived file), filed as performance work under FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 'prioritize performance improvements'; it moves an existing check earlier, adds no behavior beyond refusing a stale file the gate already refuses.

decisions.summary: checks/documents/derived_quick.rs pins the quick recipe to preflight's DERIVED table; a derived target quick does not check, or one the table does not know, is red naming the line to add
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested behavior only: with the derived lines deleted from the spec the pin has nothing left to check (GM 2026-09-20 on checks that make the asked thing keep happening). FR-012 red-first is honored in the table.

decisions.summary: reviews prereq standing names a unit whose last PASS/NEEDS-WORK is carried to the sheet as just snapshotted and whose every open finding (not review-accepted) is nitpick, outside or confirmation; review-tree.sh prints it answered and leaves it out of the dispatch count
decisions.why: Implements the GM's approved 2026-11-23 rules 'only factual findings cascade' and 'settled choices stay settled' and his 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies' for building reviews; measured first (4 byte-identical sheets dispatched anyway), with one-shot labels on the figures.

decisions.summary: a fixed error or questionable finding owes its round even on an unchanged sheet (e.g. fixed in the docs)
decisions.why: An error or questionable finding is a factual one; 'only factual findings cascade' is the GM's rule, so a factual fix owing a round is the rule applied, not a carve-out from it. The sheet being unchanged does not show the fix was right.

decisions.summary: a finding of no or an unknown severity owes a round, failing closed as T188 does
decisions.why: The standing rule exempts only findings shown to be non-factual; a finding whose class is unknown cannot be shown so, and failing closed keeps the GM's 'only factual findings cascade' from passing an unclassified factual finding.

decisions.summary: a nitpick fixed on the sheet owes only a change-scoped, adversarial building-review of the edit (make review-fixed UNIT= FINDING=, the kept reviewed sheet, T189's before/after pairs); a clean SCOPE=change verdict (PASS, every finding minor, gate not red) is carried by carried/answered/standing/checkpoint/push review gate
decisions.why: Directly the GM's words 'make only the smallest possible changes perhaps with some kind of adversarial subagent review process' and the approved rule 're-reviews scoped to the change'. The plan says plainly the saving is unmeasured and the rule is the GM's, which is correct framing.

decisions.summary: an error or questionable finding fixed on the sheet is refused by make review-fixed and owes the full round, not a change-scoped one
decisions.why: In tension with 're-reviews scoped to the change', which the section itself applies to building reviews, so it is ruled. Legitimate on the GM's own words: 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies. And it might be that when we are cascading, we are only interested in factual inaccuracies' - the scoped route he proposed was for the small, non-factual edits, and a factual fix is the class he said matters. Purpose test: the oscillation the GM described was rounds driven by style findings; under this same section any nitpick the full round raises then stands (T199-standing) and, if fixed, owes only a scoped round, so the full round cannot restart the oscillation. Nor is it a defect left: a full review after a real-flaw fix is not a wrong outcome. Resting this on the request's words, not on T199's task line, which the bundle does not carry.

decisions.summary: a change-scoped round that is not clean (not PASS, a finding above minor, or its gate red) owes the full round
decisions.why: The adversarial scoped round exists to catch an edit that did more than the named fix or made something wrong; when it finds that, the change is no longer the small one the GM's scoped route covers, so falling back is the route working, not an exception to it.

decisions.summary: a verdict recorded before T199 (no kept reviewed sheet hashing to its content_key) owes the full round
decisions.why: Physically impossible otherwise: the change-scoped round reviews the diff between the sheet the verdict read and the sheet now, and before T199 the reviewed sheet was not kept (the snapshot is replaced by the next make verify), so there is no 'change' to scope a review to. It lapses on its own as verdicts are re-recorded.

decisions.summary: the pairing lifted from bundle::earlier into core::difflib::paired; the push's review gate's content-key branch now calls reviews prereq answered; make verify names the route
decisions.why: Implementation structure serving the requested route (one copy of the carry rule for every reader); no scope added.

decisions.summary: Pages::locate finds {NNNN#id} on question NNNN's pages, else on the one other question whose pages tag id; two such questions are refused naming both
decisions.why: The GM's approved 'a split is a move': an item moved between questions keeps resolving. Refusing an ambiguous two-home case fails closed rather than guessing.

decisions.summary: a claim whose item moved is followed through the cited page's split pointers to the one page that now tags it, owes no edit, and is held to that tag's class (a flip owes no impl-drift)
decisions.why: The GM verbatim: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page where the full information can be found, then nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs', and 'attested versus guess ... cascades mechanically' / labels are data propagated by regeneration.

decisions.summary: two pages reached by the pointers that both tag the item are refused naming the case
decisions.why: Outside the GM's condition (the old page does not direct the reader to THE page with the information); failing closed on ambiguity is not a carve-out from 'nothing needs to cascade'.

decisions.summary: where no pointer from the cited page directs the reader to the item's new page, the claim is named with the pointer to write
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own condition: 'as long as the original page ... directs a reader to the other page'. Where it does not, the condition fails and something must be written; the plan asks for the pointer, the smallest change, not a re-review.

decisions.summary: item 12c changes nothing: owed::record::modals::followed calls triage::change::follow, which walks pointer targets to a fixpoint since 451 T196
decisions.why: Taken on the pinned test the block names (change/tests.rs' a_split_s_target_split_again_is_followed_each_page_once), which this bundle-only review cannot re-run; the closing checks run that test, so a false premise turns them red.

decisions.summary: items.rs logs every page a Guesses reference reads (take_read), drained by l7r_mode_a::reads::take, so a relabel regenerates a cached sheet; a page named only in About prose is never read and owes the cache nothing
decisions.why: A defect fix (a cache that could serve a stale sheet after a relabel), the GM's 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration'; the About-prose case is not an exception since nothing is read from it, so nothing it says reaches the sheet. Measured 2026-11-23 by grep, with its method.

decisions.summary: T198 and T199 counted as [perf] tasks under FR-013 (fewer red make done runs, fewer review rounds); T200 not
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that speeds the gate, landings or builders' loop as performance work; the checklist's guesses are labeled GUESS and its measurements carry date and method.

decisions.summary: reviews prereq standing names a unit whose last PASS/NEEDS-WORK is carried to the sheet as just snapshotted and whose every open finding (not review-accepted) is nitpick, outside or confirmation; review-tree.sh prints it answered and leaves it out of the dispatch count
decisions.why: Implements the GM's approved 2026-11-23 rules 'only factual findings cascade' and 'settled choices stay settled' and his 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies' for building reviews; measured first (4 byte-identical sheets dispatched anyway), with one-shot labels on the figures.

decisions.summary: a fixed error or questionable finding owes its round even on an unchanged sheet (e.g. fixed in the docs)
decisions.why: An error or questionable finding is a factual one; 'only factual findings cascade' is the GM's rule, so a factual fix owing a round is the rule applied, not a carve-out from it. The sheet being unchanged does not show the fix was right.

decisions.summary: a finding of no or an unknown severity owes a round, failing closed as T188 does
decisions.why: The standing rule exempts only findings shown to be non-factual; a finding whose class is unknown cannot be shown so, and failing closed keeps the GM's 'only factual findings cascade' from passing an unclassified factual finding.

decisions.summary: a nitpick fixed on the sheet owes only a change-scoped, adversarial building-review of the edit (make review-fixed UNIT= FINDING=, the kept reviewed sheet, T189's before/after pairs); a clean SCOPE=change verdict (PASS, every finding minor, gate not red) is carried by carried/answered/standing/checkpoint/push review gate
decisions.why: Directly the GM's words 'make only the smallest possible changes perhaps with some kind of adversarial subagent review process' and the approved rule 're-reviews scoped to the change'. The plan says plainly the saving is unmeasured and the rule is the GM's, which is correct framing.

decisions.summary: an error or questionable finding fixed on the sheet is refused by make review-fixed and owes the full round, not a change-scoped one
decisions.why: In tension with 're-reviews scoped to the change', which the section itself applies to building reviews, so it is ruled. Legitimate on the GM's own words: 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies. And it might be that when we are cascading, we are only interested in factual inaccuracies' - the scoped route he proposed was for the small, non-factual edits, and a factual fix is the class he said matters. Purpose test: the oscillation the GM described was rounds driven by style findings; under this same section any nitpick the full round raises then stands (T199-standing) and, if fixed, owes only a scoped round, so the full round cannot restart the oscillation. Nor is it a defect left: a full review after a real-flaw fix is not a wrong outcome. Resting this on the request's words, not on T199's task line, which the bundle does not carry.

decisions.summary: a change-scoped round that is not clean (not PASS, a finding above minor, or its gate red) owes the full round
decisions.why: The adversarial scoped round exists to catch an edit that did more than the named fix or made something wrong; when it finds that, the change is no longer the small one the GM's scoped route covers, so falling back is the route working, not an exception to it.

decisions.summary: a verdict recorded before T199 (no kept reviewed sheet hashing to its content_key) owes the full round
decisions.why: Physically impossible otherwise: the change-scoped round reviews the diff between the sheet the verdict read and the sheet now, and before T199 the reviewed sheet was not kept (the snapshot is replaced by the next make verify), so there is no 'change' to scope a review to. It lapses on its own as verdicts are re-recorded.

decisions.summary: the pairing lifted from bundle::earlier into core::difflib::paired; the push's review gate's content-key branch now calls reviews prereq answered; make verify names the route
decisions.why: Implementation structure serving the requested route (one copy of the carry rule for every reader); no scope added.

decisions.why: The GM's approved 'a split is a move': an item moved between questions keeps resolving. Refusing an ambiguous two-home case fails closed rather than guessing.

decisions.summary: a claim whose item moved is followed through the cited page's split pointers to the one page that now tags it, owes no edit, and is held to that tag's class (a flip owes no impl-drift)
decisions.why: The GM verbatim: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page where the full information can be found, then nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs', and 'attested versus guess ... cascades mechanically' / labels are data propagated by regeneration.

decisions.summary: two pages reached by the pointers that both tag the item are refused naming the case
decisions.why: Outside the GM's condition (the old page does not direct the reader to THE page with the information); failing closed on ambiguity is not a carve-out from 'nothing needs to cascade'.

decisions.summary: where no pointer from the cited page directs the reader to the item's new page, the claim is named with the pointer to write
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own condition: 'as long as the original page ... directs a reader to the other page'. Where it does not, the condition fails and something must be written; the plan asks for the pointer, the smallest change, not a re-review.

decisions.summary: page_words drops every well-formed item tag (a malformed one stays visible), so a tag-only page edit owes no pop-up triage
decisions.why: The task's own goal (tagging owes no check) and the GM's approved convergence rules (labels are data and propagate by regeneration; only a claim-changing edit triggers review). A tag adds nothing a reader meets.

decisions.summary: a pop-up's {NNNN#id} reference is filled from its tag's data-guess whatever the label, resolved as the registry does (own question first, else the one other question tagging the id); verbatim reference owes nothing, a reworded data-guess owes the pop-up its checks, a relabel owes nothing

decisions.why: Method of carrying out the request; run before the GM approved the cheap route and kept, its results confirmed by sessions.

decisions.summary: cheap.py tags each remaining block that names its own label with an id and label and no bullet (476 GUESS, 32 CONVENTION, 27 DEVIATION); sessions only for the 9 blocks the script could not decide
decisions.why: Exactly the route the GM approved 2026-11-23: 'a script tags each block that names its own label ... only truly ambiguous blocks go to a session' - 'please proceed with that as the way forward'.

decisions.summary: the page check no longer requires a GUESS tag's data-guess; the registry refuses a reference to a GUESS tag without one, naming the fix (the referencing pop-up's author writes it from the block)
decisions.why: The GM's approved route verbatim: 'a Guesses sentence is written only when a pop-up first cites the item'. The registry refusal is enforcement of that clause, not new scope.

The plan measures that condition rather than assuming it (every reader of an item tag in rust/ read; grep of ATTESTED over rust/; an untagged block reads as unknown, never attested; the registry drops a non-GUESS reference), so the GM's condition is shown met, not completed on his behalf.

decisions.summary: of the 9 blocks sent to sessions (negated or back-referring label words, nested-list blocks), 7 were tagged
decisions.why: The sessions are the GM's 'truly ambiguous blocks go to a session'; a block a session reads as stating no label (e.g. a negated convention word) has no label to tag, so leaving it is the goal met, not narrowed.

decisions.summary: an opus judge read the 94 classed claims still unanchored against their page's same-label tags; 72 now name their item; 22 cite a page where no tagged block states their decision and are left, listed in claims-verdicts.json; plain claims are not anchored
