Whether any of the 22 is itself a research defect is not shown by the plan; nothing here establishes one, and they are listed for reading.

decisions.summary: question_size counts an item tag for nothing
decisions.why: A tag is not prose; without this, tagging put 0196 over its cap and would have owed a split or a trim, contrary to the GM's rule that no size edit is ever substantive and to the goal that tagging owes no check.

decisions.summary: three found defects (relabeled_only impl-drift on anchored classed claims; refs.rs filling from its own question only; a dangling research pointer in registry tests) are each fixed in this task or by T200/T204, landed with its code
decisions.why: Each known defect is fixed before the step ends, as the fix-as-we-go rule asks; none is deferred.

decisions.summary: the strip and filled references land before or with the first tag batch; claims' anchors after T204; the whole bulk lands before the port resumes
decisions.why: The GM's condition 'tag the rest of the record before resuming our port'.

decisions.summary: the task is classed performance work
decisions.why: A scheduling class under FR-013; the task removes triages and pop-up checks a tag would have owed, and it is ordered before the port as the GM asked either way.

decisions.summary: Part (1): after each build the launcher writes $BIN.build.json {commit, dirty}. The dirty set covers only the binary's SOURCES, rust/guard, the Cargo files and .cargo/config.toml, untracked files included
decisions.why: This is gap-audit item 9's build id, which the arbiter confirmed is what item 9 asks for (ask:t197-rejudge-verb). The scoping only decides which files count as the build's input, so a busy clone's unrelated edits do not mark a clean build dirty. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Part (1): the id is written at build time, not on each run, and exported as L7R_GATE_BUILD (empty for a binary built before T197)
decisions.why: Mechanism. A per-run id would misname a binary run under L7R_GATE_STALE_OK or L7R_GATE_FRESH, so writing it at build time is the faithful choice.

decisions.summary: Part (2): write_answer keeps builds {fingerprint: build}. A settled answer keeps its judge's build, a pending settle takes its answer's build, and an adopted sibling brings its own
decisions.why: It records the build that actually judged each answer, which is the section's goal. The found-and-left item gives its census method (every write_answer caller read), as FR-009 requires.

decisions.summary: Part (2): a claims-triage clear records build only where the build was dirty; a clean build removes the stamp, so the tracked dev/claims-index.json moves only then
decisions.why: A clean build holds no uncommitted code, so it cannot be mixed in part (3)'s sense, and leaving its stamp out loses nothing the re-owe test reads. Step 2 gives the constraint behind it (the index is tracked).

decisions.summary: Part (3): under L7R_LAND_ALONE, unanswered_in and the claims owed re-owe an answer whose build held an uncommitted file whose blob differs from the landing's HEAD:<path>, naming the files. A file deleted then and absent now counts as landed
decisions.why: This is the gap's own fix, and the arbiter's ruling states it as item 9's ask: land-alone stops trusting answers from mixed trees. Counting deleted-and-absent as landed is simply what HEAD is.

decisions.summary: Part (3) exception: an answer with no build (recorded before T197) stands as it always did
decisions.why: Physically required: nothing is recorded to compare against HEAD, so the mixed test cannot be applied. Re-owing every such answer would refuse every landing in every clone, the cascade that changes nothing which the GM asked to stop (2026-11-23: 'a cascading set of reviews ... not fixing any real flaws'). That defeats the request's purpose, and the rule still governs every answer from T197 on. The round arbiter also ruled it explicitly (ask:t197-rejudge-verb item 4: 'so does 3b: answers with no build stand'). The seam with part (4) is gone now that part (4) is cut. Taken by class, the known-mixed T184 triage runs fall under ask:t184-stale-triage-marks, which the section's heading now cites: the 81 marks stand and T184 takes the batched modal-research route. Letting them stand is that ruling, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Part (4), the REJUDGE withdrawal verb, is cut. The heading states the 81 marks stand under ask:t184-stale-triage-marks and that no withdrawal verb is built. The goal (step 1), step 3's R source, step 5, the red-first list (step 9) and step 12 are restated without the verb
decisions.why: This applies ask:t197-rejudge-verb option (b) as ruled. The verb's withdrawal of marks was what round 1 found NOT LEGITIMATE, and removing it restores the standing ruling ask:t184-stale-triage-marks ('No re-triage verb is built, in T184 or as a separate task'; 'The 81 marks stand as recorded'). I read the section through for leftovers and found none: no 'covers all 81 stale marks', no 'REJUDGE on T184's pop-ups', no 'sanctioned way out', and no rejudge test in the red-first list.

decisions.summary: Step 3: the S source is restated as the session's task line (tasks.md T197, filed from the 2026-11-23 gap audit), not a GM quote, with the two arbiter rulings as R
decisions.why: An accurate statement of where the task came from narrows nothing. It also fixes round 1's point that the gap-audit ask is not in request.md. The scope the task keeps (build ids and the mixed-tree re-owe) is the scope the arbiter found item 9 asks for.

decisions.summary: Constraints and order: modals.rs and the registry are left alone (other builders' files); the task lands after T195 in the same landing; its exits run through closing-checks or arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Sequencing and non-interference. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Performance work? re-read as no: the task changes which answers a landing alone trusts, not how long anything takes
decisions.why: The arbiter asked for this re-reading (ask:t197-rejudge-verb item 2). With part (4) gone, part (3) only adds owed work, so 'no' is the faithful reading under FR-013, and the [perf] tag is dropped to match. A small leftover not worth a block: step 2 still lists 'FR-013: the landings faster' as a constraint. Read with 'no', that is a limit (do not slow the landings), not a claim of speed.

decisions.summary: Naming the item of a claim whose class word is unchanged owes no impl-drift re-check: the claims crate reads a stored claim against Claim::unanchored (class kept, anchors dropped) as well as normalized, in a Rust unit's claim (index.rs relabeled_only)
decisions.why: Carries the GM's 2026-11-23 rules 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' and 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration', and serves 'tag the rest of the record before resuming our port' (T192): without it every named claim owes an agent check for an edit that changes no meaning.

decisions.summary: The same reading extended to a doc section's claim (index.rs owed_one, units.rs Unit::code_unanchored), whose row stores only code
decisions.why: Same purpose as D1 on the other unit kind the claims take; the before/after measurement shows the fix does not do what it is for without this arm (77 of 94 still owed).

decisions.summary: The stale-figure check (stale.rs label_free) given the same symmetry: a constant's doc that only named the item, class kept, is no change; fixed in this task
decisions.why: A defect found in the work (24 false stale flags on an edit that changes no claim) fixed in the task that found it, as the GM's fix-as-we-go rule requires; same request purpose as D1.

decisions.summary: A class changed with the naming (GUESS p to DEVIATION p#id or plain p#id), or a changed account, still owes
decisions.why: A claim's own class word changing (GUESS to DEVIATION, or to a plain attested pointer) changes what the claim asserts about the code, so under the GM's 2026-11-23 rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' it still owes; the GM's 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration' / 'cascade mechanically' concerns a page label echoing to the entries that cite it, not a claim changing its own class. The brief's 'its class word staying the same', as the block quotes it, draws the same line. Within, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: The tag's agreement with the class is left to the label check (item_labels.rs), which refuses a landing on its own, rather than repeated in owed
decisions.why: The brief's 'agreeing with the tag' condition, as the block quotes it, stays enforced: by the block's account the label check (item_labels.rs) refuses such a landing on its own, so a disagreeing tag cannot land owing nothing. Where the enforcement sits is design, not scope.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests on the 12 sample shapes (both unit kinds) and 3 changed shapes, plus a measurement on a copy of the clone with all 94 unanchored classed drawing-page claims anchored: 94 owed + 24 stale before, 0 and 0 after
decisions.why: Verification of exactly the requested behavior (enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope). The 94 are, by the block's regex count over rust/mode_a and the two docs on 2026-11-23, every unanchored classed drawing-page claim; the already-anchored ones are already named.

decisions.summary: Order (after T187/T197, before T192's claims pass and T22), exits (red recorded and set down, impossibility ruled through make arbiter-ask), budget one landing
decisions.why: Places the fix ahead of the T192 tagging the GM asked for before the port resumes; nothing the request settles is changed.

decisions.summary: A piece the clone changed only in its blank lines counts as no change of the clone's (merge_pieces, unblank), so the take takes main's rewritten archive mark.
decisions.why: Fixes the measured cause of both exit-4 takes (land191b.log, land196.log) so the clone holds main's tick: the task line's goal and a defect fix, the whole class (every sectioned file's pieces) covered.

decisions.summary: An append-only .jsonl appended on both sides keeps both sides' new lines (merge3 union); a line rewritten on both sides still conflicts, named.
decisions.why: Fixes the arbiter.jsonl conflict measured in the same hand merges; it drops no line, and a real two-sided rewrite is still refused, so nothing the task line asks for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Main comes back at the take (land-alone step 7), the existing merge that leaves uncommitted files untouched or merged; no second merge is added after it.
decisions.why: The task line asks that main be merged back at a landing's end with uncommitted work untouched; the take is that merge, and its giving up on these two shapes was the measured reason the clone fell behind. Fixing it meets the goal (the clone holds main's tick) and does not narrow it.

decisions.summary: Step 3 counts a file as the task's own only where some hunk of its uncommitted diff holds a line one of the task's Edits wrote or removed (leaves_change, Edit calls read by tool-use id); a file whose task edits are all put back is listed putback, left uncommitted, not refused.
decisions.why: Is the task line's 'the own-edit list counts only a change of the task's own', fixing the measured refusal of T195+T197's landing on T198's Makefile lines.

decisions.summary: A replace_all Edit's flag is read with its strings; a line of another task's holding its repeated string is not counted as its, only a replacement put back on the hunk's other side.
decisions.why: Closes the same defect for replace_all edits (a landing refused for another task's lines), red first; inside the task line.

decisions.summary: A Write, a Bash call's write, or an Edit whose call cannot be read counts as the task's own, so a put-back of one of these is still refused.
decisions.why: It narrows 'counts only a change of the task's own' for three kinds of write, judged one by one. A Bash write and an Edit whose call cannot be read leave no string to look for, so no one can tell whether the change was put back. A Write's string is the whole file, so the hunk test would match common lines ('}', blank lines) from any task and could not separate the task's lines from another task's. In each case, counting the file as own is the only reading that keeps the goal's other half: a landing must never go out missing the task's edit. Treating the file as not own would defeat the task line's purpose, while counting it as own only refuses a landing, and the refusal names the file. No instance of these three was observed, so this leaves no known defect in place.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests from the real sides cut to the region (take, append-only log, put-back edit, replace_all put-back), the replay on both real shapes as Done, an arbiter ask on a claim it cannot be done.
decisions.why: Checks that enforce exactly what the task line asks, red first as it requires; they add no behavior.

decisions.summary: Lands after T193's landing (a4e2bf4f0b).
decisions.why: Scheduling, which narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The task is classed as performance work (the landings' loop: hand merges and refused-landing reruns).
decisions.why: The GM asked to prioritize performance improvements (2026-11-20) and the approved six improvements include landing fixes (item 6). Removing measured hand merges and reruns falls under that.

decisions.summary: log.rs quiet(): a process that inherits this run's own test log path (<temp>/l7r-test-scratch/guard-tests-log) as GUARD_LOG_DIR, with the directory present, keeps it; any other inherited value is replaced as before; beside_binary unchanged
decisions.why: Fixes a measured defect (a hang pin's child run emptying its parent's log; 26 of 280 loaded runs red, inotify trace) in test-only code; it changes nothing the request or spec asked for, and leaving beside_binary as it is keeps a non-defect as it is.

decisions.summary: log::dir() reads the test thread's own GUARD_LOG_DIR first (env::opt), then the process's; the escape test names its own TempDir log; a normal build's answer is unchanged
decisions.why: Makes FR-012's own red-first escape test (an escape is recorded) own its state and pass under load; enforcement of what was asked, no behavior change in a normal build.

decisions.summary: scratch_sweep_hooks pace test sets the 40-day mark's mtime by path (touch -m -d) rather than through an open descriptor; the other put(.., true) uses left because their outcome cannot flip
decisions.why: A found defect (3 red of the same 280 loaded runs) fixed in this task, per the fix-as-we-go rule; the tests left mark files kept either way, observed by grep, so nothing defective is left.

decisions.summary: A failed log write stays silent (log.rs's recorded rule kept); the brief's ask that a record never drop silently (wait or fail closed) is not done, and fire is not made to refuse on a failed write
decisions.why: Neither the GM's request nor the spec asks how a log write that fails on I/O behaves: FR-012 asks that an escape be recorded, and the guard does record it; the brief's premise (a lock wait dropping records) was measured false, no write failed in any run, and the drop was test-only code. A disk-full loss is a hypothetical, not a measured wrong outcome, so keeping existing behavior narrows nothing the GM asked for and needs no ruling. Making fire refuse would add refusal behavior the GM did not ask for.

decisions.summary: After T201/T202's files; one landing; green exit is the two red tests passing and 100 loaded runs green (104 of 104 shown); red exit set down, an impossibility claim through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Scheduling and proof choices inside the task; no requirement narrowed.

decisions.summary: stalls::in_progress names a builder only while its task is in progress: box open, started since its last landing (task-starts row after the last land end, or the active mark), not held by waits, not held by name by a binding ruling (holds::named), its feature not set down at or after its last start
decisions.why: The GM approved (2026-11-23) a periodic check that 'speaks only when it is idle with actionable work and respects binding rulings and set-downs'. A parked (set down since start), waiting, held-by-name, landed or never-started builder is not actionable work; naming it with a wake command is the wrong outcome the request was filed to end. Each condition carries a clause of the approved proposal; none narrows it.

decisions.summary: A ruling that holds NEW work (holds::held) does not hold a task already started, and a set-down BEFORE the task's start does not either: T184's builder, started 19:22:55Z under 451's new-work hold and after an 11:06:29Z set-down, is still named
decisions.why: 'Respects binding rulings and set-downs' is honored to each ruling's own reach: a hold on new work holds the tasks not yet started (the plan's statement of holds::held and T183; rulings.md carries no ruling text, so the hold's scope is taken from the plan). The request itself describes the offending block as a 'builder slot is free' prompt under a ruling 'that held new work' - i.e. a prompt to START work; naming a live builder of an already-started task starts nothing. A set-down before a later start is superseded by that start (active's own test). No ruling or set-down is overridden, so nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: WAIT_SECS 600 -> 2,400 s (MONITOR_SECS 1,800 measured + STALL_SECS 600 GUESS), so a watch that runs its full 30 minutes and ends unheard is named within one check
decisions.why: Fixes a defect in the approved check: a builder stalled after a Monitor that outlived the 600 s wait was never named, i.e. the check stayed silent while idle with actionable work, contrary to the request. A constant change serving the request.

decisions.summary: The Idle hook entry's timeout 960 -> 2,760 s (the two waits + 60 s reads, a CONVENTION), pinned by the_hook_timeout_holds_both_waits under MEASURED_TIMEOUT_SECS 2,900 (measured 2026-11-23, hook2.log, D3000s2900 ran to its end and rewoke)
decisions.why: Mechanism needed for the wait above, held under a measured run; the task line asked to measure the cap and design within it, and it was measured (10 s and 1,200 s enforced as set; 2,000, 2,900 and 3,700 s runs completed and rewoke). No narrowing.

decisions.summary: When live work is still going at the check's deadline, the check exits 2 with one short notice ('IDLE CHECK: N builder(s) still working past its wait. End the turn; the next Stop re-arms the check.', each builder's id and description) instead of exiting silently
decisions.why: Presumed not legitimate: the approved proposal says the check is 'silent while the session is active or waiting on a tracked agent', and this speaks while a builder is working. It passes on MODE 1's third route: silence here would defeat the request's own purpose, concretely. The check exists to speak 'when it is idle with actionable work'; a hook cannot outlive its timeout (measured 2026-11-23: enforced as set), and only the hook's own exit 2 wakes the session (hooks reference, read 2026-11-23; a detached successor cannot), so a silent exit at the deadline ends all checking until some unrelated Stop. A builder whose unbounded background run (or a chain of runs) then stalls, the session silent, is never named - the session sits idle forever with actionable work, the exact defect this task fixes. The only way to keep a Stop-armed check alive is one wake; the notice is the minimum text for it (BREVITY-cut by message-check), and with the 2,400 s wait covering a Monitor's full cap it arises only for runs longer than that. The GM's own framing ('a cron that fires every 5 minutes') presumes a check that keeps firing; this is the only means here to keep it firing. Not a word-level carve-out: it serves the purpose rather than gutting it.

decisions.summary: The notice is said every time live work outlasts the wait, not once
decisions.why: Adjudicated separately, same route: each wake is a new check with the same physical limit, so saying it once and then exiting silently at the next deadline reintroduces the dead check and the never-named stalled builder. Repetition is the existence decision applied at every deadline, not a further departure.

decisions.summary: Cadence one notice per IDLE_SECS + WAIT_SECS (45 minutes, a CONVENTION) while a builder's run outlasts the wait
decisions.why: Not a separate departure: given the legitimate wake, how often it comes trades notice frequency against how late a stalled builder is named; a 4,000 s timeout was measured to run with no clamp found, so a longer cadence is available, but choosing among them is design and cost, not fidelity - the request fixes no cadence. The plan flags the cost to the GM ('the GM may cut it').

decisions.summary: The hand-on notice is outside make guard-messages' corpus (as T193's idle words are) and was judged by message-check on a hand-built bundle: FIDELITY passed, BREVITY cuts applied
decisions.why: The 2026-11-23 hook-output request asked for brevity with no loss of fidelity, reviewed by a subagent; the notice was so reviewed and cut. The corpus gap is an existing reach of a check, not a narrowing of this request, and it leaves no wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: After T193 (landed) and before T200; classed as performance work (removes false wakes, names a Monitor-length stall ~10 minutes after the watch ends instead of never)
decisions.why: Order follows the GM's 2026-11-20 rule that performance work comes first and the 2026-11-23 request that motivated the idle check; no scope beyond the defects named.

decisions.summary: declare reads a bare sheet name (UNIT=ochiba-roundtrip-test) as its building-review--<sheet> unit and prints that slug
decisions.why: Removes cause (a) of the measured refusal, a bare name looked up as a unit with no verdict record; directly fixes the defect the GM approved fixing (T214: the change-scoped review refuses a sheet with no earlier verdict).

decisions.summary: owed is taken from unit_sheet (reviews owed's own list) before any snapshot; a unit no delta owes gets exit 0 'not owed by this delta, no round', its last verdict left on file; a name with no pool sheet is refused as such, never read as not owed

Serves the 2026-11-23 rule that only a claim-changing edit triggers review and re-reviews are scoped to the change. Refusing an unknown name keeps a typo from passing as not owed; that is correctness, not new scope.

decisions.summary: where no .reviewed copy was kept, scoped/recover.rs finds the sheet as reviewed from git history (DEPTH 200 commits) plus the drawing as it reads now, hashed by files_key so the hash is the verdict's own; the match is written as the kept copy and the change-scoped prompt pairs it as before
decisions.why: Removes cause (c), a verdict written before T199 kept copies. Measured on the real sheet: the notes at 03cc1514d1 with today's drawing hash to the verdict's 9b7b9464d35cc002. DEPTH 200 is a search bound against 15 commits observed over seven weeks; a bound, not a carve-out of a case.

decisions.summary: the full round is still owed (1) for an owed unit with no PASS or NEEDS-WORK on file, i.e. a sheet never reviewed, and (2) where the sheet as reviewed is neither kept nor found in git history; the message now says which
decisions.why: Read against the GM's approval of 'T214 the change-scoped review refuses a sheet with no earlier verdict', keeping a full round anywhere could read as preserving the behavior asked to change, so it is ruled. Each case separately: (1) a sheet never reviewed has no earlier review to scope a re-review to, so a change-scoped round is physically impossible; the measured defect was a sheet that HAD a verdict being misread as having none, and that is fixed. (2) With no reviewed version anywhere, there is no baseline to diff the change against, which is again physically impossible, not merely awkward; the measured case is recovered. Neither case guts the purpose (no full round for a notes-only or nitpick fix on a sheet that was reviewed).

decisions.summary: the rest of T199's rule unchanged: a named non-nitpick, an open error or questionable finding, or an unchanged sheet still owes/refuses as before
decisions.why: The GM asked to fix the six defects named; T199's rule (an error or questionable finding owes the full round) was not among them and matches the 2026-11-23 rule that only factual findings cascade. Leaving it is not a carve-out of the requested fix.

decisions.summary: only the reviews crate's files touched; FR-012 red-first tests; 100% line coverage; exits via crate-checks and closing-checks
decisions.why: Constraints of execution and enforcement of the fix itself (red-first tests pin the requested behavior); no added behavior.

decisions.summary: left as not defects: make verify's first run taking 4 of 27 files (review tree takes the started task's files by design); per-clone verdict records differing; docs/reviews.md, the Makefile help line and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md's reviews row left as they read, still true but less complete
decisions.why: Per constitution XIV v2.36.0 a defect is a wrong outcome; none of these is one: the first two are by design and owed nothing either way, and the docs stay true. Nothing here is a defect deferred, so FR-009's filed-task demand does not bite.

decisions.summary: the task is tagged [perf] under FR-013 as builders'-loop work (no full review round for a notes-only nitpick fix)
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that makes the builders' loop faster as performance work; this ordering choice sits inside the GM's 2026-11-20 rule and inside his 2026-11-24 instruction to fix all six before resuming.

decisions.summary: The phrase arm of change::fires (ABSENCE: 'the one case', 'only one case', 'every plan', and says_absence) is removed rather than narrowed; the alternative of tying a phrase to the pop-up sentence sharing the new block's subject was measured and rejected.
decisions.why: The GM (2026-11-24) approved fixing T212, '8 false sends from three fixed phrases'. The convergence talk separates cascades that could plausibly have needed review from changes that never could. Removing the arm that produced the false sends serves that directly. It stays within the request only if real absence breaks still send. Item 9's dated replay (2026-11-24, the three landings) says they do: 0 of the 17 page-caused corrections and none of the cascade test's 3 are missed, and the arm (c) corrections are each sent by the addition rule alone. That replay was not re-run here (bundle-only review), so this ruling rests on it. Choosing the drop over the narrower alternative is a design choice, not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: judged (triage.rs) passes no new findings; T209's addition rule and then the triage agent decide instead, landed as one change with T209 (item 5).
decisions.why: This follows from the drop. Absence detection moves to T209's addition rule, which is itself one of the six fixes the GM approved on 2026-11-24. Because the two land together (item 5), there is no window in which absence breaks go undetected.

decisions.summary: new_findings stays, because the claims' triage reads it.
decisions.why: Keeping a reader that another part of the pipeline still uses removes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The fix covers all 11 sends the arm made over the three landings (10 cleared, 1 kept by the addition rule), not just the 8 named in the task title.
decisions.why: The '8' in the GM's line is the cascade test's count: item 12 names main-gate's three checks and servants' quarters' depiction, each on two pairs (0097/0334 and 0108.drawing/0334). Item 9 clears all of those pairs. Applying the same fix to the arm's other sends in the same replays is the same defect at wider reach, not added scope.

decisions.summary: Two sends remain and are recorded with 'Found and left? none': residence x 0107, sent by the addition rule (the doma phrase), and servants' quarters x 0097, sent through the echo check (a check session's rewording of 'a few men to each').
decisions.why: Neither is a send from the three phrases. One comes from T209's addition rule reading the pop-up's stated absence. The other comes from the echo check, which the GM approved on 2026-11-23 as T186's first filter, and it fires on a pair other than the 8 false ones. Item 9 records both openly, so nothing T212 was asked to fix is left undone.

decisions.summary: The task is labeled performance work ([perf]): 10 phrase-only sends no longer reach the triage agent.
decisions.why: The GM (2026-11-20) asked to prioritize performance improvements, and the convergence talk is about time spent on cascades that fix nothing. Fewer triage-agent dispatches fits that. The label affects scheduling only, not what the fix does.

decisions.why: These are the standard exits. The green condition matches both what the request asks for (no false sends) and its purpose (no missed corrections).

decisions.summary: change::fires gains change::addition: a sentence of a block new outright that shares a word trigram with the pop-up, all three words naming a thing (SUBJECT_WORDS = 3, NOT_SUBJECT excluded), sends the pop-up on with a reason naming sentence and phrase.
decisions.why: This is the fix the GM approved on 2026-11-24 for T209 ('a new fact contradicting a pop-up is cleared'): new facts now reach the agent triage behind a mechanical first filter, the shape the GM approved on 2026-11-23 (echo first, agent after). Dated replay (item 9, 2026-11-24): the stables x 0108 drawing pair is sent, 18 of 167 cleared pairs newly sent.

decisions.summary: Only blocks new outright are read by the addition rule; a rewritten block stays the echo's.
decisions.why: A division of labour between two filters, not a reach left out: rewritten blocks already pass through T186's echo, which the GM approved as the first filter for edits on 2026-11-23. The defect T209 names is a pure addition the echo cannot see (the section's title).

decisions.summary: A block that arrived with an edit from a page the reader reached before (Change::arrived_edited, paired at PAIR_RATIO) is treated as a move; its edit is read by the echo on the source page, not by the addition rule.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-23: 'a split is a move' and 'nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs'. The edit riding on the move is not dropped: the echo still reads it on the source page (T194's rule; the pinned test a_split_like_t184_s_owes_only_the_pop_up_repeating_changed_words still owes the pop-up that repeats the changed words), which is the GM's 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' applied to it.

decisions.summary: fires keeps its signature (found unused) so the claims crate's caller is untouched; the claims triage therefore gets the addition rule and loses the phrase arm with the pop-ups', not replayed on claims.
decisions.why: Both behaviors are the same two approved fixes (T209 and T212) reaching the one shared function; nothing the GM asked is withheld from either consumer. The lack of a claims replay is a verification gap stated openly (no tool replays a past claims triage), not a narrowing of the fix.

decisions.summary: Ordered after T186 and T194; landed as one change with T212, whose phrase arm the addition rule replaces.
decisions.why: Sequencing inside the six fixes the GM asked for together before the port resumes ('Yes let's fix all 6 of those before we resume').

decisions.summary: Of the 18 newly sent pairs, 13 share only a phrase (7 from the north/south/edo town magistracy family) and are left for the agent triage to clear.
decisions.why: An over-sending first filter whose extra sends reach only the agent triage, not a review or an edit, is the shape the GM accepted on 2026-11-23 (the echo fired on 55 of 119 pairs). Dated replay, item 9: 149 of the 167 cleared pairs stay cleared. Whether the net against T212's 8 removed fixed-phrase sends holds is T212's section's to answer.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the rule matches a 3-word phrase, not a meaning, so a new sentence that contradicts a pop-up in other words is still cleared by the tool (the stables Depiction itself shares no phrase; its pair is sent through the About's 'classic warrior stable').
decisions.why: The task as told to the GM is a class ('a new fact contradicting a pop-up is cleared') and the rule catches only the part that shares a subject phrase, so this narrows it. It is legitimate on the GM's own words, not on the record's clean count: on 2026-11-23 he approved a MECHANICAL first filter with the agent triage after it, and a tool cannot match meaning, so meaning-level matching means sending every addition pair to the agent. That would send up to all 167 pairs the tool clears today (item 9, 2026-11-24) instead of 18, and would bring back the cascade of reviews 'mostly not finding actual problems' that he stopped on 2026-11-23. A pair that is sent is read whole by the agent, so the named stables Depiction does reach a judge. SUBJECT_WORDS is a recorded knob to move if a missed case is measured.

decisions.summary: Marked as performance work ([perf]).
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 rule on prioritising performance work; the tool keeps unrelated additions cleared so no full check is owed.

decisions.summary: One reading of 'did this claim's code move': the triage's gather_code calls index::code_kept (the fingerprint, or the pre-anchor fingerprint with the class word kept, T204) as claims-owed's owed_one does, instead of comparing the fingerprint alone.
decisions.why: This is the fix the GM approved on 2026-11-24 ('Yes let's fix all 6 of those before we resume') for T211, '22 claims forced by the item anchors'; it applies the approved convergence rule that only a claim-changing edit triggers review.

decisions.summary: A cleared row's record writes the anchored fingerprint so the row heals to it.
decisions.why: Completes the same fix: without it the row would keep reading as unanchored and the anchor would be re-compared each time; it changes no claim.

decisions.summary: Only an anchor named with its class word kept is no code change; a class change still reads as changed (T204's reading, shared).
decisions.why: The defect is anchors forcing claims; the replay shows all 22 unforced under this reading, so the class condition leaves no part of the defect unfixed, and it reuses the already-accepted T204 rule rather than adding one.

decisions.summary: Exit counted as the 22 no longer forced, each cleared or sent by the filter; one (#wells by use) goes to the triage agent on words of the edit it repeats.
decisions.why: The one sent is routed by the echo filter the GM approved as T186's first filter, not forced by its anchor; no defect is left.

decisions.summary: Constraints: red test first, 100% coverage, only this crate's files; no map changes; ordered after T204, beside T210 and T213.
decisions.why: Process and order inside the task; nothing the GM asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: Booked as performance work: 22 full impl-drift checks per section edit move to the filter.
decisions.why: Scheduling class under FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 rule; it narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Found and left: none.
decisions.why: No defect deferred.

decisions.summary: relabeled_only's MISLABELED arm passes only a relabel: the stored claim's account equal word for word to the claim's account now (account_of, split as parse_claim splits it); the backing (class or cited question) free to change.
decisions.why: This is the fix the GM approved on 2026-11-24 ('T213 a claim marked mislabeled can be rewritten unchecked' ... 'Yes let's fix all 6 of those'): a restated account is now owed. Leaving the label and its backing free keeps the convergence talk's 'attested versus guess ... cascades mechanically' and the approved rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration'.

decisions.summary: A row storing no claim is no relabel, so it is owed.
decisions.why: Where no stored account exists the account cannot be shown unchanged; treating it as owed checks more, not less, and serves the request that a mislabeled claim not be rewritten unchecked.

decisions.summary: relabel_answered (the push's carry, carry.rs) reads the same rule, so a restated account no longer answers a MISLABELED verdict there either.
decisions.why: Closes the same defect on the second path that reads it; without it a rewrite could still pass at the push, defeating the fix.

decisions.summary: A relabel alone still owes nothing; T204's item-naming arms are untouched.
decisions.why: Preserves what the GM asked for in the convergence talk (labels cascade mechanically) and leaves another task's settled behavior alone; it is not a carve-out from T213, whose defect is the account rewrite only.

decisions.summary: Two fixtures that asserted the defect (an account rewrite passing as a relabel) are restated as true relabels; a new red-first test pins a restated account as owed.
decisions.why: Tests that encoded the defect are corrected to the fixed behavior while still covering the relabel-passes case; the new test only fails when the requested fix is absent - enforcement of the request.

decisions.summary: The 8 MISLABELED claims newly owed (the T400 miss among them) are owed impl-drift at this task's landing claims round, not deferred; no map change; nothing found and left.
decisions.why: Those 8 are exactly the unchecked restatements the defect let through; checking them at landing is the fix taking effect, not a narrowing or deferral.

decisions.summary: Order after T204, beside T210 and T211; one landing; exits green/red via arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Scheduling inside the GM's instruction to fix all six before the port resumes.

decisions.summary: A section snapshot keeps its words in the per-clone blob map (key section:<core>), written by each bundle that snapshots a section and kept by every record of a snapshot; section_words reads kept words first, then git history, so a regenerated row shows as a pair judged per claim by T191's filter.
decisions.why: This is the fix for the defect the GM approved fixing on 2026-11-24 (T210: 147 claims forced after a generated doc regenerated), and it serves the convergence rule that only a claim-changing edit triggers review. It fixes the root cause, not only the 147.

decisions.summary: gather_section reads each section's edit once and its claims share it (Gathered::section_lost), where the history search used to run once per claim; keep_blobs shared.
decisions.why: This is performance work on the same path (an unfixed replay ran for over 180 s). FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 words put performance first, and no behavior the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The kept texts and the removed-words search move to triage/kept.rs and the backfills to commands/backfill.rs, re-exported under their old paths, to meet constitution X clause 13's file-size bar.
decisions.why: This is a mechanical move to meet a standing project rule and changes no behavior.

decisions.summary: A removed block whose words neither the kept snapshot nor the history holds still forces its section's claims to a full impl-drift. That happens for a snapshot recorded before T210, a snapshot of uncommitted words triaged in another clone, or one older than the history depth.
decisions.why: I judged each case separately. (a) Snapshots recorded before T210 of words no commit holds: the old words do not exist anywhere, so no diff can be shown and the general rule is physically impossible. (b) Beyond the 60-commit history: this can arise only for a stale snapshot whose section changed away long ago without a new snapshot. A section unchanged since its snapshot is found one commit back, and every post-T210 snapshot carries kept words. (c) An uncommitted snapshot triaged in a different clone: the snapshotting clone's own landing claims round triages with the kept words and re-records the snapshot (claims-triaged keeps sections), so this needs a stale snapshot to travel unrecorded. In all three cases the outcome is one extra full check, never a missed claim, which is not a wrong outcome under XIV's definition of a defect. The case the GM approved fixing (a regenerated row reverting words the same clone snapshotted) is fixed and measured: 147 owed, 0 forced, 3 sent. The cascade test's own pre-T210 state was already settled by the arbiter's accept ruling (ask:449-T403-claims-147-forced). The carve-out does not gut the purpose.

decisions.summary: gather_code's empty-hunk force (a code fingerprint moved with no hunk to show) is left as it is.
decisions.why: This is not part of T210's defect, which concerns a section's words after regeneration. The code did change and there is no hunk to show how, and leaving an unrelated existing path untouched narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The plan prices and declines refusing claims-checked while a generated doc is stale against its generator.
decisions.why: This is a design alternative that was not taken. make quick already turns red on a stale generated doc, and the chosen fix covers every reverted snapshotted section, not just generated rows.

decisions.summary: T210 runs after T191 and T204, lands beside T211 and T213 in one landing, and is tagged [perf].
decisions.why: The task depends on T191's filter. The [perf] tag follows FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 rule on scheduling performance work first.

decisions.summary: A section snapshot's words move from the clone's .git blob map into a committed file, dev/claims-section-words.jsonl, read in any clone.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-24 question ('should it live in the clone rather than in the repo?') was about T210's kept section words, and his 'Yes let's fix all 6 of those before we resume.' covers T210's wrong outcome: 147 claims forced in another clone. Keeping the words in the repository removes that outcome, measured by the replay (fresh clone 147 forced unfixed, 0 fixed).

decisions.summary: The file holds one line per block, keyed by block digest, sorted, and pruned to the blocks of the snapshots the index's rows name. It is written only when it changes.
decisions.why: This is a choice of storage format for the same goal and narrows nothing. The prune keeps every block of every snapshot a row still names, so no word the triage needs is dropped.

decisions.summary: Every writer that records a section snapshot writes its words through one path, save_recorded, plus claims backfill-sections. The class census is stated with its method (rg over save_store( and "section").
decisions.why: Making every writer write the words is what makes the fix whole. The census carries its search space and method, as FR-009 asks of a fix that names a class of writers.

decisions.summary: Page texts stay per clone and are not moved into the repository.
decisions.why: The GM's question and the defect T215 fixes (T210's) name section words only, so page texts lie outside what was asked rather than being cut from it. Ruled on that scope, not on the block's unmeasured premise that git history holds every page's text.

decisions.summary: The per-clone section path (kept_section, the section: keys) is deleted, and a stale section: key in a clone's blob map is ignored.
decisions.why: Purpose test: another clone forces nothing. The backfilled file resolves all 257 blocks of the 20 snapshots the committed index names, measured 2026-11-24. That measurement does not reach a clone holding a snapshot recorded but not yet landed. The worst case there is a one-time force, which is the pre-fix behavior and not a new wrong outcome, and the bundle shows no such clone exists. So the deletion does not gut the fix.

decisions.summary: The one force left: a removed block whose words are in neither the file nor history owes in full. A line that does not parse, or whose words do not hash to its digest, is not read.
decisions.why: No path the block describes loses the words of a named snapshot. The prune keeps them, a union merge only adds lines, and every record writes them. So this is the fallback for lost or corrupt data, not a case carved out of the fix.

decisions.summary: The file merges with merge=union. A union may keep a pruned line or leave the file unsorted, which the reader tolerates and the next write repairs.
decisions.why: This keeps two clones' records from conflicting, measured by the merge test (a conflict without the attribute, clean with it). It is a mechanism serving the same goal.

decisions.summary: The file is registered wherever dev/claims-pages.json is: the push's claims gate (cohort, push::judges) and the gate preflight's RECORDS.
decisions.why: This treats the new record the way the existing claims records are treated so the gate judges it. It is consistency and enforcement of the fix, not new scope.

decisions.summary: section_words and gather_section no longer return a Result, after clippy's unnecessary_wraps.
decisions.why: An incidental signature change forced by the static checks once the functions can no longer fail. It is not a scope decision.

decisions.summary: Not performance work, with no [perf] tag. Found and left: none.
decisions.why: It fixes a wrong outcome (a full impl-drift owed for text already checked) under 'fix all 6'. No defect is deferred.

decisions.summary: The carrier: an ad-hoc dispatch with no model asks for the session's model by a prompt line `SESSION_MODEL: <reason>` (line start, reason of two words / eight characters, logged as the guard log's detail).
decisions.why: The GM asked that judging agents inherit the session model while the Sonnet rule for read/fetch/translate/extract stays enforced ('that ruling from before is something that I still want'). Omitting the model is how inheritance happens, and the guard needs some way to tell an omission the caller decided on from an accidental one, or reading work would land on the session's model by default. A marker line is a mechanism for doing what was asked and narrows nothing. Recording the reason follows the project's every-firing-recorded convention.

decisions.summary: Any named model other than sonnet or haiku is refused, the session's own model included (stricter than the task line's 'a named opus or fable that is not the session's'). The allow-list form means a future alias is refused until its tier is decided.
decisions.why: Judged against the GM's words, not against the task line (which is the session's text; spec-cited.md is empty). The GM asked for 'inheriting the parent session model for anything that judges' and 'if I switch back to Opus 5.5, then I would want them to use that'. A pinned name that happens to equal today's session model stops following at the next switch, so refusing it moves toward the request rather than away from it. What this costs is the ability to pin an ad-hoc judging agent to some other model, and nobody asked for that.

decisions.summary: A named sonnet beside the SESSION_MODEL line passes as sonnet; the line is inert.
decisions.why: Sonnet is the tier the GM's kept ruling enforces for reading work. The caller named it, and what is named is what runs. Neither request quote is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A dispatch with no model and no SESSION_MODEL line stays refused (no-model).
decisions.why: This is the GM's own words verbatim: 'that ruling from before is something that I still want with regards to enforcing that Sonnet should be used to read, fetch, translate, or extract.' Letting an unmarked omission through would put reading work on the session's model by default.

decisions.summary: Defined agent types (files under .claude/agents/) pass whatever model they name, with that check moved ahead of the model check. Their pinned tiers in agent_models.rs ('judgment is on Opus') are left alone.
decisions.why: This is the one decision here that could narrow the GM's literal 'anything that judges', so it is decided on his words alone. The subject of his question is 'the general purpose subagents that you're firing off to do stuff', and he wants them to 'use whatever model it is that I have selected'. His second message changes 'that ruling from before', which he identifies by its enforcement of Sonnet for read, fetch, translate and extract. That is the ad-hoc dispatch rule whose text said 'opus for anything that judges'. Nothing in either quote reaches the defined review agents' frontmatter tiers, so the request as written never covered them. Leaving them alone therefore does not carve anything out of it. The same builder-versus-defined-review-agent line is drawn by the spec at FR-006. I relied on neither the session-written heading nor the plan's own assertion of scope.

decisions.summary: The inheritance rule covers ad-hoc agents that build as well as those that judge.
decisions.why: The GM's first quote asks that the general-purpose subagents 'you are firing off to do stuff use whatever model it is that I have selected', and builders are among them. The request was set off by builders named opus under a Fable session.

decisions.summary: haiku is in the allow-list beside sonnet.
decisions.why: Per the Approach, the old guard passed any named model, so haiku was already allowed. The GM asked to keep the Sonnet half of the ruling and to replace only its Opus half. Keeping haiku allowed changes nothing he asked to change. (The bundle does not quote the 2026-09-19 rule's text, so this rests on the plan's description of the guard as built.)

decisions.summary: workflow_hooks holds a script's ad-hoc agent() call to the same rule: the model literal is read, a computed model is refused as '?', the marker is accepted anywhere in the call's text including a comment, and a marked call is recorded session-model.
decisions.why: An agent() call from a workflow script is an ad-hoc subagent the session fires off, so the GM's rule reaches it. Without this change, scripts would go on pinning opus. Refusing a model the guard cannot read is how it enforces the Sonnet half of the kept ruling. Accepting the marker in the call text is the carrier of (a), fitted to that call's form.

decisions.summary: The SESSION_MODEL line is a compliant form, not an escape, and the guard has no escape.
decisions.why: The guard already had no escape, and the compliant dispatch is always available. FR-012's escape requirement covers FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, not this guard, so nothing that was asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The rule is restated in the root CLAUDE.md and its suite check, docs/guards.md, docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md, docs/research-doctrine.md, page-session-rules.md and rust/guard/CLAUDE.md. Spec directories 252 and 293 are left alone as history.
decisions.why: These make the rule's written text match the rule the GM set. The search space is stated: grep for the rule's two phrases over the tree outside .git, observed 2026-11-24. Leaving history unedited narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The SESSION_MODEL line passes only on general-purpose, Plan and claude, the types measured 2026-11-24 to run on the session's model; any other ad-hoc type without a named sonnet/haiku is refused with one message naming the two routes; defined types and sonnet/haiku dispatches unchanged.

The probe showed a marked Explore ran Opus 5.5 under a Fable 5.2 session and was logged session-model, which is the opposite of the request. Accepting the line only where the type is measured to inherit is what makes the rule true. The reading route (sonnet) is untouched.

decisions.summary: The list holds types measured to inherit, not types found pinned, so the unprobed built-ins (web-fetch, claude-code-guide, statusline-setup) and any type added later are refused for judging until probed.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested behavior. The GM asked that judging run on his selected model, not that every built-in type be usable for judging. general-purpose has every tool those types have, so no judging work is lost. Letting an unprobed type through would assume an inheritance nobody measured. That is the gap T217 exists to close, and the earlier MODE 4 round ruled passing web-fetch a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Every refusal of an unlisted type (marked, unmarked, or naming another model) prints the new two-route message instead of the rule text's 'Re-send the SAME dispatch', and the rule text is unchanged.
decisions.why: Wording of the refusal only. It refuses nothing that T216 and Decision (a) do not already refuse. It stops the old message from pointing the caller into a second refusal, so it serves the request and the project's refusal-names-the-compliant-command convention.

decisions.summary: A workflow agent() call that names no agentType is treated as an unmeasured type. It passes only if it names sonnet or haiku to read, and is otherwise refused (PINNED), with the route agentType 'general-purpose' plus the line. A GP_OK untyped stage may only read.
decisions.why: The untyped call is the default workflow subagent, not general-purpose, and nobody has probed what model it runs on. The reference's sentence that it inherits is a document, not a measurement, and this project's standing rule is measured, never assumed. Refusing it applies Decision (a)'s standard to a route the request covers ('anything that judges'). A judging stage keeps a working route (agentType general-purpose, which already passed without GP_OK), so nothing the GM asked for is lost. The refusal reaches only judging dispatches on an unmeasured path, which is exactly what the GM asked to have enforced.

decisions.summary: The docs, rules page, index line, doc comments and suites that carry SESSION_MODEL are restated. The list comes from a stated grep over the tree outside specs/ and .git. The root CLAUDE.md's two clauses are left unchanged, and the guard's message carries the type list.
decisions.why: Documentation follows the guard. The census states its search space. The root clause's two routes (sonnet to read; no model plus the line to judge or build) are still true and are not narrowed.

decisions.summary: A FINDING row keeps the claim as said (class word kept, anchors dropped) and its unit's claim labels fingerprinted; bundle.rs writes them to units.json, reply.rs copies them onto finding rows only.
decisions.why: Record tooling that makes a relabel visible to the index, which is what 'attested versus guess ... cascades mechanically' (convergence talk, 2026-11-23) needs; storing them on findings only is a design choice inside that.

decisions.id: D2 relabel answers MISLABELED via said
decisions.summary: index::relabel_answered reads the backing from said, so a relabel the fingerprint cannot see answers its MISLABELED verdict; one index::answered is shared by the push, the report and the clean gate.
decisions.why: Directly carries the labels-cascade-mechanically rule and T213 (the account unchanged, only the backing may change); one shared reading changes no scope.

decisions.why: The task's own wrong outcome (findings that no longer stand printed beside owed 0); nothing is hidden since the count is shown and ALL=1 lists them.

decisions.id: D4 sibling change re-owes the finding
decisions.summary: A finding whose unit's claim labels changed since judged is owed impl-drift again rather than answered or hidden.
decisions.why: Only a claim-changing edit re-owes a check and only the finding is re-owed (review scoped to the change), and 'if there are real defects, then I do want to find them' forbids answering it mechanically where only a judgment can say.

decisions.id: D5 legacy rows stand until T220 re-judges them
decisions.summary: A row recorded before T221 has neither field; it is answered only where its stored claim differs from the claim with and without anchors, otherwise it stands until judged again; the task's four named rows are re-judged in T220's claims round, ordered after T221.
decisions.why: The task's four rows keep printing until T220 instead of being cleared by T221, so this narrows what the task fixes. A mechanical answer is not possible for them: the trio's stored claim equals normalized() of today's claim (the class word was never stored), and palette.rs's finding needs a judgment on whether its new sibling claims answer it. Clearing them without that data would risk hiding a wrong outcome, which the GM's 'real defects ... find them and fix them' forbids. The re-judgment is the ordinary path in an open, ordered task of the same bundle, not an unfiled deferral.

decisions.summary: Fixes a found bug: a MISLABELED claim that only named its item, class kept, read as rewritten and so as answered at the push.

decisions.id: D7 tests as the step pins

decisions.summary: core/record/effect.rs reads one form, `effect: <map|sheet|page|tool> - <wrong outcome>`; `effect: none`, an effect naming none of the four, and no effect name none
decisions.why: The four now cover constitution XIV's whole definition of a defect (a map/sheet/page that reads wrong or contradicts a finding; a tool, guard or check that crashes, hangs, refuses valid input or answers wrongly, which takes in a check passing bad work or refusing good). The round-1 narrowing (tool defects dropped) is repaired, and a tool note is filed in the tests (451 found row 26).

decisions.why: Serves the convergence talk ('cascading changes ... not fixing any real flaws ... we have to fix that') and XIV's rule that a difference is not a defect; a true row is still filed (row 170 test) and an unfiled line is shown with the form, so 449's 'real defects are found and fixed' is not cut back.

decisions.summary: make review-verdict refuses an `outside` finding whose `what` names no effect, with the form

decisions.summary: every emitter states the same rule, enumerated from `grep -rln 'OUTSIDE THE CHANGE' rust scripts docs .claude Makefile l7r` plus a grep for the `outside` severity, each hit read, measured 2026-11-24; a note naming no effect goes under NOTED, NOT FILED in the reply

decisions.summary: what names none of the four (a wording, a page only silent, a difference that reads fine) is listed and dropped
decisions.why: These are not defects under XIV v2.36.0 and the GM 2026-11-19 ('things which are different than you expected but still work perfectly well'); a silence that makes a page read wrong still names `page`.

decisions.summary: the third channel (`[outside the change]` verdict on an owed key) already files nothing at claims `report`; impl-drift.md and the claims MANIFEST corrected from 'filed as a task' to `make claims-report` lists it

decisions.summary: verification: unit tests red with the form's reading removed, plus live impl-drift rounds on row 170 (filed) and row 178 (not filed) replay bundles after the verdict; order after T221 before T220; exits via set-down and make arbiter-ask; found-and-left none

decisions.summary: The record search runs in the tool at make claims-checked (silent.rs, called before the reply is vetted), not in the bundle builder, so IN-STEP claims cost nothing and OUTSIDE THE CHANGE lines are covered.

decisions.summary: The task line names make canon / the registry as the search; the plan uses a word ranking over research/questions in the tool instead, because make canon searches the GM's setting notes and semantic-find did not return 0107 in its first five (measured 2026-11-24).
decisions.why: The parenthetical is the task author's guess at a means, not the GM's words; the substitute is the one that finds the motivating sentence, so it serves the task's purpose better rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: Read the nearest three pages then file; NEAREST=3 is a knob labeled GUESS; no score threshold.
decisions.why: A design parameter inside the requested behavior; labeled as a guess per the project's rule.

decisions.summary: The pages a hold named are kept in .git/claims-searched.json under the claim's key; the next reply on that key passes once those pages are bundled, however reworded, then the entry is forgotten.
decisions.why: Ends the round after one widened reading, which is what the convergence talk asks (no cascade of reviews that change nothing); the finding is still read against the pages the search named.

A conservatively labeled GUESS whose cited pages are silent is not a wrong outcome under XIV's defect definition (no map reads wrong, no finding is contradicted), so leaving it carries no deferred defect and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: building-review.md: a dated entry of a sheet's notes (Review log line, line under a dated heading, entry naming its feature/task) is history, not held to the sheet as it stands; an overtaken older entry is no finding and owes no 'since superseded' pointer; only present-tense text (choices, program, Result/summary paragraph) is held to the drawing

The present-tense text, including the Result paragraph, stays held, so real defects are still filed; no requested review is removed.

decisions.summary: record-format.md: HISTORY rule kept whole, gains one sentence - a dated entry is history by its form, ruled on as HISTORY (useful kept, rest proposed for removal), never reported as a stale present-tense statement; permits no change log on a research page
decisions.why: Leaves the GM's 2026-09-07 HISTORY rule intact (dated entries are still found and proposed for removal); it only fixes which finding class they are filed under, so nothing the GM asked for is narrowed. One of the two agent files the task names.

decisions.summary: Verification by one ad-hoc agent following the clone's edited building-review.md over the two notes files as they stood before 452's fixes, since a dispatched defined agent reads the mirror's file (T219); record-format's sentence stated on the rule alone, no recorded case found
decisions.why: A method of checking the change, with a red case (Hayakawa T312/T299/T276 not filed) and a green case (the round-trip Result paragraph's figures still filed) that together show real defects are still found; narrows no requirement.

decisions.summary: Order: last of the restatement audit's five, after T219; classified not performance work; found-and-left none; no map changes
decisions.why: Scheduling and classification inside the task set; it is not measurement work (the GM 2026-11-20 rule) nor a speed-up of a tool, and leaves no defect unfixed.

decisions.summary: impl-drift.md's FILED DEPARTURE paragraph re-judges a filed departure each time it is bundled: no longer departs -> DRIFTED fix: claim; departs but not a wrong outcome -> DRIFTED fix: claim; effect: none; only a standing wrong outcome keeps known (NNN Tnn) fix: code, with ask:417-T49-claims kept whole for it

The arbiter's ruling stopped relabeling of a departure that stands; a departure that no longer exists or is not a defect is outside what it protected, and the one that stands keeps it whole.

decisions.summary: A procedure section's finding judged DRIFTED fix: code keeps a 'drawn' digest of every .rs file under rust/mode_a/src and is owed again (full check) when it differs; the over-owing cost accepted; per-claim unit pointers and re-owing every known drift each report priced and not taken
decisions.why: Tooling that makes 'once the code moves it is judged again' actually happen so stale code fixes are not printed and real defects are still found (449 request 2026-11-24). Choosing the coarser digest over alternatives is design, not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: Rows judged before the digest lands keep none; every standing row was re-judged and recorded in this task, and the one still a code fix (452 T24's compound shrine) now carries its drawn digest via make claims-checked; no fix: code section row is left without one, measured 2026-11-24 by reading the index's rows by key
decisions.why: Round 1's finding closed: the section now states the 452 T24 re-judgment was recorded (second reading after the bundle was rebuilt with the pages make claims-checked named) and the row keeps its digest, with a one-shot measurement label. With no standing fix: code row undigested, the no-backfill rule leaves no row outside the fix.

No wrong outcome is left standing.

decisions.summary: The six standing keys and 452 T24 bundled by make claims-bundle, judged by an agent told to follow the clone's impl-drift.md (the dispatched agent reads the mirror's), recorded by make claims-checked
decisions.why: Procedure for running the round on the edited rule; decides nothing about scope.

decisions.summary: The arch dimensions claim (docs/buildings.md) and NOTICE_BOARD_MAX_FT's claim (compound.rs), both DRIFTED fix: claim; effect: none, are left to their owners' restatement tasks (452 doc restatements, 449 Mode A claims); not filed as defects
decisions.why: Each is a claim's wording with no visible effect, which constitution XIV v2.36.0 says is not a defect; leaving a non-defect to its owner is not a narrowing and needs no ruling, and claims-report keeps listing both until restated.

decisions.summary: 417 T33 stays open; closing it is its own feature's
decisions.why: Outside this task's request; the report surfaces it to its owner once no claim names it.

decisions.summary: The clean 'before' of a mixed row is read from dev/claims-index.json's own git history: walk from HEAD as far as checked_at, take the newest row whose build is not mixed.
decisions.why: The arbiter's tooling_fix (ask:mixed-build-241-claims) orders a mixed answer re-triaged by the clean build; a triage judges a change from a before, and the mixed row overwrote it, so reading it from the index's history is the mechanism the ruling needs, not a change of what it asks.

decisions.summary: At a landing only the fields a triage writes (research, pages, section, code, core, reads, triaged, cleared, triage, build) are withdrawn; verdict, note, date, claim and rests stay.
decisions.why: Withdraws exactly the mixed build's answer the ruling says must not be trusted, and keeps the verdicts the ruling keeps; no claim text or full verdict is touched.

decisions.summary: A mixed clear or agent triage owes what claims-owed's ordinary rules find between the clean answer before and the tree: nothing where the tree is back where that answer judged it (73), a tool clear then the agent where a section, page or code moved (147 cleared, 21 to the agent), a full check only where no triage judges the change (1, the rewritten barracks claim).
decisions.why: This is the tooling_fix verbatim in effect: re-judge with the clean build, mechanical clear first, then claims-triage, impl-drift only for what neither reproduces. Owing nothing where nothing changed since a clean verdict is the clean build's own ordinary answer and is the GM's convergence rule (2026-11-23: only a claim-changing edit triggers review). The ruling's 229/57 split is a count, not a rule; formerly agent-triaged rows the tool now clears are cleared 'mechanical clear first' as the tooling_fix orders.

decisions.summary: A mixed answer with no clean answer in the walk, or whose claim has no row in a commit of the walk, owes impl-drift with its files named (fails closed).
decisions.why: Presumed wrong and ruled legitimate on three grounds: it fails toward more checking, never less, so it can pass no bad work; the ruling itself sends to impl-drift a claim 'neither reproduces', and with no clean before in the walk there is no change for a tool clear or the agent to judge, so neither can reproduce it; and T197's rule that a landing never trusts a mixed answer forbids the only other outcome (trusting it). The replay found a before for all 242 mixed rows, so the case guts nothing the ruling asked for.

decisions.summary: A full impl-drift verdict is never re-owed: verdict_row builds a fresh row with no build, and the 14 edited claims keep their verdicts.
decisions.why: The ruling's what says verbatim 'The 14 edited claims keep their full impl-drift verdicts'; a row with no build is not mixed and so lies outside the rule being fixed.

decisions.summary: The route is L7R_LAND_ALONE=1 make claims-triage, which writes the withdrawal, clears what the tool can and bundles the rest for the agent; agent TOUCHES go to impl-drift; no command added; claims-owed and the push's gate say the count, files and command.
decisions.why: The tooling_fix names landing-mode claims-owed/claims-triage as the place of the fix. No verb is added, so ask:t197-rejudge-verb (which cut a withdrawal verb for T184's 81 modal marks) stands; the withdrawal here is the re-judging the later ruling ordered, inside the existing command. Naming the count, files and command is the project's guard-message rule.

decisions.summary: Outside a landing the index is read as it stands.
decisions.why: T197's mixed-build rule and the ruling's fix are both landing-mode only; nothing outside a landing changes.

decisions.summary: section_words also reads the kept words' own history (dev/claims-section-words.jsonl), so the 8 pruned base blocks are found rather than forced.
decisions.why: Required for the re-triage to work on the measured rows, and T210/T215's rule that a section's words are never forced where they can be found.

decisions.summary: Fix found here: clear_page_moves never stamped its build, so a mixed clear went unmarked and a clean clear of a marked row stayed marked; stamp_build fixes it.
decisions.why: A wrong outcome in the very check this task corrects (the landing answers wrongly either way); fixing a known defect in the task is the standing fix-as-we-go rule, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Committed before the landing of 449 T423 T424 T418 T422 is run again; the coordinating session then re-judges; red exits through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The ruling's what (1)-(2): make and commit the tooling fix before any re-judging, then re-run the landing.

decisions.summary: The task is not tagged performance work.
decisions.why: The GM's words class this kind of fix as a defect, not a performance improvement: on 2026-11-24 the cascade rules' over-sends (T210's 147 forced claims, T211's 22) were 'defects' to 'fix all 6 of those before we resume', and T223 is the same class - a check owing a full check to claims nothing changed for, refusing a green landing. Its time saved is the effect of correcting a wrong outcome, as the plan says. The label also moves nothing: the ruling already orders T223 before the landing re-run.

decisions.summary: A record answer is counted as mixed only by an uncommitted file in RECORD: owed, bundle, their path dependencies (core, pool, registry, research, rust/guard/shared), rust/gate/src and the record crate; the record crate's other dependencies (archive, downloads, pages, semantic, trials, uncited) are left out on a grep of every caller of write_answer/write_judged.
decisions.why: This is the tooling_fix of ask:mixed-build-53-record-answers: an answer is mixed only when a dirty path lies in the closure of the crates that built and recorded it (owed, bundle and their transitive deps). RECORD is a superset of that closure. It adds rust/gate/src and the record crate, which keeps more of T197 than the ruling requires. The crates left out are not in the ruling's closure in the first place.

decisions.summary: A Markdown file outside the table's crates never counts; a Markdown file inside a table crate counts (include_str! fixtures).
decisions.why: The ruling names rust/gate/CLAUDE.md as a dirty path whose code could not have run. Markdown inside a table crate still counts, and the closure walk flags any included file the table does not count, so no file that can run is dropped.

decisions.summary: tests.rs and tests/ files inside a table crate still count; no test-only exclusion.
decisions.why: This counts more than the ruling's closure would strictly require, so T197 is kept. It is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Any Cargo.toml, rust/Cargo.lock and .cargo/config.toml always count, and so does a path the rule does not know.
decisions.why: This is conservative. It keeps T197's rule for every file whose effect on the build the closure cannot rule out.

decisions.summary: The claims side's mixed-build test is narrowed the same way through its own table CLAIMS (the claims crate's path-dependency closure, rust/gate/src, and the record crate's one included file), through the single Landing::paths call.
decisions.why: The tooling_fix names only the owed crate's record gate, so narrowing the claims side's T197 rule goes past its letter. The ruling's own why gives the reason. It calls the fault a false positive 'of the same class as mixed-build-241-claims', and it orders that the rule be narrowed by a tool and not waived again. Counting a dirty file that no claims verb can run is that same wrong outcome: a check refusing good work. Fixing it in this step is required by fix-as-we-go. The purpose test holds: T197 exists so that an answer judged by code that is not its own is not trusted. Code outside the claims verbs' closure cannot have judged the answer, and the closure test keeps the table honest as dependencies change.

decisions.summary: build::closure::gaps walks the [dependencies]/[build-dependencies] path entries and the include_str!/include_bytes! lines from each table's roots. It reports an unlisted crate that is reached, an entry nothing reaches, or an uncounted included file. Core's test runs it on the real tree, and core's Cargo.toml declares those crates so rust-test re-runs when a manifest moves.
decisions.why: This is the ruling's own requirement, 'a fixed table whose test fails when a dependency is added', and it only enforces that. Reading the include lines closes the rust/guard/shared to record-crate gap the plan found.

decisions.summary: The refusal message is unchanged. The fix is built before T218..T223 are re-landed, while nothing else records in the clone.
decisions.why: This follows the ruling's what (3) to (5) exactly.

decisions.summary: One reading type, Own, in core/build.rs; mixed asks it; Judged (owed/answers.rs) and Landing (claims/index.rs) each hold one Own in place of their own HEAD lookups
decisions.why: Where the fix lives, not what it trusts. The ruling's tooling_fix names both the owed record and the claim answers, and one shared reading puts the same rule in both.

decisions.summary: A stamped blob is the landing's own where it is its path's blob at HEAD, at a commit of the delta, or at the base; a stamped deleted is own where one of those commits holds no such file
decisions.why: This is the ruling's tooling_fix nearly word for word. The deleted arm is the same rule applied to a file's absence.

decisions.summary: Base = git merge-base HEAD origin/main (the base make land already diffs from); delta = base..HEAD; a merge of main moves the base and keeps the clone's own commits in the delta
decisions.why: The ruling names 'the landing's delta (f7c105b4a0..HEAD)' and 'its base' without saying how to find them. Using the landing's own diff base reads them as make land already does.

decisions.summary: Where no base is found (no origin/main, no shared history) the delta is empty and a blob is held to HEAD, the rule before this task ((d) still applies where the stamp commit is known)
decisions.why: With no base the ruling's delta and base are undefined, so the ruling's rule has nothing to compare against. The fallback is the stricter earlier rule: it trusts less, never more.

decisions.summary: A blob no commit holds still reads mixed (the real case: another builder's work in progress); measured over 302 record entries and 205 claim rows, one superseded answer holds such blobs
decisions.why: This keeps T197 unchanged. The ruling widens 'own' only to committed blobs, so an uncommitted blob still reads mixed, as it did before.

decisions.summary: A blob held at a commit of <stamp commit>..HEAD is also committed code, asked after HEAD/delta/base miss; a stamp commit git does not know adds nothing
decisions.why: This trusts more than the ruling's words, so it is tested as an exception. Taken literally, the ruling's rule would defeat the ruling's own stated purpose: 'ends the loop' and 'do not ask this question again'. The block measures it: once this landing is pushed, its commits fall behind the next landing's base. 189 claim rows stamped 1b064aa0de would then read mixed at the next landing of any clone, the same loop run once more. Against T197's purpose: (d) admits a blob only if a commit reachable from HEAD holds it, so it can never admit a blob that no commit holds. Another builder's uncommitted work therefore still reads mixed under (c). With (d), the block measures 0 of 205 rows and 0 of 302 record entries, the (c) one aside, left holding a blob that no commit since its stamp holds. It trusts only committed code, which is the ruling's own ground for its rule.

decisions.summary: build::current() drops from the stamp each dirty file whose stamped blob equals the launcher tree's HEAD now, so an answer by a binary whose sources were since committed unchanged carries a clean stamp and a triage clear by it writes no build row
decisions.why: The ruling's second clause is worded as a reading rule ('reads a stamp as clean once all its dirty blobs equal HEAD'). (f) applies it when the stamp is written, per file, against HEAD at that moment, which goes past the words, so it is tested as an exception. It is implied by the ruling's own clause, and it admits nothing T197 guards: a file is dropped only when its blob is committed at HEAD when the answer is recorded, so uncommitted work (T197's object) is never dropped and still reads mixed under (c). The one case where it differs from the read-time rule is a write-time HEAD the landing later loses through an amend or reset. That gives the answer the same standing a clean build at an amended-away commit already has, because the mixed rule reads only dirty blobs, so it opens no new class of trusted code. Without (f), the defect the block records goes on: each triage clear writes a build row into the tracked index for files that were HEAD's own. That is a wrong outcome the ruling's clause was aimed at.

decisions.id: D1 fifth label in the tooling
