decisions.summary: The root CLAUDE.md, research/CLAUDE.md, docs/research-doctrine.md, docs/research-record-rules.md, the page-session rules, the plan template's XII entry, the constitution 2.39.0 (XII narrowed), research-pass.md and escalation-check.md: a new guess is recorded UNRESEARCHED with no search; a search still comes first where a decision is foundational or a guess is likely visibly wrong; UNRESEARCHED is a question for the backlog, never for the GM
decisions.why: This is the rule change the GM accepted, exception included. 'XII narrowed' narrows the search-first rule, which is the change he asked for, not a narrowing of his request. The copies were found by a grep of the tree for the old wording, so the search space is stated.

decisions.summary: quote-check: an UNRESEARCHED sentence owes no footnote. impl-drift: five classes; UNRESEARCHED is never a finding for lacking a source, and is MISLABELED where its account states as found what no page gives. record-format: UNRESEARCHED is no session note. modal-research: an UNRESEARCHED bullet is not a finding for want of a search
decisions.why: These carry the GM's rule into the checks: a session may record an unsearched guess and move on. The MISLABELED case enforces his own distinction ('unresearched would mean that we know we have not yet checked'), so it is enforcement, not new scope.

decisions.summary: quote-check's old step 5 exempted every labeled GUESS. It now flags a GUESS with no absence note as GUESS-UNNOTED. The 148 GUESS blocks without a footnote (a proxy scan, 2026-11-25) are fixed as their pages are rechecked, by an absence note or by relabeling them UNRESEARCHED, with no sweep
decisions.why: One reading covers both halves. GUESS-UNNOTED only flags; it does not block or rewrite work. It enforces the GM's line between unsupported ('we did research and couldn't find anything') and unresearched, and that line means nothing if a GUESS need not record that a search ran. The 148 blocks are not defects under constitution XIV v2.36.0: a missing absence note changes no map, contradicts no research finding, and is a record gap no reader of the map sees. Leaving them to page rechecks with no sweep therefore carries no defect forward. It also fits the GM's purpose (move forward faster) and the 2026-11-23 rule against cascades that fix no real flaw.

decisions.summary: A standard question the record does not answer no longer owes a research pass before the modal is written. decisions.why: This applies 'a new guess recorded as UNRESEARCHED with no search' to pop-ups, with the exception the GM accepted, worded as he accepted it.

decisions.id: D6 make research-backlog as the backlog's reader

decisions.why: The offer named claims-report's UNRESEARCHED list as the backlog. This target adds grouping and a stage filter on top of that list and keeps claims-report's count, so nothing the GM accepted is removed. It serves 'searched at each port stage's end for the items that stage touched', and it adds page items because the label also lives on the pages.

decisions.summary: STAGE= selects the stage's own module (<stage>.rs and <stage>/) in the crates that define stage_<name>, plus every file of those crates that no stage's module holds, listed under a heading marking it shared. Excluding rust/mode_a only stops a name collision ('labels' matched eight Mode A files). No UNRESEARCHED item disappears: the unfiltered list shows every claim and item, and a glob reaches any path. Both choices rest on figures measured 2026-11-25.

decisions.id: D8 where the stage-end search lives

decisions.summary: After T237 (a builder's claims round split off) and before page sessions P13 and P14, 'which the GM's rule drops from the pre-port list'

decisions.id: D10 no map changes; exits, proofs and done

decisions.summary: theirs tells another task's file list apart by FILENAME == o and skips an empty line; blocked returns on an empty attribution, never BLOCKED

decisions.summary: a path is read only from a line opening with ^ *--> or Diff in, so a quoted source line holding an arrow is not read as a path
decisions.why: Fixes a second wrong outcome found here (a red on another task's file quoting such a line went untagged); fixed in this task, nothing deferred.

decisions.summary: a static red whose lines name no file says none could be attributed and all are counted as the caller's, listing the first 8 failure lines of the counted red, an APART crate's lines left out; hooks-test and quick, counted whole under T86, carry no note
decisions.why: Not a narrowing: hooks-test and quick do no attribution (T86 counts them whole), so there is nothing unattributed to report there and no wrong outcome is left; leaving an APART crate's lines out follows T86's rule that another task's red is reported apart. The red stays red (counted as the caller's), so no verdict is weakened.

decisions.summary: the BLOCKED line's wording is left as it is, since it already names each file and its task once the attribution is read
decisions.why: A difference left as it is that is not a defect once the attribution is fixed; BLOCKED stays red as constraint 2 requires.

decisions.summary: T239 carries T230's fix and tests and nothing of its own, ticking in T230's landing (make land F=451 T=T230,T239).
decisions.why: The same closing-checks fault filed twice; deferring wholly to T230's within-scope fix decides nothing new and leaves no defect.

decisions.summary: The size-edit rule (T184) reads the same measure as the cap and make question-sizes: one prose(text) function (money marks unwrapped, item tags stripped), called by size() and by size_edit_refusal on base and new text.
decisions.why: Fixes a defect (a wrong outcome: a search pass's claim correction was refused as a size trim and needed an escape) in T184, which implements the GM's 2026-11-23 'no edit to maintain entry size should ever be substantive'. An edit is 'to maintain entry size' only against the cap, and the cap is on prose; a correction under the cap by prose before, after and with its removed words restored is not maintaining size. Measuring the rule by the cap's own measure serves the purpose rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: is_size_edit keeps T184's rule unchanged (over before, or the removed words putting it back over: the add-then-trim clause), now on the prose measure.

decisions.summary: The refusal says 'bytes of prose'; make question-sizes's help line, which said 'question + notes', now says it counts the question's prose.

decisions.summary: Red-first test carrying P12's real block on a page whose item tags put the raw file over 20,000 bytes while its prose stays under; red on HEAD, green on the fix.

decisions.summary: The 20,000-byte cap is unchanged.
decisions.why: No change to the limit the GM's size rules address.

decisions.summary: Lands alone; T237 (performance work) is ordered after T240 by the coordinating session under a PERF_LATER_OK escape recorded at task-start.
decisions.why: FR-013/SC-006 provide a recorded escape for starting non-performance work while a performance task is open; this block records the escape the spec's own mechanism allows and does not alter the performance-first rule.

decisions.summary: record_task appends a block_reviews row for a BLOCKED section verdict, naming the section's blocks (the CLEAR path's keys) and in tasks the task plus any bundle member sharing the section; the blocks' own verdicts stay unwritten
decisions.why: Fixes the defect the task was filed for: a section's BLOCKED rounds left no row, so the root CLAUDE.md tripwire on a check's third round never fired (T432). Listing bundle members follows 451 T141 (one review of a bundle is one round of each of its tasks). Leaving the blocks' verdicts unwritten keeps a BLOCKED from posing as their CLEAR review.

decisions.summary: a round is a recorded verdict, not a dispatch: a NOT-REVIEWABLE return (records nothing) and a dispatch another guard refused do not count
decisions.why: The agent contract itself says a NOT-REVIEWABLE return does not consume a round, because nothing was reviewed, and a refused dispatch reviewed nothing either. The section cites the ask's `asked` text for T432's case. That text is not in this bundle (rulings.md carries only the ruling, why and what), so the quote is unconfirmed here. Nothing in the ruling contradicts it, and the rule stands on the contract without it. This keeps the existing row-based counter and does not narrow the tripwire.

decisions.summary: the same verdict recorded again on unchanged bytes (the same tasks.<id> entry) is the same round
decisions.why: Tied by its parenthetical to the identical tasks.<id> entry, this makes re-recording idempotent rather than letting a double write count as two rounds. A fresh reviewer's new verdict is not excluded by this text.

decisions.summary: the guard takes its subject from the section the dispatch names (feature and task, task_prompt's words) or, for a block review, the feature its prompt names and the tasks in its bundle directory's name, each counted with the first past its cap holding; a plan round's continue/accept is read from its trigger's feature's arbiter.jsonl
decisions.why: Answers round 1's NOT LEGITIMATE finding by option (c): a block review of task blocks now counts against those tasks, not against the active task under .specify/feature.json. Reading the ruling from the trigger's feature fixes a found defect: a hold under another active feature could never be lifted. Both serve the tripwire as written.

decisions.summary: only a dispatch naming neither a section nor a task-bearing block bundle (a hand-written prompt, or a block review of no task's blocks) falls back to the active task
decisions.why: Each case judged separately. (1) A hand-written prompt names no subject, so there is nothing to read one from, and falling back is the only reading available. (2) A block review of no task's blocks: the cap's unit is the task, in the section's own terms (plan_rounds counts the task's rows, the refusal reads 'round 3 of <T>'s', the trigger is plan:<slug>#<T>@3). Such a review holds no task whose third round is at stake, so round 1's failure, a task's third round going unheld, cannot pass through this path. It leaves a difference, not a shown defect.

decisions.summary: the refusal's first line is shortened to 'BLOCKED: round 3 of <T>'s plan review. Nothing was dispatched.' with the arbiter-bundle line after; the shared refusal's ARBITER_OK hint gains '<reason, two words or more>'
decisions.why: Message wording under message-check's BREVITY and FIDELITY findings. The hint fixes a found defect (a one-word reason was refused with no hint why) in the one function that writes it, and the search's method is stated. No requested behavior is removed: the rule is still stated on the next line.

decisions.summary: T227 (the record checks' counter kept per active feature) is left as a separate task
decisions.why: A separate, already-filed task about a different counter. This task's own counter no longer carries that flaw. No defect of this task's subject is carried forward.

decisions.summary: The split's enforcement lives in the context-cap guard as a new submodule context_cap_hooks/split.rs, reusing D8's builder test and D9's transcript read.
decisions.why: Where the enforcement lives is design; the request (2026-11-25, 'sounds good please do that ASAP') asks for the claims round split off code builders, and the feature's 2026-11-19 approval asks that enforcement be real. Placing it in the guard that already reads builders' transcripts narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The rule applies to code builders, not every builder: record and pop-up bundles, page-session cascades and claims-round dispatches keep their own claims work.
decisions.why: The request is about code builders ('most code builders ... hit the 300k context cap', the cause 'one builder doing the fix, ... and the claims round'). A cascade's or bundle's claims round is that builder's own correct work and was never asked to be split off; the block's measurement (the P15 cascade on the split's first day) shows an every-builder rule would refuse it.

decisions.summary: A code builder is recognized only by a line opening STOP POINT in its brief (the brief template sets it); an unmarked builder passes, so the guard is silent where the coordinating session omits the template.
decisions.why: This narrows enforcement: an unmarked code builder (the session dispatching without scripts/container/builder-brief.md) is unguarded, and the split there rests on the session remembering the template - the gap is real and is named in the block ('silent where the brief is omitted'). It is legitimate on purpose, not on consistency: the block's own evidence shows that no transcript-only test separates a code builder from other builders without refusing correct work - an every-builder rule refused the P15 cascade on the split's first day, and even the claims round's own dispatches are not worded uniformly (3 of the 85 opened 'Claims round: arch claim re-check' and 'Finish 449 T430's claims round', which an opener-keyed rule would refuse). A default-on test from prompt wording would therefore refuse correct work, which the project's guard rule ranks worse than none, so the only false-positive-free mark of a code builder is one its brief sets. The purpose - keep the claims round out of a code builder's context - is enforced on every builder dispatched as a code builder through the template, which is the coordinating session's standing order and the same brief that tells a builder where to stop at all; the 06:21Z-on measurement (12 briefed builders, 0 claims dispatches) is consistent with this but is not the ground.

decisions.summary: A builder whose prompt itself opens 'Run the claims round' is not a code builder even if it quotes a STOP POINT line.
decisions.why: The claims round's own dispatch is the half the request moves to the coordinating session; refusing it would refuse the requested split's own work. A claims round worded otherwise that quotes the brief would be refused and has SPLIT_OK, which is an escape, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Any transcript read that fails passes; the main session and defined agents are never read.
decisions.why: The accepted D8/D9 design of this same guard: it passes what it cannot tell and never reads the main session or a defined agent. No narrowing of the request beyond the accepted spec.

decisions.summary: A code builder's Agent call of claims-triage or impl-drift, or a Workflow naming either as an agentType (args, a unit's then step, a script literal), is refused, naming the agent, the brief's STOP POINT (make claims-triage and stop) and what to report.
decisions.why: This is the requested split, enforced; covering the Workflow form closes a hole (check-wave units replay without agent_id) rather than adding behavior beyond the request. The message names the compliant action per FR-012.

decisions.summary: Escape SPLIT_OK="<reason>" in the prompt, recorded split-ok; firings recorded builder-split.
decisions.why: The project's guard rule restated in FR-012 (a reason escape, recorded); 'by default' in the request admits a deliberate exception path.

decisions.summary: The cap's handoff refusal, for a code builder only, adds one line: hand off at the STOP POINT and do not run the claims round; a claims-round dispatch past its cap is not told that.
decisions.why: The task's own enforcement line ('the context-cap guard's handoff names the split'); scoping it to code builders follows the request's subject.

decisions.summary: The brief template states that the guard keys on its STOP POINT line.
decisions.why: Documents the mark the guard reads; no behavior beyond the request.

decisions.summary: workflow_hooks' replay of check-wave units without agent_id is left as it is; this rule reads the Workflow call itself instead.
decisions.why: Not a defect left: the wrong outcome for this rule (a builder's wave of claims checks passing) is fixed here, and the block states no other builder-keyed Agent rule exists today (its premise, not measured by this review; nothing in D8, D9 or FR-006 contradicts it - the cap refuses the builder's own Workflow call directly). Leaving a difference that causes no wrong outcome stays within (constitution XIV v2.36.0).

decisions.summary: Declared not performance work; the performance checklist is left as its template.
decisions.why: A guard that refuses a dispatch; the checklist is prompts, never a gate. No narrowing.

decisions.summary: The cause is placed in the reading, not the owing: the plan records three readings (a replay at 01549f3828~1, P15's check-session listing, the cascade's report, all 2026-11-25) that record-owed already owed modal-depiction:hamlet/marsh, and that the coordinator's `| tail -6` cut the count off the listing's first line. The fix makes report's last line repeat the count and list every pop-up an unanswered unit owes, so a tail still shows both.

The fix reaches the stated case (any tail that includes the last line shows the count and the owed pop-ups). Pure tooling; nothing on a map changes.

decisions.summary: The task line's 'make that pop-up owed, red-first on the pair' is met by a red-first test on the listing's last line (recorded red on HEAD, 125 passed / 1 failed; 126 passed on the fix), not a red on the pair, because the pair was owed on HEAD's code and on the fix.
decisions.why: The task line is the session's wording, not the GM's; the GM asks that cascades fire where called for, and a red on a pair that was never unowed cannot exist. The red-first test enforces the defect actually found.

decisions.summary: The over-flag measured on the same run (windbreak and both wells owed through 0031's moved drawing page; of 43 owed, the tool cleared 32, the agent 8, 3 sent on) is judged the intended filter and left unchanged.
decisions.why: The GM's concern is 'unnecessary edits as a result of something trivial changing'; the owing is cheap and the triage dropped the trivial ones before any edit, so no wrong outcome exists (constitution XIV: a defect is a wrong outcome). Leaving a non-defect is within what was asked and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: Found and left: a moved Drawing: page owes only modal-depiction, never modal-form, so a page's new labeled guess (here 0057's UNRESEARCHED block, marsh's Guesses bullet) never owes the Guesses-tab check. Left to the already-open 451 T226, which 'lands before T242', with 0057/hamlet-marsh given to it as a second fixture.

decisions.summary: 'Performance work? no: one line more in a listing.'

decisions.summary: A labeled item new on a drawing page owes modal-form of each About-form pop-up whose Drawing: names the page, triaged first, with the item shown to both agents.

decisions.summary: items::items reads a comment inside an item tag's token as part of it; items::faults names any item tag still unreadable, with the form to write.
decisions.why: A defect fix (a tool that answers wrongly: the owing, the backlog and the claims missed toe-shoulder-past-corner). Fixing it serves the cascade request and the 2026-11-25 UNRESEARCHED backlog; the faults line only fails when a tag is unreadable, which is enforcement of the same thing.

decisions.summary: Only GUESS, UNRESEARCHED, DEVIATION and CONVENTION items owe; ATTESTED-type items do not owe a form unit.
decisions.why: Does not narrow anything asked: a moved Drawing: page still owes modal-depiction for every other change (modals::owed_row, unchanged). The four labels are the ones whose disclosure is the form check's job.

decisions.summary: A CONVENTION item also owes a modal-form unit, though the form contract leaves CONVENTION to modal-depiction.
decisions.why: Widens rather than narrows owing, and the triage bounds it; whether a form unit with nothing to judge is worth its cost is design, not fidelity. The rationale cites T236's line, which is not in this bundle and is not the GM's words; nothing here rests on it.

decisions.summary: A tag added to words that stood on the page before (T192's tagging) owes nothing.
decisions.why: Is the GM's own approved rules, not a carve-out from them: 2026-11-23 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' and the T192 route ('a script tags each block that names its own label'). Adding a tag to words already there does not change a claim.

decisions.summary: A pop-up whose Guesses tab already references the item as {NNNN#id} is not owed; the bullet regenerates from the tag (T187).
decisions.why: Directly the GM's 2026-11-23 rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration' and his question 'Shouldn't attested versus guess be something that cascades mechanically rather than requiring a review'.

decisions.summary: A changed label on a drawing-page item owes the form check of a pop-up that does not reference the item.
decisions.why: Counted as an exception to 'labels ... propagate by regeneration' (GM 2026-11-23), so it was judged per case, starting from presumed illegitimate. (a) Where the pop-up references the item, the exemption above applies and regeneration carries it, which is the rule as written. (b) Where the pop-up does not reference the item, regeneration has nothing to act on, so the rule cannot apply there. The plan also records that the label word is held in the block's prose (items::faults), so a relabel is a claim change under the GM's 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. A relabel to GUESS or UNRESEARCHED also gives the pop-up a new duty under the 2026-11-25 rule the GM approved ('UNRESEARCHED a fifth label on the research pages as well as in the claims'). Where a relabel only exposes a gap that already stood (GUESS to UNRESEARCHED on an unreferenced item), the 2026-11-25 rule still applies, because it puts the new label in the claims. The exception does not empty the regeneration rule, which still covers every referenced item.

decisions.summary: Triage rule (D): a labeled figure of the pop-up's own thing that its Guesses tab does not hold is sent on; the plan names it the one exception to 'a gap filled is a completion, not a correction'.
decisions.why: Starting from presumed illegitimate, and testing both pairs. The GM's own words reach both, so this is not inference. P7: the pop-up says rows ran to 300 ft while the map draws none past 145 ft as a GUESS. A reader is misled, which is a factual finding of the kind the 2026-11-23 rules keep cascading ('only factual findings cascade'), not a style gap. P15: a new UNRESEARCHED toe-shoulder-past-corner that hamlet/marsh does not hold. Here the GM's approval of 2026-11-25 ('UNRESEARCHED a fifth label on the research pages as well as in the claims'; 'note it as being something that is unresearched') requires the label to reach the claims, so leaving it out breaks a rule he approved. The 2026-11-24 instruction ('we really are cascading in situations that do call for it') covers both cases. Purpose test: the gap-fill clause was dropped because completion edits fixed no real flaw. A drawn guess that the pop-up never discloses is the flaw the label rules exist to show, so applying the drop here would defeat their purpose. The scope is narrow: only new or relabeled items, and only of the pop-up's own kind ('An item about another kind on the same page is not (D)'). The cited dev/modals.md M8/M11/M13, the T226 line and the coordinator's brief are not in the bundle and are not the GM's words. The ruling does not rest on them.

decisions.summary: The unit is owed only where the pop-up's own text did not already owe its form check.
decisions.why: Avoids a double owing; narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: The occasion opens 'a page its ', so make modal-triage runs first.
decisions.why: Feature 375 FR-001, quoted in spec-cited.md: a page-moved unit is triaged first.

decisions.summary: The fingerprint is the form fingerprint plus the owed items; unchanged when none are owed.
decisions.why: An answer covers exactly what it was owed for, and no earlier answer is moved: serves 'not doing anything silly' (GM 2026-11-24).

decisions.summary: A form unit reads its Drawing: pages (pages_of); the filter may not clear a page carrying an owed item (Unit::held); the MANIFEST lists such items.
decisions.why: Mechanism that makes the triage see the item the owing names; without it the cascade the GM asked for is cleared by a filter that reads only what the pop-up states.

decisions.summary: A D: reply line marks the form unit alone; A:-C: lines mark the other checks.
decisions.why: Scopes the cascade to the check that owns the finding: the 2026-11-23 rule 're-reviews scoped to the change'.

decisions.id: L2 the clue recorded with the data
decisions.summary: 'Blocks: <feature> T<n> | T<n> | none' in a dispatch prompt, page brief or builder brief's STOP POINT block, written as 'blocks' on the Agent call's event lines and on the page session's Phase line; 'L7R_BLOCKS=' read from a command's text; the line added to builder-brief.md and the research-record brief rules.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l): 'to the extent that we can pass that kind of context clues to our tooling when the data is collected, whether through environment variables or I don't even know what else'. Reading the variable from the command text because a hook cannot see the shell environment is the mechanism, not a narrowing; the templates carrying the line are what make future data carry it.

decisions.id: L3 GUESS defaults where no clue is given
decisions.summary: Main session's own turns and waits block the task its lines carry; a builder's time blocks its own task, else its waiter's; a run or review agent blocks its waiter's task (a background run only from when it is waited on); a page session or research pass blocks nothing. Each labeled GUESS in book.rs's doc.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l): 'not something our tooling can inherently know ... it doesn't have to be 100% exact ... only 90% of the time are we correct ... basically fine'. Labeled defaults for the unclued case are the approximation (l) accepts; research defaulting to nothing is overridden by a Blocks: line, which (l)'s decide-between-implementations case is to carry.

decisions.id: L4a prefer task-blocking work over work blocking none
decisions.summary: Among several in flight, what blocks a task is preferred to what blocks none.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l): work done in parallel that blocks nothing 'is really not blocking anything'; a piece is never taken from a blocked task by non-blocking work.

decisions.id: L4b each task its own piece (round 5's L4b, fixed)
decisions.summary: Every task with blocking work in flight that second is booked its own piece, its own work's ends-last one (each_task); while a session or builder is in its own time - a turn or run, and a session's waits on the GM or idle hours too - its background work blocking ANOTHER task blocks that task beside it (beside); 'Waited on, blocking no task' only where no task-blocking work is in flight. Round 7 restatements: Blocking minutes reads 'each second once per task it blocks'; beside's reach through GM waits and idle hours is stated (the code did so already); the new test row names three Blocks: T4 passes of different ends (pinning the within-task ends-last pick) and two unclued passes waited on alone (the ends-last one apart, 8 s); the older blocking-by-dependency row states the page-session test's re-expectation (the review's 4 s to T1).
decisions.why: Within, as round 6 ruled, and the restatements keep it so. (a) 'each second once per task it blocks' now agrees with each_task instead of contradicting it. (b) beside through the session's GM waits and idle hours is (l) as written: research a task waits on 'would be blocking even if there was a different unrelated task happening' - a session waiting on the GM or idle is likewise unrelated to whether T4's next step waits on its research; it does not touch amendment (i), since the GM's own rows keep their time and only T4's booking, a working-time row, is added. Stated behavior the code already had, not a new decision. (d) the three-pass case pins that the ends-last pick stays within one task's work, and the two-unclued-passes case is L5's apart booking where no task-blocking work is in flight - both test rows of the ruled behavior, figures labeled measured 2026-11-25. (e) closes round 6's wording note. Wording only, not a finding: line 52's 'met after a shorter and before one' reads garbled (presumably 'before a longer one'), and it names 'an unclued pass' then 'the two unclued passes'.

decisions.id: L4c two paths to one task in one second each booked
decisions.summary: Where one task's work is waited on directly and again inside a builder in the same second, each path is booked: a GUESS, an overstatement where it happens.
decisions.why: Within, unchanged in substance from round 6: an approximation inside one task's own blocking, labeled GUESS, of the kind (l) accepts ('it doesn't have to be 100% exact ... only 90% of the time are we correct ... basically fine'); erring toward counting a task's blocking drops nothing (l) asks for. Round 7 only drops 'the data has not shown' for 'where it happens', a wording change.

decisions.id: L5 work blocking no task named apart
decisions.summary: Where only work blocking no task is in flight, the piece is booked to that work on the header's 'Waited on, blocking no task' line by category, never in the blocking columns.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): (l) says such work is not blocking; amendment (c) requires nothing silent, and a named line satisfies both.

decisions.summary: 'waiting: nothing in flight - a page session running, no monitor on it' blocks what the page session blocks: its brief's task, else nothing (apart).
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): The same dependency rule as L3 applied to an untracked wait; keeps the (j) class and books it by (l).

decisions.id: L7 window blocking as the sum over tasks; denominators
decisions.summary: The window's blocking is the sum over tasks, the landed tasks' sum beside it, the header saying it passes the clock; every blocking percentage is of that sum less the GM's rows (amendment (i)), never of the clock; the GM's rows show their share of the whole.
decisions.why: Carried from round 6's CLEAR (not re-judged; since then the section changed only by restatement): Checked against (i) by name: the GM's minutes stay out of every other percentage's denominator and his share is stated of the whole, as (i) asks ('those minutes should not be part of the denominator when calculating the other percentages'). Excluding work that blocks no task from a blocking denominator follows (l)'s definition of blocking; a denominator that is the sum over tasks keeps each table summing to 100 when that sum passes the clock, and the header names each column's denominator and that the sum passes the clock, so no percentage math is left to the GM. Consistent, and stays consistent once L4b is fixed.

decisions.summary: A `research` axis (open|deferred) in dev/switches.json beside claims and port, thrown by make research-deferred / research-open with a recorded reason, who and when; one reader l7r_shared::switches::research.
decisions.why: The GM (2026-11-25): defer the queued research 'until at least tomorrow', and asked what can stop procedures kicking it off. A reversible, recorded switch is the deferral itself; it has no automatic expiry, so reopening stays the GM's call, which fits 'at least tomorrow'.

decisions.summary: A missing file or entry reads open; a malformed entry reads open with MALFORMED in its why.
decisions.why: Open is the shipped rules (research binds), as clean is for claims; this follows the switches' existing form and governs only a broken file. It carves no research out of a deferral thrown correctly.

decisions.summary: switches::write serialized only claims and port; now writes every axis, pinned by a test.
decisions.why: Without it the next claims or port throw would silently erase the deferral and defeat the request; a wrong outcome fixed as found.

decisions.summary: While deferred, a research: physical task's boxes may be answered 'deferred: UNRESEARCHED' on the box line; the box stays [ ], BOXES=1 does not tick it; tick and land accept it only while deferred and refuse it, naming the switch, while open.
decisions.why: This is how a physical task lands without starting a research pass, i.e. the deferral the GM asked for; leaving the box unticked keeps the record honest that no pass ran, and refusing the answer while open restores the shipped rules. The bundle does not list the five boxes; if any of them is not a search (e.g. a review of the guess), letting it be answered too is wider than research, but it widens nothing the GM asked to keep and narrows nothing he asked for.

decisions.summary: research_boxes.rs::violations accepts an answered box whatever the switch's state (a task ticked while deferred stays green after reopening), and the tick does not check that make research-backlog lists the deferred decision; the answer's text and the refusal name the backlog instead.
decisions.why: Judged together because each leans on the other. T244 asks that procedures not start research while it is deferred; it asks for no new check that deferred decisions reach the backlog, and the UNRESEARCHED labeling of a guess is the 2026-11-25 backlog rule's existing mechanism, which this plan leaves as it was. Nothing in the bundle makes the task's decision appear on research-backlog, so the plan's goal line ('lands with its decision drawn UNRESEARCHED onto the backlog') states an intent, not an enforced outcome; but the deferred box itself stays '[ ] ... deferred: UNRESEARCHED' in tasks.md permanently, a findable record of every search not run, so reopening does not turn the deferral into a silent waiver. The plan's 'cheaper route' reason is not what makes this within; that the request does not ask for the check is. Not building an unasked check narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Root CLAUDE.md Research bullet, research-doctrine.md and the research-backlog help line restated: while deferred, a port stage's end lists what it touched (make research-backlog STAGE=) and does not search it.
decisions.why: The stage-end search is a procedure that would start queued backlog research, exactly what the GM deferred.

decisions.summary: While deferred, the approved search-first exception (a decision that other code builds on, or a guess likely visibly wrong) goes through RESEARCH_OK: the doctrine prose says so, and the guard refuses a research-pass dispatch for it without the escape.
decisions.why: Read against request.md: 'all of it' is 'the research that we currently have queued', deferred because none of it is blocking or likely to change the maps, so suspending the 2026-11-25 search-first exception for decisions that ARE foundational would exceed his words. The plan does not suspend it: the search still runs first, on the session's judgment, once a reason is given in RESEARCH_OK and recorded. What changes is that the search becomes a recorded, deliberate act rather than a procedure firing by itself, which is the GM's concern ('inadvertently kicking off'). The exception's purpose (do not build on a wrong foundation) is untouched, so this neither narrows the T244 request nor guts the earlier rule. The ruling depends on the escape staying a reason-only escape; a version that refused such a search outright would be NOT LEGITIMATE.

decisions.summary: PreToolUse guard: while deferred, refuses an Agent dispatch of research-pass (check-wave units included) and a Bash invocation of make page-session; RESEARCH_OK="<reason>" escape, logged; silent while open.
decisions.why: Real enforcement of 'not inadvertently kicking off research'; an escape with a stated, recorded reason means what passes is deliberate. Note on reach: request.md shows page sessions also used for non-search work (T192 label tagging, cascade repairs); the guard refuses those too while deferred, passing only via RESEARCH_OK. That is reach beyond research, but it removes nothing the GM asked for (the escape keeps that work reachable). If page sessions are routinely needed for non-research work while deferred, the escape will get used often and that is worth watching.

decisions.summary: No code for impl-drift NEEDS-RESEARCH verdicts: they already stay listed and refuse nothing while claims stand at report (feature 445).
decisions.why: Doing nothing where existing behavior already starts no research narrows nothing asked. The premise depends on claims staying at report, and the bundle shows no measurement of it; if claims is moved to clean while research is deferred, this path needs re-checking.
