decisions.summary: After 926e10e593, no dependency on T234; one landing; closing checks green or recorded red with a claim of impossibility ruled through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Sequencing and exits only; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The task's words read literally: a split ADDS the target page to the Drawing: line of each pop-up whose Drawing: names the source and whose Depiction states a moved block, rather than M14's 'the pointer counts as listed, the line is not edited'.
decisions.why: It is the task's own wording. It serves the GM's split rule (2026-11-23: 'nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs') and the approved rule 'a split is a move': without it, D5/LINKS would read the target as a missing link, and a check would be owed because of the split.

decisions.summary: split_links.rs follows each split pointer from a pop-up's listed Drawing: pages to an unnamed .drawing.html target and appends it to the line, a continued line included.
decisions.why: It is the mechanical addition the task names.

decisions.summary: The appended target carries the condition of the listed page that reaches it ([settlement_form=dispersed]), or none where an unconditional listed page reaches it.
decisions.why: Without this, the link would apply under conditions where the pop-up does not rest on the page, which is a wrong outcome under D5/LINKS ('every drawing page the modal rests on, and no other'). Carrying the condition is part of adding the page correctly and does not narrow the task.

decisions.summary: The fingerprint rule (Drawing: is part of depiction()) is left unchanged. The pop-up's existing answer is carried to the new fingerprint with answers::settle, because an applied LINKS fix states no fact (451 T188).
decisions.why: This implements 'owing nothing' as the task states it. Leaving the fingerprint rule unchanged avoids moving every pop-up's fingerprint, which would itself be a cascade.

decisions.summary: A pop-up that is not answered as it stands is not edited. It is named, and its owed check makes the link as a LINKS fix. The writer runs after modal-triage's own clears so that this set is as small as it can be.
decisions.why: The task says the split adds the target to EACH such pop-up, mechanically and owing nothing. For a pop-up that already owes a check, those two clauses conflict: the edit would turn the triage it is owed into a full check, so the split would cause more owing, against 'owing nothing' and against the GM's 'nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs'. Following the literal reading there would defeat the request's stated purpose. The carve-out does not empty the rule: the link is still made, by the check the pop-up already owes (now bound by the new D5/LINKS clause), and the pop-up is named rather than skipped silently. It covers exactly one class: pop-ups that already owe a check.

decisions.summary: 'States a moved block' is made mechanical: at least 3 shared word trigrams of at least 2 naming words between the Depiction and the target's blocks, with a pointer back excluded. Two knobs, measured 2026-11-25 over 52 (pop-up, target) pairs; they select exactly the two pairs that state the moved sections, as read by eye.
decisions.why: The task requires a test for 'states', and this is that test, with its thresholds measured against the whole tree and checked by eye. Nothing the request covers is left out: hamlet/well and settlement_form--nucleated are excluded with the reasons given (water, not the rice's reach; a single repeated phrase). If the rule misses a pop-up, the D5/LINKS clause still makes the link as a fact-free LINKS fix.

decisions.summary: dev/modals.md D5 gains the clause and is copied to each modal check by agent-sync. modal-depiction's LINKS contract gains it too. modal_split_pointer.rs pins both.
decisions.why: 'D5 says so' is the task's own words. The LINKS clause and the pin only enforce that same rule where the check reads it; their sole effect is that the requested behavior happens and keeps happening.

decisions.summary: The tool's run also adds 0349 to choice/settlement_form--dispersed, the same gap left by P11's split.
decisions.why: This is the same rule applied to every pop-up it covers ('each pop-up'), not a new behavior.

decisions.summary: The addition runs inside make modal-triage, and announces each addition before making it, rather than at the moment of the split.
decisions.why: It remains a mechanical addition that owes nothing; the timing is an implementation choice the task leaves open, and the outcome the request asks for is unchanged.

decisions.summary: The first pass's 'uncommitted changes' refusal becomes writer_refusal: it lists the clone's foreign git status lines (first six and a count), the landing's own escape records committed first (408).
decisions.why: A fix to the landing's refusal message, which makes the landing tooling report what blocks it. It keeps the refusal and narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: An open builder handoff names the clone only when its text names the clone root as a whole path, its task is not being landed, its task is open in some tasks.md, and it was written in the last 24 h (HANDOFF_FRESH_S, a CONVENTION knob). A handoff is named only beside changes, never as a refusal on its own.
decisions.why: These conditions decide which pointer the refusal prints. They never decide whether a dirty clone is refused, because the changes alone decide that. The 24 h bound is measured 2026-11-25: 26 of 538 handoffs would otherwise be wrongly named, all 2 to 5 days old. Nothing in request.md or the spec asks for a handoff to be named, so the bound narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The same check runs again at the push step's start, before the ticks; a refusal there ticks and pushes nothing.
decisions.why: Extends the refusal to the window between the claims wait and the ticks. It adds a refusal and carves nothing out.

decisions.summary: The tick's git add and git commit are read (commit_tick). A commit refused for index.lock is retried 3 times, 500 ms apart (CONVENTION knobs). On a failure the ticks are put back by unstaging and a checkout from HEAD, archives removed, fix rows set pending again, and the tick's escape record committed. Nothing is left staged.
decisions.why: Fixes the measured defect: an unread commit left the tick staged and sent the revert at the wrong commit. The undo is a checkout and never a history rewrite, which follows CLAUDE.md. The cause of the commit failure is left as a hypothesis, but the fix reads every failure, so the cause does not limit what it covers.

decisions.summary: After a failed push the revert always names the tick's own commit. Where another writer's edit blocks that revert, the tick commit stands, committed and never staged, with the existing message.
decisions.why: Corrects the revert's target. When the revert is blocked, the tick is left committed and stated, which is the outcome the plan's goal names ('committed or put back'). No defect is left: nothing is staged and the message says what happened.

decisions.summary: A clone dirty at make land's start still lands alone (451 T88/T101): alone_owed is asked before the first pass, and the new refusal is not placed before it.
decisions.why: Keeps earlier approved behavior that this task was not asked to change. It is not an exception to anything this task or the request asks for.

decisions.summary: The claims wait (CLAIMS_WAIT_S, 20 min) keeps waiting rather than refusing; check (2) covers the seconds after it.
decisions.why: Leaves an existing, pinned behavior as it is, with a stated reason (the claims round's records are committed beside the gate). Nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A builder's linked worktree with uncommitted work, and a handoff naming that worktree, bear on nothing; such a landing lands (pinned).
decisions.why: A worktree's files and index are not in the clone's git status, so the rule's own subject (another writer in the tree the landing ticks in) does not include them. This states the rule's reach and carves no case out of it.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T235's section as it stands
`which` kept in ASK only as the interrogative (`which (one |of these|...)?(do you|would you|should I|shall I)`)
decisions.why: The task is to stop statements firing as asks (the task line, and the GM's 2026-11-25 question about efficiencies in the check). On the corpus this alternative fired on 18 F (relative clauses) and on no T that another alternative missed, so no ask is lost; the interrogative form is kept.

decisions.summary: A STATED decision (`your call`, `needs your ...`, `ask you`, `waiting on you`, ...) is exempt when `nothing`/`none`/`nobody`/`neither`/`no one` stands earlier in its clause, or `not`/`never`/`-n't` within two words before it
decisions.why: Exempting a negated statement (`Nothing is waiting on you`, `didn't ask you anything`) serves the purpose: the GM asked for efficiencies and each false firing costs an escalation-check run. But the bound as written also exempts ordinary asks, which feature 429 FR-002 says are refused and which this section's own goal (item 1) and its Recall paragraph say still fire. The `-n't` within-two-words window exempts `This can't land without your call.` (can't [land without] your call). The clause-wide `nothing` exempts `Nothing else needs your decision except the budget.` and `Nothing is left but your call on the split.` The old rule refused all three. A tighter bound is possible: the negation governs the stated phrase itself, with no `without`/`until`/`unless`/`but`/`except` between them. So the case is not impossible, it is not implied by the GM's words, and the literal rule does not defeat the purpose. The corpus shows no real T lost, but round 1 judged the same way on a constructed form (`Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.`). Fix: tighten the bound, and pin these forms as asks in the new test.

decisions.summary: A STATED decision after `of` or `spent` (`442 minutes of waiting on you`, `the time spent waiting on you`) is a measure, not an ask
decisions.why: These are reports of time, and they fired on corpus F messages. `of`/`spent` immediately before the phrase does not reach a decision put to him in any ordinary form, so the bound holds to its purpose: stopping statements from costing a check run, as the GM asked on 2026-11-25.

decisions.summary: A sentence-opening `waiting ...` is a measure's name when it is the subject of is/was/were, or when it is a table cell with no `:`
decisions.why: Judged in two parts. (a) The subject of is/was/were (`**Waiting on you** is still reported`) is a measure's name. That part is LEGITIMATE on its own and is bounded. (b) 'A table cell with no `:`' reaches past measure names to status rows. `| T26 | Waiting on your budget answer |` and `| T22 | Waiting on your go-ahead |` are exempted. In sentence form this section itself treats them as asks or borderline-kept (`T26 is still waiting on your budget answer` stays firing; `Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.` fires). The pinned table ask has a colon, so the test does not reach this form. A tighter bound exists: the row's first cell, or a cell followed by a numeric cell, as in the measure example `| Waiting for you to answer | 0.5 | 1% |`. Fix: bound (b) so that a status cell still fires, and pin a no-colon status cell as an ask.

decisions.summary: OFFER gains `if you agree` and a sentence opening `Say if`
decisions.why: This adds refusals and removes none. It enforces feature 429 amendment 1's rule that an offer owes the filter, so it is enforcement of what was asked, not unrequested scope. Measured over 6,374 end-of-turn messages: 28 new firings, each an offer on reading. Amendment 1's text is not in the bundle (spec-cited.md carries only 429 FR-002 and 375 FR-044), so this ruling rests on the block's citation of it.

decisions.summary: The 8 borderline firings stay firing
decisions.why: No change to them. Each puts something to the GM (a pointer to a question, a deferred decision, a pause for his word, an invitation), so they keep firing under FR-002. The feature-432 kept-id exemption is unchanged. Feature 432's text is not in the bundle, so this rests on the block's citation of it.

decisions.summary: A narrower prompt to escalation-check (only the flagged sentences, not the draft) is not built
decisions.why: The GM's words ask whether more efficient ways exist and do not request this lever. The session's own reply named the narrower bundle as a separate change. Leaving it out drops nothing the GM asked for in T235.

decisions.summary: A strict '?'-or-offer detector is not adopted
decisions.why: The '?'-or-offer wording is the session's sketch, not the GM's words. The sketch's purpose is that only messages putting something to him reach the agent, and the plan's rule implements that purpose. The literal form would drop 24 of the 74 true asks on the corpus (measured 2026-11-25), contrary to feature 429 FR-002. Even read as a narrowing of the relayed brief, it would be LEGITIMATE, because the literal rule defeats the check's purpose.

decisions.summary: The 112-message labeled corpus stays in the session scratchpad, not the repository; the task's named statements are the committed cases
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for the detector's hit rate, a sample of hits and recall to be recorded, not for the raw messages to be committed. The section records the figures (with date and method) and quotes a sample of the forms, and the repository is public.

decisions.summary: `Performance work? no`
decisions.why: This label decides only scheduling under FR-013, and the task is being done now, so no ordering the GM asked for is lost. It arguably undersells the work: each false firing avoided saves an escalation-check run and a turn, which is the efficiency the GM's 2026-11-25 words ask about. That is not a narrowing of what is built.

decisions.summary: make disk-audit: every place the container writes, size, largest entries with owner and age, a GUESS budget each, the total against the disk, the unaccounted remainder, what the eviction would free now; read-only
decisions.why: The GM's second sentence asks for 'some kind of audit of disk space and what this container specifically is leaving sitting around'. Budgets per place are the coordinating session's build and are stated as GUESS knobs. The remainder is reported, not hidden; I measured independently (du -x over / on 2026-11-25): the container's visible tree is about 240 GB plus the ~/.claude bind mount, against 411 GB used on df, so the plan's 'about 177 GB outside the container's view' holds.

decisions.id: D2 the trigger on the host disk
decisions.summary: A prompt reads df; below L7R_DISK_FREE_PCT (GUESS 20) free, at most hourly, starts the eviction detached and says what it freed in one line; the share is read on the host's disk
decisions.why: The GM's third sentence: 'trigger something automatically if our disk space ever drops below a certain percentage of free space'. The disk he names is the host's ('my host has a 461G disk drive'), so reading the share there is the plain reading. The threshold is a GUESS knob.

decisions.id: D3 the budget evicts idle and gone trees' profiles
decisions.summary: Past the cache budget, whole profiles of trees that are gone or idle (HEAD log unmoved for 12 h, no live cwd) go first, least recently built first, only until back within budget
decisions.why: It relaxes T158's keeping of every live tree's build directory whole. Ruled on purpose: the GM's T245 words locate the problem in 'artifacts sitting around', and his 2026-11-22 request was to 'clean up after ourselves ... to not have 30 gigs of stuff suddenly get eaten without us realizing it'. Under the old rule the budget held nothing (190 GB against 100) and evicting only gone trees freed 27 MB, so the literal old rule defeats both requests. A profile unbuilt for 12 h in an idle tree is exactly an artifact sitting around, and the cost (a cold rebuild) is priced in the plan and tied to three knobs.

decisions.id: D4 active trees' idle profiles, the profile as unit
decisions.summary: An active tree's profiles idle past 12 h rank after idle trees' and may go; the unit is the profile, not the tree
decisions.why: Judged apart from D3 because the tree is in use. A profile not built for 12 h is sitting around whatever tree holds it; the plan measured a 25 GB cover-gate idle while its tree's tool profile was fresh, so a per-tree age keeps idle artifacts and defeats the GM's purpose. The working set stays protected: in_use, the running-build hold, the mirror exclusion, and the dry run touched none of diagram-backlog's debug, cover-gate or tool, nor a parallel builder's tree.

decisions.id: D5 the budget path without a low disk
decisions.summary: The eviction also runs from cargo::plan past the 100 GB budget when the disk is not below the share
decisions.why: The low-disk path is the GM's third sentence. The budget path answers his 2026-11-22 request ('not have 30 gigs ... eaten without us realizing it'), which is about growth, not about a full disk. The budget already existed under T158 and is what that request built; D5 makes it hold for artifacts sitting around rather than inventing a new rule. Waiting for the disk to be low would bring back the 2026-11-22 failure the request exists to prevent.

decisions.id: D6 a removed worktree's build directory with it
decisions.summary: T158's proven-dead rule loses its idle wait; the day's sweep removes clean scratch worktrees before planning; make land removes each cleaned tree's build directory; a hand removal is caught at the next sweep
decisions.why: A build directory whose tree is gone is an artifact left sitting around with no possible user; in_use still guards a running build. It is in the coordinating session's build and serves the GM's first sentence.

decisions.id: D7 never under a running build
decisions.summary: T158's global hold kept; each removal re-checks it (sweep::take)
decisions.why: Stricter than before; preserves the existing protection of builds in progress.

decisions.id: D8 the cache stays over budget where live working sets exceed it
decisions.summary: When the working sets alone pass the budget the cache is left over it and the audit says by how much; an active tree's working set is never evicted to hold the number
decisions.why: This narrows the coordinating session's build ('the cache budget made to hold'), not the GM's words. It is implied by his words: what he asked to deal with is what the container is 'leaving sitting around', and a working set built that morning in a tree in use is not. The build itself limits eviction to 'idle trees' targets' and 'never under a running build'. The overage is reported by the audit, so nothing is silent, and the budget is a GUESS knob.

decisions.id: D9 'found nothing it may take' said once
decisions.summary: When the disk is under the share but nothing is evictable, the notice is said once until an eviction frees something again
decisions.why: The trigger still runs hourly and says every eviction that frees something. Reporting the same empty result every hour is not asked for anywhere. The plan's own figures show the share is unreachable on the host disk (about 18.7% free after everything evictable goes), and that is stated as the knob's question. Whether the notice repeats is a design choice, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.id: D10 the audit register's disk entry noted, not built
decisions.summary: 449 T437 item 13 gets the disk entry noted here; no register is built in this task
decisions.why: Checked: 449 T437 is a discussion task, explicitly 'NOT a build task'. Its item 13, an audit register with falsifiers, is a possibility to put to the GM, not something he approved. Building it here would be unrequested. The GM's 'add to our performance tuning and checks' is carried by make disk-audit, the automatic low-disk check at each prompt and the budget's eviction, and the task is filed as performance work.

decisions.summary: L7R_DISK_FREE_PCT (20) and the per-place budgets are GUESS constants with their why beside them; L7R_CACHE_IDLE_HOURS and L7R_CACHE_BUDGET_GB reused
decisions.why: The build names 'a knob, GUESS 20% free'; the GM's 'a certain percentage' leaves the value open.

decisions.summary: The task line's premise (the hand write of 449 T418/T422's rows was needed because the landing disagreed with WRITE=) is corrected by replay: the landing wrote both rows and was refused on P7's passes; the listing, not the landing's check, disagreed. The fix is built on the corrected diagnosis.
decisions.why: Every symptom the task line names is still removed: the hand write against a refusing WRITE= (the listing no longer offers WRITE= for these rows), the 'N check pass(es) have no row' notice on unrelated pushes and commits (the listing and --brief leave an open task's review), and spec-only pushes carrying rows forward (the push's write leaves it). The correction changes the route, not the outcome; the replay is labeled with its date and method.

decisions.summary: A MODE 4 plan review whose task has an open line belongs to its task's landing (make land's write now passes --landing <feature> --tasks <its tasks>); the push's write with no landing, the push's and landing's checks, the listing and the commit notice all leave it and name it in the existing left note.
decisions.why: The task line's own goal ('one of the two writes them') and the constraints the block names (371/385 FR-019: every pass owes its row; 451 T105: no row written twice). Case walk: open and landed - the landing writes it; no open line - the next push writes it; open and not yet landed - left until its landing, which the push's and landing's checks already did (451 T147), so no row loses its writer. FR-019's refusal still names WRITE= for rows that are actually owed by hand; these are not.

decisions.summary: A recorded plan review whose task has no open line (ticked, withdrawn, absent, or a block review naming no task) is written by the next push, whichever it is, and the listing names it 'N recorded plan review row(s) the next push writes', never as WRITE='s.
decisions.why: Removes a tool answering wrongly (the notice told the session to run a command that refuses these rows) while keeping 385 T72's push-route write for every row that no landing owns.

decisions.summary: left.rs's open test becomes an open '- [ ] T<n>' line in tasks.md instead of 'ticked in neither file', so a withdrawn or renumbered task is no longer open for ever.
decisions.why: Needed for the ownership rule not to leave a row unwritten for ever once the push's write also leaves open tasks' reviews; it widens who writes, narrows nothing. Pinned by the first test's T7 (no line) written by the push.

decisions.summary: make ledger-owed WRITE='s refusal of recorded plan reviews (451 T105) stays; its message names both owners (the task's landing, or the next push).
decisions.why: T105's constraint (a hand write must not write a row a landing writes again) is kept; the defect was the listing offering WRITE=, which the plan fixes; the refusal's message changes to name the real owner.

decisions.summary: whose.rs (451 T157, other checks' passes of a STARTED task) keeps its own ticked test.
decisions.why: A different class of pass whose rows the started task's session writes itself; nothing in this task changes who writes them, so the 'open for ever' consequence that motivates the left.rs change (a row nobody writes) is not created there. Not a defect left by this task.

decisions.summary: The fix's reach, 'every reader and writer of the rows', rests on the census of four readers (push check, landing check, push write, WRITE=, listing/--brief notice), measured 2026-11-25 by reading the code and replaying the real pass log and ledger.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing: the plan routes every named reader through left.rs's one split, the shared waist, so a caller through it inherits the fix. Limitation noted: the census's method is stated as 'the code', with no search command, so its reach could not be checked from the bundle (the reviewer read nothing in the repository, as the manifest directs).

decisions.summary: Outside::said walks the reply's lines; an OUTSIDE THE CHANGE or NOTED, NOT FILED heading (with or without #, bold or colon) opens a section, ended by any other # heading, a --- rule, or prose after a blank line.
decisions.why: Widens the reader to the two forms P7's cascade actually used, so the notes the task line says were dropped are read; serves the GM's 2026-11-24 instruction to watch what cascades do, and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: In an OUTSIDE section a row naming its effect is filed as before; a row naming none, any other bullet, and the section's first-paragraph prose are listed.
decisions.why: Keeps T219's rule (filed only with its effect) and the convergence talk's 'only factual findings cascade'; adds listing, files nothing more.

decisions.id: T229-D3 an empty-section line (new since the first CLEAR)
decisions.summary: A line saying the section is empty (None., none (every block ... listed)), never 'None of the pages ...', is no note and still ends its paragraph.
decisions.why: A line saying there is no note is not a note; echoing it would be a false listing. 'None of the pages ...' is kept as a note, so a real note is not swallowed by the form. Its frequency figure (13 of 23) carries a dated method label. Nothing the request or the task asks for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: In a NOTED, NOT FILED section every line is listed and none filed, whatever it names.
decisions.why: The check chose not to file; filing it would add the cascade the GM's convergence talk asked to stop. Every line is still echoed.

decisions.id: T229-D5 the echo line and its unit
decisions.summary: Each listed note prints '<cmd>: listed, not filed - <file> | <block> | <note>', a note naming no file and block taking the reply's units (claim keys / answered units).
decisions.why: Is the echo the task asks for, with a unit so the session can place it.

decisions.summary: Kept in specs/<feature>/noted.jsonl (one row a note, deduplicated on check, file, block), named by the closing echo line and by make found-list; not found.jsonl; the task line's 'the round's report keeps them' read as this record, since no command keeps a round's report.
decisions.why: Keeps the notes where a later session meets them, which is what the task line's keeping is for; keeping them out of found.jsonl is T219's rule (a listed note is not open work), not a carve-out. The reading is stated with the measured reason (claims-index and answer stores hold no notes).

decisions.summary: noted.jsonl is added to preflight.rs's feature records beside found.jsonl.
decisions.why: Treats the new record as a record the round writes; mechanical consequence of D6.

decisions.summary: The gitignored .git and the /tmp bundle directory priced and not taken.
decisions.why: Both would lose the note for a later session; the taken route keeps more, narrows nothing.

decisions.id: T229-D9 done, measured (new since the first CLEAR)
decisions.summary: Item 9 records crate-checks green on owed, claims, record, measure and the new test red with HEAD's reader, green with the new one.
decisions.why: A record of the exits item 6 set, not a new decision; nothing deferred (found and left: none).

decisions.id: T227-1 no wipe on a feature change; a unit's home feature
decisions.summary: handle_locked no longer replaces the check state on a feature switch; every key stays keyed by unit or subject; a unit's count keeps a home (round_home, the feature its first round was counted in, or the state's old feature for a unit counted before the change); its triggers are filed, and its continue/accept read, under that home; an owed record round is held and batched by every feature.
decisions.why: This repairs the tripwire the root CLAUDE.md and 375 FR-010/FR-011 already require: the same check on the same thing reaching its cap dispatches the arbiter, one binding ruling per unit per trigger. Before this fix a feature switch reset the count, so the cap never fired. Choosing a home over reading every feature's log is a design choice, and the reason the plan gives (an old continue must not lift a new cap, and a new trigger must not read as already ruled) protects FR-011's one-ruling-per-trigger. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.id: T227-2 first look only for other checks' EDIT text
decisions.summary: A round is uncounted as a first look only when every unread sentence carries another check's EDIT words on that subject and none carries its own, matched sentence by sentence (containment either way). Hand fixes the session made between rounds count as the fix loop.
decisions.why: This makes the code do what the 374 wave 120 / 0190 rule says it does ('text OTHER checks' edits added'). The code tested 'anything not its own', and a span EDIT could never match a whole sentence, so the measured barracks rounds 2 and 3 went uncounted. The fix restores a ruled rule and widens nothing past it.

decisions.id: T227-3 the arbiter bundle's count read under any feature
decisions.summary: arbiter/bundle.rs counted no longer returns 0 when the state's feature differs from the active one; its counter section and rounds line drop 'in this feature'.
decisions.why: A defect fix that follows from T227-1: the bundle the arbiter rules from (375 FR-011) must show the rounds actually counted. Before this, misnumbered named @1 for a unit on round 3.

decisions.summary: The cap refusal reads 'round N of <check> on <subject> passes its cap of C - ...', with 'in this feature' cut.
decisions.why: The message is reworded to match the new behavior and still names make arbiter-bundle, the compliant command. A wording change, not a change of scope.

decisions.summary: The cap constant is unchanged.
decisions.why: 375 FR-010 caps record checks at two rounds, the same as review checks.

decisions.id: T227-6 found and left: the batch rule restarts the count on any origin/main move (filed T248, lands before T22)
decisions.summary: new_cause restarts a unit's count whenever origin/main moves. With several sessions landing, a third round in one batch is rare, so the 0097 record-format case that prompted this task would still not have been held. Deferred to T248 with a reason, its id and its order.
decisions.why: This narrows the task's motivating case: T227 alone would not have caught P7's 0097 cascade. It is still a legitimate deferral. It is a separate defect in a separately ruled rule (c5db336fd3, 2026-10-12, 'count afresh only in a later batch'). Changing that rule is not this task's fix, and it needs its own measured definition of when the subject has moved. Folding it in here would silently overrule a ruled rule. The deferral meets 451 FR-009's form: why it is not fixed here, the filed task id, and its order ('lands before T22'). Nothing in the GM's request asks for it to be fixed in this task rather than in its own. The defect is filed and sequenced, not dropped.

decisions.id: T227-7 found and left: the record bundle's 'Earlier rounds' still lists only this feature's rounds (not filed)
decisions.summary: bundle/earlier.rs (feature 393) shows a reviewer only the active feature's earlier rounds, with rulings read from the active feature. Left as it is and not filed, because it has no effect on the cap and matches 393's contract wording.
decisions.why: Under the defect rule (constitution XIV, the GM 2026-11-19) this is not a wrong outcome for what T227 fixes. The cap, the trigger and the arbiter's bundle (T227-1 and T227-3) now all follow the unit across features. This section is what a record reviewer is shown, and it does what feature 393 specified. Leaving behavior that matches its own contract is not a narrowing. If someone later shows a reviewer reading wrongly because of it, that would be a defect to file then.

decisions.summary: Performance work? no.
decisions.why: The task holds a review round. Its only added cost is one extra arbiter.jsonl read on a capped repeat. Scheduling under 451 FR-013 is unaffected.

decisions.summary: build() runs cargo under env -u of every variable cargo llvm-cov show-env sets, every rustflags/rustdocflags channel, both wrapper channels (RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER, RUSTC_WRAPPER) and CARGO_LLVM_COV_BUILD_DIR, so the tool's flags come only from .cargo/config.toml
decisions.why: The task line asks for the rebuild with the instrumentation flags cleared; the plan measured (toy workspace, 2026-11-25) that the builder's env -u RUSTFLAGS workaround misses the RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER channel, and clears every channel that can carry the flag. This is the requested fix, no wider.

decisions.summary: After a successful build, a binary holding __llvm_prf_cnts is removed with its build.json, the launcher exits 1 naming why and where to look, and L7R_GATE_PRINT_FRESH names no binary
decisions.why: The task line: an instrumented binary is never left as the tool; feature 449 T61: the launcher fails closed. The false-positive check (0 of 19 plain tool binaries hold the section) shows no correct build is refused.

decisions.summary: The instrumentation scan runs only at a build (0.038 s over the 33 MB binary), never on a fresh call
decisions.why: T205: no extra work on a fresh call. Where the check runs is a cost choice that does not narrow what is enforced, since every new binary passes through a build.

decisions.summary: A binary instrumented before this fix is not hunted down; the <bin>.plain freshness stamp was priced and not built, because the scan finds no such binary in any clone
decisions.why: Nothing is left unfixed here: the scan of every clone's tool target (2026-11-25) found 0 instrumented binaries, so there is no wrong outcome. A guard against a state measured to exist nowhere is not owed (constitution XIV, what a defect is), and every binary built from now on passes through the new refusal. The plan states this openly with its evidence rather than hiding it.

decisions.summary: scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh, which builds the same way into the same target, is left unchanged
decisions.why: The task is the gate launcher's tool build. The plan measured that no Rust test runs l7r-guard.sh (grep -rn l7r-guard.sh rust/, 2026-11-25), so it is never started inside a cover environment and shows no defect, and its build writes l7r-guard, not the gate's programs. Caveat for the builder, not a ruling: that search finds the script by name in rust/ only; a Rust test reaching it through another script would be missed.

decisions.summary: Red-first tests in tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.1.sh: cargo is handed none of the coverage environment, a later call drops no profile, and the instrumented-build refusal (refused, removed, says why, print-fresh names nothing)
decisions.why: Enforcement of what the task line asks (red-first on a cover-run environment); each test fails only when the requested behavior is absent.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T232's section as it stands
No change to make record-owed: an answered unit on an unchanged fingerprint is not re-owed; the incident's re-run was forced by the arbiter's ruling ask:mixed-build-53-record-answers, not owed.
decisions.why: Leaves existing correct behavior as it is; the ruling quoted in rulings.md itself ordered the 4 guest-quarters answers re-run.

decisions.summary: No new contract line as the whole fix, because the variance came from a contract line an agent did not follow.
decisions.why: Choosing a tool-enforced mechanism over an instruction matches the GM's 2026-11-19 'make sure all of the enforcement is real enforcement and not just instructions'.

decisions.summary: A re-run's new WORDING finding on text an earlier answer stood on is held and listed, not applied; a re-run's FACTUAL finding applies and cascades as a first round's does (checks::reply::factual).
decisions.why: Carries the GM's 2026-11-23 rules verbatim in request.md: 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies ... when we are cascading, we are only interested in factual inaccuracies', approved as 'only factual findings cascade' and 'settled choices stay settled'. Letting factual findings through keeps the alcove-gap class of correction landing. A held wording finding is a difference, not a defect (XIV v2.36), and it is kept, not dropped.

decisions.summary: make record-checked marks an answer at a fingerprint already answered (rerun: fingerprint and earlier result), says so one line per unit, records the answer and re-stamps the build; the mark clears with the next answer or settle at another fingerprint.
decisions.why: The mechanism that makes D3 enforceable; recording the forced answer is what the arbiter ruling asked for.

decisions.id: D5 every-check rule for a mixed reply
decisions.summary: apply-edits holds a wording EDIT only when the unit carries rerun at its current fingerprint for EVERY check of the reply; a reply mixing a re-run and a first round holds nothing.
decisions.why: Errs to the prior behavior (apply) rather than wrongly holding a first round's edits. Observed 2026-11-25 (WORDING_CHECKS / WORDING_CATEGORIES against reply_checks) that every pop-up reply with wording EDITs names one check today, so no case reaches the gap; no defect is left. Should a multi-check wording reply appear, re-run wording edits in it would apply - worth revisiting then.

decisions.id: D6 held EDITs kept in noted.jsonl
decisions.summary: Each held EDIT becomes a row of the feature's noted.jsonl via T229's keep_noted_rows, counted by make found-list, reaching the next session.
decisions.why: 451 T219/T229: a note outside the change is listed and kept, never filed or applied; nothing the check found is lost.

decisions.id: D7 RERUN_OK escape and dry run
decisions.summary: RERUN_OK="<reason, two words or more>" applies held edits, logged to dev/bypass-log/; a dry run holds nothing.
decisions.why: The project's guard rule (FR-012's form: a recorded escape of two words or more).

decisions.summary: The 30-pair/25-difference proxy is rejected as measuring fix rounds; the decision rests on the two true same-fingerprint pairs and a six-unit re-run sample, stated as unable to bound a rate.
decisions.why: Measurement method; the limit of six units is stated rather than hidden.

decisions.summary: The 5-then-2 triage difference is not shown to be variance on one bundle (no triage reply kept; the claims crate held T223's uncommitted fix between the dispatches); the hold does not cover triage.
decisions.why: No wrong outcome is shown; triage sends claims on rather than applying EDITs, so the hold's purpose does not reach it.

decisions.id: D10 round-5 snapshot restored (found and fixed)
decisions.summary: The measurement's historical bundle overwrote sheet/guest-quarters' round-5 snapshot, producing a false change section; set back to the text that round judged.
decisions.why: A defect found and fixed in the task (fix defects where you find them).

decisions.id: D11 research-page record re-runs not held (found and left, T249)
decisions.summary: The hold covers pop-up files only; a record check re-run on a research page answered before at its text still applies its EDITs and re-owes. Filed as T249, lands before T246.
decisions.why: The task's goal ('a check run again on text nothing changed leaves that text's wording as it was') is generic and the build reaches pop-ups only, so it narrows. Legitimate because it is scheduled, not dropped: FR-009's form is met (why: a page's units are its notes and questions, a different mapping; filed id; order 'lands before T246'), no record-check re-run has been measured to occur, and the observed incident's class (pop-up re-runs) is fully covered. The GM's 'settled choices stay settled' is still owed in T249.

decisions.id: D12 no line saying what a round covers (found and left, T249)
decisions.summary: Where a subject's last round predates the kept snapshots (451 T189), a later round gets no change section and no line saying what it covers - the cause of the 2026-11-24 morning round missing the alcove gap. Not fixed here (bundle::earlier, outside this task's hold); filed as T249, lands before T246.
decisions.why: This is a defect (a check round passing work with a factual gap), so leaving it narrows. Legitimate as a scheduled deferral meeting FR-009 (reason, filed id, order before T246), not an abandonment; the factual finding itself still lands under D3, and the arbiter-forced whole-text re-run caught the gap. Note: D11 and D12 are two unlike defects both 'Filed as T249'; T249's line must carry both, or one needs its own id.

decisions.summary: make land's last step takes a landed number's DIRECTORIES t<N>... in the git directory and l7r-handoffs/T<N>-...; never a file (handoff note, land log); a number another feature started within the day is left by tmp::landed's rule
decisions.why: Answers the GM's 'the old task scratch folder is over 1/3 of a gigabyte? That doesn't seem right to me': a landed task's scratch directories (the handoff folder held 207 MB) go at landing. The files left are small (1.1 MB measured), read by land/writers.rs and the context-cap guard, and audited under a budget; the same-number rule keeps another feature's live task's scratch, which taking would be a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: the .git/t<N> and l7r-handoffs/T<N>- directories are taken only for a LANDED number; a set-down or never-landed number's scratch has no age rule and stays, sized under the audit's budgets (1 GB, 0.5 GB)
decisions.why: Narrower than the goal's 'or by the sweep's age'. Legitimate by purpose: the GM's complaint is about OLD task scratch, and an unlanded task's scratch is the handoff material a set-down task resumes from, so taking it by age would lose live work, which is a wrong outcome. The residue cannot grow unseen, because each place has its own audit line and budget, flagged OVER (measured 2026-11-25: 0.0 of 1.0 GB and 0.2 of 0.5 GB).

decisions.summary: a review snapshot without tree.json is taken once idle SCRATCH_SWEEP_SNAPSHOT_DAYS (GUESS, a week)
decisions.why: The brief's 'first measure whether any review reads a snapshot older than its current unit's, and keep what one does' was measured first (one snapshot per unit; 245 reads, none past 72 h after its take); a week is many times the oldest read, so nothing read is taken.

decisions.summary: a review snapshot WITH tree.json is kept whatever its age, until its unit is snapshotted again (about 0.9 GB held); taking one whose copy matches the live pool priced and not built
decisions.why: It narrows the plan's own goal that every leftover goes by age. Legitimate on the wrong outcome alone: tree::of_unit keys the unit's verdict carry, checkpoint and arbiter round count to that copy, so taking it would make them read the live pool, which breaks the reviews and is not merely awkward. The GM's purpose (nothing piling up unseen) survives: the snapshots keep a place and a 1.5 GB budget in make disk-audit and are flagged OVER past it.

decisions.summary: every .gencache store but rust taken once idle SCRATCH_SWEEP_DAYS in each tree; rust never taken
decisions.why: A leftover the container keeps (6.1 GB dead Python roll store, measured) cleaned by age as T245/T246 ask; the live rust store has its own lock and readers, and taking it would break a live read.

decisions.summary: (1) finished sessions' scratchpad entries judged one by one by idle SCRATCH_SWEEP_DAYS (GUESS 3 days); prompting and registered-running sessions kept; task outputs keep their own rule; the low-disk trigger runs the age shares before the cache's share, a build running or not
decisions.why: The host's point (1): an age sweep, GUESS 3 days, at session start (already, 451 T158) and at the low-disk trigger, the running session's scratchpad kept. The per-entry rule reaches the 12.8 GB the whole-session rule kept by its transcript.

decisions.id: T249(a) the hold reaches a research page
decisions.summary: apply-edits' re-run hold maps an EDIT's file to its unit's subject with unit_of: a pop-up's unit as before, or the question number for any research/questions/NNNN-* file, the subject of record-format:NNNN and intro-check:NNNN; T232's rule otherwise unchanged (wording EDIT held and listed in noted.jsonl where every check carries rerun at the current fingerprint, RERUN_OK applies it, logged).

That is the GM's 2026-11-23 rules as approved ('only factual findings cascade', 'settled choices stay settled', 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies'), carried to the record checks' own units. Enforces what was asked; adds no new behavior beyond T232's hold.

decisions.id: T249(a) factual checks' EDITs apply and cascade
decisions.summary: quote-check and translation-check EDITs are factual (in neither WORDING_CHECKS nor WORDING_CATEGORIES), so they apply and cascade as a first round's; their per-note units are never looked up; pinned by a test green before and after.

decisions.id: T249(a) a source write-up's and a GLOSSARY term file's EDIT not held
decisions.summary: A write-up under research/sources/ names no question, and a GLOSSARY block writes a term file, never the question, so neither EDIT is held.
decisions.why: The hold's condition is 'unchanged text', read as a re-run at the current fingerprint of the check's subject; record-format's and intro-check's subject is the question (units::fingerprint reads the question's files), so neither file is part of what the earlier answer settled or what the fingerprint proves unchanged. The defect found is on the question unit; no wrong outcome on write-ups or term files is named or measured, and FIX AS WE GO reaches defects, not hypothetical cases. Adjudicated separately: write-up EDITs come through the factual checks (applied by the decision above); a term file is outside the unit entirely.

decisions.id: T249(a) the re-run mark is not rebuilt
decisions.summary: No change to how rerun is written for record checks: answer_unit serves every check, and a page session records its answer before applying EDITs (settle requires it); measured 2026-11-25 that record-format's 82 and intro-check's 7 records are per question and none yet carries rerun.

decisions.id: T249(b) a later round with no kept snapshot says its scope

decisions.why: Fixes the wrong outcome of 2026-11-24: a later round with no change section judged one bullet where the whole unit was owed, and missed the alcove gap for a round. The GM's 'Re-reviews scoped to the change' presupposes a change to scope to; where none is kept, feature 393's Earlier rounds rule (a round with no change section judges as a first round, GM 2026-10-18) applies, and the line makes it happen. The fix sits at headed_in, the function the bundle writers pass through, rather than at each writer.

decisions.summary: A first round, a subject with rulings only, and a later round whose last bundle was kept get no line; a rebuild before dispatch keeps it.
decisions.why: These are the cases the defect does not reach: a first round already judges the whole unit, and a kept snapshot gives a change section. Nothing the GM asked for is excluded.

decisions.id: D1 the restart kept for another session's change
decisions.summary: A later origin/main batch restarts a unit's count when moved_upstream finds a non-push (fetch or pull) reflog step whose diff names a file of the subject. A batch whose moves leave the subject alone no longer restarts it.
decisions.why: Baseline: the GM's request, 451's spec, 375 FR-010 (the cap dispatches the arbiter) and FR-011 (the arbiter's ruling binds where the GM was asked). Under that baseline, the binding 374 ruling (a fresh count for a later page change no counted round saw) is part of what was asked. Another session's change to the subject is that case, and it is kept. Batches that never touched the subject were never that case. Measured 2026-11-25: nine of 0097's ten moves were such batches. Dropping their restart restores FR-010's cap where it had stopped firing, a defect fixed under fix-as-we-go.

decisions.id: D2a a page the unit only reads
decisions.summary: A change to a page the unit reads but which is not one of its own files (the 374 ruling's own 0077 trigger) no longer restarts the count. The third round is held for one arbiter ruling.
decisions.why: This narrows the 374 ruling's automatic fresh count, so it is judged as an exception and presumed wrong. It is legitimate on the GM's own rule and on purpose. The root CLAUDE.md tripwire (labeled G in the block) owes the arbiter a ruling at a check's third round on one subject, so the fresh count was the exception and this returns that case to the rule. The ruling's purpose survives: such a cause still gets its look. The arbiter rules on it under FR-011 and can rule continue, which is exactly how the 374 ruling itself was reached (the cap tripped at round 3 and the arbiter ruled continue). FR-010 says the tripwire 'does not stop the feature'. The GM's 2026-11-24 words, 'that we really are cascading in situations that do call for it', still hold: the cascade owed by a read page's change still runs, through modal-triage and one ruling, and is neither dropped nor settled silently. Restarting on every read page's move would bring back what the GM's 2026-11-23 cascade talk was about, every pop-up citing an edited page re-owed without limit. This is the ruling's reach narrowed to its own mechanism, not a carve-out against it. Not counted as grounds: 'the task's words' and cost.

decisions.id: D2b the subject's own files changed by other work in this clone
decisions.summary: Every push from this clone counts as the round's own edits. So a later edit to the subject's own files by other work of this session (another task, a page session), landed by push, no longer restarts the count and goes to the arbiter.
decisions.why: This is a different case from D2a and is ruled on its own. It is a change to the subject itself that no counted round saw, so it falls inside the 374 ruling's words, and the mechanism reaches further than goal line 1 says ('the round's own edits'). It is legitimate on the same two grounds. First, the GM's tripwire is a third round on one subject, and that holds whichever of this session's edits re-owed it. Second, a session's own later edits re-owing its own checks is the very loop the cap exists to catch (the GM's 2026-11-23 cascade talk), while another session's change, which D1 keeps, is not this session's loop. The case still reaches the arbiter, who can rule continue. With 147 of the clone's last 150 reflog entries pushes (measured 2026-11-25, as the block states), D1's restart still reaches every fetched landing from another session, and those arrive in large fetches (one of 36 commits), so the kept restart is not hollowed out.

decisions.id: D3 fallback where authorship cannot be read
decisions.summary: If the reflog does not reach the stored batch (expired or no tracking log), any change to the subject between the batches restarts the count. An unrecognized reflog message counts as another session's.
decisions.why: In this branch the round's own edits can reset the count, which goes past the 374 ruling (a page change no counted round saw) and against FR-010's cap, so it is ruled as an exception. It is legitimate because the deciding fact, who made the change, cannot physically be read here. Either default breaks one owed rule some of the time: holding puts another session's real new cause into a capped count against the binding ruling, and restarting lets own edits reset it. It still requires an actual change to the subject, and it needs two rounds on one unit further apart than the reflog's expiry, so it does not gut the cap.

decisions.id: D4 fallback where git cannot read the stored batch or its diff
decisions.summary: A stored batch git cannot read, or a diff git refuses, moves nothing. The cap holds and the arbiter rules.
decisions.why: Fails toward FR-010's cap and FR-011's ruling.

decisions.why: Its only effect is to keep the requested determinism from regressing in this suite; delete the requested fix and it has nothing left to check. It does not reach other suites, commands or agents.
