decisions.summary: The same pipe-into-grep -q form in the other 17 pipefail suites of tests/hooks/ (98 sites, observed 2026-11-25 with the stated grep) is not fixed here; filed as T253, landing before T139 (whose suite test-no-poll-hooks.sh is one of the 17).
decisions.why: T252's task is the one suite; the other suites are not dropped but filed with a reason, a task id and an order, the shape FR-009 sets for a found-and-left defect, and ordered before the task whose suite would otherwise carry the flake. The census states its search space (the grep pattern over the suites that set pipefail), and restricting it to pipefail suites and grep -q matches the mechanism (without pipefail, or without an early-exiting grep, the pipeline's status cannot be the writer's SIGPIPE). Aside, not a ruling: the space is tests/hooks/ only; T253 may wish to state whether pipefail scripts outside tests/hooks/ (other test directories, scripts/gates/) use the same form, and early-exit readers other than grep -q (grep -m, head).

decisions.summary: Scope is every tracked shell file under tests/ and scripts/ (149), pipefail or not.
decisions.why: Fixes a known defect (a check whose verdict depends on scheduling, a wrong outcome under constitution XIV) in every place the task names. Taking in files without pipefail widens the fix and does not narrow it: sourced files inherit the caller's pipefail. FR-009's how-found line is there (git ls-files, 2026-11-25).

decisions.summary: The 31 '| head' pipes (and zero sed-q / awk-exit pipes) are left unconverted.
decisions.why: Censused with a stated method: none has its status read by &&, ||, if or set -e. So no verdict moves and no wrong outcome is left. Under XIV a non-defect left as it is stays within and needs no ruling. 'Found and left? none' agrees with FR-009 because nothing deferred is a defect.

decisions.summary: The pipe-race check refuses only a pipe into an early-exit grep, not head / sed q / awk exit readers.
decisions.why: The block states the ask as: recount every early-exit form (done, with a method), fix every instance (every defect instance is grep), and move T252's self-check, which is a grep check, to make hooks-test. Its reach matches that self-check, and the same fix spreads it over all 149 files. Nothing the GM or the spec asked for requires refusing reader forms that hold no defect.

decisions.summary: Fix by form: seen V for printed variables, o=$(cmd) && seen o for commands, here-string inline in scripts/; the writer's status is kept by && on 14 lines and analyzed where it is dropped.
decisions.why: This is a design choice of the fix. Each place the writer's status is dropped is analyzed site by site with a method, and no verdict becomes wrong. The one change (grep -rl now counts the matches it printed) is the right answer, not a regression, under XIII and XIV.

decisions.summary: Four suites (engine-freeze, land-tooling, stall-watchdog, workflow) and all of scripts/ grep a here-string inline rather than through the shared seen helper.
decisions.why: Every instance of the defect is still fixed, so this is design, not fidelity. 'One shared helper' is the task line's wording, not the GM's request or the spec. The Approach paragraph says the suites use seen while item 9 says four do not; that is a wording inconsistency the builder should reconcile, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate check pipe-race in make hooks-test's unconditional tail replaces T252's self-grep; escape '# pipe-ok: <reason>' of two words or more.
decisions.why: This is the enforcement the task asks for (T252's self-check moved to where every suite runs), so it is enforcement of the requested fix, not unrequested scope. Its two escaped uses are judged separately. (a) A guard's payload text is never run as a pipe, so no race exists there. (b) T252's forcing line exists to produce the race on purpose for the red test. Neither hides a defect.

decisions.summary: Red first by a forced race (matching line plus seq 200000) on each form, 50 runs each; the check's tests run each form once on the forced text.
decisions.why: This is the task's own red-first requirement, met for one representative of each form, with a stated method.

decisions.summary: T139's no-poll flake is not this race.
decisions.why: This answers the question the task asked, with a stated method. T139 stays open and is ordered after T253, so nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The suites keep their set lines (pipefail stays).
decisions.why: The race is removed at the grep, so pipefail's protection of writers stays. Nothing asked for removing it.

decisions.summary: The census and the check cover tests/ and scripts/; the Approach says the check refuses the pipe form 'anywhere'.
decisions.why: tests/ and scripts/ are the roots the task text names, and the census follows them. 'Anywhere' is read as anywhere in that scope. The builder could word it so; this is not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: Lands after T252 and before T139; 'Performance work? no'.
decisions.why: The order is a dependency: T139's suite is one of those changed. The task makes checks deterministic and does not make them faster, so 'not performance work' is a plain classification and no exception to FR-013.

decisions.summary: The MANIFEST names the tree the bundle was built from (the spec directory's tree, made absolute) and gives the recording command as make -C <tree> plan-verdict ..., on both the task and the blocks form.
decisions.why: This is the task line's own constraint (the MANIFEST names the tree and the exact recording command with its root); make -C is the means, chosen because a reviewer's shell starts wherever its session's did. Serves the request's purpose of removing measured rework (refused recordings and re-dispatches).

decisions.summary: On a section-digest refusal, make plan-verdict searches the trees git worktree list names (the clone and its worktrees) for the one whose plan gives the reviewed digest and names it with the command to run there; with none, today's message; the search runs only on a refusal.
decisions.why: The task line asks that a refusal from a tree whose section differs name the right one; searching the clone's worktrees is how the right one is found, and keeping the old message where no tree holds the text drops nothing asked for. The worktree count is labeled as observed 2026-11-25 with its method.

decisions.summary: Both section checks are fixed (the task route, record_task, and the blocks route, record_blocks' check_named); the whole-plan route keeps its message.
decisions.why: The task line names a section mismatch and a bundle MANIFEST; the whole-plan route records a plan digest, has no section and no bundle MANIFEST naming a tree, so leaving its message alone narrows nothing the task asked for. Covering both bundle routes is the fault's full reach, not added scope.

decisions.summary: Fixed in this task: plan/bundle.rs drops a task's own decision label T<n>-D<n> before decision ids are read (in expand_ranges, which every id reading of a block passes through, and in answered), ranges D<n>-D<n> untouched; pinned by a_task_s_own_decision_label_is_not_the_spec_s_decision.
decisions.why: A defect found in the review tooling (a bundle's spec-cited.md carried spec decisions the section never cited, so a reviewer read uncited text as cited), fixed in the task that found it rather than deferred, which the project's fix-as-we-go rule asks. It names a class of id forms and carries how every instance was found (the census of hyphen-prefixed decision ids in specs/*/plan.md and plan-done.md: T<n>-D<n> 14 times, D<n>-D<n> 107 times, no other form), labeled observed 2026-11-25 with its method, as FR-009 requires. It leaves no defect: the range form the fix leaves alone is the legitimate citation form. Not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: The route is a git merge driver for specs/*/plan-review.json (l7r-gate plan merge-record), not per-task verdict files; no reader changes.
decisions.why: The task line offers exactly these two routes ('each task's verdicts in their own file, or the record merged by a git merge driver') and requires make plan-verdict and every reader unchanged in what they read; choosing the driver is a choice between the offered routes, and it is the one that leaves the readers untouched. The cost comparison is labeled measured 2026-11-25 with its method.

decisions.summary: Three-way, key-by-key merge of the top level and the blocks and tasks maps; an entry is taken whole, never field by field; a both-changed key goes to the later 'reviewed' day, a tie to the incoming side.
decisions.why: This is how the requested driver keeps both sides' entries. Taking an entry whole means no verdict ends up paired with a digest nobody cleared. The tie-break covers only the case where both sides changed the same key, which the goal (two builders each adding their own task's verdict) does not produce. Even a wrong pick only leaves a block owed a review again, because the gate re-compares the digest. Nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: block_reviews is merged as an append-only log: ours, then the incoming rows not in base and not already in ours, order kept.
decisions.why: Keeps both sides' rows (measured 303 to 305) and keeps each side's order, which the review-round guard's trailing count reads. That serves 'both verdicts with no hand merge' and 'every reader unchanged'.

decisions.summary: Registration via sync-with-main.sh ensure_git_config at every sync-in, idempotent; the driver runs with L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1; if it is unregistered or the binary is older than the verb, git falls back to its text merge.
decisions.why: A merge driver's command lives only in local git config, so registering it is how the task line's route works at all. It is registered on the session clone that the goal names, and its worktrees share that config. The fallback is the state from before the task, not an exception to it. Item 5 orders sync-in before the first carry-over it serves.

decisions.summary: A side that does not parse as JSON fails the merge with our side untouched, and the message says to merge it by hand as JSON, both sides' entries kept.
decisions.why: This is a case the driver leaves to a hand merge. It is legitimate on the physically-impossible ground: a structured JSON merge cannot run on a side that is not JSON. It also does not gut the purpose. A record written by make plan-verdict through the recorder's own pretty writer parses, so the two-builder carry-over the task exists for is always handled by the driver. Only a corrupt or hand-broken file falls out, and it gets today's hand merge with a message naming it.

decisions.summary: next_id becomes one past the highest id across this tree's tasks.md/tasks-done.md/plan.md/plan-done.md, the same files on main and on origin/main as last fetched (no fetch under the lock), and a reservation file in the git common directory
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome of make task-add (the FR-011 tool): two worktrees filing the same id, measured in the 2026-11-25 trials. Each added source only widens what counts as taken; nothing that was refused before is now allowed and nothing asked is dropped. Not fetching under the lock is an implementation choice; the stated goal (two worktrees of one repository) is fully met by the shared reservation file.

decisions.summary: the id is written to the reservation file under the existing 451 T84 filing lock before the task box is written
decisions.why: The mechanism of the fix; keeps T84's one-filing-at-a-time constraint and adds nothing beyond it.

decisions.summary: a filing that make quick withdraws (FR-011) gives its id back, so the next filing takes it, as before
decisions.why: Preserves FR-011's withdraw behavior as it stood; an id never written to any tasks file is not a taken id, so returning it cannot recreate the collision.

decisions.summary: a tree git does not know has no other worktree and keeps no reservation
decisions.why: Not a carve-out from the goal: with no git common directory there is no second worktree to collide with, so the case the task fixes cannot arise there.

decisions.summary: two earlier task-crate tests now commit their files first, because main's ids count
decisions.why: Follows from the change; the tests still check what they did. A new red-first test (two_worktrees_never_take_one_id, red on HEAD's numbering: the second tree filed T10) proves the fix.

decisions.summary: lands with T254, before the first port batch at three builders
decisions.why: Ordering only; nothing is deferred or left (Found and left: none).

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T254's section as it stands
make task-start writes <common git dir>/task-marks/<feature>/<task>.json (feature, task, bundle tasks, tree, time); no start overwrites another task's mark
decisions.why: This is the fix the GM approved by name: 'a started-task mark per task' (request.md, 2026-11-25, 'sounds good, please start with that'), answering trial 1's overwritten mark.

decisions.summary: a tree's own task is the newest mark that tree wrote (marks::of_tree)
decisions.why: The per-task mark needs a rule for which mark is a tree's own. Before, the one mark was the clone's, so reading it per tree keeps what it meant with one builder per tree.

decisions.summary: the main worktree reads the old active-task file as its oldest mark; that tree's next start removes it
decisions.why: A migration that keeps a start made before the change counting. It narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: a mark goes when its task lands (the landed sweep, by task ids as given) or when its feature is set down in its own tree (marks::clear); other trees' marks stay; a ticked task's stale mark holds nothing
decisions.why: This narrows 451 T29: a set-down used to clear its feature's mark, and now clears only the marks this tree wrote. The ground is the request's purpose. With per-task marks, a set-down that cleared other trees' marks would wipe a parallel builder's started task, and that brings back the very failure the request fixes (trial 1, one start removing another tree's mark). When there was one mark, it was always the clone's own, so T29's scope in effect is unchanged. A ticked task's leftover mark holding nothing follows from every reader asking for an open box.

decisions.summary: each task-starts.jsonl row names its tree
decisions.why: The data the per-tree readers need. It adds no behavior beyond the fix.

decisions.summary: another tree's started task (its box open, not ticked by this landing) holds this push, make land or CI merge only when the push's delta carries one of its edits (T101's rule in speckit/touch.rs, read against every tree's prefix); L7R_LAND_READY still not held; a mark that is not an object fails closed
decisions.why: This narrows feature 405 D4 ('the active task holds, nothing else'). The plan turns D4 into every started task of any tree holding the push, so taken literally a push from any of the three worktrees would be refused while another builder's task was started. That is the exact refusal the trials recorded (port-talk-agenda item 1: 'a push of one task was refused while the other was started'). It would defeat the purpose of the GM's 2026-11-25 approval, which is three parallel builders, so the rule applied literally defeats the request. A push that carries another tree's edits is still refused, which is broader than D4 ever was, so the hold's purpose of keeping an unfinished task's work out of main is kept across trees.

decisions.summary: the pushing tree's OWN started task (a mark this tree wrote, box open, not ticked by this landing) no longer holds a push whose delta carries none of its edits; before T254 it held the push whatever the push carried (the section's own constraints item 2; feature 405 D4)
decisions.why: The section justifies the narrowing as 'the fix the trials asked for - a push of one builder's task refused while another builder's was started'. That covers another tree's task only: the trials' refusal came from a different worktree's start. The GM's words in request.md ('a started-task mark per task' ... 'sounds good, please start with that') approve per-task marks so three builders can work side by side. Nothing in those words, and nothing in that purpose, needs a tree's OWN open started task to stop holding its own push. Keeping D4's hold for the tree's own task is possible, the GM's words do not contradict it, and it does not defeat three parallel builders: each builder's tree lands its own task(s), and that landing ticks them, so they do not hold it. The rest of the plan's case comes from text outside the request. One is consistency with 451 T101's landing rule, which is cited by paraphrase only and is not in spec-cited.md. The other is that a push without the task's edits carries none of its work. Neither is a ground under this review: they show the exception does no harm, not that the request needs it. One justification is stretched over two unlike cases, and only one of them is needed. Cure: keep D4's hold for the started tasks this tree wrote, so one of them holds this tree's push while its box is open and the landing does not tick it, whatever the delta carries. Apply the carried-edits rule only to other trees' marks. Restate goal item 1 and constraints item 2 to match, and add a test that a tree's own open started task still refuses a push that does not carry its edits. Or bring the GM's words approving the own-tree case.

decisions.summary: edit lines read against every tree (git's worktrees, the trees marks and starts name, the clone), longest first, a nested worktree read as its own
decisions.why: Fixes a known defect: T101's rule skipped every edit a worktree builder made. Fixing it in this task is what the GM's fix-as-we-go rule asks for.

decisions.summary: speckit::active_task, the plan crate's task::active_task and their callers (declared placement, decide's refusal, approach tripwire, plan door active-task) read this tree's mark
decisions.why: What a one-mark reader meant (this builder's task), carried over to per-task marks.

decisions.summary: event-log booking (filed.rs::starts), context cap fallback, and land-tooling's log line read their own tree's starts; a row with no tree read as before
decisions.why: The same per-tree reading. land_tooling was round 1's note and is now per tree, fixed with a red-first test.

decisions.summary: stall check and the hold read every mark
decisions.why: The stall check serves the coordinator over all trees. The hold is ruled above.

decisions.summary: Stop hook started/idle, events-refile, measure reports (task_time, where_time, feature_report) stay clone-wide on purpose
decisions.why: These serve the coordinating session and the GM's task time breakdown across every task. Leaving them clone-wide is no defect and narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: readers that already take the task from an argument or per-task row (ready.rs started_tasks, builder_stop, static_runs, closing-checks, wording, the Makefile sweep, check_bundle own, approach in_flight, whose.rs) unchanged
decisions.why: They were never tied to the one mark. Unchanged is within the request.

decisions.summary: the landed sweep removes marks by task ids as given, so lettered ids (T07b) are removed
decisions.why: Fixes a known defect found while building. Fixed here, not deferred.

decisions.summary: lands with T255 before the first three-builder batch; green by closing-checks, red set down and ruled through arbiter-ask
decisions.why: This is the order the GM approved: the fixes before three builders.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T259's section as it stands

The check does not detect prose rules (a CLAUDE.md or docs/ line to wait, serialize or always do a step), a new mandatory round of an existing agent, or a standing order added to the builder brief; they are added as found and audit-register.md names the gap.
decisions.why: This is about the check's reach over FUTURE additions only. These have no form in a delta that a check can tell from correct prose, and the GM's own words expect such misses: 'something like this limit on builder token window context size might not even show up as an optimization ... after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. The gap is recorded. Whether the EXISTING instances belong in the initial backfill is ruled under T259-backfill.

decisions.summary: A refusal that make land's first pass adds inside an existing step (a stops.push(...) call in land/cheap.rs, 6 today, measured) is not detected, grouped with the prose kinds under 'none has a form a check can tell from correct work'.
decisions.why: One reason is stretched over unlike things. The other three kinds left out are prose, which no check can tell from correct prose. This one is code: the block found it with a grep and counted 6 instances, and it does not show that these lack a form a check can read (a rise in the count of stops.push( calls in rust/gate/crates/land/src/ against the base, for example). A refusal at landing is the task line's 'mandatory check' and costs every builder time, the same class round 1's D1b found missing. For it to be legitimate the block must show that such a form would false-fire, by replaying it over the same 20 landings. Otherwise detect it. Either way the six existing refusals belong in the initial backfill (T259-backfill).

decisions.summary: A guard module is a file named <name>_hooks.rs or <name>_gate.rs (guard or shared crate) added as A; a rename adds nothing; a submodule is not a module.
decisions.why: The guard crates name their modules this way, and the whole-tree run finds 50, so this detects the task line's 'a guard' as it exists. Renames and submodules add no mechanism.

decisions.summary: The constant scope is widened from the checks crate to rust/guard/ and the gate's checks, land and cohort crates, and Duration joins the numeric types.
decisions.why: This closes round 1's D2 finding: CLAIMS_WAIT_S and the other nine landing knobs (measured 2026-11-26) are now read, and so is a wait written as a Duration.

decisions.summary: The rest of rust/gate/ stays out of the constant scope ('74 names there pass the filter, many of them knobs of the research tooling (CHASE_CHARS, PASSAGE_CHARS) that cost a builder nothing'), so those constants are neither checked on a delta nor listed in the backfill.
decisions.why: (1) The test the scope applies is 'the crates whose constants hold a builder's or a landing's time'. That is narrower than the GM's 'a list of all of the auditable optimizations and processes and procedures', and narrower than the block's own goal line ('Every optimization or procedure that costs time or tokens'). Nothing in request.md limits the register to a builder's time. (2) 'cost a builder nothing' is asserted, never measured, and it does not say whether these constants cost tokens. (3) These names PASS the block's own threshold filter, so in the guard crates they would count as thresholds and are dropped here by crate alone. (4) The 74 was measured on 2026-11-25, when the scope was the checks crate alone, so it may still include the ten land and cohort names now in scope. Only 'many of them' are described, and the rest are not named. (5) 'Corrections the agenda excludes' is not shown: the block names no excluded constant that is a pure correction costing nothing. It would be legitimate if a current measurement NAMED the excluded constants and showed each costs neither time nor tokens and is no cap or threshold. Otherwise read those crates with the same filter, and their names join the initial backfill.

decisions.summary: Only module-level constants (column 0) are read. A threshold constant inside a function, an impl or an inline test module is not.
decisions.why: Leaving out inline test modules is right. For functions and impls, the bundle shows no threshold constant there that is being missed, and skipping them keeps the detector simple and free of false fires. Like D3's miss, any found later are backfilled as the GM's route allows. Aside, not a finding: the block should count the threshold-named constants inside functions and impls in the scope's non-test files.

decisions.summary: A constant is new by NAME over the whole scope, not by file, so a move or a 1,000-line split adds nothing. Stated miss: a new threshold reusing a name already present (a second CAP) is not seen.
decisions.why: Comparing by name keeps the check from firing on a constant moved or a file split by the 1,000-line bar, which would be firing on correct work. The miss it states (a second CAP) is the kind of thing the GM's words expect to be found later: 'after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. Aside, not a finding: counting a name's lines would also catch a second CAP, and it would help to measure how many names in the scope appear more than once.

decisions.summary: The name filter: a constant counts if a part of its name is a threshold word and the name is not unit words alone. On the widened scope it keeps 69 of 105 names (34 dropped, plus 2 dropped as units).
decisions.why: The filter was measured and its drops examined: of the first scope's 84 names it keeps every knob the agenda names, and it drops display sizes and fixed facts (LARGEST, SHOWN, CHUNK, SIGTERM, DAY, MICROS) and units. The replay showed the unfiltered check firing on GB and LARGEST, which cost no time and refuse nothing. Firing on those would be firing on correct work. Aside, not a finding: the seven land and cohort names the filter drops are counted but not named.

decisions.summary: The gate chain is the targets the eight fixed roots (detect::CHAIN) reach transitively, through prerequisites and $(MAKE) calls. A target-specific variable line is no rule.
decisions.why: This detects the task line's 'a gate step', and the replay found closing-checks and _quick, both real additions.

decisions.summary: A landing step is a new push-table row, a make land phase or a GATES script name, each compared against the base text of the same file.
decisions.why: This closes round 1's D1b: push rows and land phases are now detected, and the re-run found T233's gm-attributions push check.

decisions.summary: An entry counts only whole: all eleven fields are checked on every run, and unmeasured is allowed only with first-audit.
decisions.why: This enforces what was asked (the logic, the measurements, the falsifier, the last audit) and stops a stub from silencing the check.

decisions.summary: One Markdown file per entry, with key-value front matter, parsed without a new dependency.
decisions.why: The task line asks for one file per entry, and the form is a design choice inside that.

decisions.summary: The check runs in make static and in the push. The push row needs dev/audits, so a fixture push without a register stays silent.
decisions.why: Running in both places refuses a missing entry earlier. The real tree holds dev/audits, so nothing the GM asked for is exempted.

decisions.summary: The escape AUDIT_ENTRY_OK with a recorded reason. Each escape is logged escaped and each refusal blocked.
decisions.why: This follows the project's guard rules, and the log lets the check be audited against its own falsifier.

decisions.summary: Cadences, and any threshold no record states, are GUESS knobs; never-audited entries get the shortest cadence.
decisions.why: The GM asked for each entry to know its last audit and be re-audited. Labeling the unmeasured knobs GUESS is the project's rule.

decisions.summary: A declined option is an entry of kind declined in the same register: its evidence, a falsifier and threshold that would reopen it, and a cadence. The three options in process-decisions.md become entries.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 2026-11-25 words directly: 'record decisions about what NOT to implement ... in the same way'.

decisions.summary: Thirteen first entries: ten adopted (among them T254-T257's mechanisms and the check itself) and three declined.
decisions.why: The task line asks for the first entries, and the agenda's 'Order' paragraph puts T254-T257's entries here.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the initial backfill is T260's list, which is defined as make audits' BACKFILL section, the five detectors' output (181, measured). The kinds the detectors cannot see are left to 'as found', with audit-register.md naming the gap.
decisions.why: Round 1's item is half closed: the kinds left out are now listed (D1), and the 181 has a count and a method. But the block's constraint 2 says agenda item 13 names 'the backfill's sources', and the found-and-left item defines T260's list as the detectors' BACKFILL output alone. No sentence puts into the INITIAL backfill the mechanisms that are already known and that the detectors leave out: the six stops.push refusals counted in D1, whatever D2-rest leaves out, and the agenda's backfill sources beyond the detectors. The GM's 'backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed' comes AFTER 'the initial backfill' and covers things nobody has found. It does not cover a set the block has itself counted or that the agenda names as a source. It would be legitimate if the deferral to T260 said T260 takes item 13's backfill sources, the six stops.push refusals and what D2-rest leaves out, each with how its instances will be found.

decisions.summary: A bare git mirror at <common .git>/tooling-state.git, committed from where the files lie, not tar snapshots
decisions.why: The mechanism that carries 'the tooling state' to the GM's repository; chosen by measurement (item 9, dated, methods named). Nothing the GM asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: Logs committed as whole-line segments (split -C, SEGMENT a GUESS knob), the mirror repacked each run
decisions.why: A storage layout that keeps every log line in the repository and keeps pushes clear of GitHub's per-file limit, which would otherwise end every push. Nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: The landing's push runs detached (push --detach); make land / land-tooling exit with their own code
decisions.why: Implements the task line's 'never refusing it'. The GM's words set no timing for the push.

decisions.summary: A detached push's failure is logged and said in one line at the NEXT landing; make state-push is the foreground form
decisions.why: The cost of D3a, named and priced against a foreground push. A failure is still reported, so the state does not silently stop reaching the repository.

decisions.summary: A push that meets a running push (flock held) is skipped; the next landing's push carries its state
decisions.why: 'At each landing' is in the section's quotation of the task line, not in request.md or the spec. On the block's own text, state written after the running push's commit is unsaved until the next landing, and so is all state written between any two landings. The skip widens that gap by one landing and does not lose state. The cost is named here rather than ruled as a narrowing.

decisions.summary: One branch per clone, named for the clone the common .git belongs to; a replacement container's clone of that name takes it
decisions.why: A layout inside the GM's repository. Every clone's state still reaches the repository.

decisions.summary: Never a force push; a fresh mirror fetches and merges the branch before its first commit; a refused push is fetched, merged and pushed on top
decisions.why: Keeps state already in the repository from being overwritten. Serves the purpose and drops nothing.

decisions.summary: Restore merges and never overwrites: answers by l7r-gate record merge-answers (newer utc kept), logs by appending missing lines; .tmp files not pushed
decisions.why: Restoring the state into a fresh clone is the point of the repository. A .tmp file is a half-written answer or log line, not finished tooling state.

decisions.summary: Session-clone setup is sync-with-main.sh sync-in, running restore --if-fresh (mirror made and restored in the background); a clone that already has a mirror does nothing; make state-restore by hand
decisions.why: A clone that has a mirror is not the fresh or replacement clone the restore exists for, and the by-hand door stays open. The background restore delays nothing.

decisions.summary: A clone whose origin is not GitHub main's does nothing unless STATE_REMOTE names a remote
decisions.why: Ruled class by class. (1) Other suites' fixture clones, which run sync-with-main.sh with local origins and made-up answers and logs: pushing them would put fake data into the GM's private repository and have tests reach the real remote. Excluding them is implied by the purpose ('for the tooling state', the real record-check answers and event logs), so this class is legitimate. (2) A real working clone whose origin is something other than GitHub main: the stated justification does not cover it, because its state is real tooling state. The bundle shows one real push, from diagram-backlog. It does not say whether make state-push goes through this origin check, or what any other clone's origin is. D7 says clones are made by a bare git clone, presumably of GitHub, and the block names no real clone the check leaves out. So no defect is shown here. If such a clone exists, STATE_REMOTE is its door, and leaving it silently unbacked would be a defect for its owner to fix.

decisions.summary: Token via l7r-gate github-token into GITHUB_TOKEN with the askpass script; credential.helper emptied; remote passed by URL per call, never stored in the mirror's config
decisions.why: Implements the task line's 'never printed, never on a command line, never in a config' for the GM's private repository.

decisions.summary: A shell script beside sync-with-main.sh and land-tooling.sh, not a gate crate; the answers' merge reused from the gate
decisions.why: A choice of implementation form. Not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: Only record-checks and l7r-events are added to the mirror's index; handoffs and caches stay out
decisions.why: Matches the GM's 'for the record-check answers and event logs' and the task line's exclusion.

decisions.summary: Found and left, not a defect: a grown log's last segment is sent whole (no thin-pack delta base), about 125 KB for a 7 KB diff
decisions.why: A size cost, measured with its method. There is no wrong outcome: the push is detached and every line still arrives.

decisions.summary: Found and left, not a defect: check audit-register's detectors do not see a script newly called from a landing recipe; the entry is written by hand, and a task title is handed to the coordinating session
decisions.why: The GM's own T259 words expect misses and say how they are handled: 'after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. This entry is that backfill, so no mechanism goes unregistered. The detector's reach is left as it was, and the title is passed on so the miss can be filed.

decisions.summary: At the tick, where the plan gate owes nothing and PLAN_REVIEW_OK is set, the tick proceeds, prints 'drop PLAN_REVIEW_OK', and writes no bypass record or guard-log event; make land's tick prints it too.
decisions.why: No gate is passed by the escape, so nothing is escaped and nothing is weakened: the gate still refuses wherever it owes something, whether or not the session obeys the line (real enforcement, the GM 2026-11-19). Feature 243's recorded escape is unchanged where the gate holds something.

decisions.summary: plan-gate.sh asks l7r-gate plan push before honoring the escape; on an empty list with the escape set it prints the drop line and exits 0 with no record.
decisions.why: Corrects the order that made clean pushes write escape records; the gate's scope (451 T84 in_scope) and its refusal are untouched, so enforcement does not depend on the instruction being followed.

decisions.summary: A bare PLAN_REVIEW_OK token on a clean gate is told the drop line and not asked for a reason.
decisions.why: The two-word reason rule applies to an escape taken; here none is taken. Where the gate holds something the reason is still required (feature 243 unchanged). FR-012's escape rule covers FR-006 to FR-013 and is not narrowed.

decisions.summary: An honored escape's record gains held: rows of {feature, rule, blocks}, the full key list from status::judge_held (stale keys, BLOCKED keys, none under plan-review-missing and plan-missing, where the gate lists no block); the push's record computed over the range by a new door subcommand.
decisions.why: Adds data to the record; empty blocks under missing/plan-missing reflects that the gate itself names no block there, not an omission. Serves the GM's audit-register request (what would falsify an optimization) and his ask that time and process be measured.

decisions.summary: 'Checked against what the gate held' is built as the record carrying held beside the reason for a reader to compare; the reason's wording is not parsed or refused.
decisions.why: No clause of request.md and no FR in the spec asks for a reason to be machine-checked against the held blocks; a word-list check that refuses reasons would be new refusing behavior the GM did not ask for. The block's reading of T262's task line (title and body) could not be verified from the bundle, which does not carry the task line; judged against the GM's request and spec, which is the standard, it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: make audit's Bypasses listing is not changed and no listing or measurement over held is built or filed here; a count by held is a title in the builder's report.
decisions.why: Neither request.md nor the spec asks for make audit to classify plan-gate escapes; the line asking it is the session's task line, not the GM's, and is not in the bundle, so the block's reading of it could not be verified. Not building the listing leaves no wrong outcome (no defect): the data is recorded and countable. The aside: if T262's own line promises the classification, the builder's report title should be filed so the line's purpose is not silently dropped - a tasks matter, not a fidelity narrowing of the GM's request.

decisions.summary: DEFER_FORM_OK's record, by the same writer, carries no held.
decisions.why: It escapes the decide lint, not the plan gate; there is nothing the plan gate held to record.

decisions.summary: dev/audits/plan-gate-escape.md with falsifier 'honored escapes per landing above about 0.3 over a week after 449 T439' (GUESS), baseline 158 escape records against 354 commits measured 2026-11-26 by stated commands.
decisions.why: Directly serves the GM's 2026-11-25 audit-register request (logic, measurements, and what would falsify it). Figures carry date and method. Note only: the falsifier is per landing while the baseline is per commit on main.

decisions.summary: docs/guards.md's plan-gate row states the rule.
decisions.why: Documents the enforced rule; no scope change.

decisions.summary: The section marks the task 'Performance work? no'.
decisions.why: The task changes a guard's escape handling and its record; it is not measurement of where time goes in the GM's 2026-11-20 sense (FR-013's full text is not in the bundle). The classification affects scheduling only and narrows nothing the GM asked for in this task.

decisions.summary: Fix the flake at its cause in the test fixture: World::new's in-process std::fs::copy of the template is replaced by one `cp -a <template>/. <world>` child, so no descriptor of the test process writes a world's fakes and no fork can inherit one. The why and a 'do not copy in-process again' sit at copy, and the module header is corrected.
decisions.why: T263's line as relayed in the block (find the race, make the test deterministic, fix the cause and not a retry) asks for exactly this. It removes the cause rather than retrying, and covers every fake the template carries at once.

decisions.summary: The cause is attributed to ETXTBSY from a descriptor inherited across another thread's fork during the fixture's copy. 451 T258's state restore is excluded because the fixture runs a three-line fake sync. The failing notice is reconstructed by forcing, not recovered from the red gate.
decisions.why: This is a finding, not a scope choice. The block itself says the attribution rests on a forced reproduction and a fixture read rather than recovered output, and the first-assertion print hedges a misattribution. Whether the mechanism is right is a design and correctness question, not a fidelity one.

decisions.summary: The first assertion prints the notice it read ("{full}"), so a future failure shows what was said.
decisions.why: It serves 'find the race' for any recurrence. The test checks the same thing and only says more when it fails.

decisions.summary: The guard's code is not changed. A refresh that cannot START its script still says `mirror refresh FAILED: ` with nothing after the colon.
decisions.why: Measured against the wrong-outcome definition (constitution XIV v2.36.0), this is not a defect. The notice says truthfully that the refresh failed, it is said in full every time, and it is the same branch a failing script takes. In a real clone the script is a git-written file that this process never holds open, so the cause cannot occur there. A sparser message than one might like is a difference, not a wrong outcome, so leaving it needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: No kept test forces the race. The red-first was a one-shot stub on the unfixed copy: a sleep-3 child handed the copied script's write handle. It gave 520 passed and 1 failed at this test's first assertion, then 521 passed with the stub removed and 521 passed with the fix.
decisions.why: The relayed task line asks for red-first by forcing the interleaving, and the forced red answers that. Nothing in the GM's request or the task line asks for a kept regression pin of this race, so leaving it out narrows nothing that was asked. The plan's impossibility argument covers a behavioural pin only, since the fixed copy holds no descriptor to race. A structural pin, such as a lint on in-process copies in the fixture, would be possible, but it is not required by anything asked.

decisions.summary: The sibling census of ways a rust/guard test could directly run a file its own process wrote names its forms (from_mode, set_permissions, 0o literals, .mode(0o, chmod children, fs::copy, and fs::write/File::create/OpenOptions on .sh or scripts/bin/hooks paths), reads every hit, and finds no other instance. Crates outside rust/guard were not searched.

decisions.id: D2 task's own bundle left un-keyed
decisions.summary: plan-<feature>-<task> (make decide) is not keyed by tree; the plan labels this narrower than the task line's 'key the plan review bundle by tree'
decisions.why: The block's stated reason, that keying it would change the -T<n> shape the plan hold reads, is a cost argument and does not carry this ruling. The ruling rests on a different premise: leaving the name alone leaves no defect. The purpose of the task and of the GM's 2026-11-25 fix ('a review recording in its own tree') is that no reviewer reads a bundle another tree rewrote, or records in the wrong tree. That bundle's name already carries its task. Its MANIFEST already names its tree (T257), as this very bundle's does: diagram-backlog-t271. Each builder works in a worktree of its own task. The GM approved 'a started-task mark per task' (2026-11-25, the same four fixes) so that one task is not started twice. So two trees can only rebuild one task's own bundle if one task is decided in two trees at once, and that is the case the started mark exists to prevent. The block states 'a task has one builder' without measuring it. It holds as far as the started mark does, and no GM word asks for more. The task line's 'by tree' wording is the session's own, not the GM's. If a second tree is ever found deciding a builder's task (the coordinating clone, for example), that is a defect and would need this reopened.

Read plainly, it does not reach this 2026-11-25 trials task, and stretching it to T271 would be completing the GM's thought. A builder that ignores it can still overwrite another's file, so the goal is aimed at, not guaranteed.

This covers the three things the task line and brief name (make land, make land-tooling, the push), and the roster lines it leaves out are not calls. Steps the gate chain runs are already items of their own: `$(MAKE)` edges through make_graph, and l7r-gate's gates as STEPS.

decisions.summary: A script's name is a `scripts/<path>` ending in a file extension, with a trailing full stop cut and `#` lines skipped. Globs, directories and variable paths name no script.
decisions.why: How names are parsed is a design choice inside the request. It follows T259-D1 as the block states it (read paths and names, never prose).

decisions.summary: A script is new by name across all the read sources together, base against head. A moved call, or a script already called elsewhere, adds nothing.
decisions.why: A script the landing already ran is no new mechanism, so the register owes it no new entry. This is T259-D3's shape as the block states it.

decisions.summary: Rule-line reading becomes one shared function `rule` used by make_graph and landing_recipes, so a target-specific variable line is not a rule. make_graph's behavior and tests are unchanged.
decisions.why: An internal refactor that changes no behavior. Nothing in the request touches it.

decisions.summary: dev/audits/tooling-state.md gains `covers: landing script scripts/state-sync.sh`, its prose drops the claim that the check cannot see the script, and guards.md, process-decisions.md and audit-register.md describe the new reading and its replay.
decisions.why: This records the register's own entry for the mechanism the fix covers, which is what the GM asked the register to hold.

decisions.summary: Accepted miss: a script that a called script calls in turn is not followed.
decisions.why: Test it against the purpose. T258's failure one level down would be a new script that state-sync.sh or l7r-gate.sh starts calling, and this limit would miss it. Even so, the limit is legitimate. The GM's own words expect a detector that does not see everything and is grown as misses are found: 'after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. The block names no such nested case today (observed 2026-11-26, the replay over 40 landings found only state-sync.sh), so this leaves no known defect, only a possible future miss handled the way the GM prescribed. Following calls literally would ask entries for every script l7r-gate.sh and the guard launcher name, which is beyond the landing steps the task covers. The limit is written beside the rule in detect.rs, where a later miss would reopen it.

decisions.summary: Accepted miss: a script reached by a path not written `scripts/...`. One exists today, sync-with-main.sh's dirname call of state-sync.sh at sync-in.
decisions.why: The one instance today is state-sync.sh, and this task gives that script a `covers:` line. Since a script is new by name across all the read sources, that instance owes nothing more, and nothing the register needs is missed. Reading `)/name.ext` would misread make land's `.../task-starts.jsonl` as a script, and the GM's backfill-as-we-go words cover any future case.

decisions.summary: Not read: what `l7r-gate land` itself runs.
decisions.why: Those gates are already detected as STEPS (`landing gate <name>`), so nothing is left uncovered.

decisions.summary: Accepted: a message in the push scripts that newly names a script reads as a call. No shell reader is built. The escape is AUDIT_ENTRY_OK and the reopener is a false fire in the guard log.
decisions.why: This narrows nothing the GM asked for. It is a design trade-off in the check's precision, priced on a measured replay (0 such cases in 40 landings, 2026-11-26) and given a falsifier. It is a hypothetical, not a known defect left in place. None of the accepted limits has a case today, which is why 'Found and left? none' holds.

decisions.summary: The six scripts the landing already calls with no entry go into T260's backfill (make audits' BACKFILL 254 -> 260) rather than being written here. T260's line keeps its dated 254.
decisions.why: The GM's request plans for an initial backfill, and T260 is that task, so routing the six there carries out the request rather than deferring a defect of T269. T269's fix makes the six visible, and item 5 asks for T269 to land before T260 writes its backfill. Keeping a dated figure as dated is fine.

decisions.summary: an operation in progress (CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, MERGE_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, sequencer/todo, rebase-merge, rebase-apply incl. am) read in the tree's own git directory refuses the landing, naming the unmerged paths and the continue or abort
decisions.why: Ends the wrong outcome the section names (main said T270 landed while its code was not on main); no GM words or spec requirement bear on it, and the block says the task line asks for it (the task line is not in the bundle). Reading the linked worktree's own git dir is what makes the check reach the case at all.

decisions.summary: a standing rebase is offered only --abort, never --continue
decisions.why: Follows constitution VI (no history rewrite) cited in the constraints; nothing asked for continuing a rebase.

decisions.summary: unmerged paths with nothing in progress are refused, naming resolve, add, commit
decisions.why: Same purpose as D1a; refuses a tree whose carried work is not committed.

decisions.summary: staged changes with nothing in progress are refused (unmeasured over past landings; falsifier in the audit entry)
decisions.why: The block says the task line asks it. The premise that no correct work stages is by reading, not measured, but it leaves no defect: every exit printed (commit, or restore --staged) loses no work, so a false fire costs one command; T88's dirty-clone landing alone still holds for unstaged work.

decisions.summary: the refusal runs first and apart from the first pass's other refusals, not in their list
decisions.why: A departure from the coordinating session's brief ('together with its other first-pass refusals'), not from the GM's request or the spec, which say nothing on it. Its reason holds on purpose grounds: the first pass commits on its way, and a commit while a pick or merge stands concludes it with whatever is staged - the very failure the task ends. Its cost (a second refusal met on the next make land) loses nothing. The coordinating session should note it departs from its brief.

decisions.summary: no escape on the refusal
decisions.why: FR-012's escape requirement covers FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013 refusals only, not this one; every refusal prints a lossless command that finishes the state, so no correct work is left without a way through. Consistent with 'real enforcement and not just instructions' (GM 2026-11-19).

decisions.summary: one copy, l7r-gate land --unfinished, asked by sync-with-main.sh push_cmd before its uncommitted-changes message and by land-tooling.sh before its fetch
decisions.why: Extends the same refusal to the other landing doors so the wrong outcome cannot reach main by another route.

decisions.summary: make carry FROM= [COMMIT=]: refuses unfinished trees, fetches the commit, says so if already in history, cherry-picks, resolves all or none, verifies at the end
decisions.why: The block says the task line and brief ask for make carry in place of the hand cherry-pick; its verified end serves the goal that a carried commit's code is in HEAD before anything lands.

decisions.summary: on a conflict make carry resolves every unmerged path or none, else stops with the pick standing and D1's line as the next command
decisions.why: A partial resolution would leave a tree D1 must refuse anyway; stopping whole keeps the chained make land refused, which is the task's purpose.

decisions.summary: keep-both only for tasks.md hunks with empty base whose added lines are list lines, and plan-review.json via plan::merge_files; rewrites of one line or added prose stop
decisions.why: Nothing in the GM's request or spec asks for automatic conflict resolution at all; the narrower rule stops where keeping both sides would produce two versions of one task line (a wrong outcome), and a stop prints the next command, so nothing is lost. The 2026-11-26 conflict's shape is covered and pinned.

decisions.summary: make carry carries one commit; several are carried one COMMIT= at a time, oldest first
decisions.why: No loss of function: every commit can still be carried, and a hand-picked range left paused is refused by D1 (sequencer/todo).

decisions.summary: the history guard lets `git rebase --abort` through (exact form only); every other rebase form still refused
decisions.why: Loosens an existing guard by one exact command that rewrites no history (it restores the branch to where the rebase began), so constitution VI is untouched; without it D1 would print a command no session can run, and a refusal must name a compliant command. Its reach is no wider than that command.

decisions.summary: the audit register's check counts refusals in land/unfinished.rs beside land/cheap.rs; the entry's covers: lines name them
decisions.why: Enforces the GM's audit register words (2026-11-25: document each process with its measurements and falsifier) on this refusal, which the check otherwise missed; enforcement of what was asked, not new scope.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T285's section as it stands
the pool's registry at <clone>/.git/builder-pool.json with its log; membership by registry, never by a name's shape; new trees <clones>/<clone>-b<N>
decisions.why: how the tooling records the reused trees the GM asked it to keep; settles nothing the request left open against it

decisions.summary: make builder-tree hands out the task's tree, else the first free tree at HEAD, else ONE new cold tree under the cap with its guard binary built (1800 s GUESS knob); at the cap refused naming holders
decisions.why: the tooling performing the reuse ('automatically ... performs the correct behavior'); a cold tree is made only when no warm one exists, and is said to be cold

decisions.summary: a free tree with uncommitted content not in HEAD holds it: the handout is refused naming the paths, DISCARD with a reason takes it over; a held free tree is never passed over for a new cold one
decisions.why: refusing rather than making a cold tree past a warm one is the request's rule enforced, not narrowed; DISCARD is the project's reasoned, logged escape (FR-012's pattern)

decisions.summary: builder-tree-release and make land / land-batch free the tree and leave it and its cache in place; a release never fails a landing
decisions.why: the deletion after landing was the mistake; the landing now performs the correct step itself

decisions.summary: at every handout a tree whose holding tasks are ticked or archived is freed first
decisions.why: removes a hand step on which reuse would otherwise depend - 'without the opportunity for this kind of mistake'

decisions.id: D4c every hold names its feature
decisions.summary: a handout or adoption with a task and no feature is refused
decisions.why: makes D4b able to read every hold; serves the same clause

decisions.summary: make builder-trees lists; builder-tree-drop is the one removal (reason, logged, held tree refused); builder-tree-adopt joins a pre-pool worktree under its own name, the tooling's trees refused
decisions.why: drop is a deliberate, logged give-back of disk that the GM's disk words (2026-11-22, 2026-11-25) keep necessary, not the unthinking deletion after every landing; adopt keeps the three existing warm trees

decisions.id: D6 adopt by name, not rename
decisions.summary: the three trees of 2026-11-26 adopted under their names because a moved tree rebuilt every workspace crate (66.5 s / 41.7 s against 0.11 s / 0.08 s warm, measured 2026-11-26 with method)
decisions.why: the measured choice that keeps the caches warm, which is the request's purpose

decisions.summary: CAP = 4 (L7R_BUILDER_POOL), a GUESS knob from the sizing rule; T284 measures the count
decisions.why: a bound on the pool's size; refusing at the cap makes no hand route to a cold tree, and the request sets no count

decisions.id: D8a guard reach bounded to the clones directory
decisions.summary: the guard refuses `git worktree add` only for a path under <mirror>/.clones/; scratch worktrees elsewhere pass
decisions.why: Test: is the refused act a builder tree made by hand. The clones directory is where every builder tree lives (the pool's own trees, the hand trees of the mistake, -t269/-t270/-t271), so under it the guard reaches exactly the mistake's class. A worktree elsewhere is a scratch tree whose correct behavior is to be made and removed; refusing it would reach work the GM did not ask to stop (UNREQUESTED reach), and a hook cannot tell a scratch tree from a builder's except by where it lands. Taking the bound literally away would defeat no part of the request's purpose that the pool does not already serve.

decisions.summary: refuses worktree remove/move of a pool tree and rm of a pool tree, its cache or a directory holding either; BUILDER_TREE_OK with a reason escapes, checked first
decisions.why: the deletion half of the mistake, refused; move refused because it was measured to chill the cache; the reasoned escape is the accepted spec's guard pattern (FR-012)

decisions.id: D8c tooling trees exempt by call site
decisions.summary: land-alone.sh, land-tooling.sh, review-tree.sh and the pool tool call git inside a program, which a hook does not read; a hand `git worktree add .../<clone>-land` is refused
decisions.why: physically impossible otherwise: a PreToolUse hook reads only the tool call, not git calls inside a program; and these are the tooling the GM asked to perform the behavior, while the hand form of the same tree is still refused, so the exemption guts nothing

decisions.id: L1 cp -a into the clones directory
decisions.summary: a tree under the clones directory made by `cp -a` is not a worktree and not read (limit accepted)
decisions.why: Same test as D8a: under the clones directory any tree made by hand is a builder tree of the mistake's class, whatever command made it. 'Not a worktree' is the word-level argument; the purpose ('without the opportunity for this kind of mistake') is that no builder starts in a hand-made cold tree, and a copied tree is cold (the cache is keyed by the tree's name; D6 measured that a moved tree is not warm). The block's own goal (part A item 1, 'the only way to get a builder's tree is the pool') is contradicted by it. None of the three tests is met: it is not impossible to read a cp whose destination is a new directory directly under <mirror>/.clones/, nothing in the request implies it, and the literal reading defeats no stated purpose. A guard that passes bad work is a defect: either refuse it in T285 (same escape, red first), or carry it under 'Found and left?' with a filed task and its order, as T295 is carried.

decisions.id: L2 git clone into the clones directory
decisions.summary: a tree under the clones directory made by `git clone` is not a worktree and not read (limit accepted)
decisions.why: Judged on its own: a `git clone` to <mirror>/.clones/<name> handed to a builder is a fresh, cold, hand-made builder tree in the place builder trees live, which is the mistake the GM asked to have no opportunity for; the registry would not even hold it. The exemption rests on the word 'worktree', not on the request's purpose, and is not impossible to guard (a clone's destination under the clones directory is read from the command like a worktree's). Remedy as L1: refuse it in T285 with the same reasoned escape, or carry it as a filed defect with an order under FR-009's form.

decisions.id: L3 a new cold tree's cache not seeded
decisions.summary: a newly made pool tree's cache is not seeded from a warm one
decisions.why: not asked for; and the rename measurement (D6) shows a cache at a different absolute path rebuilds anyway, so seeding would not make a new tree warm

decisions.summary: /usr/bin/git worktree add passes the shared walk; filed as T295, fixed across every tree guard, lands before T284
decisions.why: a defect carried in FR-009's form: why not here (the shared walk every tree guard asks), filed id T295, order (lands before T284, the next work that relies on warm trees) - a scheduled fix, not a carve-out

decisions.id: D9c the budget never takes a pool tree's build directory
decisions.summary: the cache budget's eviction skips a registered pool tree's build directory; the pool's share is bounded by cap x tree cache (about 40 GB, GUESS) and given back by builder-tree-drop
decisions.why: a carve-out from the disk budget of T245, but implied by the GM's own words on the build caches (2026-11-22: 'your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken'), and without it the sweep would empty every free pool tree between builders, defeating T285's purpose (handouts cold while called warm). The GM's disk concern ('without us realizing it') is met: the share is bounded and visible in make builder-trees, and drop returns it. Note for the builder: the block does not say whether the low-free-space trigger also skips pool trees; if it does, say so, since that is the place the GM asked for automatic action.

decisions.summary: Rendered guard messages are kept in each tree's own git dir (hooks-test/messages/), found by one resolver (l7r-guard messages store, git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) that both the hooks-test and guard-messages recipes use.
decisions.why: This is the task line's own fix (reproduce with two worktrees, then key the store by tree), and it corrects a defect: a check reading another tree's renderings tells a builder nothing is owed when wordings are owed, or turns red on a guard the tree does not hold.

decisions.summary: dev/guard-messages.tsv, the reviewed record, stays one tracked file.
decisions.why: The reviewed record is tracked content, not run state. Keeping it as one file leaves 451 T170's rule (every rendered wording reviewed or baselined) as it was, and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The tree's store is made to match this run's roster: a file of no suite on the run's list is removed, so a rendering from a guard the tree no longer holds is not judged.
decisions.why: This fixes the second fault the plan found (messages::corpus read every .jsonl in the directory, not the run's roster), which is a check passing or refusing on the wrong input. It is red first in test-parts.3.sh.

decisions.summary: Suite freshness stamps stay shared across worktrees (stamps per tree was priced and not taken). A green job also writes <common dir>/hooks-test/rendered/<job>@<key>.jsonl, and a suite is skipped only where a rendering at its stamp's key exists. A gather step fills a skipped suite's files from that keyed rendering.
decisions.why: This keeps the existing measured saving (commit d7456c4c8d, 5 of 46 suites rerun, 83 s against 151 s) and stops it from defeating the per-tree store. Declining per-tree stamps leaves existing behavior that works as it is. It carves nothing out of the fix, because each tree is still judged on its own content's renderings.

decisions.summary: If a skipped suite's keyed rendering was replaced by another tree's run between the skip and the gather, the run fails by name and names the fix (make hooks-test again, which reruns that suite).
decisions.why: This is a loud, self-healing failure in a narrow race, not a wrong outcome. The run never judges stale or foreign renderings, so the defect the task fixes is not carried forward. Rerunning the suite automatically instead is a design choice, not a fidelity question.

decisions.summary: Each clone's first make hooks-test after landing reruns every suite once (about 160 s, measured 2026-11-26), plus one extra launcher call per run.
decisions.why: This is a one-off cost of the fix, not a narrowing. The plan measured and labeled it.

decisions.summary: scripts/land-alone.sh and scripts/gates/review-tree.sh stop copying the common hooks-test/ into their tree's git dir.
decisions.why: Under the new layout that copy would fill the tree's store with the clone's renderings before the tree's own run, which is the same defect again, so removing it is part of the fix. Note: the search that showed nothing else read the copy (grep -rn hooks-test rust scripts tests) does not cover the Makefile. The plan covers the Makefile's recipe by a separate statement (it reads the stamps from the common directory since d7456c4c8d). Even if a missed reader existed, dropping the copy could only cost reruns, never a wrong verdict.

decisions.summary: Nothing is found and left. The task is classed as not performance work.
decisions.why: No known defect is deferred. The shared-stamp saving is kept rather than added to, so calling it a correctness fix is accurate.

decisions.summary: Synchronize the checks' compiling cargo calls through a counted set of machine-wide flock slots under ~/.cache/l7r-build-slots/, freed when the holder dies, no daemon; the builder count itself is not capped
decisions.why: This is the GM's request as written (2026-11-26): 'address that with some synchronization rather than pre-emptively limiting builders just in case'. A counted lock on the coinciding compiles is that synchronization, and builders past the count queue only for the compile.

decisions.summary: Every cargo call through cargo_in except cargo fmt, plus cover.rs's coverage build, takes a slot; fmt, llvm-cov show-env/report, cargo --version and direct test-binary runs do not
decisions.why: 'That' in the GM's words is the compiles coinciding. Leaving out the calls that do not compile drops nothing the request reaches, and the measurement puts the peaks in coinciding cover-builds.

decisions.summary: L7R_BUILD_SLOTS defaults to 2 (labeled GUESS) and caps compiling calls at once, not builders; 0 means no slot
decisions.why: A semaphore has to have a count. The default comes from the measured peak (three compiles at once, about 15 rustc each on 22 cores) rather than from a builder cap, and the 0 escape and the knob keep it a tunable piece of synchronization, not a pre-emptive limit on builders.

decisions.summary: If the slot directory cannot be made, a slot file cannot be opened or flock cannot start, the call runs without a slot and says so on stderr
decisions.why: Physically impossible case: when the lock primitive is missing there is nothing to synchronize on. The alternatives are refusing, which is a red gate for a throughput control (nothing in request.md asks for that), or hanging. The stderr notice keeps it visible.

decisions.summary: A wait past L7R_BUILD_SLOT_CEILING (900 s, GUESS) runs the call without a slot, written as a slot-wait line of code 1 with an audit reopen on one such line in a week
decisions.why: Purpose ground: the request is for synchronization that lets more builders work, and an endless wait would let one hung cargo stop every tree's checks for good, which defeats that purpose concretely. The plan states the cost, prices the alternatives and names a falsifier. Aside, non-blocking: 'a pass is then one more compile at once, three' holds for a single pass only. Several starved waiters passing at once under four or five builders are not bounded by it; the slot-wait code-1 lines and the audit's reopen are what would show that.

decisions.summary: Cargo started by a holder carries L7R_BUILD_SLOT_HELD, and a gate run under it takes no slot; a call holds one slot and never waits for a second; the run lock is taken first and the slot inside it
decisions.why: This is deadlock avoidance inside the mechanism. The nested run is already counted under its parent's slot, so no compile goes unsynchronized and the request's reach is not narrowed.

decisions.summary: The wrapper's own tool build (scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh build) takes no slot
decisions.why: The bootstrap argument does not hold, because the slot is a flock program call that shell can make. 'Shell, no Phase line' is implementation cost and is no ground either. The one ground that survives is the measurement: where no check's phase ran, the samples top out at 2.6 GiB and 13 rustc, against 5.9-6.4 GiB where coverage builds coincide (measured 2026-11-26). So leaving this build unslotted does not bring back the coincidence the request is about. The limits are real. The figure is joint with the guard build and comes from one three-builder run, and this is a compile whose coincidence still grows with the builder count. The ruling stands on that measurement and falls with it: the plan's own reopen condition (the re-measurement showing one at a peak) is the right trigger, and the candidate it names should be filed if that happens.

decisions.summary: The hook suites' guard build takes no slot
decisions.why: Ruled on its own, on the same and only surviving ground: the measured ceiling of the no-phase samples (2.6 GiB and 13 rustc, measured 2026-11-26) bounds this build too, well below the coinciding-cover-build peaks. Shell-only is cost, not a ground. This ruling also falls with that measurement, and the three- and four-builder re-measurement is what tests it.

decisions.summary: T284's line's re-measurement of three and four code builders with the slot is not done in this task; the coordinating session runs it once the slot has landed, and docs/process-decisions.md records it as owed
decisions.why: Physical ground: measuring several builders 'with it' needs the slot in every builder's tree, which only a landing gives, so the task cannot do it before it lands. FR-009's filed-task-id rule covers deferred defects, and this is not one. But the payoff of the GM's request (builders no longer pre-emptively limited) arrives only with this re-measurement. Landing T284 alone leaves the builder cap of two in place until it is run and recorded.

decisions.summary: A wait writes one Phase line, step slot-wait, read as its own category ('waiting on a build slot', first of PHASE_COLUMNS) in make task-time and make where-time, with a notice each minute naming the holders; a lint, test build or test run's phase spans its wait and the readers subtract it, while a coverage build's slot is taken before its clock starts
decisions.why: This serves the GM's standing 2026-11-22 words: 'we want everything measured so we know where our time goes, especially for compiling'. A new wait that went unbooked would go against that. Where the clock boundary falls is design, and the readers take the wait out.

decisions.summary: Tests run with Slots::off() and the slot's own tests use a scratch directory; a landing's gate takes the same slot as a builder's
decisions.why: The landing's gate is part of what the cap was protecting ('their compiles and a landing's gate would not coincide'), so covering it keeps the request whole. Tests keeping off ~/.cache is hygiene and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Recorded in dev/audits/build-slot.md (measurement, falsifier, cost, alternatives), docs/process-decisions.md and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md; no make target and no guard added
decisions.why: The audit entry with a falsifier answers the GM's 2026-11-25 register words ('what we would look at that would falsify the notion that this is a good idea'). Adding no target or guard adds nothing the request did not ask for.

decisions.summary: The task line's fourth case (the guard-messages store) is left to 451 T281's builder; T295 does three jobs, and goes wider than the line where the same spelling defect sits in other readers (history guard, make detector, ledger, conflict-marker, gate-write, gm-tree).
decisions.why: No GM words name T295; the task line is the coordinating session's. Handing the guard-messages case to T281's builder is, on the block's own claim (not verified here: the bundle holds no T281 text), an assignment to the task that owns it rather than a defect left unowned; widening a defect fix to every reader with the same defect is what fix-as-we-go asks.

decisions.summary: One shared reader (spelled.rs) names a program by its command word's last path part, past a backslash, quotes, VAR= words and wrappers with their options; the name compared whole; command -v/-V and VAR=/path/git are not runs of the program.
decisions.why: Ends a guard passing bad work (a git by its path or behind a wrapper ran past builder-pool and the history guard), which is the 2026-11-19 'real enforcement and not just instructions' and a defect under XIV; reading invocations and not mentions keeps the project's rule.

decisions.summary: gm-tree's git exemption now also covers a git behind A=1 or timeout 5, which the old first-three-letters test refused.
decisions.why: The exemption is for git commands; refusing the same git command because of how its command word is spelled is a check refusing good work, a defect. It does not open any non-git command.

decisions.summary: The one make detector (make.rs, invoked) reads make by its path, a backslash, or behind command/exec/builtin/sudo (with options, and a wrapper by its path); /tmp/mymake and the like stay other programs.
decisions.why: static-runs, the gate guards and no-poll never saw these spellings; FR-007 and FR-008 refusals are only real if the detector reads them.

decisions.summary: Readers that exempt a git command or rule no tree write (claims-file, parked.rs git mv, phase-source, house-style, shell-check) are not changed here; filed in T306, ordered before T302.
decisions.why: None is a tree guard passing a tree write; where an exemption misses a spelling the effect is an extra refusal of a rare spelling. Filed in T306 with an order before T302 (the block's 'lands before T302'), which meets FR-009's why, id and order and fix-as-we-go's 'fixed before the next step', while T306 keeps that order.

decisions.summary: A program run by another (xargs git worktree add, sh -c 'git push -f') is read by no guard of the walk. Filed as T306, lands before T302.
decisions.why: 'Outside three jobs' is not by itself a ground. The ground is that the GM's words and the accepted spec allow a defect to be deferred with a why, a task id and an order (FR-009; fix-as-we-go's 'fixed before the next step's port begins'): the block gives the why (the walk would read another program's argument as a command, a change to what every walk guard sees), names T306 and orders it before T302. Not waived; holds only while T306 lands before T302.

decisions.summary: A quoted "git" passes the history guard and discard, two guards T295 itself edits; their quote blanking runs before the pattern. Filed as T306, lands before T302.
decisions.why: This is D1's own class left in guards this task edits, so it is the weakest of the deferrals, and the block's goal and the test names ('however it is spelled') overstate what those two guards now read. It still carries FR-009's three parts (why: the fix is each guard's own blanking, not the shared reader; T306; before T302), and fix-as-we-go asks for it fixed before the next step, not within this task. Holds only while T306 lands before T302.

decisions.summary: cargo by its path or behind command, exec, sudo or builtin passes make-only and no-poll (FR-008's cargo refusal), their own patterns. Filed as T306, lands before T302.
decisions.why: A different program in different guards, touching FR-008's refusal of a backgrounded cargo run. Deferred with FR-009's why (their own patterns, not the shared reader), id and order before T302, as fix-as-we-go permits. Holds only while T306 lands before T302.

decisions.summary: A name the shell builds ($GIT, g\it) is read by no guard; T306 may only document it in docs/guards.md as a limit. Filed as T306, lands before T302.
