decisions.why: Process order and exits under the project's standing landing rules; nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The report opens with one table of the window (minutes, blocking, each as a percentage of the working time) and one line per landed task; builder minutes are the builder's event-log span.
decisions.why: This is how the report is laid out. It keeps T243's percentages of working time ((i)) and the breakdown the GM asked for. The table and the lines are the coordinating session's task-line words, and they narrow nothing he asked.

decisions.summary: Every make land is a batch keyed (feature, 'second tier: <tasks>'), owned by no task, with one category in the window table and its own section of one line per batch.
decisions.why: This is the GM's second message nearly word for word: 'move batched landing stuff that happens as the second tier of checks into its own separate category rather than counting it against any individual task.' Under the two-tier trial a single-task make land is also the second tier, so keying every landing as a batch matches his words.

decisions.summary: A task's own table ends at its make carry, found through the pool's log. With no carry found it ends where the batch's first attempt starts, a labeled GUESS knob (Batch::from).
decisions.why: This puts the GM's second message into effect: the second tier's time is not counted against a task. The fallback is a stated default of the kind (l) allows ('it doesn't have to be 100% exact'), and it is labeled where it is used.

decisions.summary: GUESS defaults for the second tier's blocking. A gate blocks nothing while any task's own blocking work is in flight. It blocks the batch (never a task) (a) when the session waits on it alone, (b) when it runs in the foreground, and (c) through a repair. A builder dispatched with Blocks: none leaves the gate waited on alone.
decisions.why: Each part was judged on its own. (c) A repair stops the batch from landing until the repair is done, which is (l)'s 'waiting on it to be done before it can be started' exactly. (b) A foreground run holds the session's next step by construction. (a) This is the weakest part: the T303 T305 batch had one green run and no repair, yet 3.9 of its 4.9 min books as blocking, while the GM said 'new tasks beginning is not something that blocks on it.' His third message, though, is an expectation that ends in 'Right?', not a rule that the line must read zero. (l) allows stated defaults at about 90% accuracy. Building his expected answer into the default would rig the instrument to agree with him and defeat its purpose, which is to find where the bottlenecks are. The plan calls the rule a knob and not a target, says what most of the line rests on, and names it the first knob to turn. The first measurement (24.8 of 27.9 min blocking) runs against his expectation and rests on default (a). That is a difference to report, not a defect.

decisions.summary: When a batch's own landing run is in flight, a wait is booked to that run, whatever else in flight ends later. This moves 12.1 min out of wait loops.
decisions.why: This fixes a wrong outcome as it was found. A builder's leftover loop was booked as the cause of a session's wait on a gate. Minutes are unchanged by the fix.

decisions.summary: The task line's four booking faults, and a fifth target name found: a main session's background command under the mark alone belongs to no task; the session's own quick or done goes to the batch whose span holds it; the builder-* targets and make carry get named categories; a carry belongs to the carried task. prewarm is left to T316.
decisions.why: These are the task line's own items, each a stated default. The fifth target (make builder-trees) is the same fault class, fixed as it was found.

decisions.summary: SINCE=last reads the greatest 'until' from an append-only l7r-events/task-time-asked.log. Only a SINCE=last run writes the marker, after its report. With no marker the window is 24 hours and the report says so. The window used is stated on the report's first line.
decisions.why: This is the GM's first message: 'keep track of whenever I last asked, so that I don't have to remember the period.' Only SINCE=last runs write the marker so that the session's own measuring runs, such as this task's --since runs, do not move it. That serves his purpose. A gap is noted to the caller and not ruled: if he names a period himself, that ask is not recorded.

decisions.summary: A carry held behind a running gate and another run's wait for a build slot are not attributed to the gate, and neither is a carried task that no make land has named yet. Two of the three signals the task line names read zero. Filed as T319, lands before T302.
decisions.why: All of the GM's own words are delivered: a category of its own, never counted against a task, its blocking on a line of its own. The three signals appear only in the coordinating session's relay, which request.md marks as 'the coordinating session's, not his'. The missing two cannot be attributed from this report's inputs, because no log line records a carry's refusal or a slot's holder. The deferral takes FR-009's form: why, the filed id, and 'lands before T302', and T302 is the comparison that reads this line. It does not defeat the purpose: the line already reads well above zero, so it is not hiding a bottleneck behind a forced zero.

decisions.summary: The shared event-log reader keeps one start and one stop per agent, so a resumed builder's later spans are dropped and builder minutes read low (8.8 of T289's 13.7). Filed as T324, lands before T302.
decisions.why: None of the GM's three messages, and no part of the T243 request, asks for builder minutes per task. The column is the session's own addition, and the plan states its shortfall where it introduces the column. The defect is in a shared reader that predates this task, and the deferral takes FR-009's form (why, filed id, lands before T302). It narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Wait loops are still 25.6 min of the window's blocking in tasks' own tables. Whether those loops held tasks up must be measured loop by loop first. Filed as T328, lands before T302.
decisions.why: This is a suspicion still to be measured, not a known wrong outcome. The defect that was established, inside a batch, is fixed in this task. It narrows nothing in the T298 request.

decisions.summary: T298 lands before the before-and-after comparison of two-tier checking, which it does not make. The green exit is make builder-checks in the builder's tree, with the full gate at landing. T316 extends columns::category afterwards.
decisions.why: This is ordering and the two-tier trial's exits as docs/process-decisions.md records them. Nothing the GM asked is left out.

decisions.summary: The category names are split out of book.rs into book/cats.rs because book.rs passed the file-scale bar.
decisions.why: This is code layout and carries no fidelity content.

decisions.summary: a warm handout starts, detached, the test builds of the crates whose build moved, so they compile while the builder reads
decisions.why: This is the GM's question of 2026-11-26 ('would it make sense to begin compiling immediately within a work tree builder?') answered in the form T316's line records; measured first, as the project requires.

decisions.id: D2 measured from the tree's last handout (prewarm-base)
decisions.summary: the moved range starts at the commit the tree was last handed out at, not its HEAD; a tree with none on record from where it stood before the handout; a cold tree's first handout starts nothing
decisions.why: Departs from the brief's sketch, not from the GM: a release brings the tree to HEAD, so a HEAD-based range would find nothing moved and defeat the request's purpose. The base is the one that makes 'compile what others landed' happen. A cold tree has nothing warm to extend, and the handout already reports it cold.

decisions.summary: only commits touching rust/ or .cargo/ start anything; each crate whose build reads a changed file, through Kept::reads_any, fewest dependencies first
decisions.why: This picks out the crates the request is about. Building them in dependency order is how the mechanism works and narrows nothing.

decisions.id: D4 the same build as a real run's
decisions.summary: cargo test --no-run per crate through cargo_call (now shared with cargo_in), the tree's own target dir; nothing run, no result kept
decisions.why: A pre-warm only helps if its build is the one a real run then finds fresh. Measured: 7.7 s to 0.1 s for the first test build after the core crate moved. Keeping no result keeps a kept result a real run's alone, so the gate is untouched.

decisions.summary: it takes a slot only when a second is free beside it, never queues, kills its cargo group and rebuilds later once none is spare; builds nothing at L7R_BUILD_SLOTS=1, builds freely at 0
decisions.why: This narrows 'begin compiling immediately' to when a slot is spare, which on the two-slot machine means both slots free, and it covers two cases. (a) Two or more slots: the ruling rests on the GM's T284 words ('address that with some synchronization rather than pre-emptively limiting builders'). Those words make real compiles of any tree the thing the slots serve, and a pre-warm holding the last free slot would make a real compile wait behind speculative work. The block shows the yield live against a slot held by hand, but a real compile of another tree starting beside a pre-warm is shown only by the test. How often a handout finds a spare slot is not measured. The earlier waiter's-mark form was measured holding a slot while two real runs waited 39.3 s and 25.2 s, and was replaced. (b) One slot (L7R_BUILD_SLOTS=1): the pre-warm builds nothing. Its only slot would be the one every real compile needs, so building would break the same T284 synchronization. This is a knob setting, not this machine's two slots.

decisions.id: D6 ended by a real run in its tree
decisions.summary: a live member of the tree's run lock ends the pre-warm
decisions.why: The builder's own run takes over the build. The pre-warm exists to serve that run, so it gives way to it. Measured live nine times.

decisions.summary: never waited on by the handout, own process group, logged to prewarm.log, exits 0, one per tree, ceiling 900 s (GUESS, L7R_PREWARM_CEILING), POLL 0.5 s (GUESS), off at L7R_PREWARM=0
decisions.why: These are the safety limits of a speculative background build. The knobs are labeled GUESS and recorded in the audit register (the GM's T259 register asks for this). Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.id: D8 booked apart; task-time category deferred to T317
decisions.summary: each cargo call writes a prewarm Phase line booked to no call; make task-time does not yet show it as a category, filed T317, lands before T302
decisions.why: The GM asked that everything be measured (2026-11-22) and that the breakdown name every minute (2026-11-25 (c)). The seconds ARE measured, one Phase line per cargo call in the event log. Booking them to no call is correct, because a detached run is no builder call's compile, and charging it to one would misstate the breakdown. Only the report's reading of them by task is deferred. That is the measure crate's readers' work, filed under FR-009's form with its order before T302. The measuring the GM asked for is not removed.

decisions.id: D9 the lint's build not warmed; T318
decisions.summary: only the test build is warmed; clippy's build (4.8 s for land on the measured handout) is filed as T318, lands before T302
decisions.why: The GM's word is 'compiling', and the lint compiles too, so this narrows it. It is a sequencing, not a carve-out. It is filed with its order before T302 and kept in scope, and the stated reason is measured: a second build per crate doubles how long the pre-warm holds a slot, which runs into the T284 synchronization the GM asked for. Measuring first is the project's rule. Leaving it is not a wrong outcome, since the first lint compiles as it did before this task.

decisions.id: D10 one red test run in nine; T329
decisions.summary: one of nine real runs that ended a pre-warm failed in its tests (code 101, build green) and passed on rerun; its output was not kept and eight further tries did not repeat it; filed T329, lands before T302
decisions.why: A possible red run on good work would be a defect, so leaving it needs a ruling. The cause is not known: the block names the killed cargo, the guard's rebuild under the suite and the land suite itself, and none is excluded. The ground is impossibility. Fixing needs a cause, and there is none to act on: the output was not kept, and eight further tries, three by the same recipe, did not reproduce it. What can be done now is to reproduce it with its output kept, and that is the filed T329. It carries its order before T302, so under the FIX AS WE GO rule and the GM's T104 priority on tests that fail good work, it is fixed before the work moves on, not left.

decisions.id: D11 a pre-warm ended early leaves crates unbuilt; T330
decisions.summary: prewarm-base is written when the pre-warm starts, so crates a cut-short pre-warm never built are not counted at the next handout; filed T330, lands before T302
decisions.why: In one case a builder's first run still compiles crates others moved, so this narrows the request's purpose. The block states, by its mechanism, that this is no worse than no pre-warm: those crates are compiled by the builder's own run, as before this task. That is a smaller gain, not a wrong outcome. The fix (writing the base when a pre-warm finishes) is named and filed under FR-009's form with its order before T302.

decisions.summary: dev/audits/builder-prewarm.md (measurement, falsifier, cost), rustc/task rows of rust/gate/CLAUDE.md, builder-tree help; tagged [perf] under FR-013; performance-checklist not applied (not engine speed); exits by the first tier here and the full gate in the clone
decisions.why: The audit entry is what the GM's T259 register asks for. The [perf] tag is FR-013's definition (it makes the builders' loop faster). The exits are the project's two tiers.

decisions.summary: This section is one part of T308 (the plan review's later rounds). The two tiers, the batch gate, the trial's measurement and the coverage run stay open on the task's box, which is not ticked from this landing.
decisions.why: Nothing of T308 is dropped: the remainder is named and stays open on the task. Splitting a task's landings is scheduling. It does not narrow the GM's two-tier words (2026-11-26) or the approved improvement 4, 'Fewer plan re-rounds' (2026-11-19 approval).

decisions.summary: Every later round is classed (a)-(e) from the round before it, before any rule is written. The record is kept under dev/measurements/2026-11-26/plan-review-rounds/.
decisions.why: This serves the request directly. The GM asked for actual numbers before process changes ('I'd like to see some actual numbers', 2026-11-19) and wants everything measured (2026-11-22). The class counts sum to the heading's 56 rounds and to its 169 minutes (169.1, rounded). T285's move from (d) to (a) is carried through the table and the 'root of 8' sentence (4+2+2).

decisions.summary: make decide refuses a task whose box line quotes words after 'the GM' that request.md does not hold, and names the heading to append them under. MIN_WORDS=4 and REACH=80 are GUESS knobs. It runs at make decide only, not at plan-delta.
decisions.why: It removes a measured mechanical cause of later rounds (class b, the GM's words missing) at decide, before dispatch. That is what improvement 4 and T308's line ask. Running it at decide only is design: the rule is per task line, and plan-delta reads blocks. The rule was replayed over the reviewed sections before it was kept, which is constraint 2.

decisions.summary: Replayed over 77 tasks, the rule refuses 11. 6 are true, 3 are the replay's artifact, and 2 (T241, T235) are refusals that no review raised. The 2 are accepted, cured by one edit each.
decisions.why: These 2 are not refusals of good work. Each line attributes quoted words to the GM that his recorded request does not hold. The GM's T233 section (2026-11-24) says a ruling attributed to him names his recorded words: 'I never made a ruling that ... That was never at any point something that I said'. Its audit counted 74 of 180 such attributions as the defect. A quote with no record behind it is that defect, whether or not a review happened to raise it. So refusing it enforces the GM's own standing rule, and the cure is to record the words or correct the line. This is not a check refusing correct work under constitution XIV, so it needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: The figure lint reads a k/K/M-suffixed numeral and a rounded figure with a unit ('20-odd minutes') as figures. A threshold's suffixed numeral ('past 300k tokens') stays a limit.
decisions.why: It removes a measured cause of NOT-REVIEWABLE rounds (class b). The threshold reading keeps the lint from refusing correct work, since a stated limit is not a count. It is not an exception to anything the GM asked. In the replay, each form flags one sentence over the 124 sections.

decisions.summary: decide's notice states the verdict-voiding rule as the code has it. For an uncommitted reviewed section, any edit voids the verdict. For a committed one, typo-scale edits are kept. An edit during review gets its record refused. The notice refuses nothing.
decisions.why: It serves the section's goal that 'a builder knows before it dispatches which edits will cost it another round'. A test found the earlier wording false, and it was made true. It describes a rule the plan gate already enforces, so there is no enforcement to add (the GM's 'real enforcement and not just instructions', 2026-11-19, is not engaged).

decisions.summary: A CLEAR is voided by a typo-scale edit of a section not yet committed. That tolerance is not built here. It is filed as T337 and lands before T302.
decisions.why: This is a found defect: a needless round in a builder's tree. It pre-existed this part and was found by this part's own test, not introduced by it. Nothing the GM asked for leaves the feature. It is filed in this feature in FR-009's own deferral form, with why, the T337 id and 'lands before T302'. The GM endorsed filing found defects and bundling them ('not bother cutting back on new tasks filed', 2026-11-22). The convergence rules (2026-11-23), that only a claim-changing edit triggers review, govern page and pop-up cascades. The plan gate already applies that idea to committed sections, and T337 extends it on schedule. The 'fix all known bugs in each step' rule (2026-11-18) is about port steps, and the order 'before T302' honors it anyway. So this is not a narrowing that needs a ruling.

decisions.summary: NOT built: a digest over decisions rather than the section. None of the 132 sections marks a decision line. At most 5 of the 16 (c) rounds (6.1 min) changed no decision. A prose-tolerant digest could keep a verdict across a changed decision.
decisions.why: The GM never asked for a decision digest. It was a candidate in the coordinating session's build. It is declined on measurement: no machine-readable decision line exists. It is also declined because building it would break feature 375's standing promise that a decision cannot change under a kept verdict. The decision not to build is recorded with its reopening condition, which honors the GM's 'record decisions about what NOT to implement' (2026-11-25, T259).

decisions.summary: NOT built: reading 'N of M' as a count. In the replay it flags 47 sentences in 26 of the 124 sections, and reviews objected to 1.
decisions.why: A rule that refuses 46 sentences the reviews accepted would refuse good work, so dropping it after the replay is within the request. The GM did not ask for this pattern, and the decline is recorded in the plan with its measurement.

decisions.summary: The T55 order notice tells a builder (agent_id present) to run make builder-checks first and names the closing run as the other tier's. A builder-checks run since the last edit silences it. The main session is told what it was told before. It stays a notice, and the hook suite gains cases that render it.
decisions.why: It serves the GM's two-tier words: 'the correct place for that level of rigor is checking whether something in the session clone can land back in the main checkout'. Until now the notice told a first-tier builder to start the run its brief forbids. The closing run's rigor is enforced at the session clone's gates, so the notice adds no refusal that the 'real enforcement' words would require. The new hook-suite cases only make the new wording visible to guard-messages, which is enforcement of what was asked, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Three of the six GM's-words rounds cited him by reference, which D1 cannot see. It is left, filed as T333, and lands before T302.
decisions.why: It is a different class from D1's quoted span on the line: a reference to a record the bundle does not carry. So one argument is not stretched over two unlike things. It stays inside the feature, filed in FR-009's form (why, id, order), and the GM endorsed filing found work (2026-11-22). Nothing the GM asked leaves the feature.

decisions.summary: After T289, before T308's remainder and T302. One landing. Green: the new tests green and red with the rules off, plus builder-checks on both crates. Red: recorded and set down, with a claim that it cannot be done sent to the arbiter.
decisions.why: This is scheduling and exits, and nothing of the request is narrowed. The red-first counts and the items not seen red are stated. Those are test quality, not fidelity.

decisions.summary: A quoted or backticked phrase that is the subject of 'does/did ask you' is blanked with its verb before spans are blanked; the session's own 'I do ask you' still fires.
decisions.why: T282: a report describing an ask's wording was read as an ask. Removing a statement the detector misread serves the GM's 2026-11-26 words ('I would prefer not to see these messages about false positives') and FR-002's narrow detector. The rule is bounded by the span, and the true-ask twin is pinned. Nothing FR-002 or amendment 1 owes the filter is exempted.

decisions.summary: The '?' rule skips a last sentence running from 'asks:'/'asks whether'/'asks if' to its '?' with no you/your and no other '?' on the line.
decisions.why: It removes the check-described-by-its-question false firing from the corpus. Four twins that put something to him still fire and are pinned, including a reported question addressed to 'you' and a second question on the line. Only statements leave the detector's reach.

decisions.summary: The '?' rule skips items of a 2+ item all-'?' list under a lead-in naming a checklist, or naming what something has/asks/holds/lists/poses/carries/answers, when the lead-in names neither the GM nor the session.
decisions.why: It removes the listed-checklist false firing. Lists put to him all still fire and are pinned: 'Two questions for you:', 'Open questions:', 'I have two questions...', a mixed list, a single item, no lead-in, and question-word items with suite case 9 kept. This is precision on statements and does not narrow FR-002's asks.

decisions.summary: 'waiting (on|for) you' is a measurement when a time count or share is the past-tense subject of was/were and the clause ends or goes on to another figure.
decisions.why: It removes the two time-breakdown figure firings. Work put to him ('Two hours of review are waiting on you', 'waiting on your budget answer', present tense, count of things) still fires and is pinned in the Rust test. It is bounded on both sides.

decisions.summary: 'with waiting on you kept/counted/... separate/apart/...' names a breakdown category.
decisions.why: It removes the 'Blocking minutes, with waiting on you kept separate:' firing. The twins 'Two tasks are waiting on you, kept separate below.' and 'with waiting on you: the budget's words.' still fire. It reaches statements only.

decisions.summary: STATED's 'needs your words' becomes 'words?' so 'What needs your word: ...' is caught; pinned in both suites.
decisions.why: This is a widening: a true ask HEAD's guard passed (a check passing bad work, a defect). Fixing it enforces FR-002 and narrows nothing. It was measured on both corpora: no T235 firing changes, and one already-firing message's quoted line moves.

decisions.summary: Both refusals gain 'If the line puts nothing to him (offers him nothing), go on and say nothing of this to him.'; reviewed by message-check.
decisions.why: This sentence directly carries 'I just don't want to see the explanation of the false positives reach me'. FR-002's obligation attaches only to a message that asks or puts a decision to him, and amendment 1 adds offers. A line that puts nothing to him owed the filter nothing, so 'go on' restates FR-002's scope and is no carve-out from it. The GM's words take as given that sessions recognize false firings; what he struck is their explanation reaching him. Goal item 1 keeps every true ask refused until filtered. The new wording went to message-check (T170).

decisions.summary: The restated morning offer still fires; recognizing an ad-hoc escalation-check's kept verdict needs a new record and is filed as T335, landing before T302.
decisions.why: Under FR-002 the firing is arguably not false. The GM wrote after the 08:10Z ad-hoc check, so 'no escalation-check dispatched since his last message' holds. The restatement is an offer (amendment 1) in new words, and no gm-review.jsonl row records it as kept. Read most harshly as a residual false firing, it is one of 13, which 'I am okay with some number of false positives' covers. It is filed with an id, an order and the reason it is not fixed here (FR-009).

decisions.summary: The GM's question is answered with the measured rate, 33% before and 8% after on the 28 firings with no T lost, against 'under about one false firing in five'.
decisions.why: It answers 'it probably is worth asking whether the number of false positives is within ... an acceptable range' with numbers he can judge. The one-in-five threshold comes from the coordinating session's brief, not from the GM. The plan names it as 'the brief's aim' and does not attribute it to him, so the range stays his to accept. The plan also states that a firings-only corpus cannot show a newly dropped ask, and points to the pinned bounds instead.

decisions.summary: suite_tools::messages masks the quoted second line after a 'QUESTION UNFILTERED:'/'OFFER UNFILTERED:' head, so each refused suite case is not a new guard message.
decisions.why: T282's defect: each refused suite case created a new message key to review. The mask covers only the quoted user text under the two heads. The refusals' own wording is still keyed, so a change to it is still reviewed (451 T170), and no other message's key moves. A red-with-the-mask-off test pins it.

decisions.summary: A rust-lld link failure after the pool tree's pre-warm is filed as T336, landing before T302, to be reproduced first.
decisions.why: This build-tooling defect lies outside this section's request (T316's pre-warm). It is filed with an id, an order and the reason it is not fixed here, so nothing asked of T299 or T282 is left undone.

decisions.summary: The plan shows no ask is lost with two firings-only corpora (the 28 of 2026-11-25/26 and T235's labeled 112) through the fixed guard, plus pinned true-ask twins for every rule, and does not run a fresh recall sample.
decisions.why: FR-002 (429) asks for a detector measured for hit rate, a sample of hits, and recall on an independently labeled sample. Rules (a)-(e) only remove firings; the needs-your-word change only adds them. So any ask the new rules drop would have fired on HEAD, and the two corpora cover HEAD's firings in their windows. All 12 T of the two-day corpus and all 74 T and 8 B of T235's independently labeled corpus still fire. Asks outside those windows are covered by the bounded twins pinned in both suites, and the block states that limit itself. On the two-day corpus the builder's labels are not independent. I relabeled the five F lines the block quotes from the line alone and agree each is a statement (a report of a hook's reading, a check described by its question, a checklist item listed, two time figures). The whole messages are not in the bundle. This keeps FR-002's measured-detector standard and does not narrow it.

A line that puts nothing to him owed the filter nothing, so 'go on' restates FR-002's scope and is no carve-out from it. The GM's words take as given that sessions recognize false firings; what he struck is their explanation reaching him. Goal item 1 keeps every true ask refused until filtered. The new wording went to message-check (T170).

decisions.summary: The restated morning offer still fires; recognizing an ad-hoc escalation-check's kept verdict needs a new record and is filed as T335, landing before T302.
decisions.why: Under FR-002 the firing is arguably not false. The GM wrote after the 08:10Z ad-hoc check, so 'no escalation-check dispatched since his last message' holds. The restatement is an offer (amendment 1) in new words, and no gm-review.jsonl row records it as kept. Read most harshly as a residual false firing, it is one of 13, which 'I am okay with some number of false positives' covers. It is filed with an id, an order and the reason it is not fixed here (FR-009).

decisions.summary: The GM's question is answered with the measured rate, 33% before and 8% after on the 28 firings with no T lost, against 'under about one false firing in five'.
decisions.why: It answers 'it probably is worth asking whether the number of false positives is within ... an acceptable range' with numbers he can judge. The one-in-five threshold comes from the coordinating session's brief, not from the GM. The plan names it as 'the brief's aim' and does not attribute it to him, so the range stays his to accept. The plan also states that a firings-only corpus cannot show a newly dropped ask, and points to the pinned bounds instead.

decisions.summary: suite_tools::messages masks the quoted second line after a 'QUESTION UNFILTERED:'/'OFFER UNFILTERED:' head, so each refused suite case is not a new guard message.
decisions.why: T282's defect: each refused suite case created a new message key to review. The mask covers only the quoted user text under the two heads. The refusals' own wording is still keyed, so a change to it is still reviewed (451 T170), and no other message's key moves. A red-with-the-mask-off test pins it.

decisions.summary: A rust-lld link failure after the pool tree's pre-warm is filed as T336, landing before T302, to be reproduced first.
decisions.why: This build-tooling defect lies outside this section's request (T316's pre-warm). It is filed with an id, an order and the reason it is not fixed here, so nothing asked of T299 or T282 is left undone.

decisions.summary: The plan shows no ask is lost with two firings-only corpora (the 28 of 2026-11-25/26 and T235's labeled 112) through the fixed guard, plus pinned true-ask twins for every rule, and does not run a fresh recall sample.
decisions.why: FR-002 (429) asks for a detector measured for hit rate, a sample of hits, and recall on an independently labeled sample. Rules (a)-(e) only remove firings; the needs-your-word change only adds them. So any ask the new rules drop would have fired on HEAD, and the two corpora cover HEAD's firings in their windows. All 12 T of the two-day corpus and all 74 T and 8 B of T235's independently labeled corpus still fire. Asks outside those windows are covered by the bounded twins pinned in both suites, and the block states that limit itself. On the two-day corpus the builder's labels are not independent. I relabeled the five F lines the block quotes from the line alone and agree each is a statement (a report of a hook's reading, a check described by its question, a checklist item listed, two time figures). The whole messages are not in the bundle. This keeps FR-002's measured-detector standard and does not narrow it.

decisions.summary: a new read-only make task-progress showing held trees' builders, landings in flight, page sessions, review agents, free trees and staged tasks; no booking rule and no make task-time output changed
decisions.why: The GM asked (request.md, 2026-11-26, 451 T293) that 'we should be able to see while a task is in progress where the time is going'. A read-only view in the landed report's own categories does exactly that and changes nothing he did not ask to change.

decisions.summary: the code is a submodule of task_time with its own subcommand
decisions.why: Where code lives. No request text bears on it.

decisions.summary: a builder's minutes come from the landed report's booking run over its family alone, summed over every key by category
decisions.why: It shows where the time is going in the same categories the task time breakdown (T243) uses, with no second booking that could drift from it.

decisions.summary: one block per held pool tree, then one per running builder no tree is held for
decisions.why: It shows the tasks in progress, including a builder that has stopped while it waits on its plan review. The method is labeled an observation with its method.

decisions.summary: RUNNING is two tests (no stop or own lines after it, and named inflight by the latest Stop or later than it)
decisions.why: It decides which work is in progress. The measured case is labeled. A Stop that predates the field is taken as running, so the view shows more rather than less.

decisions.summary: the step now is the open make run with its last finished phase; the phase running now sits in the run's category until its line lands, and the header says so
decisions.why: It departs from the coordinating session's task line, not from the GM's words, which ask where the time is going and never ask for the open phase. The running phase's minutes are still shown, in their run's category, so no time drops out of the view, and the output states its limit. The plan's reason for adding no start marker is a cost reason, but no ruling is owed because nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: an open call is closed at the moment of the view by a line made in memory, never written
decisions.why: Mechanism. It lets the existing booking count in-progress time, which is what the request asks to see.

decisions.summary: the model turn open now is a row of its own, its tool not yet known
decisions.why: The open turn's time is named rather than dropped, consistent with the breakdown's rule that every minute is named (T243 amendment (c)).

decisions.summary: context is read live from the transcript by the context-cap guard's reader, else from the stop line's ctx, else said to be not known, each figure naming its source
decisions.why: It is extra information about a task in progress, with its sources stated. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: a pool tree's Phase lines are re-tasked from builder-pool.log, and runs are tied by clone (a workaround for the open T332)
decisions.why: It makes the view assign time to the right task where the shared writer would mislabel it. The workaround is stated openly and the writer's defect is filed as T332.

decisions.summary: a resumed builder is shown RUNNING on the in-flight test alone, its minutes headed AT LEAST (a workaround for the open T324)
decisions.why: The view states a floor and says that it is a floor, and that the builder may have stopped again. That matches the GM's 'broad understanding of where our time goes' and 'doesn't have to be 100% exact' (T243 (l)). The event-log reader's limit is shared with every report and is filed as T324, landing before T22.

decisions.summary: a landing in flight is an open session make land run that passes the in-flight test; its tasks come from tiers::batches, its phase is the last finished land Phase, its minutes are the same booking
decisions.why: It shows a landing in progress and where its time is going. The fallback names the landing by its call's task rather than dropping it.

decisions.summary: staged is each task's latest carry with no landed batch after it and no landing in flight
decisions.why: Part of what is in progress. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: a page session is one line (the run log since the read-back without ALL DONE, the brief it is in, how many briefs have ended) with no minutes by category; the categories are deferred to T350, filed to land before T22
decisions.why: Of all request.md's text, only the coordinating session's task line puts page sessions, broken down like a builder, in this view (request.md line 355: 'what it lists' is the session's). The GM's words ask where a task in progress spends its time. In the landed breakdown, a page session is one category of a task's time ('research and page sessions', T243), not a family broken down by category. So one line showing that a page session is running and how far it has got gives at least the granularity the GM's existing breakdown gives. The deferral departs from the session's own line, not from the GM's request. The build-cost reason given would not carry a narrowing, but no ruling is owed. The fuller breakdown is filed (T350) with an order.

decisions.summary: the read-back is the earliest held tree's take or BACK_H (GUESS 2.0 h, a knob), whichever is earlier; AT= gives a past moment
decisions.why: A labeled GUESS knob with an override. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: the minutes shown are machine minutes; blocking minutes are not shown in the live view; the header says a block's minutes can pass its clock
decisions.why: The GM's T293 words ask 'where the time is going'. In T243 he separated that (the minutes and percentage spent doing a thing) from the minutes spent blocking on it. The live view answers the first. Blocking stays in the landed make task-time, which T293 leaves untouched, so nothing the GM was given is taken away. The header states the limit.

decisions.summary: landings() kept the earliest of two carries on a held tree's block; it now keeps the latest, pinned by a test that was red before the fix
decisions.why: It fixes a wrong outcome in this command's own build half, found by its test. That is fix-as-we-go and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: the Makefile's .PHONY line ran task-progress and land-batch together; it is split so both are phony
decisions.why: A defect fix in the build half's own edit.

decisions.summary: a resumed builder's later start and stop lines are not read (the shared event-log reader); filed T324, lands before T22
decisions.why: A defect of the shared reader that every report uses, not of this command's new code. The view says so on its output. It carries a reason, a filed id and an order (FR-009).

decisions.summary: a Phase line written from a pool tree can name another task; this view re-tasks it, make task-time does not; filed T332, lands before T22
decisions.why: The defect belongs to the build tools' writer and the landed report. This view works around it in the open. Filed with a reason and an order.

decisions.summary: make task-time books the gap between a builder's stop and its resumed next line as the builder's model turn; filed T345, lands before T22
decisions.why: A defect of the landed report, outside this read-only view's scope, found and filed with a reason and an order. T293 changes no booking, as its approach states.

decisions.summary: a carry is booked to the task that took the tree in the carry's last second, so the staged list can name the wrong task (seen: T308 for T301's carry); filed T346, lands before T22
decisions.why: A wrong-outcome defect in the shared tiers::carries booking, which the landed batch tables also use. It is not new behavior of this view. Fixing it changes make task-time's tables, which belongs to a task of its own. It is filed with a reason and an order, and it lands inside the feature.

decisions.summary: a compound command is named by its first make target alone (book::run_cat, shared with the landed report); filed T348, lands before T22
decisions.why: Shared naming behavior of the landed report, which the view inherits. Within the GM's 'broad understanding ... doesn't have to be 100% exact' (T243 (l)). Filed with a reason and an order.

decisions.summary: a page session has no minutes by category; filed T350, lands before T22
decisions.why: See T293-D13. It departs from the coordinating session's line, not from the GM's words. Filed with a reason and an order.

decisions.summary: a builder's background run whose shell died silently stays listed as in the background, and one ending during the read is dropped from its builder's line; filed T349, lands before T22
decisions.why: An edge case of this view's own output with no in-flight list to test against. It is transient or rare, and the run is still shown or ends within seconds. It does not misstate where a task's time has gone in its categories, and it sits within the GM's 90%-correct tolerance (T243 (l)). Filed with a reason and an order.

decisions.summary: T315 is a measurement only: no code changed, scripts and raw results kept in dev/measurements/2026-11-26/test-run-split/.
decisions.why: The GM's words (request.md, 2026-11-26, T315) are a why-question: 'more of the compilation was not able to be cached'. Measuring and answering it is what was asked; his 2026-11-20 words make a measurement task a performance task in its own right.

decisions.summary: Answers the caching question: the build is cached as far as it can be, a one-line edit rebuilds in 1-3 s (rustc start, incremental cache read and binary rewrite, not the edit; probe-link and e2 rows); T305's slow runs were builds (first build after a handout, load) and now a build-slot queue, not tests.
decisions.why: Directly answers his words about compilation caching with this task's own measurements (probe-link rows, e2 rows, body-edit.sh, T305's own event-log Phase lines). The compile-cache ceiling also cites T301 part 1, which is not in the bundle and was not checked here; the block's own figures carry the answer without it.

decisions.summary: The recorded build medians (3-8x a one-line edit alone) are not split into own-edit, first-build-after-landings and beside-other-builds, because the event log does not record which.
decisions.why: A stated limit of the data, labeled as such, not a narrowing of the question: the answer to 'why not cached' still stands on the alone measurements and T305's own lines, and the first-build cause is T316's subject (already a GM-asked task).

decisions.summary: No load generator and no concurrent copies of a suite (the brief, after the host freeze, feature 460); one run at a time; nothing T301 part 1 or T316 measured is re-measured.
decisions.why: Tested against purpose: T305's runs were under load, and the block still covers loaded behavior from T305's own event-log Phase lines, the 2026-11-25/26 phase history (57-104 lines a crate) and body-edit.sh at load 25-28 beside real builders. Not re-measuring prior tasks' figures narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: The section also splits the tests' own run (which tests start git or programs, what a run writes, sampled TMPDIR peaks) per the brief's part 2 and gives feature 460 its /dev/shm size figure.
decisions.why: Widens, does not narrow: measurement only, no behavior added, and it serves the GM's question of where T305's repeated test runs spent their seconds. Feature 460's figure is that feature's own ask, recorded as one pointer line.

decisions.summary: Seven levers priced and given NO task: /dev/shm TMPDIR, empty git template, shared fixture repository, thread count, faster linker, check-only pass, smaller crate.
decisions.why: Each priced by a labeled measurement or a citation and found worth under about 1 s a run; none is a defect (no wrong outcome), so declining to build them leaves nothing the GM asked undone.

decisions.summary: Running only the tests a change reaches filed as T342, first step a measurement of its saving under load.
decisions.why: A new option of a command, out of a measurement's brief; filed with reason, id and order ('lands before T302'), the FR-009 form.

decisions.summary: rust/guard/shared's idle test waits 8.06 s of real time, the suite's whole wall; filed as T339, lands before T302.
decisions.why: A speed cost in test code, not a wrong outcome; the measurement builder was not briefed to change test code and the fix needs its own red-first proof. FR-009 form complete: why, id, order. T302 itself not checked (outside the bundle).

decisions.summary: rust/guard tests leave sleep 5 processes holding the output pipe 3.2 s past the binary's exit; filed as T340, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Leftover processes are arguably a defect; deferred with why (the tests that start them not yet found, the pin belongs with the fix), id and order, per FR-009. A measurement task carrying it to a filed, ordered task is within; no GM words require a measurement task to fix what it finds.

decisions.summary: The checks' tool spends 2.0 s on one thread before an edited guard crate's build; filed as T341, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Speed cost whose site is unmeasured (perf and strace refused); FR-009 form complete.

decisions.summary: Every Phase line of the pool tree since 14:00 UTC carries task T285, so make task-time books T284/T305/T104/T316/T315's seconds to T285; filed as T344, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Unlike the others this is a wrong outcome (time booked to the wrong task), a true defect in builder-tree and the event log, outside this measurement's brief. It is not left: it is filed with why, id and an order that lands it before the next work (FR-009). Within.

decisions.summary: A builder's build waits up to 57.3 s for one of two build slots (451 T284); filed as T347 to retune the slot count from a measurement, lands before T302.
decisions.why: The slot is T284's GM-asked synchronization; retuning its count is a knob change needing its own measurement. FR-009 form complete.

decisions.summary: /dev/shm being noexec and 62.5 MB, and a land test run rebuilding l7r-gate inside its test phase once, are recorded as not defects and not filed.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome: /dev/shm is unused, and the rebuild moves seconds rather than adding them; tests reading live machine state are cited to 451 T312 and T143 (not checked, outside the bundle). Constitution XIV: a difference that works is not a defect.

decisions.summary: T315 counted as performance work for scheduling.
decisions.why: The GM's own words, 2026-11-20: 'I would also like for this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first.'

decisions.summary: samples under l7r-events/samples/ rather than the brief's l7r-events/mem-samples.jsonl; a consequence disclosed: state-push skips the folder, so samples stay on the container
decisions.why: The path is the coordinating session's brief, not the GM's words (the bundle holds neither the task line nor the brief, so this was judged against request.md and the spec only). The task line's 'into the tree's l7r-events' holds. The GM's tooling-state repository (2026-11-25) is for 'record-check answers and event logs'; samples are neither, and no GM sentence asks for memory samples to be kept off the container. The reason (readers that take every .jsonl there as a feature log) was read from code and labeled as such.

decisions.summary: a module of the measure crate; task gains no dependency
decisions.why: Placement; nothing the GM asked turns on it.

decisions.summary: the sampler writes and re-reads its own pid file; two starts converge on one; stop is a file removal
decisions.why: Mechanism for the one-a-clone constraint; its one cost (a duplicated line for at most one interval) is stated.

decisions.summary: alive is pid plus start time; a zombie is dead
decisions.why: Mechanism.

decisions.summary: setsid, null streams, inherited descriptors close-on-exec
decisions.why: Serves 'never failing a handout' (no handout waits on a pipe or holds a build slot's flock); measured once, labeled.

decisions.summary: a second start exits 0
decisions.why: Mechanism for asking at every handout.

decisions.summary: ends at a 4 MiB bound; the next start moves the file to mem-samples.1.jsonl, keeping at most two files
decisions.why: Bounded in size as the brief says, and bounded on disk in line with the GM's 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-25 words on cleaning up after ourselves. The rotation keeps sampling from stopping silently. Figures checked: 18,036/65 = 277 B a line, 4 MiB / 277 B x 10 s = about 42 h, 4,320 lines about 1.2 MB.

decisions.summary: each line carries max, cores and peak; the report checks itself against memory.peak
decisions.why: Gives the audit entry its falsifier, which the GM asked for in the register (2026-11-25: 'what we would look at that would falsify').

decisions.summary: median and nearest-rank 95th percentile, labeled CONVENTION
decisions.why: Chosen to reproduce the recorded hand-log figures; labeled, as the 2026-11-23 talk on labels asks.

decisions.summary: stall and OOM rises booked between consecutive samples; GAP_S 120 s, a GUESS knob
decisions.why: Arithmetic of the report, with its knob labeled.

decisions.summary: the report's rows are pool trees HELD, not builders compiling; refinement deferred as T351, lands before T302
decisions.why: This narrows the purpose in the heading (certifying the builder count against memory): the block itself says a row for N trees held cannot certify N builders compiling and reads low on memory. Ruled on purpose, not wording. (1) The purpose the task exists for, samples taken without a hand-started loop so a three- or four-at-once batch is never unsampled again, is delivered in full. (2) What is deferred is how stored samples are attributed to rows. The fix named is a join with the event log's Phase lines, so a later reader can re-book the same stored samples; nothing is lost at sampling time. (3) The report prints the caveat and its rustc column, so no row silently claims to certify a compiling count. (4) The deferral has the form FR-009 asks for (why it is not fixed here, a filed id T351, an order 'lands before T302'), the GM-approved form for a deferral. Not verifiable from the bundle: what T302 is, whether T351 is an open unticked task, and whether the samples outlive T351's landing given D7's two-file rotation (about 84 h) and D1's samples staying on the container. make decide's open-task test covers the second.

decisions.summary: CPU stall read from /proc/pressure/cpu, which may be the host's and not the cgroup's; not compared
decisions.why: The brief names that file, and the certification is against memory, not CPU stall. The premise is unmeasured but stated plainly, and it is not a defect of the memory figures the task certifies. Noted for the audit entry rather than ruled.

decisions.summary: knobs: L7R_MEM_MARGIN_GIB 7 (GUESS), L7R_SAMPLE_MAX_H 12 (GUESS), L7R_SAMPLE_S 10 (the hand loop's interval)
decisions.why: Bounded in hours as the brief says; each guess is labeled beside its constant, in the help and in the audit entry.

decisions.summary: asks after any handout that exits 0; a sampler failure is a line, never the exit code; L7R_SAMPLER=0 opts out; a cold handout's guard compile runs before the start, so on a clone's first handout it goes unsampled
decisions.why: 'Never failing a handout' is the constraint. The goal is sampling while builders HOLD trees, and during a cold handout's guard build no builder holds that tree yet. The unsampled first compile is stated. It is a gap in a reading, not a wrong outcome of the memory certification at N concurrent builders: on the first handout of a clone no sampler-covered batch is yet running.

decisions.summary: the sampler writes no Phase line and no event-log line
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-22 'we want everything measured so we know where our time goes' is about the time a task's work takes. A background monitor spends no task's time; its cost is measured separately (0.9 ms a sample, 7.2 MiB resident).

decisions.summary: the samples folder is made once at loop start, never on append
decisions.why: Keeps a deleted clone from being recreated, which serves the GM's clean-up words of 2026-11-25.

decisions.summary: sampler_words split out as its own function so its test does not depend on the test runner's environment
decisions.why: Testability, serving the brief's 100% line coverage.

decisions.summary: not built: no signal handler (a bare TERM leaves a stale pid file, which the next start replaces), and no test starts the real detached binary (a stand-in shell instead, the real path run by hand twice)
decisions.why: Both are stated. The stale pid file is recovered by the next start (pinned by a test), so no wrong outcome is left. Coverage of new Rust is clean, which is what the brief asks of the tests.

decisions.summary: baseline read over the three kept hand logs, where the brief said four
decisions.why: An observation of what the directory holds, not a choice to leave one out. Two of the three reproduce the decision record's figures.

decisions.summary: exits: first-tier builder-checks and crate-checks here; the full gate runs once over the batch in the clone
decisions.why: The GM's two-tier ruling of 2026-11-26 (T308).

decisions.summary: counted as performance work; order after T285 and T316, before T351
decisions.why: The GM, 2026-11-20: 'this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task'; FR-013.

decisions.summary: The standing part of a builder's brief is printed by a command that sizes the brief first. A PreToolUse guard refuses a builder's dispatch that does not open with the command's marker. builder-brief.md keeps each rule with its incident.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 2026-11-26 question ('putting the instructions in the right place') answered with the 2026-11-19 standard ('real enforcement and not just instructions') and T285's ('not rely on you remembering'). The instructions move into tooling that prints them, and a dispatch without them is refused.

decisions.summary: The kinds are named fix|measurement|build-half|closing-half, not the task line's fix|measurement|mechanism-build|closing.
decisions.why: Only the name changes; the set of kinds and what each does are the same. The task line's kind names are the coordinating session's, not the GM's.

decisions.summary: An unsplit mechanism is refused by the command, not by the PreToolUse guard. Only a hand-edited marker evades it.
decisions.why: The refusal still fires on the only route that makes a marker, and the guard refuses any builder's dispatch without one. The gap left is a forged marker, which is deliberate circumvention rather than the forgetting the GM's words target. The cost reason given is not needed to place this within scope.

decisions.summary: A task is recognized as a mechanism by mechanism(): phrases on its tasks.md line, or a make target with a hyphen that the Makefile does not define.
decisions.why: This is how the sizing rule 'a mechanism as two builders' is detected. It reads the task's own line, not the caller's words.

decisions.summary: The escape SIZING_OK="<reason>" passes the mechanism refusal and is logged.
decisions.why: It is the project's escape pattern (FR-012: a reason, recorded). It covers a line that names a guard the task only repairs, which would otherwise be refused as correct work.

decisions.summary: A builder's dispatch is an ad-hoc Agent call whose prompt names a pool-registry path or carries a marker. This is narrower than spec D8's 'no defined agent' definition, so an ad-hoc builder working in the session clone with no pool tree passes unchecked (filed as T353, lands before T302).
decisions.why: Spec D8 defines a builder for the context cap, where reading every ad-hoc agent costs nothing. This guard demands a marker. On the replay day, applying D8's definition here would refuse the 17 ad-hoc dispatches that named no pool tree, measuring agents among them (observed 2026-11-26, the block's replay). That is a guard firing on correct work, and it defeats the purpose of real enforcement by teaching bypass (root CLAUDE.md). The prose cannot tell a reader from an editor, so the literal rule cannot be met without that cost. The leftover is filed with its reason and ordered before T302 (FR-009's form), so the feature still owes it.

decisions.summary: Defined agents, Explore and Plan are never a builder's dispatch.
decisions.why: Spec FR-006 and D8 exclude defined review agents from 'builder' too, and Explore and Plan do not build.

decisions.summary: A prompt opening 'Run the claims round' is exempt, as split.rs reads it.
decisions.why: The claims round was split off from the builders by the GM's 2026-11-25 'sounds good please do that ASAP'. It is not a code builder, and the exemption matches the existing split.rs reading.

decisions.summary: The marker and the escape count only on a line of their own. A pasted '<' placeholder is no reason.
decisions.why: This is a parsing convention that stops a mention in prose from passing as a marker or an escape. It is stricter, not narrower.

decisions.summary: The escape is checked after the 'is this a builder's dispatch' test and before every refusal, so every escape taken is logged.
decisions.why: It is an ordering convention that keeps the escape log truthful. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: KIND=measurement requires MEASURES.
decisions.why: It is stricter than the brief. It makes the measurement bound fire for T315's case, which is one of the motivating incidents.

decisions.summary: A bundle T=a,b is briefed as one builder on one tree, with the marker naming both. A mechanism among the tasks still refuses KIND=fix, and the guard holds the tree to every task named.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-22 bundling words ('small defects can be bundled together and worked at the same time') and builder-brief.md's 'one task or one bundle' both allow it. Refusing bundles, or escaping every one, would refuse correct work.

decisions.summary: Every sizing refusal runs before the pool's handout, so a refused brief holds no tree.
decisions.why: It is an ordering convention and is pinned by a test.

decisions.summary: JOBS_MAX is 3 (the sizing rule's own limit). MEASURES_MAX is 6, a GUESS knob. Both are listed in the audit register's covers.
decisions.why: JOBS_MAX follows the written rule. MEASURES_MAX is a labeled knob sitting under T315's observed seven, and it is registered for audit as the GM's 2026-11-25 register words ask.

decisions.summary: The measurement rule reads only lines opening 'Job|Part|Step <n>' that hold a fixed edit word, not every sentence. It misses T316's numbered list and is labeled GUESS; the T316/T308 shape is filed as T354, which lands before T302.
decisions.why: Taken literally, 'names a source edit' would require reading every prose sentence for an edit, and that would refuse correct measurement briefs. That is a guard firing on good work, which defeats the purpose by teaching bypass. The narrow form, what it misses and its false positive are stated at the guard's head and under Found and left. The detector was not tuned to fit the five incidents (the anti-overfit rule).

decisions.summary: Sizing reads the caller's declared KIND, JOBS and MEASURES. Only the mechanism test reads tasks.md independently. Item 4 says that even with a truthful caller, the sizing misses two of the five motivating briefs (T316 and T308).
decisions.why: Judged against the purpose (real enforcement, not reliance on remembering). The command runs before the brief's text is written: Approach item 1 says the brief 'is sized before it is written', and D8 puts every sizing refusal before the handout. So the wider reach (leftovers of tags this process never makes) is not a narrowing and needs no ruling. The search-space gap in the '.keep()' grep is reported apart from this verdict, as a finding for the builder; it does not block.

decisions.summary: Kept and pinned in a_gone_process_s_directories_go_with_the_next_process_of_any_tag: the pre-T101 form, hook-suite directories, l7r-test-scratch, files, a live pid's, anything changed within three hours, untagged names and names not opening l7r-.
decisions.why: This keeps the constraints the section reports from the GM's 2026-11-11 words as tempdir.rs quotes them: a leftover younger than three hours, and the form before T101, are not touched. Those words are not in this bundle, so this ruling rests on the section's report of them. It also keeps T365's rule that nothing a later run could reuse is deleted.

decisions.summary: A leftover now goes at the next process's first TempDir of any tag, which is sooner. A process that changes its TMPDIR after its first TempDir does not sweep the second directory.
decisions.why: Cleanup comes sooner in the common case. In the TMPDIR edge the leftover is still removed by a later process whose first TempDir is there, so nothing is lost. A difference from the old behavior is not a defect (constitution XIV), and no caller is said to do this.

decisions.summary: Of the task line's two routes, the plan takes the cleanup once a run: hookrun.sh --sweep on the Makefile's fan-out line before xargs. It does not move the suites' directories under one subdirectory.
decisions.why: The section says the task line offers two routes; the task line itself is not in the bundle. Either route is performance work the GM asked to come first (2026-11-20), and the GM gave no instruction on which to take. The route chosen moves no path, and the grep the section cites (with its method) shows three places that know the path's shape.

decisions.summary: The cleanup loop becomes the function sweep_gone, with unchanged removal. --sweep runs it and exits; --swept skips it; a job without the mark sweeps as before. The mark is a command word, not an exported variable, so nested runners in test-parts.2/3 still sweep.
decisions.why: This is a mechanism for doing the cleanup once a run. What it removes is unchanged, and a job run by hand or by a test keeps its old behavior.

decisions.summary: A suite run alone stays untouched, and a suite's TMPDIR stays <temp>/l7r-hooks-suite-<guard>-p<pid>.<x>.
decisions.why: No behavior or path changes for a lone suite or for a guard that reads a fixture by its /tmp path.

decisions.summary: A killed runner's leftover now waits for the next make hooks-test run that has a suite to run, where before it waited for the next suite of any run.
decisions.why: The section says the task line names this cost; the task line is not in the bundle. A killed runner's leftover waits for the next make hooks-test run that has a suite to run. That is the same event as before except in a run where every suite is skipped, and such a run makes no directory. Nothing is left unswept and no GM words are departed from, so no defect is left and no ruling is needed.

decisions.summary: Each process's first listing stays (the leak pin in rustc.rs, file-scale --selftest's one listing, the ledger and gate-write guards' TempDir per event), left to the already-filed T371 or T377.
decisions.why: Listing once a process is what T370 is. The remaining first listings are performance not yet taken, not a defect, and filed tasks own them. The hook suites' glob is taken here by T372. Found-and-left is truthfully 'none'.

decisions.summary: One landing. Crate-scoped builder-checks on rust/guard/shared and rust/guard plus tests/hooks/test-parts.2.sh in the builder's tree, then the full gate at landing. Red-first tests are recorded.
decisions.why: Crate-scoped checks run in the builder's tree and the full gate runs at the landing. That matches the GM's two tiers of checking (2026-11-26, T308: full rigor deferred to the session clone's gate). It is the procedure for checking the work and does not change what was asked.

decisions.summary: Two commands, make task-withdraw and make task-unstart, and the four filed tasks (T322 T323 T356 T358) withdrawn with the first. Now built in two halves.
decisions.why: Process tooling filed by the coordinating session from two observations of 2026-11-26. The GM's words name neither command, and having them narrows nothing in request.md. The GM's approval asks for real enforcement, and both commands refuse rather than instruct. Splitting the build in two halves is the order of the work, not a scope decision.

decisions.summary: A withdrawn box is ticked and carries ' Withdrawn YYYY-MM-DD: <why>'. The date is added to the form the task line gave.
decisions.why: Unchanged since round 1. A tooling form. It deviates from the coordinating session's task line, not from the GM's words.

decisions.summary: Only a stub that is the template byte for byte is removed, by the one stub test plan::template::stubs that the plan gate also uses. A filled section is refused.
decisions.why: Round 1 ruled it within. The only change is that without_stub now uses the same stub test as the plan gate (T359-D15). One test serving both places narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A task with an entry in plan-review.json's tasks is refused
decisions.why: Unchanged. It keeps reviewed work on the landing path.

decisions.summary: Code carried means a commit in origin/main..HEAD whose subject head names the feature and the task
decisions.why: Unchanged. A tooling convention.

decisions.summary: Two refusals beyond the brief: a box with an open box under it, and the feature's last open boxes
decisions.why: Unchanged. Adding refusals narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Every refusal is printed together, nothing is written while one stands, the filing lock is held, and the id stays reserved
decisions.why: Unchanged. A tooling convention.

decisions.summary: A TaskWithdrawn event line through the hooks' own writer
decisions.why: Unchanged. It records who withdrew the task and why.

decisions.summary: The unstart row's shape, with feature and task nested
decisions.why: Unchanged. A tooling convention.

decisions.summary: An unstart cancels every earlier start of its feature and task in its tree, so the filtered start log agrees with the tree's mark
decisions.why: Unchanged in substance. Every filtered reader agrees with the one mark, and that narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: An unstart followed by a new start resets no count of make static runs: static_runs_hooks reads the raw log for the count and counts the runs since the task's last landing from its first start, whatever unstarts lie between. STATIC_OK="<reason>" stays the one escape.
decisions.why: Round 1's item is answered. This is round 1's option (a), which is FR-007's own wording ('a third make static in one task since its last landing'): the count no longer restarts at an unstart, so task-unstart is no longer an escape from FR-007 without a recorded reason, and the one escape left is STATIC_OK with its reason (FR-012). Item 1 restates the goal to match. The test an_unstart_and_a_new_start_restart_no_count pins it, and item 9 reports it red first (rust/guard 550 passed, 1 failed, then 551 passed). The test cases are: start, the allowed runs, unstart, new start, next run refused; and a landing between resets the count. This was re-classed within because the narrowing is gone.

decisions.summary: A task worked, then unstarted and never started again, loses its earlier start in the time breakdown
decisions.why: Unchanged since round 1. The unstart row stays in the log, and the GM's definition of the breakdown does not ask it to be exact.

decisions.summary: Newly stated: a task unstarted and not started again 'carries no task, so it has no count and owes no closing order'. The guard's reading of whose task a call is uses the filtered view.
decisions.why: Weighed for one sequence: start, two runs, unstart, N runs while no task is started, start again. The N runs in the gap are not refused by FR-007. That is FR-007's own scope, which is runs 'in one task'. Leaving the started state by command is not new: D12 cites make set-down, which already clears a tree's mark. Once the task is started again it meets its full count, and the runs before the unstart still count (D9b). Neither the GM's words nor FR-007 ask for a count of runs made while no task is started. So this case opens no route past FR-007 that the no-task state did not already have. Nothing in the bundle shows that the no-task state was unreachable mid-work before T359. If it was, this entry would need to be reopened.

decisions.summary: A bundle is unstarted whole under its first task
decisions.why: Unchanged.

decisions.summary: The legacy one-mark file is unstarted as its own tree's mark, and a phase hold is lifted along with the start
decisions.why: Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Another tree's mark is refused, and the refusal names make -C <that tree>
decisions.why: Unchanged.

decisions.summary: The filter is used by every reader but one (fifteen call sites in seven crates). static_runs_hooks reads the raw log for its count of runs on purpose.
decisions.why: This was restated from 'all sixteen readers'. The one raw reader is the mechanism that enforces FR-007 (D9b), and the task it counts for is still taken through the filtered filed.rs. The list counts to fifteen, with land/ready.rs's two reads counted separately, across seven crates. The search space is stated in item 7: one search for the log's name over rust/, scripts/ and the Makefile. Each reader has a test in item 9's table.

decisions.summary: T366 is covered here: a withdrawal is refused when a builder holds a pool tree for the task, and the refusal names make builder-tree-release
decisions.why: Unchanged. An added refusal that names its compliant command.

decisions.summary: A withdrawn task's removed block owes no plan review only where its earlier text is a block of that task's template stub byte for byte, by the one stub test, with the trailing newlines aside
decisions.why: This is round 1's LEGITIMATE narrowing, now bounded as round 1 required. The plan-stage gate exists so that decisions do not reach a tick without an independent verdict. A block that is the unfilled template holds no decisions. Matching per block, with the trailing newlines aside, still decides nothing, because a filled block of the same section remains owed on its own. Round 1's case (a)-(b) did not depend on whether the stub is compared whole or by its blocks.

decisions.summary: The exemption is narrowed: the Withdrawn form of a box alone exempts nothing. A Withdrawn-form box whose filled section was deleted is answered for at the tick and at the push. A removed block whose earlier text cannot be read is owed.
decisions.why: Round 1's item is answered. The exemption now requires both a Withdrawn-form box and earlier text that is the stub byte for byte. That earlier text is read from the kept record or from the plan's history at the recorded digest, the same way removed_blocks reads it. So the hand-written case round 1 described (a box ticked by hand in the Withdrawn form, its filled section deleted) is caught at the gate, not only inside make task-withdraw. Unreadable earlier text is treated as owed, which fails closed. The red fixture round 1 asked for is pinned: a_withdrawn_form_box_whose_filled_block_was_removed_is_still_answered_for. Item 9 reports it red first (rust/gate/crates/plan 195 passed, 1 failed, then 197 passed). The case of a live block under a withdrawn heading that has no other owner stays owed. This entry narrows nothing, so it carries no ruling.

decisions.summary: The second-tree overwrite of a task's mark is deferred to T369, which lands before T302
decisions.why: Unchanged. It states why it is not fixed here, its filed id and its order, as FR-009 asks.

decisions.summary: Not performance work by FR-013's test
decisions.why: Unchanged. The tooling speeds nothing that FR-013 names and measures no time.

decisions.summary: T324: a SubagentStart/SubagentStop line (agent id, no call id) is keyed by agent, kind and second (Key::Agent), so every start and stop of a resumed agent is kept and a line two logs hold in one second is kept once
decisions.why: This is the fix itself. The T243 breakdown (request 2026-11-25) and the live view (T293) are asked to show where a task's time goes, and the old key dropped every start and stop after an agent's first. Keeping a same-second repeat once keeps the existing two-log dedup, so nothing new is decided.

decisions.summary: T324: descend and beside cut a wait at every span's end and at the ends of what an agent started (Ix::edges), where before they cut only at the first start and the last stop
decisions.why: This follows from keeping the lines. The booking had never seen an agent with two spans, and without this the 220 s red case was booked to 'after the work its Stop named had ended'. It applies the existing T243 rule that a wait is booked to what was in flight. It adds no new rule.

decisions.summary: T324: task_phases::windows is fixed here so that a stop ends its run, where it had kept an agent's first start for every later stop
decisions.why: This is a defect in another reader of the same stream: a session's own call between an agent's runs was marked as the agent's. It is fixed in this task with a red-first test. That is fixing as we go, not added scope.

decisions.summary: T324: subagent_runs, foreground_spans, feature_report/tables.rs, task_phases::cuts and where_time's walk were each read for repeated starts and stops and are left as they are, or yield each run. stepback_bundle and tool_yield are untouched
decisions.why: The section says what each reader does with repeated lines and finds no wrong outcome. A reader that already behaves correctly has nothing to fix.

decisions.summary: T324: in make task-progress, a resumed builder is RUNNING and one stopped again is stopped at its last stop. The hedge is dropped, the state line reads 'RUNNING, resumed after a stop', and make task-time's footnote says builder minutes are every span with the stopped time left out, and are a floor where T382's lines are
decisions.why: This serves T293 ('see while a task is in progress where the time is going'). The hedge is dropped only because the live view's rows come from the builder's own lines and not from its spans, so T382's gap does not reach them. The footnote tells the reader the one place the figures are still a floor, so nothing is hidden.

decisions.summary: T345: from a builder's stop to its next line (and from the line before a start, where no log holds the stop) the builder is STOPPED: a wait on everything it started, with no minutes of its own, so the time leaves the builders' model-turn rows
decisions.why: Amendment (i) makes the percentages 'of the time that our Claude Code sessions spent working', and a stopped builder is not working. The breakdown's existing rule already gives waits blocking and no minutes, as the main session's 'waiting: ...' rows have none. So the 25.6 min the old booking gave as the builder's model turn was a wrong outcome, and removing it is the fix. Amendment (c), 'never a silent other', is met because the time is not dropped unnamed: a reader sees it as blocking on what the stopped builder had in flight, or under the new STOPPED category's blocking, and task-time's footnote says the builder minutes leave the stopped time out.

decisions.summary: T345: one new category, 'builders: stopped, waiting to be resumed' (STOPPED in book/cats.rs), for stopped time with nothing of the builder's own in flight. Where its own run or agent is in flight, the wait is booked to that
decisions.why: Amendment (c) asks for every minute to be named, and the existing names would misstate this time: 'waiting on its background work' says something is running, and 'waiting: nothing in flight' is the main session's and is special-cased in descend. The wording says only what the log shows. Naming a category is within a breakdown the GM asked to be broken down automatically (j).

decisions.summary: T345: a builder is in flight from its first start to its last stop, and its stopped piece is booked through its stop's wait. A review agent between two rounds is not in flight
decisions.why: This applies the per-task, by-dependency blocking definition (l) to a resumed builder. The task does not end while its builder can still be resumed, but a review agent's next round is a new dispatch. No narrowing of the request.

decisions.summary: T345: a stopped builder with nothing of its own in flight is what a wait is on only where nothing else in flight blocks the task (stopped ranked last in each_task and descend). So beside a claims round, the session's wait is on the round
decisions.why: This applies (l), 'blocking ... when something else is waiting on it to be done'. A stopped builder does no work, so what the session waits on is the running round that will lead to its resumption. The GM accepted approximation in blocking attribution in (l) ('it doesn't have to be 100% exact'). There is a red-first test with the rank switched off.

decisions.summary: T345: stopped looks one level down, to the runs and agents the builder itself started
decisions.why: The section states that this is as deep as a builder's dispatches go: it dispatches review agents, not builders. Nothing deeper exists, so nothing is left out.

decisions.summary: Found and left: a builder's own lines after a stop with no SubagentStart between, or with no start at all, are in no span (columns::flight opens a span only at a start line), so the builder-minutes column and 'Working at once' leave them out (64 of 1,390 agents, 1,981 of 94,136 lines). Filed as T382, to land before T346
decisions.why: This is a defect, a column that understates, and it is left in place, so it is ruled. Its mechanism is different from the one T324 fixes. T324's is the reader's dedup key dropping start and stop lines that exist. T382's is the span rule in columns::flight having no line to open a span from, so there is no start or stop line for T324's goal ('every span from the log's own start and stop lines') to recover. The deferral meets FR-009 in full: it says why it is not fixed here, gives the filed id and gives its order ('lands before T346'). The defect is not hidden: task-time's footnote calls the builder minutes a floor where T382's lines are, and the live view's rows are unaffected. It is ordered ahead of the next measurement task, so it is not carried past the next step. The ruling does not rest on 'past this bundle's two jobs', which is a cost argument.

decisions.summary: T346 (a carry booked to the task that retook the tree) and T332/T344 (a pool tree's Phase lines carrying an old task) stay open and separate. The section states which columns they distort in its figures and that neither touches the builder-minutes column or the builders' turn rows
decisions.why: These are tasks already filed for other mechanisms, not defects this section found or was asked to fix. Saying what they distort in the published figures keeps those figures honest. Leaving a separately filed task to its own order is the bundling the GM described on 2026-11-22.
